title: Završna konferencija projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“
excerpt: Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore organizovalo je 7. jula 2026. godine u Naučno-tehnološkom parku Crne Gore završnu konferenciju projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“,…
content:
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore organizovalo je 7. jula 2026. godine u Naučno-tehnološkom parku Crne Gore završnu konferenciju projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“, čime je zaokružen višemjesečni proces edukacije, informisanja, zagovaranja i aktivnog uključivanja mladih u unapređenje njihovog položaja na tržištu rada.
Konferencija je okupila 57 učesnika, među kojima su bili predstavnici javnih institucija, obrazovnog sistema, organizacija civilnog društva, stručne javnosti, medija i mladi ambasadori dostojanstvenog rada. Konferenciji su prisustvovali i predstavnici ključnih institucija koje imaju važnu ulogu u kreiranju i sprovođenju politika u oblastima obrazovanja, zapošljavanja, inspekcijskog nadzora i zaštite i zdravlja na radu: Mladen Bigović iz Ministarstva prosvjete, nauke i inovacija, Dragana Đurović i Ljek Ljucgjonaj iz Ministarstva javne uprave, Maja Mijović iz Direktorata za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga, Alisa Dizdarević iz Zavoda za zapošljavanje Crne Gore, Nada Šekarić iz Centra za stručno obrazovanje i Slavko Čogurić, direktor Direktorata za inspekcijske poslove u Ministarstvu rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga.
Događaj je predstavljao završnu fazu projekta tokom koje su predstavljeni ostvareni rezultati, naučene lekcije i preporuke mladih za unapređenje javnih politika u oblastima dostojanstvenog rada, radnih prava i zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
U uvodnom dijelu konferencije prisutnima se obratila Aida Perović, izvršna direktorica NVO Prima, koja je predstavila projekat „Jači glasovi za bolje izbore“, u okviru kojeg je podržana realizacija projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“, kao i mrežu „Omladinski Hab za Zapadni Balkan i Tursku“. Poseban akcenat stavljen je na značaj uključivanja mladih u procese donošenja odluka, razvoja javnih politika i zagovaranja promjena koje odgovaraju njihovim stvarnim potrebama.
Nakon toga, Zdenko Janković, predsjednik Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, govorio je o značaju obrazovanja i kontinuirane edukacije mladih za izgradnju kulture prevencije i dostojanstvenog rada. Posebno je istakao da se svijest o radnim pravima i zaštiti i zdravlju na radu mora razvijati još tokom obrazovanja, prije prvog zaposlenja, jer upravo nedovoljna informisanost mladih često predstavlja jedan od razloga njihovog ulaska u nesigurne oblike rada. Takođe je predstavio dosadašnje aktivnosti Udruženja usmjerene ka edukaciji mladih, kao i planove za dalje unapređenje programa koji doprinose razvoju znanja o radnim pravima, bezbjednom radu i kulturi prevencije.
Rezultate projekta predstavila je Đina Janković, koordinatorka projekta, koja je kroz detaljnu prezentaciju prikazala pregled svih realizovanih aktivnosti, ostvarene pokazatelje uspješnosti, ključne rezultate i naučene lekcije. Predstavljene su edukativne radionice realizovane u srednjim stručnim školama širom Crne Gore, aktivnosti Help-line servisa / „Pravnog kutka za mlade“, medijska i online kampanja, saradnja sa institucijama i obrazovnim ustanovama, kao i aktivnosti usmjerene na jačanje učešća mladih u procesima javnog zagovaranja. Posebno je naglašeno da je kroz projekat otvoren prostor za dijalog između mladih i donosilaca odluka, te da su upravo mladi, kroz ulogu ambasadora dostojanstvenog rada, postali aktivni kreatori preporuka za unapređenje svog položaja na tržištu rada.
Centralni dio konferencije bio je posvećen predstavljanju preporuka mladih ambasadora dostojanstvenog rada, koje su nastale kao rezultat edukativnih radionica, istraživanja, rada sa vršnjacima i zagovaračkih aktivnosti realizovanih tokom projekta.
Arta Gjokaj govorila je o problemu rada na crno među mladima, ukazujući da prvi posao ne smije biti prvo iskustvo sa kršenjem radnih prava. Predstavila je preporuke koje se odnose na unapređenje informisanosti mladih, jačanje inspekcijskog nadzora, razvoj dostupnih mehanizama prijavljivanja nepravilnosti i promociju dostojanstvenog rada kao standarda, a ne privilegije.
Pavle Kovačević predstavio je preporuke koje se odnose na unapređenje položaja mladih uključenih u programe stručnog osposobljavanja i stručnog usavršavanja. Posebno je ukazao na potrebu sistemskog rješavanja pitanja nepriznavanja radnog staža tokom stručnog osposobljavanja, obezbjeđivanja kolektivnog osiguranja od povreda na radu, profesionalnih bolesti i bolesti u vezi sa radom, kao i obezbjeđivanja jednakog nivoa zaštite za sve mlade koji faktički obavljaju rad kod poslodavca.
Ivona Krgović predstavila je preporuke koje se odnose na unapređenje položaja mladih žena na tržištu rada, sa posebnim fokusom na menstrualno zdravlje, razmatranje menstrualnog odsustva kao pitanja dostojanstvenog rada, kao i potrebu prepoznavanja i smanjenja neplaćenog rada žena. Istaknuto je da dostojanstven rad nije moguć bez rodne ravnopravnosti i politika koje prepoznaju različite potrebe mladih žena.
Tokom diskusije otvoren je dijalog o mogućnostima daljeg unapređenja obrazovanja mladih u oblastima radnih prava i zaštite i zdravlja na radu, potrebi snažnijeg povezivanja obrazovnog sistema sa tržištem rada, unapređenju međuinstitucionalne saradnje, kao i jačanju preventivnog djelovanja kroz kontinuiranu edukaciju mladih. Posebno je naglašeno da preporuke mladih predstavljaju važan doprinos kreiranju budućih javnih politika, jer su nastale iz njihovih iskustava i stvarnih problema sa kojima se suočavaju prilikom ulaska na tržište rada.
Jedan od najvažnijih zaključaka konferencije jeste da su mladi pokazali da žele da budu aktivni učesnici, a ne samo korisnici javnih politika. Njihove preporuke otvorile su brojna pitanja koja zahtijevaju dalji institucionalni dijalog i zajedničko djelovanje nadležnih institucija, obrazovnog sistema, socijalnih partnera i organizacija civilnog društva.
Završna konferencija potvrdila je da je projekat „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“ ostvario svoj osnovni cilj – osnažio je mlade da razumiju svoja prava, prepoznaju izazove sa kojima se suočavaju na tržištu rada i aktivno učestvuju u kreiranju prijedloga za njihovo unapređenje. Istovremeno, konferencija je predstavljala važan korak ka nastavku saradnje između institucija i organizacija koje dijele zajednički cilj – stvaranje sigurnijeg, pravednijeg i dostojanstvenijeg tržišta rada za mlade u Crnoj Gori.
title_en: Closing conference of the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”
excerpt_en: On 7 July 2026, at the Science and Technology Park of Montenegro, the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro held the closing conference of the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”,…
content_en:
On 7 July 2026, at the Science and Technology Park of Montenegro, the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro held the closing conference of the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”, rounding off a process of several months of education, information, advocacy and the active involvement of young people in improving their position on the labour market.
The conference brought together 57 participants, among them representatives of public institutions, the education system, civil society organisations, the professional community and the media, as well as young ambassadors for decent work. It was also attended by representatives of the key institutions that play an important role in creating and implementing policy in education, employment, inspection supervision and occupational safety and health: Mladen Bigović of the Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation, Dragana Đurović and Ljek Ljucgjonaj of the Ministry of Public Administration, Maja Mijović of the Directorate for Occupational Safety and Health at the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, Alisa Dizdarević of the Employment Agency of Montenegro, Nada Šekarić of the Centre for Vocational Education, and Slavko Čogurić, director of the Directorate for Inspection Affairs at the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue.
The event marked the closing phase of the project, at which the results achieved, the lessons learned and young people's recommendations for improving public policy in the fields of decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health were presented.
In the opening part of the conference the participants were addressed by Aida Perović, executive director of the NGO Prima, who presented the project “Stronger voices for better choices”, under which the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change” was supported, as well as the “Youth Hub for the Western Balkans and Türkiye” network. Particular emphasis was placed on the importance of involving young people in decision-making, in the development of public policy and in advocating changes that respond to their real needs.
Zdenko Janković, president of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, then spoke about the importance of education and continuous training for young people in building a culture of prevention and decent work. He stressed in particular that awareness of labour rights and of occupational safety and health has to be developed while young people are still in education, before their first job, because it is precisely their lack of information that is often one of the reasons they enter insecure forms of work. He also presented the Association's work to date on educating young people, along with plans to further improve the programmes that build knowledge of labour rights, safe work and a culture of prevention.
The results of the project were presented by Đina Janković, the project coordinator, who gave a detailed presentation setting out all the activities carried out, the performance indicators achieved, the key results and the lessons learned. She presented the educational workshops held in secondary vocational schools across Montenegro, the work of the help-line service / “Legal corner for young people”, the media and online campaign, cooperation with institutions and educational establishments, and the activities aimed at strengthening young people's participation in public advocacy. It was particularly emphasised that the project opened up space for dialogue between young people and decision-makers, and that young people themselves, in their role as ambassadors for decent work, had become active authors of recommendations for improving their position on the labour market.
The central part of the conference was devoted to presenting the recommendations of the young ambassadors for decent work, which grew out of the educational workshops, research, peer work and advocacy activities carried out during the project.
Arta Gjokaj spoke about the problem of undeclared work among young people, pointing out that a first job must not also be a first experience of labour rights being violated. She presented recommendations on improving young people's access to information, strengthening inspection supervision, developing accessible mechanisms for reporting irregularities and promoting decent work as a standard rather than a privilege.
Pavle Kovačević presented recommendations on improving the position of young people taking part in professional training and professional development programmes. He pointed in particular to the need for a systemic solution to the fact that time spent in professional training is not recognised as length of service, to the need to provide collective insurance against injuries at work, occupational diseases and work-related illnesses, and to the need to provide an equal level of protection for all young people who in practice carry out work for an employer.
Ivona Krgović presented recommendations on improving the position of young women on the labour market, with a particular focus on menstrual health, on considering menstrual leave as a matter of decent work, and on the need to recognise and reduce women's unpaid work. It was emphasised that decent work is not possible without gender equality and policies that recognise the different needs of young women.
The discussion opened up a dialogue on how education for young people in labour rights and occupational safety and health could be further improved, on the need for stronger links between the education system and the labour market, on better inter-institutional cooperation, and on strengthening preventive action through the continuous education of young people. It was particularly emphasised that young people's recommendations are an important contribution to shaping future public policy, because they grew out of their own experiences and the real problems they face when entering the labour market.
One of the most important conclusions of the conference is that young people have shown that they want to be active participants in public policy, not merely its beneficiaries. Their recommendations opened up a number of questions that call for further institutional dialogue and joint action by the competent institutions, the education system, the social partners and civil society organisations.
The closing conference confirmed that the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change” achieved its basic aim: it gave young people the confidence to understand their rights, to recognise the challenges they face on the labour market and to take an active part in drawing up proposals to improve them. At the same time, the conference was an important step towards continued cooperation between the institutions and organisations that share a common goal — creating a safer, fairer and more dignified labour market for young people in Montenegro.

title: Okrugli sto – Mladi imaju glas
excerpt: Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore organizovalo je danas u Podgorici okrugli sto „Mladi imaju…
content:
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore organizovalo je danas u Podgorici okrugli sto „Mladi imaju glas – preporuke za unapređenje dostojanstvenog rada, radnih prava i zaštite i zdravlja na radu mladih u Crnoj Gori“, u okviru projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“, koji finansira Evropske unija, a kofinansira Ministartvo regionalno-investicionog razvoja i saradnje sa nevladinim organizacijama. Događaj je okupio predstavnike institucija, obrazovnog sistema, socijalnih partnera, organizacija civilnog društva i mlade ambasadore dostojanstvenog rada s ciljem otvaranja dijaloga o ključnim izazovima sa kojima se mladi suočavaju prilikom ulaska na tržište rada.
Okrugli sto organizovan je uz podršku projekta „Jači glasovi za bolje izbore“ i mreže „Omladinski Hab za Zapadni Balkan i Tursku“, a posebna vrijednost događaja bila je aktivna uloga mladih u definisanju preporuka za unapređenje javnih politika.
U uvodnom dijelu događaja, koordinatorka projekta Đina Janković predstavila je realizovane aktivnosti i ključne nalaze projekta, ukazujući na potrebu da se pitanja dostojanstvenog rada, radnih prava i zaštite i zdravlja na radu sistemski integrišu u obrazovne i omladinske politike. Izvršna direktorica NVO Prima, Aida Perović, istakla je značaj uključivanja mladih u procese donošenja odluka i javnog zagovaranja.
U panel diskusiji učestvovali su Dragan Marković, državni sekretar u Ministarstvu prosvjete, nauke i inovacija, koji je govorio o mogućnostima integracije tema dostojanstvenog rada, radnih prava i zaštite i zdravlja na radu u formalni obrazovni sistem; Anja Kečalović, načelnica Direkcije za razvoj omladinske politike u Ministarstvu sporta i mladih, koja je predstavila ulogu omladinskih politika u unapređenju položaja mladih na tržištu rada, sa posebnim fokusom na NEET mlade i mlade iz ranjivih grupa; Ilija Radunović iz Zavoda za zapošljavanje Crne Gore, koji je govorio o mjerama podrške mladima pri prelasku iz obrazovanja na tržište rada i unapređenju programa zapošljavanja za mlade; Jovana Bošković iz Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga, koja je ukazala na značaj zaštite i zdravlja na radu kao sastavnog dijela dostojanstvenog rada i potrebu jačanja preventivnih mjera i informisanosti mladih o njihovim pravima; Snežana Mijušković iz Institucije Zaštitnika ljudskih prava i sloboda Crne Gore, je govorila o mehanizmima zaštite radnih prava mladih i unapređenju jednakih mogućnosti i zaštite od diskriminacije; Nada Šekarić iz Centra za stručno obrazovanje, koja je istakla značaj unapređenja kvaliteta stručnog obrazovanja, bezbjednosti učenika na praktičnoj nastavi i povezivanja obrazovanja sa potrebama tržišta rada; te Zlatko Popović, glavni inspektor za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu, koji je ukazao na najčešće rizike kojima su mladi izloženi na radnim mjestima i značaj efikasnog inspekcijskog nadzora i dosljedne primjene propisa iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
Tokom diskusije istaknuto je da mladi u Crnoj Gori i dalje često započinju svoj profesionalni put kroz nesigurne oblike rada, bez dovoljno informacija o svojim pravima i bez adekvatne zaštite. Posebno je naglašena potreba za jačanjem saradnje između obrazovnog sistema, institucija, poslodavaca i organizacija civilnog društva kako bi se mladima omogućio bezbjedan i dostojanstven ulazak na tržište rada.
Mladi ambasadori dostojanstvenog rada predstavili su preporuke nastale kroz višemjesečne edukativne i zagovaračke aktivnosti projekta, fokusirajući se na tri ključne oblasti: suzbijanje rada na crno i drugih nesigurnih oblika rada, unapređenje položaja mladih uključenih u programe stručnog osposobljavanja i stručnog usavršavanja, te jačanje podrške menstrualnom zdravlju i prepoznavanje neplaćenog rada žena kao pitanja dostojanstvenog rada i jednakih mogućnosti.
Mladi su upozorili da rad na crno među mladima postaje zabrinjavajuće normalizovana pojava, zbog čega prvi posao za mnoge predstavlja i prvo iskustvo sa kršenjem radnih prava. Istaknuto je da mladi koji rade neprijavljeno ostaju bez ugovora, socijalne i zdravstvene zaštite, radnog staža i mehanizama zaštite u slučaju povrede na radu.
Posebna pažnja posvećena je položaju mladih uključenih u Program stručnog osposobljavanja visokoškolaca. Ukazano je na dugogodišnji sistemski problem činjenice da korisnicima programa devet mjeseci stručnog osposobljavanja ne ulazi u radni staž, iako rade u realnim radnim uslovima, obavljaju konkretne zadatke i preuzimaju odgovornost. Takođe, otvoreno je pitanje njihove zaštite na radu, obaveznog osiguranja od povreda na radu i profesionalnih bolesti, kao i kvaliteta mentorstva i nadzora tokom programa.
U okviru diskusije o položaju mladih žena na tržištu rada naglašeno je da pitanja menstrualnog zdravlja i neplaćenog rada žena ne smiju ostati isključivo u privatnoj sferi. Učesnici su istakli potrebu za otvaranjem stručnog i društvenog dijaloga o menstrualnom odsustvu, kao i za kreiranjem rodno osjetljivih politika koje će doprinijeti većoj ravnopravnosti i ekonomskom osnaživanju mladih žena.
Tokom otvorene diskusije zaključeno je da je neophodno sistemski integrisati teme dostojanstvenog rada, radnih prava i zaštite i zdravlja na radu u formalno i neformalno obrazovanje, unaprijediti informisanost mladih, ojačati preventivne mehanizme i osigurati efikasniju primjenu postojećih propisa.
Istovremeno, učesnici su istakli da je okrugli sto otvorio i brojna dodatna pitanja koja zahtijevaju dalji međusektorski dijalog i konkretne institucionalne odgovore. Među njima su potreba za sistemskim praćenjem položaja mladih na tržištu rada, unapređenje kvaliteta stručnog obrazovanja i praktične nastave, efikasniji nadzor nad uslovima rada mladih, razvoj dostupnih mehanizama podrške i prijavljivanja kršenja prava, kao i jačanje institucionalne odgovornosti za zaštitu mladih uključenih u različite oblike stručnog osposobljavanja.
Učesnici su izrazili spremnost da nastave saradnju i razmotre mogućnosti za njenu institucionalizaciju kroz memorandum o saradnji ili pismo namjere, kao važan korak ka dugoročnom unapređenju položaja mladih u Crnoj Gori.
Jer dostojanstven rad nije privilegija – to je pravo svakog mladog čovjeka.
title_en: Round table – Young people have a voice
excerpt_en: Today in Podgorica the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro held the round table “Young people have a…
content_en:
Today in Podgorica the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro held the round table “Young people have a voice – recommendations for improving decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health for young people in Montenegro”, under the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”, financed by the European Union and co-financed by the Ministry of Regional Investment Development and Cooperation with Non-Governmental Organisations. The event brought together representatives of institutions, the education system, the social partners, civil society organisations and young ambassadors for decent work, with the aim of opening a dialogue on the key challenges young people face when entering the labour market.
The round table was organised with the support of the project “Stronger voices for better choices” and the “Youth Hub for the Western Balkans and Türkiye” network, and the particular value of the event lay in the active role young people played in defining recommendations for improving public policy.
In the opening part of the event the project coordinator, Đina Janković, presented the activities carried out and the key findings of the project, pointing to the need to integrate decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health systematically into education and youth policy. The executive director of the NGO Prima, Aida Perović, emphasised the importance of involving young people in decision-making and public advocacy.
The panel discussion brought together Dragan Marković, state secretary at the Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation, who spoke about the scope for integrating decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health into the formal education system; Anja Kečalović, head of the Directorate for Youth Policy Development at the Ministry of Sport and Youth, who presented the role of youth policy in improving young people's position on the labour market, with a particular focus on NEET young people and young people from vulnerable groups; Ilija Radunović of the Employment Agency of Montenegro, who spoke about measures supporting young people in the transition from education to the labour market and about improving employment programmes for young people; Jovana Bošković of the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, who pointed to the importance of occupational safety and health as an integral part of decent work and to the need to strengthen preventive measures and young people's awareness of their rights; Snežana Mijušković of the Protector of Human Rights and Freedoms of Montenegro, who spoke about the mechanisms for protecting young people's labour rights and about improving equal opportunities and protection from discrimination; Nada Šekarić of the Centre for Vocational Education, who emphasised the importance of improving the quality of vocational education, the safety of pupils during practical training and the links between education and the needs of the labour market; and Zlatko Popović, chief inspector for occupational safety and health, who pointed to the most common risks young people are exposed to at work and to the importance of effective inspection supervision and consistent application of occupational safety and health regulations.
During the discussion it was emphasised that young people in Montenegro still often begin their working lives in insecure forms of work, without enough information about their rights and without adequate protection. Particular emphasis was placed on the need for stronger cooperation between the education system, institutions, employers and civil society organisations so that young people can enter the labour market safely and with dignity.
The young ambassadors for decent work presented recommendations arising from several months of educational and advocacy activities under the project, focusing on three key areas: tackling undeclared work and other insecure forms of work; improving the position of young people taking part in professional training and professional development programmes; and strengthening support for menstrual health and recognising women's unpaid work as a matter of decent work and equal opportunity.
Young people warned that undeclared work among the young is becoming a worryingly normalised phenomenon, so that for many a first job is also a first experience of labour rights being violated. It was emphasised that young people working without being registered are left without a contract, without social and health insurance, without length of service and without any mechanism of protection in the event of an injury at work.
Particular attention was paid to the position of young people taking part in the Professional Training Programme for graduates. Attention was drawn to the long-standing systemic problem that the nine months of professional training do not count towards participants' length of service, even though they work in real working conditions, carry out concrete tasks and take on responsibility. The question of their safety at work, of compulsory insurance against injuries at work and occupational diseases, and of the quality of mentoring and supervision during the programme was also raised.
In the discussion of the position of young women on the labour market it was emphasised that questions of menstrual health and of women's unpaid work must not be left solely in the private sphere. Participants stressed the need to open a professional and public dialogue on menstrual leave, and to create gender-sensitive policies that will contribute to greater equality and the economic empowerment of young women.
The open discussion concluded that it is essential to integrate decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health systematically into formal and non-formal education, to improve young people's access to information, to strengthen preventive mechanisms and to ensure that the existing regulations are applied more effectively.
At the same time, participants emphasised that the round table had also opened up a number of further questions that call for continued cross-sectoral dialogue and concrete institutional responses. Among them are the need for systematic monitoring of young people's position on the labour market, improvements in the quality of vocational education and practical training, more effective supervision of young people's working conditions, the development of accessible mechanisms for support and for reporting violations of rights, and stronger institutional accountability for protecting young people involved in the various forms of professional training.
Participants expressed their readiness to continue working together and to consider ways of institutionalising that cooperation through a memorandum of cooperation or a letter of intent, as an important step towards a lasting improvement in the position of young people in Montenegro.
Because decent work is not a privilege — it is the right of every young person.

title: Sastanak Radne grupe za unapređenje metodologije osposobljavanja zaposlenih za bezbjedan i zdrav rad
excerpt: Dana 19. maja 2026. godine, u prostorijama Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, održan je…
content:
Dana 19. maja 2026. godine, u prostorijama Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, održan je sastanak Radne grupe za unapređenje metodologije osposobljavanja zaposlenih za bezbjedan i zdrav rad, formirane sa ciljem unapređenja kvaliteta jednog od najvažnijih preventivnih mehanizama u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
Sastanku su prisustvovali predstavnici renomiranih kompanija i institucija iz različitih privrednih sektora, i to:
• Milica Filipović, 13. jul Plantaže
• Jelena Kasalica, Port of Adria
• Radoman Bakić, Klinički centar Crne Gore
• Bojana Kalezić, Radio Televizija Crne Gore (RTCG)
• Tamara Grgurović, MTEL
• Sanja Dujović, Uniprom KAP
• Marko Đuričić, Mehanizacija i Programat, Nikšić
• Zdenko Janković, Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore
• Đina Janković, Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore
Okupljanje stručnjaka iz različitih oblasti predstavlja važan iskorak ka razvoju savremenog i praktično primjenjivog modela osposobljavanja zaposlenih, zasnovanog na razmjeni iskustava, stručnog znanja i primjera iz svakodnevne prakse.
Potreba za unapređenjem postojećeg sistema osposobljavanja
Osposobljavanje zaposlenih za bezbjedan i zdrav rad predstavlja jednu od osnovnih zakonskih obaveza poslodavca, ali i jedan od najznačajnijih instrumenata prevencije povreda na radu, profesionalnih bolesti i drugih neželjenih događaja.
Međutim, iskustva stručnih lica i analiza dosadašnje prakse ukazuju da se ovaj proces u značajnom broju slučajeva i dalje sprovodi pretežno kao formalna obaveza, bez dovoljnog praktičnog efekta na ponašanje zaposlenih i unapređenje kulture bezbjednosti.
Često se osposobljavanje svodi na upoznavanje zaposlenih sa zakonskim propisima i internim aktima, dok izostaje razvoj praktičnih kompetencija koje zaposlenima omogućavaju da prepoznaju opasnosti na radnom mjestu, pravilno procjenjuju rizike i adekvatno reaguju u potencijalno opasnim situacijama.
Upravo iz tog razloga javila se potreba za izradom nove metodologije koja će osposobljavanje učiniti sadržajnijim, interaktivnijim i usmjerenim na stvarne izazove sa kojima se zaposleni susreću u svakodnevnom radu.
Značaj multidisciplinarnog pristupa
Jedna od najvećih vrijednosti Radne grupe ogleda se u njenom multidisciplinarnom sastavu.
Predstavnici građevinarstva, industrije, zdravstva, telekomunikacija, medija, lučke djelatnosti, proizvodnje i drugih oblasti donose različita iskustva i omogućavaju da nova metodologija odgovori na potrebe različitih radnih okruženja.
Iako se rizici razlikuju od djelatnosti do djelatnosti, zajednički cilj ostaje isti – razviti sistem osposobljavanja koji će kod zaposlenih izgraditi svijest o značaju bezbjednog ponašanja, podstaći odgovornost i doprinijeti smanjenju broja povreda na radu.
Tokom sastanka razmatrana su brojna pitanja koja se odnose na strukturu buduće metodologije, način prezentovanja sadržaja, uključivanje praktičnih primjera iz prakse, studija slučaja, interaktivnih metoda rada, kao i mogućnosti prilagođavanja programa specifičnostima pojedinih radnih mjesta.
Poseban akcenat stavljen je na činjenicu da savremeno osposobljavanje mora biti razumljivo, praktično i usmjereno na promjenu ponašanja zaposlenih, a ne isključivo na ispunjavanje zakonske procedure.
Od formalnog pristupa ka stvarnoj kulturi prevencije
Savremeni koncept zaštite i zdravlja na radu zasniva se na kulturi prevencije, koja podrazumijeva da se rizici prepoznaju i sprječavaju prije nego što dođe do povrede ili profesionalnog oboljenja.
Kvalitetno osposobljavanje zaposlenih predstavlja osnov za razvoj takve kulture.
Zaposleni koji razumiju rizike kojima su izloženi, poznaju pravilne procedure rada i svjesni su svojih prava, obaveza i odgovornosti, značajno manje doprinose nastanku neželjenih događaja i aktivnije učestvuju u unapređenju bezbjednosti na radnom mjestu.
S druge strane, kvalitetno osposobljavanje doprinosi i poslodavcima, jer omogućava efikasnije upravljanje rizicima, smanjenje troškova nastalih usljed povreda na radu, povećanje produktivnosti i jačanje ukupne organizacione kulture.
Dalji koraci
Radna grupa će u narednom periodu nastaviti intenzivan rad na izradi metodologije osposobljavanja zaposlenih za bezbjedan i zdrav rad, sa ciljem da kreira dokument koji će biti praktičan, savremen i primjenjiv u različitim djelatnostima.
Po završetku izrade metodologije planirano je organizovanje stručne radionice na kojoj će rezultati rada biti predstavljeni široj stručnoj javnosti, predstavnicima poslodavaca, stručnim licima iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, institucijama i svim zainteresovanim subjektima.
Na taj način biće otvoren prostor za razmjenu mišljenja, dodatna unapređenja i zajedničko definisanje preporuka koje će doprinijeti unapređenju sistema osposobljavanja u Crnoj Gori.
Formiranje i rad Radne grupe predstavlja važan korak ka unapređenju sistema zaštite i zdravlja na radu u Crnoj Gori.
Kroz zajednički rad stručnjaka iz različitih oblasti potvrđuje se da unapređenje bezbjednosti na radu zahtijeva multidisciplinaran pristup, kontinuiranu razmjenu iskustava i spremnost da se postojeće prakse prilagode savremenim izazovima.
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore, kao inicijator ove aktivnosti, nastavlja da aktivno doprinosi razvoju stručnih rješenja i unapređenju kulture prevencije, sa jasnim ciljem – da osposobljavanje zaposlenih bude stvarni alat za zaštitu života i zdravlja, a ne samo zakonska obaveza.
Jer kvalitetna edukacija nije administrativna forma – ona predstavlja jednu od najvažnijih investicija u bezbjednije radno okruženje i očuvanje najvrijednijeg resursa svake organizacije – čovjeka.
title_en: Meeting of the Working Group for improving the methodology of training employees for safe and healthy work
excerpt_en: On 19 May 2026, at the premises of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, a meeting was held of…
content_en:
On 19 May 2026, at the premises of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, a meeting was held of the Working Group for improving the methodology of training employees for safe and healthy work, set up with the aim of improving the quality of one of the most important preventive mechanisms in occupational safety and health.
The meeting was attended by representatives of well-known companies and institutions from a range of economic sectors, namely:
• Milica Filipović, 13. jul Plantaže
• Jelena Kasalica, Port of Adria
• Radoman Bakić, Clinical Centre of Montenegro
• Bojana Kalezić, Radio Television of Montenegro (RTCG)
• Tamara Grgurović, MTEL
• Sanja Dujović, Uniprom KAP
• Marko Đuričić, Mehanizacija i Programat, Nikšić
• Zdenko Janković, Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro
• Đina Janković, Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro
Bringing together experts from different fields is an important step towards developing a modern and practically applicable model of employee training, built on the exchange of experience, professional knowledge and examples from everyday practice.
The need to improve the existing training system
Training employees for safe and healthy work is one of an employer's basic legal obligations, but also one of the most significant instruments for preventing injuries at work, occupational diseases and other unwanted events.
The experience of safety professionals and an analysis of practice to date show, however, that in a significant number of cases this process is still carried out largely as a formality, without enough practical effect on employees' behaviour or on improving the safety culture.
Training is often reduced to acquainting employees with the legal regulations and internal rules, while the development of practical competences that would allow employees to recognise hazards at the workplace, assess risks correctly and respond appropriately in potentially dangerous situations is left out.
It is precisely for this reason that the need arose to draw up a new methodology that will make training richer in content, more interactive and focused on the real challenges employees meet in their everyday work.
The importance of a multidisciplinary approach
One of the greatest strengths of the Working Group lies in its multidisciplinary composition.
Representatives of construction, industry, health care, telecommunications, the media, port operations, manufacturing and other fields bring different experience and make it possible for the new methodology to answer the needs of different working environments.
Although the risks differ from one sector to another, the shared aim remains the same — to develop a training system that will build employees' awareness of the importance of behaving safely, encourage responsibility and help reduce the number of injuries at work.
The meeting considered a range of questions relating to the structure of the future methodology, the way content is presented, the inclusion of practical examples, case studies and interactive working methods, and the scope for adapting the programme to the particular features of individual workplaces.
Particular emphasis was placed on the fact that modern training must be understandable, practical and aimed at changing employees' behaviour, not solely at satisfying a legal procedure.
From a formal approach to a real culture of prevention
The modern concept of occupational safety and health rests on a culture of prevention, which means that risks are recognised and prevented before an injury or occupational disease occurs.
Good-quality training of employees is the foundation for developing such a culture.
Employees who understand the risks they are exposed to, know the correct working procedures and are aware of their rights, obligations and responsibilities contribute significantly less to unwanted events and take a more active part in improving safety at the workplace.
On the other hand, good-quality training also benefits employers, because it makes it possible to manage risks more efficiently, to reduce the costs arising from injuries at work, to increase productivity and to strengthen the overall organisational culture.
Next steps
Over the coming period the Working Group will continue its intensive work on drawing up the methodology for training employees for safe and healthy work, with the aim of producing a document that is practical, modern and applicable across different sectors.
Once the methodology is complete, a professional workshop is planned at which the results of the work will be presented to the wider professional community, to employers' representatives, to occupational safety and health professionals, to institutions and to all interested parties.
This will open up space for an exchange of views, for further improvements and for jointly defining recommendations that will help improve the training system in Montenegro.
The formation and work of the Working Group is an important step towards improving the occupational safety and health system in Montenegro.
The joint work of experts from different fields confirms that improving safety at work calls for a multidisciplinary approach, a continuous exchange of experience and a willingness to adapt existing practice to modern challenges.
The Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, as the initiator of this activity, continues to contribute actively to developing professional solutions and improving the culture of prevention, with a clear aim — that training employees should be a real tool for protecting life and health, and not merely a legal obligation.
Because good education is not an administrative formality — it is one of the most important investments in a safer working environment and in preserving the most valuable resource any organisation has: people.

title: SASTANAK SA MLADIM AMBASADORIMA DOSTOJANSTVENOG RADA U OKVIRU PROJEKTA „GLAS MLADIH ZA DOSTOJANSTVEN RAD OD ZNANJA DO PROMJENE“
excerpt: Dana 19. maja 2026. godine održan je radni sastanak sa Milicom Rukavinom, jednom od izabranih…
content:
Dana 19. maja 2026. godine održan je radni sastanak sa Milicom Rukavinom, jednom od izabranih mladih ambasadorki dostojanstvenog rada u okviru projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“.
Sastanak je organizovan sa ciljem razmatranja dosadašnjih rezultata projekta, upoznavanja ambasadorke sa planiranom dinamikom narednih aktivnosti, kao i definisanja njenog daljeg angažmana u okviru zagovaračkih i promotivnih aktivnosti koje će biti realizovane tokom narednog perioda.
Razmatranje dosadašnjih aktivnosti projekta
Tokom sastanka predstavljen je pregled do sada realizovanih aktivnosti projekta, sa posebnim osvrtom na edukativno-zagovaračku radionicu održanu u Podgorici, kao i edukativne radionice realizovane u srednjim stručnim školama širom Crne Gore.
Naglašeno je da projekat ima za cilj unapređenje znanja mladih o dostojanstvenom radu, radnim pravima i zaštiti i zdravlju na radu, kao i njihovo osnaživanje za aktivno učešće u procesima javnog zagovaranja i kreiranja preporuka za unapređenje položaja mladih na tržištu rada.
Posebno je istaknuta važnost uloge mladih ambasadora kao nosilaca projektnih poruka i predstavnika interesa mladih u procesima dijaloga sa donosiocima odluka i drugim relevantnim akterima.
Planiranje narednih aktivnosti
Jedna od ključnih tema sastanka odnosila se na planiranje predstojećih aktivnosti u okviru projekta.
Ambasadorka je upoznata sa narednim fazama projekta, uključujući aktivnosti javnog zagovaranja, promociju kreiranih preporuka, učešće na javnim događajima i planirani okrugli sto sa predstavnicima institucija, organizacija civilnog društva i drugim relevantnim akterima.
Razgovarano je o mogućnostima aktivnog uključivanja ambasadora u pripremu i realizaciju ovih aktivnosti, kao i o načinima na koje mladi mogu doprinijeti vidljivosti tema dostojanstvenog rada među svojim vršnjacima.
Kreiranje zagovaračkih video sadržaja
Poseban dio sastanka bio je posvećen kreiranju kratkih video sadržaja koji predstavljaju jednu od planiranih aktivnosti projekta.
Razmatrani su koncepti, ključne poruke i pristupi koji će biti korišćeni prilikom snimanja zagovaračkih video materijala, sa ciljem da se na jednostavan, autentičan i mladima blizak način ukaže na probleme sa kojima se suočavaju prilikom ulaska na tržište rada.
Naglašeno je da video sadržaji treba da doprinesu podizanju svijesti o radnim pravima, značaju zaštite i zdravlja na radu i potrebi aktivnijeg uključivanja mladih u procese donošenja odluka koje utiču na njihov položaj.
Razmatranje preporuka i prioritetnih tema za zagovaranje
Tokom sastanka razgovarano je i o preporukama koje su mladi definisali tokom edukativno-zagovaračke radionice, a koje predstavljaju osnov za dalje zagovaračke aktivnosti projekta.
Posebna pažnja posvećena je problemima koje su sami mladi prepoznali kao najizraženije izazove na tržištu rada:
• rad na crno i nesigurni oblici zapošljavanja;
• potreba otvaranja javnog dijaloga o menstrualnom odsustvu kao pitanju dostojanstvenog rada i zdravlja;
• unapređenje položaja mladih uključenih u programe stručnog osposobljavanja i stručnog usavršavanja.
Razgovarano je o mogućim načinima predstavljanja ovih tema javnosti, kao i o ulozi ambasadora u promovisanju ključnih zagovaračkih poruka i preporuka.
Sastanak je protekao u konstruktivnoj i radnoj atmosferi, uz aktivno učešće ambasadorke i izraženu zainteresovanost za nastavak angažmana u okviru projekta.
Zaključeno je da će mladi ambasadori imati važnu ulogu u narednoj fazi projekta, posebno u promociji zagovaračkih poruka, kreiranju video sadržaja i predstavljanju preporuka mladih tokom javnih događaja i dijaloga sa relevantnim institucijama.
Održani sastanak predstavlja važan korak u jačanju uloge mladih u procesima javnog zagovaranja i potvrđuje opredijeljenost projekta da mladima omogući aktivno učešće u kreiranju promjena koje se odnose na njihov položaj, prava i dostojanstven rad.
📌 Projekat finansira Evropska unija, a kofinansira Ministarstvo regionalno-investicionog razvoja i saradnje sa nevladinim organizacijama, u okviru mreže YHWBT.

title_en: MEETING WITH THE YOUNG AMBASSADORS FOR DECENT WORK UNDER THE PROJECT “YOUTH VOICES FOR DECENT WORK – FROM KNOWLEDGE TO CHANGE”
excerpt_en: On 19 May 2026 a working meeting was held with Milica Rukavina, one of the selected young…
content_en:
On 19 May 2026 a working meeting was held with Milica Rukavina, one of the selected young ambassadors for decent work under the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”.
The meeting was organised in order to review the results of the project so far, to acquaint the ambassador with the planned timetable of the coming activities, and to define her further engagement in the advocacy and promotional activities to be carried out over the period ahead.
Review of the project's activities so far
The meeting included an overview of the project activities carried out to date, with particular reference to the educational and advocacy workshop held in Podgorica and to the educational workshops held in secondary vocational schools across Montenegro.
It was emphasised that the project aims to improve young people's knowledge of decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health, and to give them the confidence to take an active part in public advocacy and in drawing up recommendations for improving the position of young people on the labour market.
Particular emphasis was placed on the importance of the young ambassadors' role as bearers of the project's messages and as representatives of young people's interests in dialogue with decision-makers and other relevant actors.
Planning the coming activities
One of the key topics of the meeting was the planning of the project's forthcoming activities.
The ambassador was briefed on the next phases of the project, including public advocacy activities, promotion of the recommendations drawn up, participation in public events and the planned round table with representatives of institutions, civil society organisations and other relevant actors.
The discussion covered the scope for involving the ambassadors actively in preparing and carrying out these activities, and the ways in which young people can help make the subject of decent work more visible among their peers.
Creating advocacy video content
One part of the meeting was devoted to creating short videos, one of the project's planned activities.
The concepts, key messages and approaches to be used in filming the advocacy video material were discussed, with the aim of pointing out, in a simple and authentic way that speaks to young people, the problems they face when entering the labour market.
It was emphasised that the videos should help raise awareness of labour rights, of the importance of occupational safety and health, and of the need for young people to be more actively involved in the decisions that affect their position.
Consideration of recommendations and priority topics for advocacy
The meeting also discussed the recommendations young people defined during the educational and advocacy workshop, which form the basis for the project's further advocacy work.
Particular attention was paid to the problems young people themselves identified as the most pressing challenges on the labour market:
• undeclared work and insecure forms of employment;
• the need to open a public dialogue on menstrual leave as a matter of decent work and health;
• improving the position of young people taking part in professional training and professional development programmes.
Possible ways of presenting these topics to the public were discussed, as was the ambassadors' role in promoting the key advocacy messages and recommendations.
The meeting was held in a constructive working atmosphere, with the ambassador taking an active part and expressing keen interest in continuing her engagement in the project.
It was concluded that the young ambassadors will have an important role in the next phase of the project, particularly in promoting the advocacy messages, creating video content and presenting young people's recommendations at public events and in dialogue with the relevant institutions.
The meeting is an important step in strengthening the role of young people in public advocacy and confirms the project's commitment to enabling young people to take an active part in creating changes that affect their position, their rights and decent work.

title: Konferencija „Od regulative do zaštite: Poglavlje 19 i nova generacija lične zaštitne opreme“
excerpt: Dana 18. maja 2026. godine, u organizaciji Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga, u Naučno-tehnološkom…
content:
Dana 18. maja 2026. godine, u organizaciji Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga, u Naučno-tehnološkom parku Crne Gore održana je konferencija pod nazivom „Od regulative do zaštite: Poglavlje 19 i nova generacija lične zaštitne opreme“, posvećena obilježavanju Svjetskog dana zaštite i zdravlja na radu i jednom od najvažnijih pitanja savremenog sistema bezbjednosti i zdravlja na radu – praktičnoj primjeni standarda zaštite kroz kvalitetnu ličnu zaštitnu opremu.
Konferencija je okupila više od 200 učesnika iz institucija, privrede, međunarodnih organizacija, stručne javnosti i socijalnih partnera, dok je više od 120 članova Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore aktivno prisustvovalo ovom događaju, što jasno govori o stepenu profesionalnog interesovanja i odgovornosti stručne zajednice za unapređenje ove oblasti.
Za naše Udruženje, ova konferencija je imala poseban značaj jer je, pored regulatornog okvira i evropskih integracionih obaveza iz Poglavlja 19 – Socijalna politika i zapošljavanje, u fokus stavila upravo ličnu zaštitnu opremu kao jednu od posljednjih, ali presudnih linija odbrane zaposlenog od povrede, profesionalne bolesti i trajnih posljedica po zdravlje.
Upravo u toj oblasti Crna Gora se i dalje suočava sa brojnim ozbiljnim izazovima.
Iako zakonodavni okvir prepoznaje obavezu poslodavca da zaposlenima obezbijedi adekvatnu ličnu zaštitnu opremu, praksa često pokazuje da se ova obaveza nerijetko svodi na formalno ispunjavanje minimuma, bez suštinskog razumijevanja značaja kvaliteta, sertifikacije i stvarne zaštitne funkcije opreme koja se stavlja na raspolaganje zaposlenima.
Na crnogorskom tržištu i dalje je prisutan problem dostupnosti opreme neujednačenog kvaliteta, pri čemu krajnji korisnici, a nerijetko ni naručioci, nemaju dovoljno jasne mehanizme provjere da li ponuđena oprema zaista ispunjava propisane evropske standarde i bezbjednosne zahtjeve. Posebno zabrinjava činjenica da se u postupcima javnih nabavki i tendera izbor ponuđača često dominantno zasniva na kriterijumu najniže cijene, dok kvalitet, provjerena usklađenost sa standardima, trajnost, ergonomija i stvarna zaštitna efikasnost ostaju u drugom planu.
Takav pristup nosi ozbiljne posljedice, jer najniža cijena ne znači nužno i odgovarajući nivo zaštite. Kada je riječ o bezbjednosti zaposlenih, kompromisi po pitanju kvaliteta opreme mogu imati direktne posljedice po zdravlje i život ljudi.
Jednako važan izazov predstavlja i još uvijek nedovoljno razvijena svijest dijela poslodavaca da ulaganje u kvalitetnu zaštitnu opremu nije trošak, već investicija u ljude, kontinuitet poslovanja, smanjenje povreda i ukupnu organizacionu odgovornost. Bez stvarnog razumijevanja da prevencija uvijek košta manje od posljedica povreda na radu, teško je govoriti o zreloj kulturi bezbjednosti.
Međutim, odgovornost nije isključivo na poslodavcima.
Kao strukovno udruženje, smatramo važnim istaći i činjenicu da je kod određenog broja zaposlenih i dalje prisutna nedovoljna svijest o značaju dosljedne upotrebe zaštitne opreme, čak i kada je ona obezbijeđena. U praksi se i dalje susrećemo sa otporom prema korišćenju zaštitnih sredstava zbog navodne neudobnosti, navike, potcjenjivanja rizika ili uvjerenja da se „ništa neće dogoditi“. Takav odnos dodatno potvrđuje da kultura bezbjednosti nije samo pitanje propisa i nabavke opreme, već pitanje edukacije, navika, odgovornosti i ukupne promjene profesionalne svijesti.
Upravo zato ovakvi stručni skupovi imaju izuzetnu vrijednost.
Oni ne predstavljaju samo formalna okupljanja povodom važnih datuma, već platformu za otvoreni dijalog o realnim problemima sistema zaštite na radu — od regulatornih izazova i usklađivanja sa evropskim direktivama, do praktičnih pitanja kvaliteta opreme, odgovornosti poslodavaca, ponašanja zaposlenih i potrebe za snažnijim preventivnim pristupom.
Posebno značajnim ocjenjujemo izložbeni segment konferencije, na kojem su predstavljena savremena rješenja iz oblasti lične zaštitne opreme. Među izlagačima se istakla renomirana kompanija VATROOPREMA, članica Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, koja je predstavila savremena i standardizovana rješenja u oblasti zaštitne opreme, potvrđujući koliko je važno da stručna i odgovorna privreda aktivno učestvuje u razvoju bezbjednosne kulture.
Prisustvo kompanija koje ulažu u kvalitet, standarde i tehnološki razvoj šalje važnu poruku tržištu — da zaštitna oprema ne smije biti tretirana kao formalna obaveza, već kao suštinski element sistema zaštite zdravlja i života zaposlenih.
Konferencija je dodatno podsjetila da je oblast zaštite i zdravlja na radu jedno od važnih mjerila u procesu zatvaranja Poglavlja 19, ali i da evropske integracije ne smiju ostati samo pitanje formalnog usklađivanja propisa. Suštinski napredak podrazumijeva stvarnu promjenu prakse.
A praksa nam jasno pokazuje da je kultura bezbjednosti u Crnoj Gori još uvijek nedovoljno razvijena.
Zato je neophodno nastaviti sa edukacijom, jačanjem stručne odgovornosti, unapređenjem kontrolnih mehanizama, insistiranjem na kvalitetu zaštitne opreme i promocijom principa da bezbjednost nikada ne smije biti predmet kompromisa.
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore ostaje snažno opredijeljeno da kroz stručni angažman, partnerstva i aktivno učešće u javnom dijalogu doprinosi izgradnji sistema u kojem će bezbjedan i zdrav rad biti standard, a ne izuzetak.
title_en: Conference “From regulation to protection: Chapter 19 and a new generation of personal protective equipment”
excerpt_en: On 18 May 2026, organised by the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, the Science and Technology…
content_en:
On 18 May 2026, organised by the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, the Science and Technology Park of Montenegro hosted a conference entitled “From regulation to protection: Chapter 19 and a new generation of personal protective equipment”, devoted to marking World Day for Safety and Health at Work and to one of the most important questions facing any modern occupational safety and health system — the practical application of protection standards through good-quality personal protective equipment.
The conference brought together more than 200 participants from institutions, industry, international organisations, the professional community and the social partners, while more than 120 members of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro took an active part in the event — a clear indication of the level of professional interest in this field and of the professional community's sense of responsibility for improving it.
For our Association the conference had a particular significance because, alongside the regulatory framework and the European integration obligations arising from Chapter 19 – Social Policy and Employment, it placed personal protective equipment squarely in focus as one of the last but decisive lines of defence protecting an employee from injury, occupational disease and lasting damage to health.
It is precisely in this area that Montenegro still faces a number of serious challenges.
Although the legislative framework recognises the employer's obligation to provide employees with adequate personal protective equipment, practice often shows that this obligation is frequently reduced to formally meeting a minimum, without any real understanding of the importance of quality, certification and the actual protective function of the equipment made available to employees.
The Montenegrin market still suffers from the availability of equipment of uneven quality, while end users — and often the purchasers too — have no sufficiently clear mechanism for checking whether the equipment offered really does meet the prescribed European standards and safety requirements. Particularly worrying is the fact that in public procurement and tender procedures the choice of supplier is often based predominantly on the lowest-price criterion, while quality, verified compliance with standards, durability, ergonomics and real protective effectiveness are left in the background.
Such an approach carries serious consequences, because the lowest price does not necessarily mean an appropriate level of protection. Where the safety of employees is concerned, compromises on the quality of equipment can have direct consequences for people's health and lives.
An equally important challenge is that some employers are still insufficiently aware that investing in good-quality protective equipment is not a cost but an investment in people, in business continuity, in fewer injuries and in overall organisational responsibility. Without a real understanding that prevention always costs less than the consequences of injuries at work, it is hard to speak of a mature safety culture.
The responsibility, however, does not lie with employers alone.
As a professional association, we think it important to point out that a proportion of employees are still insufficiently aware of the importance of using protective equipment consistently, even when it has been provided. In practice we still encounter resistance to using protective equipment on the grounds of supposed discomfort, habit, an underestimation of the risk or a belief that “nothing will happen”. That attitude further confirms that a safety culture is not merely a question of regulations and procurement, but a question of education, habits, responsibility and an overall change in professional awareness.
That is precisely why professional gatherings of this kind are so valuable.
They are not merely formal events to mark important dates, but a platform for open dialogue about the real problems of the occupational safety system — from regulatory challenges and alignment with European directives to practical questions of the quality of equipment, employers' responsibility, employees' behaviour and the need for a stronger preventive approach.
We consider the exhibition part of the conference, at which modern solutions in personal protective equipment were presented, to be particularly significant. Among the exhibitors, the well-known company VATROOPREMA, a member of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, stood out, presenting modern, standardised solutions in protective equipment and confirming how important it is for expert, responsible businesses to take an active part in developing a safety culture.
The presence of companies that invest in quality, standards and technological development sends an important message to the market — that protective equipment must not be treated as a formality, but as an essential element of the system that protects employees' health and lives.
The conference was a further reminder that occupational safety and health is one of the important benchmarks in the process of closing Chapter 19, but also that European integration must not remain merely a question of formally aligning regulations. Real progress means real change in practice.
And practice shows us clearly that the safety culture in Montenegro is still insufficiently developed.
It is therefore essential to continue with education, to strengthen professional responsibility, to improve control mechanisms, to insist on the quality of protective equipment and to promote the principle that safety must never be a matter for compromise.
The Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro remains firmly committed to contributing, through professional engagement, partnerships and active participation in public debate, to building a system in which safe and healthy work is the standard and not the exception.

title: Prvomajska sindikalna akademija
excerpt: Na poziv Unije slobodnih sindikata Crne Gore, Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore uzelo je…
content:
Na poziv Unije slobodnih sindikata Crne Gore, Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore uzelo je učešće na Drugoj Prvomajskoj sindikalnoj akademiji, održanoj 30. aprila 2026. godine u zgradi Rektorata Univerziteta Crne Gore, povodom obilježavanja Međunarodnog praznika rada.
Ovaj značajan događaj organizovan je u susret 1. maju, sa ciljem afirmacije značaja radničkih prava, socijalnog dijaloga i kontinuirane sindikalne borbe za unapređenje uslova rada i zaštitu dostojanstva zaposlenih. Akademija je okupila predstavnike socijalnih partnera, relevantnih državnih institucija, sindikalnih organizacija, nevladinog sektora i medija, stvarajući prostor za razmjenu iskustava, promociju dobrih praksi i jačanje međuinstitucionalne saradnje u oblastima od zajedničkog interesa.
Ispred Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore događaju je prisustvovala Đina Janković, potvrđujući na taj način opredijeljenost Udruženja da aktivno doprinosi inicijativama koje promovišu unapređenje prava zaposlenih, a posebno pitanja zaštite i zdravlja na radu kao jednog od temeljnih segmenata savremenog radnog okruženja.
Posebno smo ponosni na činjenicu da je ovogodišnja Prvomajska sindikalna nagrada za najistaknutiju sindikalnu organizaciju dodijeljena Sindikalnoj organizaciji Radio difuznog centra Crne Gore, čiji su članovi ujedno i članovi Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore. Ovo priznanje predstavlja potvrdu dugogodišnjeg odgovornog, predanog i dosljednog rada na unapređenju radnih i sindikalnih prava zaposlenih, ali i snažan pokazatelj koliko su pitanja zaštite i zdravlja na radu postala integralni dio savremenog sindikalnog djelovanja.
Prema obrazloženju komisije, Sindikalna organizacija Radio difuznog centra Crne Gore istakla se kroz konkretne i mjerljive rezultate ostvarene u prethodnom periodu, uključujući unapređenje materijalnog položaja zaposlenih kroz povećanje zarada i izmjene Kolektivnog ugovora, ali i kroz kontinuiran i sistemski rad na unapređenju uslova zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Posebno je značajno što je prepoznata važnost ove oblasti u okviru specifičnog radnog ambijenta Radio difuznog centra, gdje priroda poslova podrazumijeva izloženost različitim profesionalnim rizicima i zahtijeva visok nivo odgovornosti u implementaciji preventivnih mjera.
Kao organizacija koja se zalaže za razvoj kulture prevencije, unapređenje bezbjednosti radnog okruženja i kontinuiranu edukaciju svih aktera u sistemu zaštite na radu, Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore ovu nagradu doživljava i kao dodatni podsticaj za dalje jačanje saradnje sa sindikalnim organizacijama koje prepoznaju značaj integrisanog pristupa zaštiti zaposlenih.
Priznanje koje je uručeno predsjednici Sindikalne organizacije Radio difuznog centra, gospođi Mili Šutulović, predstavlja ne samo potvrdu uspješnog rada ove organizacije, već i snažnu poruku da se dosljedan angažman, stručnost i istrajnost u zaštiti prava zaposlenih prepoznaju i vrednuju.
Učešće Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore na ovom događaju još jednom potvrđuje našu posvećenost aktivnom učešću u procesima koji doprinose unapređenju radnih prava, promociji kulture bezbjednosti i zdravlja na radu, te jačanju partnerstava sa institucijama i organizacijama koje dijele iste vrijednosti i ciljeve.
title_en: May Day trade union academy
excerpt_en: At the invitation of the Union of Free Trade Unions of Montenegro, the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro took…
content_en:
At the invitation of the Union of Free Trade Unions of Montenegro, the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro took part in the Second May Day Trade Union Academy, held on 30 April 2026 in the Rectorate building of the University of Montenegro to mark International Workers' Day.
This significant event was organised in the run-up to 1 May, with the aim of affirming the importance of workers' rights, social dialogue and the continuing trade union struggle to improve working conditions and protect the dignity of employees. The academy brought together representatives of the social partners, of the relevant state institutions, of trade union organisations, of the non-governmental sector and of the media, creating space to exchange experience, promote good practice and strengthen inter-institutional cooperation in areas of common interest.
The Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro was represented at the event by Đina Janković, confirming the Association's commitment to contributing actively to initiatives that promote the advancement of employees' rights, and in particular occupational safety and health as one of the foundations of the modern working environment.
We are especially proud that this year's May Day trade union award for the most outstanding trade union organisation went to the trade union organisation of the Broadcasting Centre of Montenegro, whose members are also members of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro. This recognition confirms many years of responsible, dedicated and consistent work to advance the labour and trade union rights of employees, and is also a strong indication of how far occupational safety and health has become an integral part of modern trade union work.
According to the panel's reasoning, the trade union organisation of the Broadcasting Centre of Montenegro stood out for the concrete, measurable results it achieved over the preceding period, including an improvement in employees' material position through higher pay and amendments to the collective agreement, but also through continuous, systematic work to improve occupational safety and health conditions. It is particularly significant that the importance of this field was recognised within the specific working environment of the Broadcasting Centre, where the nature of the work involves exposure to a range of occupational risks and demands a high level of responsibility in implementing preventive measures.
As an organisation committed to developing a culture of prevention, improving the safety of the working environment and providing continuous education for everyone involved in the occupational safety system, the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro sees this award as a further incentive to strengthen cooperation with those trade union organisations that recognise the importance of an integrated approach to protecting employees.
The award presented to the president of the Broadcasting Centre's trade union organisation, Mila Šutulović, is not only confirmation of that organisation's successful work, but also a strong message that consistent engagement, professionalism and perseverance in protecting employees' rights are recognised and valued.
The Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro's participation in this event confirms once again our commitment to taking an active part in processes that help improve labour rights, promote a culture of safety and health at work, and strengthen partnerships with institutions and organisations that share the same values and goals.

title: Edukativna radionica u JUSMŠ „Ivan Goran Kovačić”, Herceg Novi, u okviru projekta„Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene”
excerpt: Dana 29. aprila 2026. godine, u JUSMŠ „Ivan Goran Kovačić” u Herceg Novom realizovana je…
content:
Dana 29. aprila 2026. godine, u JUSMŠ „Ivan Goran Kovačić“ u Herceg Novom realizovana je četvrta edukativna radionica u okviru projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“, koji je usmjeren na jačanje znanja, svijesti i kapaciteta mladih u oblastima dostojanstvenog rada, radnih prava, zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kao i osnaživanje mladih za sigurniji i informisaniji ulazak na tržište rada.
Radionici je prisustvovalo 36 učenika različitih obrazovnih smjerova, što je omogućilo uključivanje mladih sa različitim obrazovnim profilima, interesovanjima i budućim profesionalnim putevima. Upravo ovakav raznovrstan sastav učesnika dodatno potvrđuje relevantnost ovakvih aktivnosti, budući da pitanja radnih prava, bezbjednosti na radu i dostojanstvenog rada nijesu ograničena na pojedine sektore, već predstavljaju univerzalne teme od značaja za sve mlade koji se pripremaju za ulazak u svijet rada.
Edukativnu radionicu vodili su Đina Janković i Marjan Brčić iz Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, kroz interaktivan i participativan pristup koji je kombinovao stručna predavanja, praktične primjere, otvorenu diskusiju i aktivno uključivanje učesnika.
Značaj edukacije mladih prije ulaska na tržište rada
Polazna osnova ove aktivnosti jeste prepoznavanje činjenice da mladi često ulaze na tržište rada bez dovoljno informacija o svojim pravima, obavezama i osnovnim principima bezbjednog rada. Takav nedostatak znanja čini ih posebno ranjivim na različite oblike nesigurnog rada, neformalnog angažovanja, kršenja radnih prava i izloženosti rizicima po zdravlje i bezbjednost.
U tom kontekstu, radionica je imala za cilj da mladima pruži osnovna, ali praktično primjenjiva znanja koja će im pomoći da sigurnije i odgovornije pristupe svom prvom zaposlenju, stručnoj praksi ili drugim oblicima radnog angažovanja.
Posebno je naglašeno da najveći rizik za mlade pri ulasku na tržište rada često nije samo priroda samog posla, već upravo neznanje – odnosno nedovoljno razumijevanje sopstvenih prava, obaveza i mehanizama zaštite.
Tematski sadržaj radionice
Tokom radionice obrađene su ključne teme koje se odnose na položaj mladih u svijetu rada.
U prvom dijelu radionice učesnici su upoznati sa konceptom dostojanstvenog rada, koji podrazumijeva ne samo mogućnost zaposlenja, već i rad u sigurnim, zakonitim i pravednim uslovima, uz poštovanje osnovnih ljudskih i radnih prava.
Poseban fokus stavljen je na radna prava i obaveze, uključujući:
• značaj ugovora o radu;
• prijavljivanje zaposlenja;
• pravo na zaradu;
• pravo na odmor i ograničeno radno vrijeme;
• zaštitu od diskriminacije i zloupotreba;
• mehanizme zaštite u slučaju povrede prava.
Kroz diskusiju je posebno obrađena tema rada bez ugovora i nesigurnih oblika angažovanja, koja je među mladima prepoznata kao jedan od najčešćih problema pri prvom kontaktu sa tržištem rada. Učesnicima je ukazano na konkretne rizike koje nosi rad „na crno“, uključujući pravnu nesigurnost, odsustvo socijalne zaštite, nemogućnost ostvarivanja prava i povećanu izloženost eksploataciji.
Zaštita i zdravlje na radu – prevencija kao ključ
Drugi značajan segment radionice bio je posvećen zaštiti i zdravlju na radu, sa ciljem da mladi razumiju da bezbjednost na radu nije tema koja se odnosi isključivo na industrijska ili visokorizična zanimanja, već da je relevantna za svaki radni angažman.
Učesnici su upoznati sa:
• osnovnim principima zaštite i zdravlja na radu;
• pravima zaposlenih na bezbjedne uslove rada;
• obavezama poslodavca;
• značajem procjene rizika i preventivnih mjera;
• potrebom osposobljavanja za bezbjedan rad prije početka rada.
Kroz konkretne primjere predstavljeni su različiti rizici kojima mladi mogu biti izloženi na radnim mjestima, kao i načini njihovog prepoznavanja i prevencije.
Posebno je istaknuto da mladi često zbog neiskustva, želje da zadrže posao ili nedostatka informacija prihvataju nesigurne uslove rada, ne postavljajući pitanja i ne prepoznajući situacije koje mogu ugroziti njihovo zdravlje i bezbjednost.
Aktivno učešće i interesovanje učenika
Radionica je realizovana u dinamičnoj i interaktivnoj atmosferi, uz aktivno učešće učenika, koji su pokazali visok nivo zainteresovanosti za teme koje direktno utiču na njihov budući profesionalni život.
Posebno interesovanje izazvale su teme koje se odnose na:
• prvi posao i prava mladih;
• rad bez formalnog angažmana;
• mogućnosti zaštite u slučaju nepravilnosti;
• bezbjednost i odgovornost na radnom mjestu.
Kroz pitanja, komentare i razmjenu mišljenja bilo je evidentno da mladi prepoznaju važnost ovih tema, ali i da postoji realna potreba za dodatnim informisanjem i edukacijom u ovoj oblasti.
Predstavljanje mehanizama podrške
U okviru radionice učenicima je predstavljen i Help-line servis / online Pravni kutak za mlade, kao mehanizam podrške kroz koji mogu dobiti informacije, savjete i podršku u vezi sa radnim pravima i pitanjima zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
Posebno je naglašeno da mladi ne treba da ostanu sami u situacijama kada nijesu sigurni da li su im prava ugrožena ili kada se suoče sa potencijalno opasnim ili nepravednim uslovima rada.
Realizacijom ove radionice nastavljen je kontinuitet projektnih aktivnosti usmjerenih na osnaživanje mladih za sigurniji i dostojanstveniji ulazak na tržište rada.
Radionica u Herceg Novom još jednom je pokazala da mladi imaju interesovanje da uče o svojim pravima i bezbjednosti, ali i da su ovakve edukacije neophodne kako bi se smanjila njihova ranjivost i povećala spremnost da prepoznaju i zaštite svoja prava.
Zaključno, ova aktivnost potvrdila je da ulaganje u znanje mladih predstavlja jednu od najvažnijih preventivnih mjera u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
Jer mladi koji poznaju svoja prava, razumiju rizike i znaju kako da reaguju – postaju sigurniji, odgovorniji i otporniji učesnici tržišta rada.

title_en: Educational workshop at the “Ivan Goran Kovačić” Secondary School, Herceg Novi, under the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”
excerpt_en: On 29 April 2026, at the “Ivan Goran Kovačić” Secondary School in Herceg Novi, the…
content_en:
On 29 April 2026, at the “Ivan Goran Kovačić” Secondary School in Herceg Novi, the fourth educational workshop under the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change” was held. The project aims to strengthen young people's knowledge, awareness and capacity in decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health, and to give them the confidence to enter the labour market more safely and better informed.
The workshop was attended by 36 pupils from a range of educational streams, which made it possible to involve young people with different educational profiles, interests and future career paths. This very diversity among the participants further confirms how relevant such activities are, since labour rights, safety at work and decent work are not confined to particular sectors but are universal topics of importance to every young person preparing to enter the world of work.
The workshop was led by Đina Janković and Marjan Brčić of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, through an interactive, participatory approach combining expert presentations, practical examples, open discussion and the active involvement of the participants.
The importance of educating young people before they enter the labour market
The starting point for this activity is the recognition that young people often enter the labour market without enough information about their rights, their obligations and the basic principles of safe work. That lack of knowledge leaves them particularly vulnerable to various forms of insecure work, informal engagement, violations of labour rights and exposure to risks to their health and safety.
In that context, the workshop aimed to give young people basic but practically applicable knowledge that will help them approach their first job, work placement or other form of engagement more safely and more responsibly.
It was particularly emphasised that the greatest risk for young people entering the labour market is often not the nature of the work itself, but a lack of knowledge — that is, an insufficient understanding of their own rights, obligations and the mechanisms available to protect them.
The topics covered
The workshop covered key topics relating to the position of young people in the world of work.
In the first part, participants were introduced to the concept of decent work, which means not only the opportunity to be employed but also work in safe, lawful and fair conditions, with respect for basic human and labour rights.
Particular focus was placed on labour rights and obligations, including:
• the importance of an employment contract;
• registering employment;
• the right to be paid;
• the right to rest and to limited working hours;
• protection from discrimination and abuse;
• the mechanisms available when rights are violated.
The discussion dealt in particular with work without a contract and with insecure forms of engagement, which young people identify as one of the most common problems in their first contact with the labour market. Participants were shown the concrete risks that undeclared work carries, including legal insecurity, the absence of social protection, the inability to exercise their rights and greater exposure to exploitation.
Occupational safety and health — prevention is the key
The second significant part of the workshop was devoted to occupational safety and health, with the aim of helping young people understand that safety at work is not a subject confined to industrial or high-risk occupations but is relevant to every kind of work.
Participants were introduced to:
• the basic principles of occupational safety and health;
• employees' rights to safe working conditions;
• the employer's obligations;
• the importance of risk assessment and preventive measures;
• the need for training in safe work before starting a job.
Concrete examples were used to present the various risks young people may be exposed to at work, and how to recognise and prevent them.
It was particularly emphasised that young people, through inexperience, a wish to keep their job or a lack of information, often accept unsafe working conditions without asking questions and without recognising situations that may endanger their health and safety.
Active participation and interest among the pupils
The workshop was held in a lively, interactive atmosphere, with the pupils taking an active part and showing a high level of interest in topics that will directly affect their future working lives.
Particular interest was aroused by topics relating to:
• a first job and young people's rights;
• work without formal engagement;
• the scope for protection when something goes wrong;
• safety and responsibility at the workplace.
The questions, comments and exchange of views made it evident that young people recognise the importance of these topics, but also that there is a real need for further information and education in this area.
Presentation of support mechanisms
The workshop also presented the help-line service / online Legal corner for young people, a support mechanism through which they can obtain information, advice and support on labour rights and occupational safety and health.
It was particularly emphasised that young people should not be left on their own when they are unsure whether their rights are being infringed or when they face potentially dangerous or unfair working conditions.
This workshop continued the run of project activities aimed at giving young people the confidence to enter the labour market more safely and with greater dignity.
The workshop in Herceg Novi showed once again that young people are interested in learning about their rights and their safety, but also that education of this kind is essential if their vulnerability is to be reduced and their readiness to recognise and defend their rights increased.
In conclusion, this activity confirmed that investing in young people's knowledge is one of the most important preventive measures in occupational safety and health.
Because young people who know their rights, understand the risks and know how to respond become safer, more responsible and more resilient participants in the labour market.
