title: Obuka iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu za zaposlene u Centru za omladinsku edukaciju (NVO COE)
excerpt: Centar za omladinsku edukaciju (NVO COE) organizovao je za svoje zaposlene obuku o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu u kancelarijskom okruženju, koju su vodili Đina Janković iz UZNR CG i glavni inspektor ZZNR Zlatko Popović.
content:
Organizator: Centar za omladinsku edukaciju (NVO COE)
Realizatori obuke: Đina Janković, Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore i Zlatko Popović, glavni inspektor zaštite i zdravlja na radu, Ministartvo rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga
Tema: Zaštita i zdravlje na radu – prepoznavanje rizika i preventivne mjere u kancelarijskom radnom okruženju
U cilju unapređenja bezbjednog i zdravog radnog okruženja, Centar za omladinsku edukaciju (NVO COE) organizovao je edukativnu obuku iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu za svoje zaposlene, potvrđujući na taj način odgovoran i proaktivan pristup očuvanju zdravlja i bezbjednosti zaposlenih.
Kao organizacija prepoznata po radu sa mladima, promociji obrazovanja, aktivizma i društvene odgovornosti, COE je prepoznao da zaštita i zdravlje na radu ne predstavljaju samo zakonsku obavezu, već i važan segment organizacione kulture, dobrobiti zaposlenih i održivog funkcionisanja svakog radnog kolektiva. COE kroz svoje djelovanje kontinuirano promoviše osnaživanje mladih, građansko učešće i razvoj bezbjednog i podsticajnog okruženja za rad i djelovanje, zbog čega organizovanje ove vrste obuke predstavlja logičan i odgovoran nastavak takvog pristupa.
Obuku su realizovali i vodili Đina Janković iz Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, i Zlatko Popović, glavni inspektor zaštite i zdravlja na radu, iz Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga, čime je učesnicima obezbijeđen spoj stručnog, praktičnog i institucionalnog pristupa temi zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
Iako se kancelarijski rad često neopravdano percipira kao radno okruženje sa minimalnim rizicima, savremena praksa jasno pokazuje da i ovakav tip rada nosi brojne profesionalne opasnosti koje, ukoliko se zanemare, mogu dugoročno uticati na fizičko i mentalno zdravlje zaposlenih.
Tokom obuke zaposleni su upoznati sa osnovnim principima zaštite i zdravlja na radu, pravima i obavezama zaposlenih i poslodavca, kao i značajem preventivnog pristupa upravljanju rizicima.
Poseban fokus stavljen je na specifične rizike kancelarijskog rada, uključujući:
• dugotrajno sjedenje i statičko opterećenje mišićno-koštanog sistema;
• nepravilno ergonomski organizovano radno mjesto;
• opterećenje vida usljed kontinuiranog rada za računarom;
• psihofizički zamor i profesionalni stres;
• povećano mentalno opterećenje usljed intenziteta rada i organizacionih zahtjeva;
• rizike povezane sa električnim instalacijama i kancelarijskom opremom;
• opasnosti od padova, spoticanja i povreda u radnom prostoru;
• neadekvatne mikroklimatske uslove (osvjetljenje, ventilacija, temperatura).
Kroz praktične primjere i interaktivnu diskusiju zaposlenima su predstavljene konkretne preventivne mjere koje doprinose eliminaciji ili smanjenju rizika na najmanju moguću mjeru, uz poseban akcenat na ličnu odgovornost, pravovremeno prijavljivanje uočenih nepravilnosti i važnost kontinuirane edukacije.
Posebno značajan segment obuke odnosio se na ergonomiju radnog mjesta, gdje su zaposleni upoznati sa pravilnim položajem tijela tokom rada, adekvatnim podešavanjem stolice i monitora, organizacijom radnog prostora, značajem redovnih pauza i jednostavnim preventivnim vježbama koje mogu doprinijeti očuvanju zdravlja. Kao pokazatelj odgovornog i proaktivnog pristupa poslodavca, odmah nakon ovog segmenta obuke preduzete su konkretne mjere unapređenja radnog okruženja, uključujući odluku o nabavci monitor riser-a za sve zaposlene, kako bi svaki zaposleni mogao individualno prilagoditi visinu ekrana svojim antropometrijskim karakteristikama i obezbijediti adekvatan položaj monitora u pogledu visine i udaljenosti od očiju, u skladu sa zahtjevima propisanim
Pravilnikom o mjerama zaštite i zdravlja na radu pri radu sa ekranima. Ovakva reakcija predstavlja pozitivan primjer neposredne primjene preporuka iz edukacije i potvrđuje opredijeljenost organizacije da preventivne mjere ne ostanu na nivou teorijskih preporuka, već da budu pretočene u konkretna unapređenja uslova rada.
Imajući u vidu savremene trendove u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, značajan dio edukacije bio je posvećen i psihosocijalnim rizicima, koji danas predstavljaju jedan od najznačajnijih izazova savremenog radnog okruženja. Govorilo se o stresu, preopterećenosti, rokovima, emocionalnom zamoru i organizacionim pritiscima, uz naglašavanje da zaštita i zdravlje na radu podrazumijevaju i očuvanje mentalnog zdravlja zaposlenih.
Učesnici su imali priliku da razgovaraju o konkretnim izazovima iz sopstvenog radnog okruženja, postavljaju pitanja i razmijene iskustva, što je dodatno doprinijelo praktičnoj vrijednosti edukacije.
Posebnu vrijednost ove aktivnosti predstavlja činjenica da je organizovana kao izraz preventivnog i odgovornog pristupa upravljanju ljudskim resursima. U vremenu kada pitanja bezbjednosti na radu sve češće dolaze u fokus javnosti, posebno nakon događaja koji ukazuju na posljedice neadekvatnog upravljanja rizicima u radnom okruženju, ovakve inicijative potvrđuju značaj pravovremene edukacije, prevencije i razvoja kulture bezbjednosti, bez čekanja da se problemi pojave kao posljedica propusta.
Sprovedena obuka predstavljala je važan korak ka dodatnom jačanju svijesti zaposlenih o značaju zaštite i zdravlja na radu, unapređenju njihovih znanja i usvajanju preventivnih praksi koje doprinose sigurnijem i zdravijem radnom okruženju.
Ovakav pristup potvrđuje da odgovorne organizacije zaštitu i zdravlje na radu ne posmatraju kao formalnu obavezu, već kao sastavni dio profesionalnog standarda, organizacione odgovornosti i brige o ljudima.
Zaključno, posebno je važno istaći da inicijativa Centra za omladinsku edukaciju predstavlja pozitivan i društveno odgovoran primjer dobre prakse, naročito za male poslodavce i organizacije civilnog društva, u kojima se pitanja zaštite i zdravlja na radu često neopravdano zanemaruju zbog percepcije da se radi o manje rizičnim radnim okruženjima ili usljed ograničenih organizacionih i finansijskih kapaciteta. Ovakvi primjeri jasno pokazuju da unapređenje bezbjednosti i zdravlja na radu ne mora nužno podrazumijevati složene i skupe intervencije, već prije svega razvijenu svijest, odgovoran pristup i spremnost da se preventivno djeluje u interesu zaposlenih. Nadamo se da će ovakva praksa poslužiti kao podsticaj i drugim organizacijama, posebno u nevladinom sektoru i među manjim poslodavcima, da prepoznaju značaj sistemskog pristupa zaštiti i zdravlju na radu i preduzmu slične aktivnosti u cilju očuvanja zdravlja, dobrobiti i radne sposobnosti svojih zaposlenih.
title_en: Occupational safety and health training for the staff of the Centre for Youth Education (NGO COE)
excerpt_en: The Centre for Youth Education (NGO COE) organised training for its staff on occupational safety and health in an office environment, led by Đina Janković of UZNR CG and the chief OSH inspector, Zlatko Popović.
content_en:
Organiser: Centre for Youth Education (NGO COE)
Trainers: Đina Janković, Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, and Zlatko Popović, chief occupational safety and health inspector, Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue
Topic: Occupational safety and health – recognising risks and preventive measures in an office working environment
With the aim of improving its safe and healthy working environment, the Centre for Youth Education (NGO COE) organised occupational safety and health training for its staff, confirming a responsible and proactive approach to preserving employees' health and safety.
As an organisation known for its work with young people and for promoting education, activism and social responsibility, COE recognised that occupational safety and health is not merely a legal obligation but also an important part of organisational culture, of employees' wellbeing and of the sustainable functioning of any workplace. Through its work COE continuously promotes the empowerment of young people, civic participation and the development of a safe and supportive environment for work and activity, which makes organising training of this kind a logical and responsible continuation of that approach.
The training was delivered by Đina Janković of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro and Zlatko Popović, chief occupational safety and health inspector at the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, giving participants a combination of professional, practical and institutional perspectives on the subject.
Although office work is often unjustifiably perceived as a working environment with minimal risk, modern practice clearly shows that this type of work too carries a range of occupational hazards which, if neglected, can affect employees' physical and mental health in the long term.
During the training the staff were introduced to the basic principles of occupational safety and health, to the rights and obligations of employees and employers, and to the importance of a preventive approach to managing risk.
Particular focus was placed on the specific risks of office work, including:
• prolonged sitting and static load on the musculoskeletal system;
• a workstation that is not ergonomically organised;
• eye strain from continuous work at a computer;
• physical and mental fatigue and work-related stress;
• increased mental load arising from the intensity of the work and organisational demands;
• risks associated with electrical installations and office equipment;
• the danger of falls, trips and injuries in the workspace;
• inadequate indoor climate conditions (lighting, ventilation, temperature).
Through practical examples and interactive discussion the staff were shown concrete preventive measures that help eliminate risks or reduce them to the lowest possible level, with particular emphasis on personal responsibility, reporting anything noticed in good time and the importance of continuous education.
A particularly significant part of the training concerned workstation ergonomics, where the staff learned about correct body posture during work, the proper adjustment of chair and monitor, the organisation of the workspace, the importance of regular breaks and simple preventive exercises that can help preserve health. As an indication of the employer's responsible and proactive approach, concrete measures to improve the working environment were taken immediately after this part of the training, including a decision to purchase monitor risers for all staff, so that each employee can individually adjust the height of the screen to their own body measurements and ensure the monitor is at an appropriate height and distance from the eyes, in line with the requirements laid down by the Rulebook on occupational safety and health measures for work with display screens. This response is a positive example of recommendations from training being applied immediately, and confirms the organisation's commitment to ensuring that preventive measures do not remain theoretical recommendations but are translated into concrete improvements in working conditions.
Bearing in mind current trends in occupational safety and health, a significant part of the training was also devoted to psychosocial risks, which are today among the most significant challenges of the modern working environment. Stress, overload, deadlines, emotional fatigue and organisational pressures were discussed, with the emphasis that occupational safety and health also means preserving employees' mental health.
Participants had the opportunity to talk about concrete challenges in their own working environment, to ask questions and to exchange experience, which added further practical value to the training.
The particular value of this activity lies in the fact that it was organised as an expression of a preventive and responsible approach to managing people. At a time when questions of safety at work are increasingly in the public eye, particularly after events that point to the consequences of inadequate risk management in the workplace, initiatives of this kind confirm the importance of timely education, prevention and the development of a safety culture, without waiting for problems to appear as the result of a failure.
The training was an important step towards further strengthening staff awareness of the importance of occupational safety and health, improving their knowledge and adopting preventive practices that contribute to a safer and healthier working environment.
This approach confirms that responsible organisations do not see occupational safety and health as a formality, but as an integral part of professional standards, organisational responsibility and care for people.
In conclusion, it is particularly important to point out that the Centre for Youth Education's initiative is a positive and socially responsible example of good practice, especially for small employers and civil society organisations, where occupational safety and health is often unjustifiably neglected because of a perception that these are lower-risk working environments or because of limited organisational and financial capacity. Examples like this clearly show that improving safety and health at work need not involve complex and expensive interventions, but above all developed awareness, a responsible approach and a readiness to act preventively in employees' interests. We hope this practice will serve as an encouragement to other organisations, particularly in the non-governmental sector and among smaller employers, to recognise the importance of a systematic approach to occupational safety and health and to undertake similar activities in order to preserve their employees' health, wellbeing and capacity to work.

title: Edukativna radionica u JU Srednja ekonomsko – ugostiteljska škola, Nikšić, u okviru projekta „ Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene
excerpt: Radionica u JU Srednja ekonomsko-ugostiteljska škola u Nikšiću, održana upravo na Svjetski dan zaštite i zdravlja na radu, okupila je 35 učenika i 5 nastavnika u okviru projekta "Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad".
content:
Dana 28. aprila 2026. godine, u JU Srednja ekonomsko-ugostiteljska škola u Nikšiću realizovana je edukativna radionica u okviru projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“, koji ima za cilj unapređenje znanja i svijesti mladih o radnim pravima, dostojanstvenom radu i zaštiti i zdravlju na radu.
Radionica je okupila 35 učenika različitih obrazovnih smjerova, kao i 5 nastavnika, čime je obezbijeđen širi obrazovni i pedagoški kontekst za razmjenu znanja i iskustava. Uključivanje nastavnog kadra dodatno doprinosi održivosti ovakvih aktivnosti, jer omogućava prenos stečenih znanja i nakon završetka projekta kroz redovni obrazovni proces.
Edukaciju su realizovale Đina Janković i Anđa Strugar iz Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, kroz pristup koji je kombinovao informativni, edukativni i participativni segment, sa ciljem da se učenici ne zadrže samo na teorijskom nivou, već da razviju sposobnost kritičkog promišljanja i prepoznavanja realnih problema na tržištu rada.
Kontekst i značaj radionice
Savremeno tržište rada karakterišu brojni izazovi, posebno za mlade koji tek ulaze u svijet rada. Nedovoljna informisanost, nesigurni oblici zaposlenja i prisustvo neformalnog rada doprinose njihovoj povećanoj ranjivosti. U tom kontekstu, ovakve radionice predstavljaju važan mehanizam prevencije, jer mladima pružaju znanja koja mogu imati direktan uticaj na njihovu bezbjednost i položaj u radnom okruženju.
Poseban značaj radionice ogleda se u činjenici da je realizovana upravo na dan obilježavanja Svjetskog dana zaštite i zdravlja na radu, čime je dodatno naglašena važnost teme i potreba za kontinuiranim podizanjem svijesti u ovoj oblasti.
Edukativni sadržaj i tematski okvir
Tokom radionice obrađene su ključne teme iz oblasti dostojanstvenog rada, radnih prava i zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
U prvom dijelu fokus je bio na razumijevanju koncepta dostojanstvenog rada, koji podrazumijeva ne samo mogućnost zaposlenja, već i rad u uslovima koji su zakoniti, sigurni i pravedni. Učenici su upoznati sa osnovnim pravima iz radnog odnosa, uključujući pravo na ugovor o radu, zaradu, odmor, ograničeno radno vrijeme i zaštitu od diskriminacije i zloupotreba.
Posebna pažnja posvećena je identifikaciji najčešćih oblika kršenja prava mladih, sa akcentom na rad bez ugovora i nesigurne oblike angažovanja. Kroz diskusiju, učenici su imali priliku da sagledaju konkretne posljedice ovakvih situacija, uključujući nedostatak pravne zaštite i izloženost različitim rizicima.
Drugi segment radionice bio je posvećen zaštiti i zdravlju na radu, gdje su predstavljeni osnovni principi bezbjednog rada, obaveze poslodavca i prava zaposlenih. Učenici su upoznati sa značajem procjene rizika, korišćenjem zaštitne opreme i važnosti osposobljavanja prije početka rada.
Interaktivni pristup i angažman učesnika
Radionica je realizovana kroz interaktivan pristup, koji je uključivao otvorenu diskusiju, razmjenu iskustava i analizu konkretnih situacija iz prakse. Učenici su aktivno učestvovali, postavljali pitanja i iznosili sopstvena zapažanja o uslovima rada mladih, što je ukazalo na njihovu zainteresovanost, ali i na potrebu za dodatnim informisanjem.
Posebno je bilo značajno što su učesnici dolazili iz različitih obrazovnih smjerova, što je omogućilo raznovrsnost perspektiva i bolje razumijevanje različitih radnih konteksta. Učešće nastavnika dodatno je doprinijelo kvalitetu diskusije i otvorilo prostor za nastavak rada na ovim temama u okviru školskog sistema.
Mehanizmi podrške i praktična primjena znanja
U okviru radionice predstavljen je i Help-line servis / online Pravni kutak za mlade, kao alat koji mladima omogućava da se informišu, postave pitanja i dobiju stručne savjete u vezi sa radnim pravima i zaštitom na radu.
Ovaj segment bio je od posebnog značaja jer je učenicima pružio konkretan odgovor na pitanje kome se obratiti u situacijama kada nijesu sigurni u svoja prava ili se suočavaju sa nepravilnostima.
Radionica u JU Srednja ekonomsko-ugostiteljska škola u Nikšiću uspješno je realizovana i doprinijela je unapređenju znanja i svijesti mladih o ključnim pitanjima vezanim za rad i bezbjednost na radu.
Kroz kombinaciju edukacije i interaktivnog rada, učenici su stekli osnovne kompetencije koje su od suštinskog značaja za njihov budući profesionalni angažman. Posebno je važno što su imali priliku da povežu teorijska znanja sa realnim situacijama, čime se dodatno jača njihova sposobnost da prepoznaju i adekvatno reaguju na rizike.
Ova aktivnost potvrđuje značaj kontinuiranog rada sa mladima i potrebu da se teme radnih prava i zaštite na radu sistemski integrišu u obrazovni proces, kao ključni korak ka izgradnji sigurnijeg i pravednijeg tržišta rada u Crnoj Gori. 📌 Projekat finansira Evropska unija, a kofinansira Ministarstvo regionalno-investicionog razvoja i saradnje sa nevladinim organizacijama, u okviru mreže YHWBT.
title_en: Educational workshop at the Secondary School of Economics and Hospitality, Nikšić, under the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”
excerpt_en: The workshop at the Secondary School of Economics and Hospitality in Nikšić, held on World Day for Safety and Health at Work itself, brought together 35 pupils and 5 teachers under the project “Youth voices for decent work”.
content_en:
On 28 April 2026, at the Secondary School of Economics and Hospitality in Nikšić, an educational workshop was held under the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”, which aims to improve young people's knowledge and awareness of labour rights, decent work and occupational safety and health.
The workshop brought together 35 pupils from a range of educational streams, as well as 5 teachers, providing a broader educational and pedagogical context for the exchange of knowledge and experience. Involving teaching staff further contributes to the sustainability of such activities, because it allows the knowledge gained to be passed on through the regular educational process after the project ends.
The training was delivered by Đina Janković and Anđa Strugar of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, through an approach combining information, education and participation, with the aim that pupils should not stop at the theory but develop the ability to think critically and recognise real problems on the labour market.
Context and importance of the workshop
The modern labour market is marked by numerous challenges, particularly for young people just entering the world of work. Insufficient information, insecure forms of employment and the presence of informal work all add to their vulnerability. In that context, workshops of this kind are an important preventive mechanism, because they give young people knowledge that can have a direct effect on their safety and their position in the working environment.
The particular significance of this workshop lies in the fact that it was held on the day marking World Day for Safety and Health at Work, which further underlined the importance of the subject and the need to keep raising awareness in this field.
Content and thematic framework
The workshop covered key topics in decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health.
The first part focused on understanding the concept of decent work, which means not only the opportunity to be employed but also work in conditions that are lawful, safe and fair. Pupils learned about the basic rights arising from an employment relationship, including the right to an employment contract, to pay, to rest, to limited working hours and to protection from discrimination and abuse.
Particular attention was paid to identifying the most common ways in which young people's rights are violated, with an emphasis on work without a contract and insecure forms of engagement. Through discussion, pupils had the opportunity to consider the concrete consequences of such situations, including the absence of legal protection and exposure to various risks.
The second part of the workshop was devoted to occupational safety and health, presenting the basic principles of safe work, the employer's obligations and employees' rights. Pupils learned about the importance of risk assessment, the use of protective equipment and the importance of training before starting work.
An interactive approach and the participants' engagement
The workshop used an interactive approach involving open discussion, the exchange of experience and the analysis of concrete situations from practice. Pupils took an active part, asked questions and offered their own observations about young people's working conditions, which showed both their interest and their need for further information.
It was particularly significant that the participants came from different educational streams, which brought a diversity of perspectives and a better understanding of different working contexts. The teachers' participation added further quality to the discussion and opened up space for continued work on these topics within the school system.
Support mechanisms and the practical application of knowledge
The workshop also presented the help-line service / online Legal corner for young people, a tool that allows young people to find information, ask questions and obtain expert advice on labour rights and safety at work.
This part was particularly significant because it gave pupils a concrete answer to the question of whom to turn to when they are unsure of their rights or face irregularities.
The workshop at the Secondary School of Economics and Hospitality in Nikšić was successfully held and helped improve young people's knowledge and awareness of key questions relating to work and safety at work.
Through a combination of instruction and interactive work, the pupils gained basic competences that are essential for their future working lives. It is particularly important that they had the opportunity to connect theoretical knowledge with real situations, which further strengthens their ability to recognise risks and respond to them appropriately.
This activity confirms the importance of working continuously with young people and the need to integrate labour rights and safety at work systematically into the educational process, as a key step towards building a safer and fairer labour market in Montenegro. 📌 The project is financed by the European Union and co-financed by the Ministry of Regional Investment Development and Cooperation with Non-Governmental Organisations, within the YHWBT network.

title: Edukativna radionica u JU Ekonomsko-ugostiteljska škola, Baru u okviru projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad - od znanja do promjene“
excerpt: U JU Ekonomsko-ugostiteljskoj školi u Baru održana je 27. aprila 2026. radionica za 40 učenika o dostojanstvenom radu, radnim pravima i zaštiti na radu, u okviru istog projekta.
content:
Dana 27. aprila 2026. godine, u JU Ekonomsko-ugostiteljskoj školi u Baru realizovana je edukativna radionica u okviru aktivnosti usmjerenih na jačanje znanja mladih o dostojanstvenom radu, radnim pravima i zaštiti i zdravlju na radu, koje se sprovode kroz projekat „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“.
Radionici je prisustvovalo 40 učenika, koji se nalaze u fazi pripreme za ulazak na tržište rada, što ovu ciljnu grupu čini posebno značajnom za realizaciju ovakvih edukativnih aktivnosti. Uzimajući u obzir obrazovni profil učenika, sadržaj radionice bio je prilagođen njihovim potrebama, sa posebnim fokusom na praktične aspekte radnih odnosa i realne situacije sa kojima se mladi mogu susresti prilikom prvog zaposlenja, stručne prakse ili sezonskog rada.
Radionicu je vodila Đina Janković iz Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, kroz interaktivan i participativan pristup, koji je podrazumijevao kombinaciju prezentacije, diskusije i analize konkretnih primjera iz prakse.
U uvodnom dijelu radionice učenicima je predstavljen projekat, njegovi ciljevi i značaj aktivnosti koje se realizuju u srednjim stručnim školama. Posebno je naglašeno da mladi često ulaze na tržište rada bez dovoljno informacija o svojim pravima i obavezama, što ih čini ranjivim na različite oblike nesigurnog i neformalnog rada. U tom kontekstu, radionica je imala za cilj da učenicima pruži osnovna znanja i vještine koje će im omogućiti sigurniji i informisaniji pristup radu.
Tokom edukativnog dijela obrađen je koncept dostojanstvenog rada, sa naglaskom na to da dostojanstven rad podrazumijeva ne samo zaposlenje, već i zakonite, bezbjedne i pravedne uslove rada. Učenici su upoznati sa osnovnim pravima i obavezama iz radnog odnosa, uključujući značaj ugovora o radu, prijavljivanja zaposlenja, prava na zaradu, radno vrijeme, odmor i zaštitu od zloupotreba.
Poseban akcenat stavljen je na problem rada na crno, koji je prepoznat kao jedan od najčešćih izazova sa kojima se mladi suočavaju pri ulasku na tržište rada. Kroz diskusiju i primjere iz prakse, učenici su imali priliku da razumiju rizike ovakvog angažovanja, uključujući nedostatak pravne zaštite, nesigurnost prihoda i izloženost različitim oblicima eksploatacije.
Drugi važan segment radionice odnosio se na zaštitu i zdravlje na radu. Učenicima su predstavljeni osnovni principi bezbjednog rada, obaveze poslodavca i prava zaposlenih, kao i značaj preventivne kulture u radnom okruženju. Kroz konkretne situacije objašnjeno je kako prepoznati potencijalne rizike na radnom mjestu i na koji način reagovati u slučaju nepravilnosti ili povrede prava.
Radionica je realizovana kroz aktivno učešće učenika, koji su pokazali visok nivo interesovanja, posebno za teme koje se odnose na prvi posao, rad bez ugovora, praksu i načine zaštite svojih prava. Njihova pitanja i komentari ukazali su na potrebu za dodatnim informisanjem i sistemskim uključivanjem ovih tema u obrazovni proces.
U okviru radionice učenicima je predstavljen i Help-line servis / online Pravni kutak za mlade, kao važan mehanizam podrške koji omogućava mladima da se informišu, postave pitanja i dobiju savjet u vezi sa radnim pravima i zaštitom na radu. Naglašeno je da je cilj ovog servisa da mladima pruži sigurnu i dostupnu podršku u situacijama kada nijesu sigurni kako da reaguju.
Realizacija ove radionice u Baru predstavlja važan segment širenja projektnih aktivnosti na različite regione, čime se doprinosi ravnomjernijem obuhvatu mladih i jačanju njihovih kapaciteta za bezbjedan i dostojanstven rad.
Zaključno, radionica je uspješno realizovana i ostvarila je postavljene ciljeve. Učenici su unaprijedili svoja znanja o radnim pravima, zaštiti i zdravlju na radu, kao i o značaju informisanosti i prevencije. Posebno je značajno što su kroz interaktivan pristup imali priliku da povežu teorijska znanja sa realnim životnim situacijama, čime se dodatno doprinosi njihovoj spremnosti za ulazak na tržište rada.
Ova aktivnost još jednom potvrđuje značaj kontinuiranog rada sa mladima u oblasti radnih prava i bezbjednosti na radu, kao i potrebu da se kroz edukaciju i informisanje doprinese izgradnji sigurnijeg i pravednijeg radnog okruženja za buduće generacije.
📌 Projekat finansira Evropska unija, a kofinansira Ministarstvo regionalno-investicionog razvoja i saradnje sa nevladinim organizacijama, u okviru mreže YHWBT.

title_en: Educational workshop at the School of Economics and Hospitality, Bar, under the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”
excerpt_en: On 27 April 2026 the School of Economics and Hospitality in Bar hosted a workshop for 40 pupils on decent work, labour rights and safety at work, under the same project.
content_en:
On 27 April 2026, at the School of Economics and Hospitality in Bar, an educational workshop was held as part of the activities aimed at strengthening young people's knowledge of decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health, carried out through the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”.
The workshop was attended by 40 pupils who are preparing to enter the labour market, which makes this target group particularly important for educational activities of this kind. Taking the pupils' educational profile into account, the content of the workshop was adapted to their needs, with particular focus on the practical aspects of employment relationships and the real situations young people may encounter in their first job, on a work placement or in seasonal work.
The workshop was led by Đina Janković of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, through an interactive, participatory approach combining presentation, discussion and the analysis of concrete examples from practice.
The opening part of the workshop introduced the pupils to the project, its aims and the importance of the activities carried out in secondary vocational schools. It was particularly emphasised that young people often enter the labour market without enough information about their rights and obligations, which leaves them vulnerable to various forms of insecure and informal work. In that context, the workshop aimed to give pupils basic knowledge and skills that will allow them to approach work more safely and better informed.
The educational part dealt with the concept of decent work, stressing that decent work means not only employment but also lawful, safe and fair working conditions. Pupils learned about the basic rights and obligations arising from an employment relationship, including the importance of an employment contract, of registering employment, and of rights to pay, working hours, rest and protection from abuse.
Particular emphasis was placed on the problem of undeclared work, identified as one of the most common challenges young people face when entering the labour market. Through discussion and examples from practice, pupils had the opportunity to understand the risks of such engagement, including the absence of legal protection, insecure income and exposure to various forms of exploitation.
The second important part of the workshop concerned occupational safety and health. Pupils were introduced to the basic principles of safe work, the employer's obligations and employees' rights, and to the importance of a preventive culture in the working environment. Concrete situations were used to explain how to recognise potential risks at the workplace and how to respond when something is wrong or rights are violated.
The workshop was held with the pupils taking an active part; they showed a high level of interest, particularly in topics relating to a first job, work without a contract, work placements and ways of protecting their rights. Their questions and comments pointed to a need for further information and for these topics to be systematically included in the educational process.
The workshop also presented the help-line service / online Legal corner for young people, an important support mechanism that allows young people to find information, ask questions and get advice on labour rights and safety at work. It was emphasised that the aim of this service is to give young people safe, accessible support when they are unsure how to respond.
Holding this workshop in Bar is an important part of extending the project's activities to different regions, helping to reach young people more evenly and to strengthen their capacity for safe and decent work.
In conclusion, the workshop was successfully held and achieved the objectives set. The pupils improved their knowledge of labour rights, occupational safety and health, and of the importance of being informed and of prevention. It is particularly significant that the interactive approach allowed them to connect theoretical knowledge with real-life situations, which further prepares them for entering the labour market.
This activity confirms once again the importance of working continuously with young people on labour rights and safety at work, and the need to help build a safer and fairer working environment for future generations through education and information.
📌 The project is financed by the European Union and co-financed by the Ministry of Regional Investment Development and Cooperation with Non-Governmental Organisations, within the YHWBT network.

title_en: Educational workshop at the “Mirko Vešović” Secondary School of Economics. Project: “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”
excerpt_en: The first workshop under activity A3.1 of the project was held on 23 April 2026 at the “Mirko Vešović” Secondary School of Economics in Podgorica, for 45 pupils on the law and economics stream.
content_en:
On 23 April 2026, at the “Mirko Vešović” Secondary School of Economics in Podgorica, the first educational workshop was held under activity A3.1 – Lectures in schools and faculties, carried out through the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”. The project aims to strengthen young people's knowledge and awareness of decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health, particularly among pupils and students preparing to enter the labour market.
The workshop was attended by 45 pupils from the law and economics stream, a particularly significant target group given that these are young people who acquire a basic grounding in law, economics, business and administration through their educational programme, but for whom additional practical education about labour rights and occupational safety and health is extremely important for their future professional development.
The workshop was led by Sanja Dujović and Đina Janković of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro. The content was adapted to the pupils' profile, with particular reference to practical situations young people may encounter in their first job, on a work placement, in seasonal work or in other forms of engagement.
The opening part introduced the pupils to the project, its aims and the importance of the activities carried out in secondary vocational schools. It was particularly emphasised that young people often enter the labour market without enough information about their rights, their obligations and the mechanisms available to protect them, which leaves them vulnerable to informal and insecure forms of work. In that context, the workshop aimed to familiarise pupils with the basic concepts and situations in decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health.
The educational part dealt with the concept of decent work, stressing that decent work means not only employment but also safe, lawful and fair working conditions. Pupils learned about the basic rights and obligations arising from an employment relationship, the importance of an employment contract and of registering employees, and rights to pay, rest, working hours and protection from abuse. Particular emphasis was placed on the problem of undeclared work, identified as one of the most common risks for young people entering the labour market.
The second important part of the workshop concerned occupational safety and health. Pupils were introduced to the basic principles of safe work, the employer's obligations, employees' rights and the importance of a preventive culture. Concrete examples were used to explain why every young worker needs to be informed about the risks of their workplace, trained to work safely and familiar with the procedures to follow in the event of an injury at work or of any irregularity.
The workshop was interactive, based on conversation, questions, examples from practice and discussion. The pupils showed a high level of interest, particularly in topics relating to a first job, work placements, work without a contract, young people's rights while working and how to respond when rights are violated. Their questions showed that there is a significant need for education of this kind, especially because for many young people a workshop like this is the first time they encounter concrete information about whom they can turn to and how they can protect their rights.
Particular attention was also paid to presenting the help-line service / online Legal corner for young people, a safe and discreet channel of support that allows young people to ask a question, get advice and find out about their rights and the options available to them. It was explained to the pupils that the aim of this service is to support them when they are unsure whether their rights are being infringed or whom they should turn to.
Holding the workshop at the “Mirko Vešović” Secondary School of Economics is an important step in implementing the project, because it directly serves one of the key project objectives — increasing young people's knowledge of labour rights and occupational safety and health through educational activities in schools. The project provides for lectures of this kind in secondary vocational schools, using an interactive approach, real-life examples, discussion and short simulations of situations from the labour market.
The participation of 45 pupils confirms the relevance of these topics and the need to introduce them systematically into education. The workshop showed that pupils are interested in, and also need, further knowledge that will help them approach the labour market more safely and better informed. It is particularly significant that these topics were covered with pupils on the law and economics stream, who will encounter questions of work, business, administration and legal relations professionally in the future.
In conclusion, the first workshop under activity A3.1 was successfully held and achieved the objectives planned. The pupils improved their knowledge of decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health, recognised the importance of being informed and of prevention, and learned that support mechanisms are available through the help-line and the Legal corner. At the same time, the workshop helped strengthen young people's awareness that knowledge is one of the key preconditions for a safe, lawful and dignified entry into the labour market.

title: Edukativno – zagovaračka radionica Projekat : “ Glas Mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene
excerpt: U prostoru UpBeat Hub-a u Podgorici održana je 22. aprila 2026. jednodnevna edukativno-zagovaračka radionica za 20 mladih uzrasta 15-29 godina, tokom koje su izabrani mladi ambasadori dostojanstvenog rada.
content:
Dana 22. aprila 2026. godine u prostoru UpBeat Hub-a u Podgorici uspješno je realizovana edukativno-zagovaračka radionica u okviru projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“, usmjerena na jačanje znanja, vještina i participacije mladih u oblastima dostojanstvenog rada, radnih prava, zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kao i javnog zagovaranja. Radionica je realizovana u skladu sa planiranom agendom i metodologijom predviđenom projektnom dokumentacijom.
Radionici je prisustvovalo 20 mladih uzrasta od 15 do 29 godina, uključujući učesnike različitih obrazovnih i socijalnih profila, među kojima i mlade iz grupa kojima je projekat posebno usmjeren. Od samog početka radionice zabilježen je visok nivo motivacije, otvorenosti i aktivnog učešća, a atmosfera tokom cjelodnevnog rada bila je izuzetno dinamična, konstruktivna i podsticajna.
I dio – Dostojanstven rad, radna prava i zaštita i zdravlje na radu
U prvom dijelu radionice učesnici su imali priliku da steknu i prodube znanja o konceptu dostojanstvenog rada, osnovnim pravima i obavezama iz radnog odnosa, kao i o najčešćim oblicima kršenja prava mladih na tržištu rada. Poseban fokus stavljen je na značaj preventivne kulture i zaštite i zdravlja na radu, uključujući prepoznavanje rizika i nepravilnosti sa kojima se mladi mogu susresti prilikom prvog zaposlenja.
Kroz prezentacije, diskusiju i rad na praktičnim primjerima, učesnici su pokazali veliko interesovanje za teme koje se tiču rada „na crno“, nepoznavanja prava, nesigurnih uslova rada i nedostatka informacija o mehanizmima zaštite. Posebno je zapaženo da su mladi aktivno povezivali predstavljene sadržaje sa sopstvenim iskustvima, iskustvima vršnjaka i primjerima iz lokalnog konteksta.
Tokom interaktivne vježbe „Prepoznaj problem – reaguj“, učesnici su u grupama analizirali realne situacije povreda prava i predlagali moguća rješenja. Ovaj segment pokazao je visok nivo razumijevanja problema, ali i sposobnost mladih da identifikuju praktične odgovore na izazove sa tržišta rada.
II dio – Javno zagovaranje i aktivno učešće mladih
Drugi dio radionice bio je posvećen javnom zagovaranju kao alatu za društvenu promjenu i aktivno uključivanje mladih u procese donošenja odluka.
Kroz brainstorming, diskusiju i grupni rad, učesnici su radili na identifikaciji problema koje smatraju prioritetnim za položaj mladih na tržištu rada, definisanju ciljeva promjene, mapiranju relevantnih aktera i formulisanju zagovaračkih poruka, a kroz ovaj dio obuke ih je vodila ekspertkinja za ovu oblast, s preko dvije decenije iskustva, Lidija Brnović.
U ovom dijelu radionice učesnici su pokazali izuzetno visok nivo angažmana i kreativnosti, dajući brojne konkretne predloge za unapređenje položaja mladih. Nakon zajedničke diskusije i prioritizacije, učesnici su se usaglasili oko tri ključne preporuke, za koje su razvili početni plan javnog zagovaranja:
1. Suzbijanje rada na crno i jačanje zaštite mladih u neformalnom radu
Učesnici su prepoznali rad na crno kao jedan od najizraženijih problema sa kojima se mladi suočavaju pri ulasku na tržište rada, posebno kroz sezonske, povremene i slabo regulisane poslove. Istaknuto je da rad bez ugovora mlade ostavlja bez osnovnih prava, socijalne sigurnosti i zaštite.
Kao zagovarački cilj definisana je potreba za jačanjem informisanosti mladih o rizicima rada na crno, unapređenjem preventivnih mjera i snažnijim institucionalnim odgovorom u suzbijanju ove pojave.
2. Inicijativa za prepoznavanje menstrualnog odsustva kao pitanja dostojanstvenog rada
Kao posebno značajna i inovativna tema, učesnici su identifikovali potrebu otvaranja javnog dijaloga o menstrualnom odsustvu kao pitanju radnih prava, zdravlja i dostojanstvenog rada.
Učesnici su ukazali na činjenicu da se ova tema rijetko prepoznaje u javnim politikama, iako direktno utiče na položaj mladih žena na tržištu rada. Kao preporuka definisano je pokretanje zagovaračke inicijative usmjerene ka većoj institucionalnoj i društvenoj prepoznatljivosti ovog pitanja.
3. Unapređenje položaja mladih na stručnom usavršavanju
Treća preporuka odnosila se na neregulisan položaj mladih angažovanih kroz programe stručnog osposobljavanja i usavršavanja, koji su često bez prava iz radnog odnosa, bez radnog staža, bez adekvatne obuke za bezbjedan rad i bez plaćenog osiguranja u slučaju povrede na radu ili profesionalne bolesti.
Učesnici su prepoznali potrebu da se status ovih mladih jasnije reguliše, uz zagovaranje uvođenja minimalnih standarda zaštite, uključujući obaveznu obuku za bezbjedan rad, osiguranje od povreda na radu i veći nivo pravne sigurnosti.
Za svaku od tri preporuke učesnici su razvili osnovne elemente zagovaračkog plana, uključujući:
• cilj promjene
• ključne poruke
• donosioce odluka kojima se obraćaju
• potencijalne saveznike
• prve korake mikro-zagovaračkih akcija.
Ovaj proces pokazao je da mladi ne samo da prepoznaju probleme, već su sposobni da formulišu konkretne i relevantne preporuke sa potencijalom za dalje zagovaranje i javnu promociju.
III dio – Mikro-zagovaračke akcije i izbor ambasadora
U trećem dijelu radionice učesnici su radili na transformaciji zagovaračkih poruka u mikro-kampanjske akcije. Posebnu vrijednost imao je praktični segment snimanja kratkih zagovaračkih video poruka, u kojem su mladi demonstrirali sposobnost jasnog i uvjerljivog komuniciranja problema i poziva na akciju.
Ovaj dio radionice dodatno je potvrdio visok nivo motivacije učesnika i njihovu spremnost za javni angažman.
Na osnovu angažmana tokom cijelog dana, kvaliteta ideja, komunikacijskih vještina i iskazane motivacije, facilitatori su, umjesto prvobitno planiranih pet, donijeli odluku da budu izabrani 6 mladih ambasadora dostojanstvenog rada, imajući u vidu izuzetno kvalitetan doprinos učesnika i potrebu da se podrži šira grupa mladih spremnih za dalji angažman. Odluka o izboru dodatnog ambasadora donesena je zbog izraženog kvaliteta kandidata i ravnopravnosti doprinosa.
Izabrani ambasadori biće uključeni u naredne aktivnosti projekta, posebno u kampanjske aktivnosti, promociju zagovaračkih poruka i javne događaje.
Opšti utisci i evaluacija
Završni evaluacioni dio pokazao je veoma pozitivne reakcije učesnika, koji su radionicu ocijenili kao korisnu, relevantnu i podsticajnu. Posebno su istakli praktičan karakter rada, mogućnost da slobodno iznesu stavove i činjenicu da su po prvi put imali priliku da o pitanjima rada mladih razgovaraju iz perspektive sopstvenih iskustava i mogućnosti uticaja.
Radionica je pokazala da mladi ne samo da prepoznaju probleme, već imaju konkretne ideje i spremnost da učestvuju u njihovom rješavanju kada im se obezbijedi adekvatan prostor, podrška i metodologija rada.
Edukativno-zagovaračka radionica uspješno je ostvarila planirane ciljeve, doprinoseći povećanju znanja mladih o dostojanstvenom radu, jačanju njihovih zagovaračkih kapaciteta i identifikaciji mladih ambasadora koji će nastaviti angažman u okviru projekta.
Posebna vrijednost radionice ogleda se u visokom nivou participacije učesnika, kvalitetu razvijenih preporuka i spremnosti mladih da preuzmu aktivniju ulogu u zagovaranju promjena.
Radionica je potvrdila relevantnost projektnog pristupa koji kombinuje edukaciju, praktičan rad i javno zagovaranje, te predstavlja važan korak ka osnaživanju mladih za dostojanstveniji i sigurniji položaj na tržištu rada.
title_en: Educational and advocacy workshop. Project: “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”
excerpt_en: On 22 April 2026, at the UpBeat Hub in Podgorica, a one-day educational and advocacy workshop was held for 20 young people aged 15–29, during which young ambassadors for decent work were selected.
content_en:
On 22 April 2026, at the UpBeat Hub in Podgorica, an educational and advocacy workshop was successfully held under the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”, aimed at strengthening young people's knowledge, skills and participation in decent work, labour rights, occupational safety and health, and public advocacy. The workshop followed the agenda and methodology set out in the project documentation.
The workshop was attended by 20 young people aged 15 to 29, including participants from a range of educational and social backgrounds, among them young people from the groups the project particularly targets. From the very start the workshop was marked by a high level of motivation, openness and active participation, and the atmosphere throughout the full day's work was exceptionally lively, constructive and encouraging.
Part I – Decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health
In the first part of the workshop participants had the opportunity to acquire and deepen their knowledge of the concept of decent work, of the basic rights and obligations arising from an employment relationship, and of the most common ways in which young people's rights are violated on the labour market. Particular focus was placed on the importance of a preventive culture and of occupational safety and health, including recognising the risks and irregularities young people may encounter in their first job.
Through presentations, discussion and work on practical examples, participants showed great interest in topics concerning undeclared work, ignorance of one's rights, unsafe working conditions and the lack of information about protection mechanisms. It was particularly noticeable that the young people actively connected the material presented with their own experience, that of their peers and examples from the local context.
During the interactive exercise “Spot the problem – respond”, participants worked in groups to analyse real cases of rights being violated and proposed possible solutions. This segment showed a high level of understanding of the problems, and also the participants' ability to identify practical answers to the challenges of the labour market.
Part II – Public advocacy and the active participation of young people
The second part of the workshop was devoted to public advocacy as a tool for social change and for involving young people actively in decision-making.
Through brainstorming, discussion and group work, participants identified the problems they consider priorities for young people's position on the labour market, defined goals for change, mapped the relevant actors and formulated advocacy messages; this part of the training was led by Lidija Brnović, an expert in the field with more than two decades of experience.
In this part of the workshop participants showed an exceptionally high level of engagement and creativity, putting forward numerous concrete proposals for improving young people's position. After a joint discussion and prioritisation, participants agreed on three key recommendations, for which they developed an initial advocacy plan:
1. Tackling undeclared work and strengthening protection for young people in informal work
Participants identified undeclared work as one of the most pressing problems young people face when entering the labour market, particularly through seasonal, casual and poorly regulated jobs. It was emphasised that work without a contract leaves young people without basic rights, social security or protection.
The advocacy goal defined was the need to improve young people's awareness of the risks of undeclared work, to strengthen preventive measures and to secure a stronger institutional response to the problem.
2. An initiative to recognise menstrual leave as a matter of decent work
As a particularly significant and innovative topic, participants identified the need to open a public dialogue on menstrual leave as a question of labour rights, health and decent work.
Participants pointed out that this topic is rarely recognised in public policy, even though it directly affects the position of young women on the labour market. The recommendation defined was to launch an advocacy initiative aimed at giving the issue greater institutional and public recognition.
3. Improving the position of young people in professional development programmes
The third recommendation concerned the unregulated position of young people engaged through professional training and development programmes, who are often without the rights arising from an employment relationship, without length of service, without adequate training for safe work and without paid insurance in the event of an injury at work or an occupational disease.
Participants recognised the need for the status of these young people to be regulated more clearly, and advocated the introduction of minimum standards of protection, including compulsory training for safe work, insurance against injuries at work and a greater degree of legal certainty.
For each of the three recommendations participants developed the basic elements of an advocacy plan, including:
• the goal of the change
• key messages
• the decision-makers being addressed
• potential allies
• first steps for micro-advocacy actions.
This process showed that young people not only recognise the problems but are capable of formulating concrete, relevant recommendations with the potential for further advocacy and public promotion.
Part III – Micro-advocacy actions and the selection of ambassadors
In the third part of the workshop participants worked on turning advocacy messages into micro-campaign actions. Particularly valuable was the practical segment of filming short advocacy video messages, in which the young people demonstrated an ability to communicate a problem and a call to action clearly and persuasively.
This part of the workshop further confirmed the participants' high level of motivation and their readiness for public engagement.
On the basis of their engagement throughout the day, the quality of their ideas, their communication skills and the motivation they showed, the facilitators decided to select 6 young ambassadors for decent work instead of the five originally planned, given the exceptional quality of the participants' contributions and the wish to support a wider group of young people ready for further engagement. The decision to select an additional ambassador was taken because of the evident quality of the candidates and the equal value of their contributions.
The ambassadors selected will be involved in the project's coming activities, particularly campaign work, the promotion of advocacy messages and public events.
General impressions and evaluation
The closing evaluation showed very positive reactions from participants, who rated the workshop as useful, relevant and encouraging. They particularly praised the practical character of the work, the opportunity to express their views freely and the fact that for the first time they had the chance to discuss questions of young people's work from the perspective of their own experience and their own capacity to influence things.
The workshop showed that young people not only recognise the problems but have concrete ideas and a readiness to take part in solving them when they are given the right space, support and working methods.
The educational and advocacy workshop successfully achieved the objectives planned, helping to increase young people's knowledge of decent work, to strengthen their advocacy capacity and to identify young ambassadors who will continue their engagement under the project.
The particular value of the workshop lies in the high level of participation, the quality of the recommendations developed and the young people's readiness to take a more active role in advocating change.
The workshop confirmed the relevance of a project approach combining education, practical work and public advocacy, and is an important step towards empowering young people for a more dignified and secure position on the labour market.

title: Kompanija Remidvis, član našeg Udruženja dobitnik je nagrade za doprinos razvoju privrede i afirmaciji poslovne zajednice

content: Sa velikim ponosom primili smo vijest da je kompanija Remidvis, član našeg Udruženja za zaštitu na radu, dobitnik prestižne nagrade za doprinos razvoju privrede i afirmaciji poslovne zajednice.Ovo značajno priznanje potvrđuje njihov kontinuirani doprinos unapređenju poslovnog ambijenta, ali i vrijednosti koje dosljedno njeguju – profesionalnost, posvećenost i visok stepen društvene odgovornosti. title_en: Remidvis, a member of our Association, has received the award for contribution to economic development and to the business community

content_en: It was with great pride that we received the news that Remidvis, a member of our occupational safety association, has received the prestigious award for contribution to economic development and to the business community.
