title: Sastanak – organizacija edukativnih radionica u srednjim stručnim školama
excerpt: Radni sastanak predavača angažovanih na projektu "Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad" održan je radi planiranja edukativnih radionica u srednjim stručnim školama; učestvovali su Sanja Dujović, Branislav Šebek, Marjan Brčić i Đina Janković.
content:
U okviru realizacije projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“, u petak je održan radni sastanak posvećen planiranju i organizaciji edukativnih aktivnosti u srednjim stručnim školama (aktivnost A3.1 – edukativni program za mlade).
Sastanku su prisustvovali predavači:
• Sanja Dujović
• Branislav Šebek
• Marjan Brčić
• Đina Janković
Zabog ranije preuzetih obaveza sastanku nijesu prisustvovali:
• Anđa Strugar i
• Tanja Šćepanović
Cilj sastanka bio je operativno planiranje realizacije predavanja u školama, definisanje raspodjele predavača, kao i usaglašavanje narednih koraka u kontekstu institucionalnih procedura i pripreme edukativnih materijala.
Institucionalni okvir i status odobrenja
Tokom sastanka konstatovano je da je proces pribavljanja potrebnih saglasnosti za realizaciju aktivnosti u obrazovnim ustanovama u završnoj fazi.
Zahtjev za sprovođenje radionica, upućen Ministarstvu prosvjete, nauke i inovacija, razmotren je i proslijeđen nadležnim institucijama. Centar za stručno obrazovanje dao je pozitivno mišljenje, dok se formalno odobrenje Zavoda za školstvo očekuje u narednim danima. Ovim će se steći svi preduslovi za nesmetan početak realizacije planiranih aktivnosti.
Raspodjela predavača i plan realizacije
U skladu sa projektnim planom, izvršena je raspodjela predavača po srednjim stručnim školama, uzimajući u obzir stručne kompetencije, prethodno iskustvo i geografski aspekt.
Kao prvi potvrđeni termin definisano je održavanje predavanja u JU Srednja ekonomska škola „Mirko Vešović“, Podgorica, gdje će radionicu realizovati Sanja Dujović.
Za ostale obrazovne ustanove očekuje se potvrda termina u najkraćem roku, nakon čega će predavači biti blagovremeno informisani o dinamici realizacije.
Sadržaj i metodologija edukativnih radionica
Tokom sastanka dodatno je razrađen sadržaj edukativnih aktivnosti, koje su usmjerene na mlade koji se nalaze u procesu pripreme za ulazak na tržište rada.
Radionice će obuhvatiti sljedeće tematske cjeline:
• dostojanstven rad i osnovni principi rada u savremenom društvu
• radna prava i obaveze mladih
• zaštita i zdravlje na radu
Metodološki pristup biće zasnovan na interaktivnom radu, uključujući:
• analizu konkretnih primjera iz prakse
• studije slučaja
• diskusije i razmjenu iskustava
• simulacije situacija sa tržišta rada
Planirano je i sprovođenje kratkih evaluacionih testova prije i nakon radionica, kako bi se mjerio nivo usvojenog znanja i efekat edukacije.
Priprema edukativnih materijala
Jedna od ključnih tema sastanka odnosila se na pripremu i prilagođavanje prezentacija koje će predavači koristiti tokom realizacije radionica.
Dogovoreno je da svi predavači:
• koriste jedinstvenu osnovnu prezentaciju kao polazni materijal
• dodatno prilagode sadržaj specifičnostima škole i profilu učenika
• po potrebi uklone ili modifikuju opšte dijelove koji nijesu direktno relevantni za ciljnu grupu
Ovaj pristup ima za cilj da obezbijedi kvalitetnu, ali i fleksibilnu isporuku sadržaja, prilagođenu realnim potrebama učenika u različitim obrazovnim profilima.
Povezanost sa projektnim ciljevima
Naglašeno je da edukativne radionice predstavljaju jednu od ključnih aktivnosti projekta, sa direktnim uticajem na povećanje znanja i svijesti mladih o radnim pravima i bezbjednosti na radu.
Ove aktivnosti doprinose:
• jačanju kapaciteta mladih za bezbjedan ulazak na tržište rada
• smanjenju njihove ranjivosti u odnosu na nesigurne oblike zaposlenja
• unapređenju njihove informisanosti o mehanizmima zaštite
Takođe, kroz promociju help-line servisa i online „pravnog kutka“, učenici će biti informisani o dostupnim kanalima podrške, što predstavlja važan dodatni element projekta.
Sastanak je zaključen uz konstataciju da su stvoreni svi operativni preduslovi za početak realizacije edukativnih aktivnosti, uz očekivanje finalne formalne saglasnosti nadležnih institucija.
Kao ključni naredni koraci definisani su:
• finalizacija i dostavljanje prezentacija od strane predavača
• potvrda termina za sve planirane škole
• koordinacija sa obrazovnim ustanovama
• početak realizacije radionica
Ovaj sastanak predstavlja važan korak u implementaciji projekta, jer omogućava prelazak iz faze planiranja u fazu konkretne realizacije aktivnosti koje imaju direktan uticaj na mlade i njihov budući položaj na tržištu rada.
title_en: Meeting – organising educational workshops in secondary vocational schools
excerpt_en: A working meeting of the lecturers engaged on the project “Youth voices for decent work” was held to plan the educational workshops in secondary vocational schools; Sanja Dujović, Branislav Šebek, Marjan Brčić and Đina Janković took part.
content_en:
As part of the implementation of the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”, a working meeting was held on Friday devoted to planning and organising the educational activities in secondary vocational schools (activity A3.1 – educational programme for young people).
The meeting was attended by the lecturers:
• Sanja Dujović
• Branislav Šebek
• Marjan Brčić
• Đina Janković
Because of prior commitments, the meeting was not attended by:
• Anđa Strugar and
• Tanja Šćepanović
The aim of the meeting was to plan the practical delivery of the lectures in schools, to allocate lecturers and to agree the next steps regarding institutional procedures and the preparation of teaching materials.
Institutional framework and the status of approvals
The meeting noted that the process of obtaining the necessary approvals for carrying out activities in educational institutions is in its final stage.
The request to hold the workshops, submitted to the Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation, has been considered and forwarded to the competent institutions. The Centre for Vocational Education has given a positive opinion, while formal approval from the Bureau for Education Services is expected in the coming days. This will put all the preconditions in place for the planned activities to begin without obstacle.
Allocation of lecturers and the delivery plan
In line with the project plan, lecturers were allocated to the secondary vocational schools, taking into account their professional competences, previous experience and geography.
The first confirmed date is a lecture at the “Mirko Vešović” Secondary School of Economics, Podgorica, where the workshop will be delivered by Sanja Dujović.
Dates for the other educational institutions are expected to be confirmed shortly, after which the lecturers will be informed in good time of the schedule.
Content and methodology of the educational workshops
The meeting further developed the content of the educational activities, which are aimed at young people preparing to enter the labour market.
The workshops will cover the following thematic units:
• decent work and the basic principles of work in modern society
• young people's labour rights and obligations
• occupational safety and health
The methodological approach will be based on interactive work, including:
• analysis of concrete examples from practice
• case studies
• discussion and the exchange of experience
• simulations of situations from the labour market
Short evaluation tests before and after the workshops are also planned, in order to measure how much knowledge has been taken in and what effect the training has had.
Preparation of teaching materials
One of the key topics of the meeting was the preparation and adaptation of the presentations the lecturers will use during the workshops.
It was agreed that all lecturers will:
• use a single core presentation as their starting material
• further adapt the content to the particular school and to the pupils' profile
• where necessary remove or modify general sections that are not directly relevant to the target group
The aim of this approach is to ensure delivery that is both good quality and flexible, adapted to the real needs of pupils on different educational profiles.
Connection with the project's objectives
It was emphasised that the educational workshops are one of the project's key activities, with a direct effect on increasing young people's knowledge and awareness of labour rights and safety at work.
These activities contribute to:
• strengthening young people's capacity for a safe entry into the labour market
• reducing their vulnerability to insecure forms of employment
• improving their awareness of the mechanisms available to protect them
Through the promotion of the help-line service and the online “legal corner”, pupils will also be informed about the support channels available to them, which is an important additional element of the project.
The meeting closed with the observation that all the operational preconditions for beginning the educational activities are in place, pending final formal approval from the competent institutions.
The key next steps defined were:
• finalisation and submission of the presentations by the lecturers
• confirmation of dates for all the schools planned
• coordination with the educational institutions
• the start of the workshops
This meeting is an important step in implementing the project, because it allows the move from the planning phase to the phase of concrete activities with a direct effect on young people and their future position on the labour market.

title: POZIV ZA UČEŠĆE NA EDUKATIVNO-ZAGOVARAČKOJ RADIONICI
excerpt: UZNR CG je pozvalo mlade uzrasta 15-29 godina da se prijave za edukativno-zagovaračku radionicu zakazanu za 22. april 2026. u UpBeat Hub-u u Podgorici.
content:
POZIV ZA UČEŠĆE NA EDUKATIVNO-ZAGOVARAČKOJ RADIONICI
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore poziva mlade uzrasta 15 do 29 godina da se prijave za učešće na edukativno-zagovaračkoj radionici koja se organizuje u okviru projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“.
Radionica će se održati 22. aprila 2026. godine, sa početkom u 09:00 časova, u prostoru Upbeat Hub-a u Podgorici.
Cilj radionice je jačanje znanja i kapaciteta mladih u oblasti dostojanstvenog rada, radnih prava i zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kao i osnaživanje za aktivno učešće u procesima javnog zagovaranja. Poseban fokus biće na uključivanju mladih iz ranjivih i nedovoljno zastupljenih grupa, uključujući NEET mlade, mlade žene, Rome/kinje i mlade sa invaliditetom.
Radionica je jednodnevnog karaktera i obuhvatiće:
• edukativni segment o dostojanstvenom radu, radnim pravima i zaštiti i zdravlju na radu;
• interaktivni dio posvećen osnovama javnog zagovaranja;
• praktičan rad na kreiranju zagovaračkih poruka i sadržaja koje će učesnici dalje promovisati kroz aktivnosti projekta.
U okviru radionice biće odabrano 5 mladih ambasadora dostojanstvenog rada, koji će imati priliku da:
• aktivno učestvuju u kreiranju i širenju kampanjskih poruka;
• predstave stavove i preporuke mladih kroz projektne aktivnosti i javne događaje;
• doprinesu vidljivosti tema radnih prava i zaštite i zdravlja na radu u Crnoj Gori.
Izbor ambasadora biće zasnovan na motivaciji, aktivnom učešću tokom radionice i spremnosti za dalji angažman u okviru projekta.
Učešće na radionici je besplatno. Za učesnike su obezbijeđeni radni materijali, osvježenje i ručak. Za učesnike koji dolaze van Podgorice biće obezbijeđena refundacija putnih troškova.
Zainteresovani kandidati treba da se prijave putem online formulara dostupnog na sljedećem linku:
LINK
Broj mjesta je ograničen, a selekcija učesnika biće izvršena u skladu sa ciljevima projekta i zastupljenošću ciljnih grupa.
Za sve dodatne informacije možete se obratiti putem e-maila: info@uznr.me ili na br.tel. 067 412 900.
Pozivamo sve zainteresovane mlade da iskoriste ovu priliku za sticanje znanja, razmjenu iskustava i aktivno uključivanje u unapređenje položaja mladih na tržištu rada.
Projekat finansira Evropska unija, a kofinansira Ministarstvo regionalno-investicionog razvoja i sardanje sa nevladinim organizacijama, u okviru mrežže YHWBT.
title_en: CALL FOR PARTICIPANTS IN AN EDUCATIONAL AND ADVOCACY WORKSHOP
excerpt_en: UZNR CG invited young people aged 15–29 to apply for the educational and advocacy workshop scheduled for 22 April 2026 at the UpBeat Hub in Podgorica.
content_en:
CALL FOR PARTICIPANTS IN AN EDUCATIONAL AND ADVOCACY WORKSHOP
The Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro invites young people aged 15 to 29 to apply to take part in an educational and advocacy workshop organised under the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”.
The workshop will be held on 22 April 2026, starting at 09:00, at the UpBeat Hub in Podgorica.
The aim of the workshop is to strengthen young people's knowledge and capacity in decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health, and to give them the confidence to take an active part in public advocacy. Particular focus will be placed on involving young people from vulnerable and under-represented groups, including NEET young people, young women, Roma and young people with disabilities.
The workshop lasts one day and will comprise:
• an educational segment on decent work, labour rights and occupational safety and health;
• an interactive part devoted to the basics of public advocacy;
• practical work on creating advocacy messages and content that participants will go on to promote through the project's activities.
During the workshop 5 young ambassadors for decent work will be selected, who will have the opportunity to:
• take an active part in creating and spreading campaign messages;
• present young people's views and recommendations through the project's activities and at public events;
• help make labour rights and occupational safety and health more visible in Montenegro.
The ambassadors will be selected on the basis of their motivation, their active participation during the workshop and their readiness for further engagement in the project.
Participation in the workshop is free of charge. Working materials, refreshments and lunch are provided. Travel costs will be reimbursed for participants coming from outside Podgorica.
Interested candidates should apply through the online form available at the following link:
LINK
Places are limited, and participants will be selected in line with the project's objectives and the representation of the target groups.
For any further information, contact us by e-mail at info@uznr.me or by telephone on 067 412 900.
We invite all interested young people to take this opportunity to gain knowledge, exchange experience and become actively involved in improving the position of young people on the labour market.
The project is financed by the European Union and co-financed by the Ministry of Regional Investment Development and Cooperation with Non-Governmental Organisations, within the YHWBT network.

title: Prezentacija projektnih aktivnosti projekta „Glas mladih za  dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“, u JUSMŠ „Ivan Goran Kovačić“ Herceg Novi
excerpt: U JUSMŠ "Ivan Goran Kovačić" u Herceg Novom održana je 8. aprila 2026. uvodna prezentacija projekta "Glas mladih", kojom je Đina Janković najavila predstojeću edukativnu radionicu u toj školi.
content:
Dana 08. aprila 2026. godine održana je uvodna prezentacija u JUSMŠ „Ivan Goran Kovačić“ Herceg Novi, u okviru aktivnosti projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“. Ova aktivnost imala je za cilj da učenike upozna sa predstojećom edukativnom radionicom, kao i da ih motiviše za aktivno učešće u programima koji se odnose na njihova radna prava, zaštitu i zdravlje na radu.
Tokom susreta, predstavnica Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore, Đina Janković, predstavila je osnovne ciljeve projekta, sa posebnim fokusom na značaj informisanja mladih prije njihovog ulaska na tržište rada. Učenici su upoznati sa ključnim izazovima sa kojima se mladi suočavaju u Crnoj Gori, uključujući nedovoljnu informisanost o radnim pravima, rizike od nesigurnih oblika zaposlenja, kao i nedostatak sistemske edukacije u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
Poseban akcenat stavljen je na predstavljanje sadržaja radionice koja će se realizovati u narednom periodu u ovoj školi. Učenicima su približene teme koje će biti obrađene kroz interaktivni rad, uključujući pojam dostojanstvenog rada, osnovna prava i obaveze iz radnog odnosa, kao i ključne aspekte zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Takođe, najavljen je i praktični dio radionice, koji podrazumijeva analizu realnih situacija sa tržišta rada i diskusiju o mogućim načinima reagovanja u slučajevima kršenja prava.
U okviru prezentacije, učenicima je dodatno predstavljen i koncept help-line servisa i online „pravnog kutka“, kao sigurnog i diskretnog kanala putem kojeg će moći da dobiju informacije i savjete u vezi sa radnim pravima i uslovima rada. Ovaj segment izazvao je posebno interesovanje među učenicima, što potvrđuje potrebu za dostupnim i povjerljivim mehanizmima podrške mladima.
Interakcija sa učenicima tokom prezentacije pokazala je da postoji značajan nivo zainteresovanosti za ove teme, ali i ograničeno prethodno znanje, što dodatno potvrđuje relevantnost planiranih aktivnosti. Učenici su aktivno učestvovali u diskusiji, postavljali pitanja i iskazali spremnost da se uključe u predstojeću radionicu.
Ova uvodna aktivnost predstavlja važan korak u realizaciji edukativnog programa projekta, jer doprinosi informisanju, motivaciji i pripremi mladih za učešće u radionicama koje imaju za cilj njihovo osnaživanje za bezbjedan i dostojanstven rad. Istovremeno, ona potvrđuje značaj direktnog rada sa mladima u obrazovnim institucijama, kao ključnog kanala za unapređenje njihove informisanosti i jačanje kapaciteta za aktivno učešće u društvenim i ekonomskim procesima.
title_en: Presentation of the activities of the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change” at the “Ivan Goran Kovačić” Secondary School, Herceg Novi
excerpt_en: On 8 April 2026 the “Ivan Goran Kovačić” Secondary School in Herceg Novi hosted an introductory presentation of the “Youth voices” project, at which Đina Janković announced the educational workshop to come at the school.
content_en:
On 8 April 2026 an introductory presentation was held at the “Ivan Goran Kovačić” Secondary School in Herceg Novi, as part of the activities of the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”. The aim was to acquaint pupils with the educational workshop to come and to encourage them to take an active part in programmes concerning their labour rights and their safety and health at work.
At the meeting, Đina Janković, representing the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, presented the project's basic objectives, with particular focus on the importance of informing young people before they enter the labour market. Pupils learned about the key challenges young people face in Montenegro, including insufficient knowledge of labour rights, the risks of insecure forms of employment and the lack of systematic education in occupational safety and health.
Particular emphasis was placed on presenting the content of the workshop to be held at the school in the period ahead. Pupils were introduced to the topics that will be covered through interactive work, including the concept of decent work, the basic rights and obligations arising from an employment relationship, and the key aspects of occupational safety and health. The practical part of the workshop was also announced, involving analysis of real situations from the labour market and discussion of possible ways of responding when rights are violated.
The presentation also introduced pupils to the help-line service and the online “legal corner”, a safe and discreet channel through which they will be able to obtain information and advice about labour rights and working conditions. This segment aroused particular interest among the pupils, which confirms the need for accessible, confidential support mechanisms for young people.
The interaction with pupils during the presentation showed a significant level of interest in these topics but also limited prior knowledge, which further confirms the relevance of the activities planned. Pupils took an active part in the discussion, asked questions and expressed their readiness to join the workshop to come.
This introductory activity is an important step in delivering the project's educational programme, because it informs, motivates and prepares young people to take part in workshops aimed at empowering them for safe and decent work. At the same time it confirms the importance of working directly with young people in educational institutions as a key channel for improving their knowledge and strengthening their capacity to take an active part in social and economic life.

title: Sastanak o unapređenju sistema osiguranja zaposlenih i formiranju Fonda za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu
excerpt: U Ministarstvu rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga održan je 2. aprila 2026. sastanak sa Agencijom za nadzor osiguranja o unapređenju kolektivnog osiguranja zaposlenih i mogućem uspostavljanju Fonda za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu.
content:
Dana 2. aprila, u Ministarstvu rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga održan je sastanak sa predstavnicima Agencije za nadzor osiguranja, posvećen unapređenju sistema kolektivnog osiguranja zaposlenih od povreda na radu, profesionalnih bolesti i bolesti u vezi sa radom. Poseban fokus sastanka bio je na razmatranju modela za uspostavljanje Fonda za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu, kao novog sistemskog rješenja u ovoj oblasti.
Sastanku su prisustvovali predstavnici Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, kao predlagača zakonske norme, kao i socijalni partneri – Unija slobodnih sindikata Crne Gore, Savez sindikata Crne Gore i Unija poslodavaca. Ovakav sastav učesnika ukazuje na važnost dijaloga između institucija, regulatornih tijela, stručne javnosti i socijalnih partnera u procesu unapređenja sistema zaštite zaposlenih.
U uvodnom dijelu sastanka istaknuta je potreba za sveobuhvatnim unapređenjem postojećeg modela kolektivnog osiguranja, koji je u praksi često ograničen na formalno ispunjavanje obaveza, bez značajnijeg uticaja na stvarnu sigurnost zaposlenih. Naglašeno je da je neophodno uspostaviti sistem koji će, osim obezbjeđivanja naknada u slučaju povrede ili bolesti, imati i snažnu preventivnu komponentu.
U tom kontekstu, posebna pažnja posvećena je konceptu Fonda za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu. Predloženi Fond predstavlja novi sistemski mehanizam kojim bi se dio sredstava iz sistema osiguranja usmjeravao ka prevenciji, edukaciji i unapređenju uslova rada. Cilj ovakvog pristupa je smanjenje broja povreda na radu i profesionalnih oboljenja, kroz proaktivno djelovanje i ulaganje u bezbjednije radno okruženje.
Tokom diskusije istaknuto je da savremeni sistemi zaštite na radu u razvijenim zemljama Evropske unije upravo počivaju na ovakvom modelu, gdje se sredstva ne koriste isključivo za isplatu naknada, već i za finansiranje preventivnih mjera, edukativnih programa, stručnih istraživanja i rehabilitacije povrijeđenih radnika. Time se postiže dugoročno smanjenje rizika i unapređenje ukupnog sistema zaštite zaposlenih.
Predstavnici učesnika saglasili su se da je od ključnog značaja uspostaviti balans između obaveza osiguravajućih društava, interesa poslodavaca i prava zaposlenih, uz jasno definisane mehanizme kontrole i transparentnosti. Posebno je naglašena potreba da se obezbijedi efikasna primjena budućih rješenja u praksi, kako bi se izbjegla situacija u kojoj zakonske norme ostaju samo formalne, bez stvarnog efekta.
U završnom dijelu sastanka zaključeno je da je nastavak dijaloga između svih relevantnih aktera neophodan kako bi se došlo do održivog i funkcionalnog modela. Istaknuto je da je zajednički cilj uspostavljanje sistema koji će obezbijediti veću sigurnost zaposlenih i dugoročno unaprijediti oblast zaštite i zdravlja na radu u Crnoj Gori.
Zaključno, sastanak predstavlja važan korak ka reformi sistema kolektivnog osiguranja zaposlenih, sa jasnim opredjeljenjem da se zaštita na radu razvija u pravcu preventivnog, transparentnog i društveno odgovornog modela, u kojem je bezbjednost zaposlenih prioritet.
title_en: Meeting on improving the employee insurance system and establishing a Fund for Occupational Safety and Health
excerpt_en: On 2 April 2026 the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue hosted a meeting with the Insurance Supervision Agency on improving collective insurance for employees and on the possible establishment of a Fund for Occupational Safety and Health.
content_en:
On 2 April, at the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, a meeting was held with representatives of the Insurance Supervision Agency, devoted to improving the system of collective insurance for employees against injuries at work, occupational diseases and work-related illnesses. The meeting focused in particular on models for establishing a Fund for Occupational Safety and Health as a new systemic solution in this field.
The meeting was attended by representatives of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, as the proposer of the legal provision, and by the social partners — the Union of Free Trade Unions of Montenegro, the Confederation of Trade Unions of Montenegro and the Employers' Union. This composition points to the importance of dialogue between institutions, regulatory bodies, the professional community and the social partners in improving the system that protects employees.
The opening part of the meeting emphasised the need for a comprehensive improvement of the existing collective insurance model, which in practice is often limited to the formal fulfilment of obligations, without any significant effect on employees' actual security. It was stressed that a system must be established which, besides providing compensation in the event of injury or illness, also has a strong preventive component.
In that context, particular attention was paid to the concept of a Fund for Occupational Safety and Health. The proposed fund would be a new systemic mechanism directing part of the resources from the insurance system towards prevention, education and better working conditions. The aim of such an approach is to reduce the number of injuries at work and occupational diseases through proactive action and investment in a safer working environment.
The discussion emphasised that modern occupational safety systems in the developed countries of the European Union rest on precisely this model, in which funds are used not only to pay compensation but also to finance preventive measures, educational programmes, professional research and the rehabilitation of injured workers. This achieves a long-term reduction in risk and improves the overall system protecting employees.
Participants agreed that it is essential to strike a balance between the obligations of insurance companies, the interests of employers and the rights of employees, with clearly defined mechanisms of control and transparency. Particular emphasis was placed on the need to ensure that future solutions are effectively applied in practice, so as to avoid a situation in which legal provisions remain merely formal, with no real effect.
The closing part of the meeting concluded that continued dialogue between all the relevant actors is essential if a sustainable, workable model is to be reached. It was emphasised that the shared aim is to establish a system that will provide greater security for employees and improve occupational safety and health in Montenegro in the long term.
In conclusion, the meeting is an important step towards reforming the system of collective insurance for employees, with a clear commitment to developing occupational safety along preventive, transparent and socially responsible lines, in which the safety of employees is the priority.

title: Sastanak sa osiguravajućim društvima
excerpt: U Ministarstvu rada održan je sastanak sa svim osiguravajućim kućama povodom definisanja minimalne visine obaveznog osiguranja koje poslodavac plaća za zaposlene od povreda na radu i profesionalnih bolesti.
content:
U Ministarstvu rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga održan je sastanak sa svim osiguravajućim kućama povodom definisanja zakonske norme o minimalnoj visini obaveznog osiguranja koje poslodavac plaća za zaposlene od povreda na radu, profesionalnih bolesti i bolesti u vezi sa radom.
🎯 Cilj je jasan: spriječiti dosadašnju praksu simboličnih premija i minimalnih isplata – da u slučaju smrti porodica dobije 1.500€, a za tešku povredu poput preloma noge zaposleni 100€.
Predlogom člana 38, u novi Zakon o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu, uvodi se:
✔ minimalna premija (procentualno vezana za minimalnu zaradu),
✔ jasna obaveza osiguranja za sve tri kategorije rizika,
✔ mehanizam kontrole i transparentnosti.
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore jasno je poručilo – zakon mora garantovati realnu, a ne formalnu zaštitu.
š
Ukoliko ne dođe do dogovora sa osiguravajućim društvima, Udruženje je predložilo sistemsko rješenje – osnivanje državnog/javnog Fonda za zaštitu na radu, po uzoru na javne evropske modele:
🇮🇹 INAIL (Italija)
🇦🇹 AUVA (Austrija)
🇩🇪 Berufsgenossenschaften (Njemačka)
🇫🇷 AT/MP fond (Francuska)
U tim sistemima osiguranje ne ide privatnim kućama koje ne ulažu u prevenciju, već javnim institucijama koje finansiraju:
🔹 prevenciju
🔹 edukaciju
🔹 istraživanja
🔹 rehabilitaciju
🔹 pravične isplate povrijeđenima
Zaštita na radu nije trošak – to je obaveza države i poslodavca prema zaposlenima.
title_en: Meeting with the insurance companies
excerpt_en: The Ministry of Labour hosted a meeting with all the insurance companies on defining the minimum level of compulsory insurance an employer pays for employees against injuries at work and occupational diseases.
content_en:
At the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue a meeting was held with all the insurance companies on defining a legal provision on the minimum level of compulsory insurance an employer pays for employees against injuries at work, occupational diseases and work-related illnesses.
🎯 The aim is clear: to put an end to the practice of token premiums and minimal payouts — in which a family receives €1,500 in the event of a death, and an employee €100 for a serious injury such as a broken leg.
The proposed Article 38 of the new Law on Occupational Safety and Health introduces:
✔ a minimum premium (set as a percentage of the minimum wage),
✔ a clear insurance obligation for all three categories of risk,
✔ a mechanism of control and transparency.
The Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro made its position clear — the law must guarantee real protection, not formal protection.

If no agreement is reached with the insurance companies, the Association has proposed a systemic solution — the establishment of a state or public Fund for Occupational Safety, modelled on European public schemes:
🇮🇹 INAIL (Italy)
🇦🇹 AUVA (Austria)
🇩🇪 Berufsgenossenschaften (Germany)
🇫🇷 the AT/MP fund (France)
In those systems the insurance does not go to private companies that invest nothing in prevention, but to public institutions that finance:
🔹 prevention
🔹 education
🔹 research
🔹 rehabilitation
🔹 fair payouts to the injured
Occupational safety is not a cost — it is an obligation of the state and of the employer towards employees.

title: Sastanak Radne grupe za izradu Pravilnika o izmjenama i dopunama Pravilnika o mjerama zaštite na radu od rizika izloženosti azbestu
excerpt: Radna grupa za izmjene Pravilnika o zaštiti od izloženosti azbestu sastala se 13. februara 2026. u Ministarstvu rada; prvi put je učestvovala dr Mile Ušćumlić, specijalistkinja medicine rada.
content:
Dana 13. februara 2026. godine u prostorijama Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga održan je peti, odnosno šesti sastanak Radne grupe formirane radi izrade Pravilnika o izmjenama i dopunama važećeg Pravilnika o mjerama zaštite na radu od rizika izloženosti azbestu. Sastanak je organizovan u okviru kontinuiranog procesa usklađivanja nacionalnog zakonodavstva sa pravnom tekovinom Evropske unije, prije svega sa Direktiva 2009/148/EZ, kao i sa izmjenama uvedenim Direktiva (EU) 2023/2668, kojima su dodatno pooštreni standardi zaštite radnika od izloženosti azbestu.
Dosadašnji rad Radne grupe bio je dominantno usmjeren na tehničko-organizacione aspekte zaštite: procjenu rizika, planiranje radova, obavezu prijavljivanja radova sa azbestom, ograničavanje izloženosti, korišćenje lične zaštitne opreme, osposobljavanje zaposlenih i nadzor nad primjenom mjera. Međutim, na ovom sastanku fokus je po prvi put sistematski pomjeren ka medicinskom aspektu izloženosti azbestu i njegovim dugoročnim posljedicama po zdravlje zaposlenih.
Posebnu vrijednost sastanku dalo je učešće dr Mile Ušćumlić, specijaliste medicine rada, koja se prvi put priključila radu Radne grupe. Njeno izlaganje bilo je posvećeno zdravstvenim efektima izloženosti azbestu, prirodi oboljenja povezanih sa azbestom, dugoj latentnoj fazi razvoja bolesti, kao i kompleksnosti dokazivanja profesionalne etiologije tih oboljenja.
U svom stručnom izlaganju, dr Ušćumlić je istakla da je azbest nedvosmisleno povezan sa nastankom teških i često smrtonosnih oboljenja, među kojima se izdvajaju azbestoza, pleuralni plakovi i difuzna pleuralna zadebljanja, karcinom pluća, kao i maligni mezoteliom pleure. Posebno je naglašeno da je riječ o bolestima koje karakteriše izrazito duga latentna faza – klinička manifestacija može nastupiti 20, 30 pa i više godina nakon početka izlaganja. Upravo ta činjenica predstavlja jedan od najvećih izazova kako u medicinskoj dijagnostici, tako i u pravnom priznavanju bolesti kao profesionalne.
U diskusiji je ukazano da je za pouzdano utvrđivanje profesionalne etiologije neophodna kombinacija medicinskih i nemedicinskih dokaza. Ključni elementi uključuju detaljnu profesionalnu anamnezu, podatke o trajanju i intenzitetu izloženosti, dokumentaciju o radnim mjestima i poslovima na kojima je zaposleni radio, rezultate mjerenja koncentracije azbestnih vlakana u radnoj sredini, kao i uredno vođene evidencije poslodavca o procjeni rizika i sprovedenim mjerama zaštite. Bez sistematskog i dugoročnog vođenja tih podataka, dokazivanje uzročno-posljedične veze između oboljenja i radnog mjesta postaje znatno otežano.
U tom kontekstu, Radna grupa je prepoznala da izmjene pravilnika ne treba da budu ograničene samo na formalno usklađivanje sa evropskim propisima, već da moraju osnažiti medicinski segment zaštite na radu. Posebno je naglašena potreba preciznijeg normiranja zdravstvenog nadzora zaposlenih koji su izloženi azbestu. To podrazumijeva jasnije definisanje početnih i periodičnih ljekarskih pregleda, sadržaja tih pregleda (uključujući funkcionalna ispitivanja pluća i odgovarajuće radiološke metode), kao i obavezu praćenja zdravstvenog stanja i nakon prestanka izlaganja, imajući u vidu dugu latentnost bolesti.
Takođe je razmatrana obaveza čuvanja evidencija o izloženosti tokom produženog vremenskog perioda, kako bi podaci bili dostupni i decenijama nakon završetka radnog angažmana zaposlenog. U svjetlu izmjena uvedenih Direktivom (EU) 2023/2668, poseban akcenat stavljen je i na snižavanje granične vrijednosti izloženosti i unapređenje metodologije mjerenja koncentracije azbestnih vlakana, što dodatno pojačava preventivni karakter propisa.
Zaključeno je da je medicinski aspekt zaštite od azbesta neraskidivo povezan sa pravom zaposlenog na priznavanje profesionalne bolesti i ostvarivanje prava iz sistema socijalne sigurnosti. Stoga će u daljem radu Radne grupe biti predložene dopune pravilnika koje će:
• preciznije urediti zdravstveni nadzor zaposlenih izloženih azbestu;
• osnažiti obaveze poslodavca u pogledu vođenja i čuvanja evidencija o izloženosti;
• unaprijediti informisanje zaposlenih o dugoročnim zdravstvenim rizicima;
• obezbijediti usklađenost sa novim, strožijim evropskim standardima u pogledu graničnih vrijednosti i metoda mjerenja.
Sastanak je zaključen ocjenom da je uključivanje stručnjaka medicine rada od suštinskog značaja za kvalitet normativnih rješenja, te da će medicinski kriterijumi i iskustva iz prakse predstavljati važnu osnovu za finalizaciju nacrta izmjena i dopuna pravilnika. Time je rad Radne grupe ušao u fazu u kojoj se tehničke, pravne i medicinske dimenzije zaštite na radu od rizika izloženosti azbestu sagledavaju cjelovito, sa krajnjim ciljem – dugoročne i efikasne zaštite zdravlja zaposlenih.
title_en: Meeting of the Working Group drafting the Rulebook amending the Rulebook on occupational safety measures against the risk of exposure to asbestos
excerpt_en: The working group amending the rulebook on protection from exposure to asbestos met on 13 February 2026 at the Ministry of Labour; Dr Mila Ušćumlić, a specialist in occupational medicine, took part for the first time.
content_en:
On 13 February 2026, at the premises of the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, the fifth — or sixth — meeting was held of the Working Group formed to draft a Rulebook amending the current Rulebook on occupational safety measures against the risk of exposure to asbestos. The meeting was organised as part of the continuing process of aligning national legislation with the acquis of the European Union, primarily with Directive 2009/148/EC and with the amendments introduced by Directive (EU) 2023/2668, which further tightened the standards protecting workers from exposure to asbestos.
The Working Group's work so far has been focused predominantly on the technical and organisational aspects of protection: risk assessment, planning of works, the obligation to notify work involving asbestos, limiting exposure, the use of personal protective equipment, training employees and supervising the application of the measures. At this meeting, however, the focus shifted systematically for the first time to the medical aspect of exposure to asbestos and its long-term consequences for employees' health.
Particular value was added by the participation of Dr Mila Ušćumlić, a specialist in occupational medicine, who joined the Working Group's work for the first time. Her presentation was devoted to the health effects of exposure to asbestos, the nature of asbestos-related diseases, the long latency period before the disease develops, and the complexity of proving that such diseases are occupational in origin.
In her expert presentation, Dr Ušćumlić emphasised that asbestos is unambiguously linked to the development of serious and often fatal diseases, prominent among them asbestosis, pleural plaques and diffuse pleural thickening, lung cancer and malignant pleural mesothelioma. She stressed in particular that these are diseases characterised by an exceptionally long latency period — clinical manifestation may occur 20, 30 or even more years after exposure begins. That very fact is one of the greatest challenges both in medical diagnosis and in the legal recognition of a disease as occupational.
The discussion pointed out that reliably establishing occupational origin requires a combination of medical and non-medical evidence. The key elements include a detailed occupational history, data on the duration and intensity of exposure, documentation of the workplaces and jobs the employee has worked in, the results of measurements of asbestos fibre concentrations in the working environment, and properly kept employer records of risk assessment and of the protective measures taken. Without those data being kept systematically and over the long term, proving a causal link between the disease and the workplace becomes considerably harder.
In that context, the Working Group recognised that the amendments to the rulebook should not be limited to formal alignment with European regulations but must strengthen the medical component of occupational safety. Particular emphasis was placed on the need for more precise rules on health surveillance of employees exposed to asbestos. That means defining initial and periodic medical examinations more clearly, defining the content of those examinations (including lung function tests and appropriate radiological methods), and imposing an obligation to monitor employees' health even after exposure has ended, given the long latency of the diseases.
The obligation to keep exposure records for an extended period was also considered, so that the data remain available decades after an employee's engagement has ended. In the light of the amendments introduced by Directive (EU) 2023/2668, particular emphasis was also placed on lowering the exposure limit value and improving the methodology for measuring asbestos fibre concentrations, which further strengthens the preventive character of the regulations.
It was concluded that the medical aspect of protection from asbestos is inseparably linked to an employee's right to have an occupational disease recognised and to exercise their rights under the social security system. In its further work the Working Group will therefore propose additions to the rulebook that will:
• regulate health surveillance of employees exposed to asbestos more precisely;
• strengthen the employer's obligations regarding the keeping and retention of exposure records;
• improve the information given to employees about the long-term health risks;
• ensure alignment with the new, stricter European standards on limit values and measurement methods.
The meeting closed with the assessment that involving occupational medicine specialists is essential to the quality of the legislative solutions, and that medical criteria and experience from practice will be an important basis for finalising the draft amendments. The Working Group's work has thereby entered a phase in which the technical, legal and medical dimensions of protecting workers from the risk of exposure to asbestos are considered as a whole, with the ultimate aim of protecting employees' health effectively and for the long term.
