title: Izvještaj sa završne konferencije projekta „Improved evidence-based policymaking, implementation practices and coordination in the ESP sector and strengthened capacities to participate in ESF“ – EU podrška sektoru zapošljavanja i socijalne politike u Crnoj Gori
excerpt: Đina Janković je učestvovala kao nacionalna ekspertkinja za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu na završnoj konferenciji EU projekta podrške sektoru zapošljavanja i socijalne politike Crne Gore, održanoj 11. februara 2026.
content:
Dana 11.02.2026. godine održana je završna konferencija u okviru projekta „Improved evidence-based policymaking, implementation practices and coordination in the ESP sector and strengthened capacities to participate in ESF“, pod nazivom „EU podrška sektoru zapošljavanja i socijalne politike u Crnoj Gori“. Konferenciju su organizovali Ministarstvo socijalnog staranja, brige o porodici i demografije i Ministarstvo rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga, uz podršku Evropska unija.
Konferenciji je prisustvovala i Đina Janković iz Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, koja je u okviru projekta bila angažovana kao nacionalni ekspert iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Kroz svoj stručni angažman dala je značajan doprinos unapređenju politika i praksi u oblasti bezbjednosti i zdravlja na radu, kao i jačanju kapaciteta relevantnih institucija u procesu usklađivanja sa evropskim standardima.
Tokom konferencije predstavljeni su rezultati višegodišnjih aktivnosti usmjerenih na unapređenje donošenja politika zasnovanih na dokazima, jačanje praksi implementacije i koordinacije u sektoru zapošljavanja i socijalne politike (ESP), kao i osnaživanje kapaciteta za buduće učešće u Evropskom socijalnom fondu (ESF). Poseban akcenat stavljen je na unapređenje institucionalnog i administrativnog okvira, razvoj mehanizama za praćenje i evaluaciju javnih politika, te jačanje međuresorne saradnje.
Ministar socijalnog staranja, brige o porodici i demografije, Damir Gutić, istakao je da Crna Gora nastavlja da gradi moderan, inkluzivan i evropski usklađen sistem socijalne zaštite, naglašavajući značaj prelaska sa pretpristupnih fondova na puno korišćenje sredstava Evropskog socijalnog fonda nakon pristupanja Evropskoj uniji.
Generalna direktorica Direktorata za evropske integracije, EU fondove i međunarodnu saradnju, Emina Mujević Kara, predstavila je ključne rezultate projekta, uključujući unaprijeđene institucionalne procedure, ojačane administrativne kapacitete, uspostavljene alate za analizu i praćenje efekata javnih politika, kao i konkretne korake u pravcu bolje koordinacije i planiranja u sektoru zapošljavanja i socijalne politike.
U ime Delegacija Evropske unije u Crnoj Gori, Brigitte Kuchar ocijenila je da rezultati projekta predstavljaju važan iskorak u usklađivanju sa evropskim standardima i potvrdila dalju podršku Evropske unije reformskim procesima u Crnoj Gori.
Projekat, vrijedan 1.431.450,00 eura, finansiran je u okviru Jednogodišnjeg akcionog dokumenta za 2020. godinu „Podrška pametnom i inkluzivnom rastu – zapošljavanje i socijalna inkluzija“ (IPA II), a sprovodi ga konzorcijum predvođen kompanijom Archidata srl iz Italije.
U narednom periodu planirana je izrada završnog dokumenta projekta, a izražena je spremnost za dalju saradnju sa Liene Maurite u procesu pripreme finalnog dokumenta, kako bi se na sistematičan način objedinjeni svi ostvareni rezultati, preporuke i pravci budućeg djelovanja u sektoru zapošljavanja i socijalne politike.
title_en: Report from the closing conference of the project “Improved evidence-based policymaking, implementation practices and coordination in the ESP sector and strengthened capacities to participate in ESF” – EU support to the employment and social policy sector in Montenegro
excerpt_en: Đina Janković took part as national expert on occupational safety and health at the closing conference of the EU project supporting Montenegro's employment and social policy sector, held on 11 February 2026.
content_en:
On 11 February 2026 the closing conference of the project “Improved evidence-based policymaking, implementation practices and coordination in the ESP sector and strengthened capacities to participate in ESF” was held, under the title “EU support to the employment and social policy sector in Montenegro”. The conference was organised by the Ministry of Social Welfare, Family Care and Demography and the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, with the support of the European Union.
The conference was attended by Đina Janković of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, who was engaged on the project as national expert on occupational safety and health. Through her professional work she made a significant contribution to improving policy and practice in occupational safety and health and to strengthening the capacity of the relevant institutions in the process of alignment with European standards.
The conference presented the results of several years of activity aimed at improving evidence-based policymaking, strengthening implementation and coordination practices in the employment and social policy (ESP) sector, and building capacity for future participation in the European Social Fund (ESF). Particular emphasis was placed on improving the institutional and administrative framework, developing mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating public policy, and strengthening cross-sectoral cooperation.
The Minister of Social Welfare, Family Care and Demography, Damir Gutić, said that Montenegro continues to build a modern, inclusive social protection system aligned with Europe, emphasising the importance of moving from pre-accession funds to the full use of European Social Fund resources after accession to the European Union.
The Director General of the Directorate for European Integration, EU Funds and International Cooperation, Emina Mujević Kara, presented the project's key results, including improved institutional procedures, strengthened administrative capacity, tools established for analysing and monitoring the effects of public policy, and concrete steps towards better coordination and planning in the employment and social policy sector.
On behalf of the Delegation of the European Union to Montenegro, Brigitte Kuchar said the project's results were an important step forward in alignment with European standards and confirmed the European Union's continued support for the reform processes in Montenegro.
The project, worth EUR 1,431,450.00, was financed under the 2020 Annual Action Document “Support to smart and inclusive growth – employment and social inclusion” (IPA II) and is implemented by a consortium led by the Italian company Archidata srl.
A final project document is to be produced in the period ahead, and a readiness was expressed to continue working with Liene Maurite on preparing it, so that all the results achieved, the recommendations and the directions for future work in the employment and social policy sector are brought together systematically.

title: Online sastanak grantista u okviru projekta „Jači glasovi za bolje izbore – Omladinski Hub za Zapadni Balkan i Tursku“
excerpt: Održan je online sastanak grantista mreže "Omladinski Hub za Zapadni Balkan i Tursku", na kojem je Đina Janković predstavila dvomjesečni napredak projekta "Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad".
content:
Odražan je online sastanak sa grantistima – predstavnicima organizacija koje su dobile sredstva za realizaciju projekata i predstavnika/ca NVO Prima, koji je organizovan nakon više od dva mjeseca od početka implementacije projekata, sa ciljem:
• razmjene informacija o dosadašnjem napretku,
• identifikovanja izazova u realizaciji aktivnosti,
• unapređenja koordinacije i međusobne podrške grantista,
• pojašnjenja administrativnih i izvještajnih obaveza.
Sastanak je otvorila Aida Perović, izvršna direktorica i nacionalna koordinatorka mreže Omladinski HUB za Zapadni Balkan i Tursku u Crnoj Gori, koja je naglasila važnost redovne komunikacije i kvalitetnog izvještavanja prema donatoru (EU).
Predstavljanje napretka – Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore
U ime Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore Đina Janković je predstavila jnapredak na projektu „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“
(opšti cilj: unapređenje položaja mladih kroz jačanje znanja o radnim pravima i zaštiti i zdravlju na radu, uz poseban fokus na ranjive grupe)
Realizovane aktivnosti
U prva dva mjeseca realizovano je:
• Iniciranje projekta i mobilizacija partnera
• Održan kick-off sastanak projektnog tima
• Finalizovan operativni plan i M&E matrica
• Uspostavljena komunikacija sa školama i lokalnim OCD
• Mapiranje i outreach aktivnosti
• Identifikovane škole i omladinski servisi u centralnom i sjevernom regionu
• Pokrenuti kontakti sa organizacijama koje rade sa NEET mladima
• Pripremljeni promotivni materijali i javni poziv
• Uspostavljanje help-line servisa (u tehničkoj fazi)
• Definisan protokol za anonimno savjetovanje
• Kreiran online formular
Izazovi u implementaciji
Tokom sastanka istaknuti su sljedeći izazovi:
• Ograničena dostupnost termina u školama zbog školskih obaveza
Sporiji odaziv NEET mladih bez posredovanja lokalnih partnera
materijala)
Administrativna pitanja vezana za dokumentovanje aktivnosti (liste prisustva, evaluacije, foto-dokumentacija)
• Istaknuto je da je u radu sa ranjivim grupama potrebno više vremena za izgradnju povjerenja i direktan terenski rad.
Diskusija i preporuke
Predstavnici NVO Prima dali su sljedeće preporuke:
• Dosljedno primjenjivati pravila EU vidljivosti na svim materijalima
• Pravovremeno dostavljati nacrte komunikacionih materijala na odobrenje
• Voditi urednu dokumentaciju (posebno liste prisustva i evaluacione forme)
• Razmotriti međusobnu promociju aktivnosti grantista (cross-post objave)
• Naglašeno je da projekti treba da zadrže snažan fokus na uključivanje mladih u procese donošenja odluka, u skladu sa ciljevima Omladinskog HUB-a.
Sastanak je ocijenjen kao konstruktivan i koristan za razmjenu iskustava.
Zaključeno je da:
• Implementacija projekata teče u skladu sa planiranom dinamikom.
• Potrebno je intenzivirati terenski rad sa ranjivim grupama.
• Posebnu pažnju treba posvetiti pravilima vidljivosti i administrativnim obavezama.
• Naredni koordinacioni sastanak biće organizovan u drugom kvartalu implementacije.
Dosadašnja realizacija projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“ pokazuje usklađenost sa planiranim ciljevima, posebno u dijelu:
• jačanja znanja mladih o radnim pravima,
• uspostavljanja help-line servisa,
• jačanja saradnje sa obrazovnim institucijama.
Nastavak implementacije biće usmjeren na intenziviranje edukativnih aktivnosti i pokretanje kampanje „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“.
title_en: Online meeting of grantees under the project “Stronger voices for better choices – Youth Hub for the Western Balkans and Türkiye”
excerpt_en: An online meeting of grantees of the “Youth Hub for the Western Balkans and Türkiye” network was held, at which Đina Janković presented two months of progress on the project “Youth voices for decent work”.
content_en:
An online meeting was held with the grantees — representatives of the organisations awarded funds to carry out projects — and representatives of the NGO Prima, organised more than two months after the projects began, with the aim of:
• sharing information on progress so far,
• identifying challenges in carrying out the activities,
• improving coordination and mutual support among grantees,
• clarifying administrative and reporting obligations.
The meeting was opened by Aida Perović, executive director and national coordinator of the Youth Hub for the Western Balkans and Türkiye network in Montenegro, who emphasised the importance of regular communication and good-quality reporting to the donor (the EU).
Presentation of progress – Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro
On behalf of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, Đina Janković presented progress on the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”
(general objective: improving the position of young people by strengthening knowledge of labour rights and occupational safety and health, with particular focus on vulnerable groups)
Activities carried out
In the first two months the following were carried out:
• Launching the project and mobilising partners
• A kick-off meeting of the project team
• Finalisation of the operational plan and the M&E matrix
• Communication established with schools and local CSOs
• Mapping and outreach activities
• Schools and youth services identified in the central and northern regions
• Contacts opened with organisations working with NEET young people
• Promotional materials and a public call prepared
• Establishment of the help-line service (at the technical stage)
• A protocol for anonymous counselling defined
• An online form created
Challenges in implementation
The meeting highlighted the following challenges:
• Limited availability of dates in schools because of school commitments
A slower response from NEET young people without the mediation of local partners
(materials)
Administrative questions relating to documenting activities (attendance lists, evaluations, photographic documentation)
• It was emphasised that working with vulnerable groups requires more time to build trust and more direct fieldwork.
Discussion and recommendations
Representatives of the NGO Prima made the following recommendations:
• Apply the EU visibility rules consistently on all materials
• Submit drafts of communication materials for approval in good time
• Keep documentation in order (particularly attendance lists and evaluation forms)
• Consider grantees promoting each other's activities (cross-posting)
• It was emphasised that projects should keep a strong focus on involving young people in decision-making, in line with the Youth Hub's objectives.
The meeting was assessed as constructive and useful for exchanging experience.
It was concluded that:
• Implementation of the projects is proceeding to the planned schedule.
• Fieldwork with vulnerable groups needs to be intensified.
• Particular attention should be paid to the visibility rules and to administrative obligations.
• The next coordination meeting will be organised in the second quarter of implementation.
Progress so far on the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change” shows it is in line with the objectives planned, particularly as regards:
• strengthening young people's knowledge of labour rights,
• establishing the help-line service,
• strengthening cooperation with educational institutions.
The next stage of implementation will focus on intensifying educational activities and launching the campaign “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”.

title: Sastanak radne grupa za izradu Nacrta Pravilnika o izmjenama i dopunama Pravilnika o mjerama zaštite na radu od rizika izloženosti azbestu
excerpt: U Ministarstvu rada održan je sastanak radne grupe za izradu Nacrta pravilnika o zaštiti od izloženosti azbestu, uz učešće Đine Janković ispred UZNR CG.
content:
U prostorijama Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga, 06.02.2026. godine održan je radni sastanak radne grupe zadužene za pripremu Nacrta pravilnika o izmjenama i dopunama propisa koji uređuje mjere zaštite na radu u uslovima rizika izloženosti azbestu. Pored predstavnika Ministarstva, sastanku je prisustvovala i Đina Janković, predstavnica Udruženja, kao članica radne grupe.
Sastanak je organizovan s namjerom da se razmotre predložene izmjene nacionalnog pravilnika i provjeri njihova usklađenost sa zahtjevima EU okvira, naročito u odnosu na Direktivu 2009/148/EC o zaštiti zaposklneih od rizika izloženosti azbestu, kao i u kontekstu najnovijih dopuna evropskih pravila kroz Direktivu (EU) 2023/2668, kao i pristigli komentari i sugestije.
Konstatovano je da važeći nacionalni pravilnik (objavljen u „Službenom listu Crne Gore“, br. 14/17) zahtijeva dopune i preciziranja kako bi se ojačala praktična zaštita zaposlenih i obezbijedilo jasnije preuzimanje obaveza koje EU standardi postavljaju pred poslodavce i nadležne institucije.
Posebno je istaknuto da EU propisi predstavljaju minimalni nivo zaštite koji države članice, ali i države koje se usklađuju sa EU pravnom tekovinom, treba da primijene kroz nacionalno zakonodavstvo.
Tematske cjeline koje su razmatrane
Tokom sastanka, diskusija je vođena kroz nekoliko ključnih cjelina:
Usklađivanje obaveza poslodavaca sa EU zahtjevima
Analizirano je šta je potrebno dodatno ugraditi u nacionalni tekst, uključujući: procjenu rizika, preventivne mjere, obavezno vođenje evidencija, informisanje zaposlenih, zdravstveni nadzor i komunikaciju sa nadležnim organima.
Granične vrijednosti izloženosti i mjerenja
Razmatrana je potreba usklađivanja graničnih vrijednosti izloženosti azbestnim vlaknima sa evropskim standardima, kao i obezbjeđivanje jasnih pravila za mjerenje izloženosti i periodične procjene rizika na radnim mjestima gdje postoji mogućnost kontakta sa azbestom.
Organizacija rada, procedure i informisanje zaposlenih
Pažnja je usmjerena na operativne obaveze poslodavaca: identifikovanje rizika, planiranje mjera kontrole i smanjenja izloženosti, obuku i obavještavanje zaposlenih o rizicima i zaštitnim mjerama, kao i obavezu praćenja zdravstvenog stanja radnika koji su izloženi ili potencijalno izloženi.
Transponovanje EU propisa i dinamika primjene
Otvoreno je pitanje načina i rokova prenošenja novih EU zahtjeva u nacionalni sistem, uključujući mogućnost prelaznih rješenja (gdje je to opravdano) kako bi primjena u praksi bila ostvariva i pravno jasna.
Sastanak je ocijenjen kao sadržajan i usmjeren na izradu propisa koji treba da bude istovremeno pravno precizan i primjenjiv u praksi. Dogovoreno je da radna grupa nastavi sa aktivnostima u skladu sa definisanim koracima, s ciljem da konačni tekst Nacrta pravilnika unaprijedi sistem zaštite radnika od rizika izloženosti azbestu i bude usklađen sa aktuelnim EU pravilima.
title_en: Meeting of the working group drafting the Rulebook amending the Rulebook on occupational safety measures against the risk of exposure to asbestos
excerpt_en: The Ministry of Labour hosted a meeting of the working group drafting the rulebook on protection from exposure to asbestos, with Đina Janković taking part on behalf of UZNR CG.
content_en:
On 6 February 2026, at the premises of the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, a working meeting was held of the working group responsible for preparing the draft rulebook amending the regulations governing occupational safety measures where there is a risk of exposure to asbestos. Alongside representatives of the Ministry, the meeting was attended by Đina Janković, representing the Association as a member of the working group.
The meeting was organised in order to consider the proposed amendments to the national rulebook and to check their alignment with the requirements of the EU framework, particularly with Directive 2009/148/EC on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos, and in the context of the most recent amendments to European rules through Directive (EU) 2023/2668, as well as to consider the comments and suggestions received.
It was noted that the current national rulebook (published in the “Official Gazette of Montenegro”, no. 14/17) needs additions and clarifications in order to strengthen the practical protection of employees and to ensure a clearer transposition of the obligations that EU standards place on employers and the competent institutions.
It was particularly emphasised that EU regulations represent a minimum level of protection which member states — and also states aligning themselves with the EU acquis — should apply through national legislation.
The topics considered
The discussion at the meeting was organised around several key areas:
Aligning employers' obligations with EU requirements
The group analysed what needs to be added to the national text, including: risk assessment, preventive measures, the compulsory keeping of records, informing employees, health surveillance and communication with the competent authorities.
Exposure limit values and measurement
The group considered the need to align the exposure limit values for asbestos fibres with European standards and to provide clear rules for measuring exposure and for periodic risk assessments at workplaces where contact with asbestos is possible.
Organisation of work, procedures and informing employees
Attention was directed to employers' operational obligations: identifying risks, planning measures to control and reduce exposure, training and informing employees about the risks and protective measures, and the obligation to monitor the health of workers who are exposed or potentially exposed.
Transposition of EU regulations and the timetable for application
The question was raised of how and when the new EU requirements are to be transposed into the national system, including the possibility of transitional arrangements (where justified) so that application in practice is both achievable and legally clear.
The meeting was assessed as substantial and directed towards producing regulations that are at once legally precise and applicable in practice. It was agreed that the working group will continue its work along the steps defined, with the aim that the final text of the draft rulebook should improve the system protecting workers from the risk of exposure to asbestos and be aligned with the current EU rules.

title: Sastanak u Ministarstvu rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga s ciljem prezentacije projekta „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rada – od znanja do promjene“
excerpt: Projektna menadžerka Đina Janković i potpredsjednik UZNR CG Branislav Šebek predstavili su projekat "Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad" Direktoratu za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu Ministarstva rada.
content:
U Ministarstvu rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga (Direktorat za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu) održan je radni sastanak na kojem su predstavnici Udruženja projektna menadžerka Đina Janković i potpredsjednik organizacije Branislav Šebek, predstavili projekat „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“. Ispred Direktorata, sastanku su prisustvovali direktor Aleksandar Memčević, kao i Maja Mijović i Jovana Bošković. Sastanak je imao za cilj da se nadležnoj instituciji predstavi koncept projekta, njegovi strateški ciljevi i planirane aktivnosti, te da se razmotri mogućnost institucionalne saradnje u skladu sa ulogom Ministarstva u kreiranju i sprovođenju politika rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga.
Razgovor je vođen u konstruktivnoj i partnerskoj atmosferi, uz obostrano prepoznavanje značaja unapređenja položaja mladih na tržištu rada.
Predstavljanje projekta
Projektna menadžerka Đina Janković predstavila je polazne osnove projekta, naglašavajući da je inicijativa nastala kao odgovor na uočenu nedovoljnu informisanost mladih o radnim pravima, zaštiti i zdravlju na radu, kao i dostupnim mehanizmima institucionalne zaštite, na osnovu istraživanja sprovedenih tokom 2022. i 2023. godine, kroz projekat „Dostojanstven rada počinje dok si mlad“..
Projekat je usmjeren na mlade uzrasta od 15 do 29 godina, sa posebnim fokusom na ranjive kategorije – NEET populaciju, mlade žene, Rome i Romkinje, mlade sa invaliditetom, kao i učenike i studente koji se prvi put susreću sa tržištem rada.
Branislav Šebek dodatno je istakao značaj povezivanja edukativnih aktivnosti sa praktičnim mehanizmima podrške, naglašavajući da je cilj projekta prelazak „od znanja do promjene“ – odnosno osnaživanje mladih da stečeno znanje primijene u praksi i aktivno učestvuju u unapređenju radnih uslova.
Ključne komponente projekta
Tokom sastanka detaljnije su predstavljene glavne aktivnosti projekta:
• Organizovanje edukativnih radionica i predavanja u srednjim školama i na fakultetima;
• Realizacija posebnog događaja usmjerenog na mlade iz ranjivih grupa;
• Uspostavljanje help-line servisa i online „pravnog kutka“ kao sigurnog kanala za savjetovanje i podršku;
• Sprovođenje medijske i online kampanje u cilju promocije koncepta dostojanstvenog rada;
• Organizovanje okruglog stola sa institucijama i socijalnim partnerima, uz izradu preporuka za unapređenje javnih politika.
Naglašeno je da projekat, pored edukativne dimenzije, ima i zagovaračku komponentu koja podrazumijeva jačanje dijaloga između mladih, institucija i socijalnih partnera.
Uloga Ministarstva i diskusija
U diskusiji je posebno istaknuta uloga Ministarstva kao ključnog aktera u oblasti rada i zapošljavanja. Prepoznato je da projektne aktivnosti mogu doprinijeti:
• unapređenju informisanosti mladih o pravima iz radnog odnosa,
• jačanju preventivnog pristupa zaštiti na radu,
• boljoj institucionalnoj povezanosti i razmjeni informacija,
• razvoju politika koje odgovaraju stvarnim potrebama mladih.
Razmotrena je mogućnost učešća predstavnika Ministarstva u planiranim zagovaračkim događajima, kao i razmjene informacija i iskustava tokom realizacije projekta. Posebno je istaknuto da agregirani i anonimizovani podaci o problemima sa kojima se mladi suočavaju mogu predstavljati koristan input za dalji razvoj mjera i programa Ministarstva.
Takođe je naglašena važnost međusektorske saradnje, uključujući povezivanje sa Zavodom za zapošljavanje, inspekcijskim organima i socijalnim partnerima, u cilju jačanja sistemskog pristupa zaštiti prava mladih radnika.
Zaključci i naredni koraci
Na sastanku je konstatovano:
• da projekat tematski korespondira sa strateškim prioritetima u oblasti rada i zapošljavanja mladih;
• da postoji prostor za institucionalnu saradnju u skladu sa nadležnostima Ministarstva;
• da je važno nastaviti komunikaciju u cilju definisanja konkretnih modela podrške.
Kao naredni koraci predloženi su dostavljanje sažetka projekta Ministarstvu, definisanje kontakt tačke za operativnu komunikaciju, kao i razmatranje mogućnosti učešća predstavnika Ministarstva u planiranom okruglom stolu.
Sastanak je potvrdio zajedničko opredjeljenje za unapređenje položaja mladih na tržištu rada i jačanje kulture dostojanstvenog, sigurnog i zakonitog rada u Crnoj Gori. Projekat „Glas mladih za dostojanstven rad – od znanja do promjene“ prepoznat je kao inicijativa koja može doprinijeti jačanju participacije mladih i kvalitetnijem socijalnom dijalogu između institucija i civilnog sektora.
title_en: Meeting at the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue to present the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”
excerpt_en: Project manager Đina Janković and UZNR CG vice-president Branislav Šebek presented the project “Youth voices for decent work” to the Ministry of Labour's Directorate for Occupational Safety and Health.
content_en:
At the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue (Directorate for Occupational Safety and Health) a working meeting was held at which the Association's representatives — project manager Đina Janković and the organisation's vice-president Branislav Šebek — presented the project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change”. The Directorate was represented at the meeting by its director Aleksandar Memčević, together with Maja Mijović and Jovana Bošković. The aim of the meeting was to present the concept of the project, its strategic objectives and planned activities to the competent institution, and to consider the scope for institutional cooperation in line with the Ministry's role in creating and implementing labour, employment and social dialogue policy.
The discussion was held in a constructive, collegial atmosphere, with both sides recognising the importance of improving the position of young people on the labour market.
Presentation of the project
Project manager Đina Janković presented the premises of the project, emphasising that the initiative arose in response to the observed lack of information among young people about labour rights, occupational safety and health and the institutional protection mechanisms available, on the basis of research carried out during 2022 and 2023 through the project “Decent work starts while you are young”.
The project is aimed at young people aged 15 to 29, with particular focus on vulnerable categories — the NEET population, young women, Roma, young people with disabilities, and pupils and students encountering the labour market for the first time.
Branislav Šebek further emphasised the importance of connecting educational activities with practical support mechanisms, stressing that the project aims to move “from knowledge to change” — that is, to give young people the confidence to apply the knowledge they gain in practice and to take an active part in improving working conditions.
Key components of the project
The meeting set out the project's main activities in more detail:
• Organising educational workshops and lectures in secondary schools and at faculties;
• Holding a special event aimed at young people from vulnerable groups;
• Establishing a help-line service and an online “legal corner” as a safe channel for advice and support;
• Running a media and online campaign to promote the concept of decent work;
• Organising a round table with institutions and the social partners, and drawing up recommendations for improving public policy.
It was emphasised that, alongside its educational dimension, the project also has an advocacy component involving stronger dialogue between young people, institutions and the social partners.
The Ministry's role and discussion
The discussion emphasised the Ministry's role as a key actor in labour and employment. It was recognised that the project's activities can contribute to:
• improving young people's knowledge of their rights arising from an employment relationship,
• strengthening a preventive approach to safety at work,
• better institutional links and information sharing,
• developing policy that answers young people's real needs.
The scope for representatives of the Ministry to take part in the planned advocacy events was considered, as was the exchange of information and experience during the project. It was particularly emphasised that aggregated, anonymised data on the problems young people face can be a useful input for the further development of the Ministry's measures and programmes.
The importance of cross-sectoral cooperation was also stressed, including links with the Employment Agency, the inspection authorities and the social partners, in order to strengthen a systematic approach to protecting the rights of young workers.
Conclusions and next steps
The meeting noted:
• that the project's themes correspond to strategic priorities in the field of youth employment and labour;
• that there is scope for institutional cooperation in line with the Ministry's remit;
• that it is important to continue the conversation in order to define concrete models of support.
The next steps proposed were to send a summary of the project to the Ministry, to define a contact point for day-to-day communication, and to consider the participation of Ministry representatives in the planned round table.
The meeting confirmed a shared commitment to improving the position of young people on the labour market and to strengthening a culture of decent, safe and lawful work in Montenegro. The project “Youth voices for decent work – from knowledge to change” was recognised as an initiative that can strengthen young people's participation and improve the quality of social dialogue between institutions and the civil sector.

title: Sastanak radne grupe za izradu Nacrta Pravilnika o izmjenama i dopunama Pravilnika o mjerama zaštite na radu od rizika izloženosti azbestu
excerpt: Radna grupa za izradu Nacrta pravilnika o zaštiti od izloženosti azbestu sastala se 2. februara 2026. u Ministarstvu rada, uz učešće Đine Janković kao članice ispred UZNR CG.
content:
Dana 2. februara 2026. godine u prostorijama Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga održan je sastanak radne grupe formirane radi izrade Nacrta Pravilnika o izmjenama i dopunama Pravilnika o mjerama zaštite na radu od rizika izloženosti azbestu. Sastanku je, pored predstavnika Ministarstva, prisustvovala Đina Janković, predstavnica Udruženja u radnoj grupi.
Cilj sastanka bio je usklađivanje predloženih izmjena i dopuna postojećeg Pravilnika sa zahtjevima Direktive 2009/148/EC o zaštiti radnika od rizika izloženosti azbestu na radu u njenom aktuelnom kontekstu i najnovijim izmjenama EU okvira.
Postojeći nacionalni Pravilnik o mjerama zaštite na radu od rizika izloženosti azbestu, usvojen kroz „Službeni list Crne Gore“ br. 14/17, zahtijeva dopune radi efektivnije zaštite zaposlenih i usklađivanja sa direktivnim EU standardima.
Posebno je naglašeno da je EU Direktiva 2009/148/EC, kojom je propisano zaštitno pravilo i sistem obaveza poslodavaca radi sprečavanja izloženosti azbestnim vlaknima na radnom mjestu, temeljen minimum standarda zaštite koji države članice i pridružene zemlje moraju implementirati.
Također, usvajanje Direktive (EU) 2023/2668, koja sadrži dopune Direktive 2009/148/EC, dodatno naglašava potrebu ažuriranja nacionalnih propisa kako bi se obezbijedila efikasnija zaštita zdravlja radnika i usklađenost sa najnovijim EU pristupima.
Ključne teme razmatrane na sastanku
a) Usklađivanje sa EU direktivom i proširenje zaštite
Radna grupa je analizirala tekst EU Direktive 2009/148/EC o zaštiti zaposlenih od rizika izloženosti azbestu na radu, uključujući nedavno donesene izmjene kroz Direktivu 2023/2668. Članovi su saglasni da nacionalni Pravilnik mora obuhvatiti sve relevantne obaveze poslodavaca, uključujući procjenu rizika, obaveznu evidenciju, mjere prevencije, zdravstevni nadzor radnika i obaveze obavještavanja nadležnih tijela.
b) Prihvatljivost i mjerljive granice izloženosti
Razmatrano je usklađivanje definisanih graničnih vrijednosti izloženosti azbestnim vlaknima u radnoj sredini sa evropskim standardima. Na EU nivou Direktiva propisuje obaveze i mjere za utvrđivanje mjerenja izloženosti te redovne procjene rizika na radnim mjestima gdje postoji mogućnost izlaganja azbestu.
c) Obaveze poslodavaca i radna procedura
• Posebna pažnja posvećena je obavezama poslodavaca, uključujući:
• obaveznu procjenu i identifikaciju rizika,
• izradu planova za kontrolu i smanjenje izloženosti,
• obaveze obavještavanja zaposlenih o rizicima i zaštitnim mjerama,
• praćenje zdravstvenog stanja radnika izloženih azbestu,
• vođenje evidencije i redovno izvještavanje nadležnih institucija.
d) Tranzicija EU zahtjeva u nacionalno zakonodavstvo
Radna grupa je diskutovala i o dinamici zakonske implementacije, s fokusom na rokove i tehničke zahtjeve transponovanja novih obaveza iz EU direktiva u nacionalno zakonodavstvo, uključujući eventualne prelazne periode.
Sastanak radne grupe je profesionalno i fokusirano usmjerio rad na izradu kvalitetnog Nacrta Pravilnika sa jasnim ciljem da se nacionalni propis o zaštiti radnika od rizika izloženosti azbestu uskladi sa zahtjevima EU direktiva i zaštitnim standardima. Radna grupa će nastaviti aktivnosti prema definisanim koracima, uz plan da finalni prijedlog bude praktičan, efikasan i pravno utemeljen.
title_en: Meeting of the working group drafting the Rulebook amending the Rulebook on occupational safety measures against the risk of exposure to asbestos
excerpt_en: The working group drafting the rulebook on protection from exposure to asbestos met on 2 February 2026 at the Ministry of Labour, with Đina Janković taking part as UZNR CG's member.
content_en:
On 2 February 2026, at the premises of the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, a meeting was held of the working group formed to draft the Rulebook amending the Rulebook on occupational safety measures against the risk of exposure to asbestos. Alongside representatives of the Ministry, the meeting was attended by Đina Janković, the Association's representative on the working group.
The aim of the meeting was to align the proposed amendments to the existing Rulebook with the requirements of Directive 2009/148/EC on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work, in its current form and in the light of the most recent changes to the EU framework.
The existing national Rulebook on occupational safety measures against the risk of exposure to asbestos, adopted through the “Official Gazette of Montenegro” no. 14/17, needs additions in order to protect employees more effectively and to align with EU directive standards.
It was particularly emphasised that EU Directive 2009/148/EC, which lays down the protective rules and the system of employers' obligations for preventing exposure to asbestos fibres at the workplace, is a baseline minimum standard of protection which member states and associated countries must implement.
The adoption of Directive (EU) 2023/2668, which amends Directive 2009/148/EC, further underlines the need to update national regulations so as to protect workers' health more effectively and to keep in step with the latest EU approaches.
Key topics considered at the meeting
a) Alignment with the EU directive and extending protection
The working group analysed the text of EU Directive 2009/148/EC on the protection of employees from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work, including the recent amendments made by Directive 2023/2668. Members agreed that the national Rulebook must cover all the relevant obligations of employers, including risk assessment, compulsory record-keeping, preventive measures, health surveillance of workers and the obligation to notify the competent bodies.
b) Acceptability and measurable exposure limits
The group considered aligning the defined exposure limit values for asbestos fibres in the working environment with European standards. At EU level the Directive lays down obligations and measures for determining exposure measurement and for regular risk assessments at workplaces where exposure to asbestos is possible.
c) Employers' obligations and working procedures
• Particular attention was paid to employers' obligations, including:
• compulsory assessment and identification of risks,
• drawing up plans to control and reduce exposure,
• the obligation to inform employees about the risks and protective measures,
• monitoring the health of workers exposed to asbestos,
• keeping records and reporting regularly to the competent institutions.
d) Transposing EU requirements into national legislation
The working group also discussed the timetable for legislative implementation, focusing on the deadlines and technical requirements for transposing the new obligations from the EU directives into national legislation, including any transitional periods.
The working group's meeting directed its work in a professional and focused way towards producing a good-quality draft Rulebook, with the clear aim of aligning the national regulations on protecting workers from the risk of exposure to asbestos with the requirements of the EU directives and their protective standards. The working group will continue its work along the steps defined, with the aim that the final proposal should be practical, effective and legally sound.

title: Realizovana obuka: „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu vaspitanja i obrazovanja“
excerpt: U restoranu Radovče je 25. decembra 2025. održana obuka o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu za instruktore praktične nastave učenika Srednje stručne škole "Sergije Stanić" koji se školuju za konobare i kuvare.
content:
Dana 25.12.2025. godine, u restoranu Radovče, realizovana je obuka na temu „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu vaspitanja i obrazovanja“, namijenjena instruktorima praktične nastave kod kojih se realizuje stručna praksa učenika Srednja stručna škola „Sergije Stanić“. Učenici ove škole se obrazuju za zanimanja konobar i kuvar, a stručna praksa se odvija u realnom radnom okruženju ugostiteljskih objekata.
Obuku je realizovala Đina Janković, autorka i realizatorka akreditovanog programa stručnog usavršavanja iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Obuka je bila usmjerena na jačanje kompetencija instruktora praktične nastave u oblasti bezbjednosti i zdravlja učenika tokom obavljanja stručne prakse u ugostiteljstvu, koje spada u djelatnosti sa povećanim rizicima.
Potreba za realizacijom ove obuke proistekla je iz specifičnosti ugostiteljske struke, naročito kada je riječ o radu u kuhinjama i uslužnim prostorima restorana, gdje su učenici izloženi različitim opasnostima i štetnostima. Instruktori praktične nastave imaju ključnu ulogu u organizaciji rada učenika, nadzoru nad njihovim aktivnostima i primjeni mjera zaštite i zdravlja na radu, zbog čega je kontinuirano stručno usavršavanje u ovoj oblasti od posebnog značaja.
Tokom obuke, učesnici su se upoznali sa osnovnim pojmovima i važećim normativno-pravnim okvirom zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kao i sa obavezama poslodavaca, škola i instruktora praktične nastave u procesu obrazovanja učenika. Poseban akcenat stavljen je na organizaciju sistema zaštite i zdravlja na radu u ugostiteljskim objektima, sagledanu kroz pravni, tehničko-tehnološki i zdravstveno-socijalni aspekt, kao i kroz razvoj kulture bezbjednog rada.
Značajan dio obuke bio je posvećen procjeni rizika u ugostiteljstvu, sa fokusom na radna mjesta konobara i kuvara. Učesnici su se upoznali sa prepoznavanjem opasnosti i štetnosti, kao što su rizici od opekotina i posjekotina, klizavi podovi, rad sa toplim površinama i aparatima, upotreba oštrih alata, električni i hemijski rizici, kao i ergonomski i biološki rizici. Posebno je naglašen značaj definisanja preventivnih mjera i adekvatnog dokumentovanja procjene rizika, kao osnove za bezbjednu realizaciju stručne prakse učenika.
Tokom obuke obrađene su i teme koje se odnose na mjere zaštite na radu u ugostiteljstvu, bezbjedno korišćenje kuhinjske opreme i sredstava za rad, pravilnu upotrebu lične zaštitne opreme, kao i higijenske i sanitarne mjere koje su od ključnog značaja u pripremi i posluživanju hrane. Posebna pažnja posvećena je odgovornosti instruktora praktične nastave u nadzoru učenika, organizovanju rada u skladu sa propisima, kao i postupanju u vanrednim situacijama, uključujući pružanje prve pomoći, zaštitu od požara i evakuaciju.
Učesnici obuke istakli su da im je ova obuka omogućila jasnije razumijevanje njihove uloge u zaštiti zdravlja i bezbjednosti učenika tokom stručne prakse. Naglašeno je da instruktori, kao neposredni mentori učenika u realnom radnom okruženju, imaju ključnu odgovornost u razvijanju bezbjednih radnih navika i svijesti o značaju prevencije rizika.
Zaključeno je da obuka „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu vaspitanja i obrazovanja“, realizovana za instruktore praktične nastave u ugostiteljstvu, predstavlja važan doprinos unapređenju bezbjednosti učenika na stručnoj praksi i kvalitetu obrazovno-vaspitnog procesa. Kontinuirane obuke ove vrste prepoznate su kao neophodne za jačanje kulture bezbjednosti, smanjenje rizika od povreda na radu i profesionalnih oboljenja, te za kvalitetniju i sigurniju pripremu učenika za buduće zapošljavanje u ugostiteljskoj struci.
title_en: Training held: “Occupational safety and health in the education system”
excerpt_en: On 25 December 2025, at the Radovče restaurant, training on occupational safety and health was held for the practical training instructors of pupils from the “Sergije Stanić” Secondary Vocational School who are training as waiters and cooks.
content_en:
On 25 December 2025, at the Radovče restaurant, training on the theme “Occupational safety and health in the education system” was held for the practical training instructors who supervise the work placements of pupils from the “Sergije Stanić” Secondary Vocational School. Pupils at this school train for the occupations of waiter and cook, and their work placements take place in the real working environment of hospitality establishments.
The training was delivered by Đina Janković, author and provider of an accredited professional development programme in occupational safety and health. It aimed to strengthen the competences of practical training instructors in the safety and health of pupils during work placements in hospitality, an industry with heightened risks.
The need for this training arose from the particular features of the hospitality trade, especially work in kitchens and restaurant service areas, where pupils are exposed to a range of dangers and harmful factors. Practical training instructors play a key role in organising pupils' work, supervising their activities and applying occupational safety and health measures, which makes continuous professional development in this field particularly important.
During the training, participants learned about the basic concepts and the current legal framework of occupational safety and health, and about the obligations of employers, schools and practical training instructors in the education of pupils. Particular emphasis was placed on organising the occupational safety and health system in hospitality establishments, considered from the legal, technical and technological, and health and social points of view, and through the development of a culture of safe work.
A significant part of the training was devoted to risk assessment in hospitality, focusing on the workplaces of waiters and cooks. Participants learned to recognise dangers and harmful factors such as the risk of burns and cuts, slippery floors, work with hot surfaces and appliances, the use of sharp tools, electrical and chemical risks, and ergonomic and biological risks. Particular emphasis was placed on the importance of defining preventive measures and documenting the risk assessment properly, as the basis for pupils' work placements being carried out safely.
The training also covered occupational safety measures in hospitality, the safe use of kitchen equipment and work tools, the correct use of personal protective equipment, and the hygiene and sanitary measures that are of key importance in preparing and serving food. Particular attention was paid to the responsibility of practical training instructors in supervising pupils, organising work in line with the regulations, and acting in emergencies, including giving first aid, fire protection and evacuation.
Participants said the training had given them a clearer understanding of their role in protecting pupils' health and safety during work placements. It was emphasised that instructors, as the pupils' direct mentors in a real working environment, have a key responsibility for developing safe working habits and an awareness of the importance of preventing risk.
It was concluded that the training “Occupational safety and health in the education system”, delivered for practical training instructors in hospitality, is an important contribution to improving pupils' safety on work placements and the quality of the educational process. Continuous training of this kind is recognised as essential for strengthening a safety culture, reducing the risk of injuries at work and occupational diseases, and preparing pupils better and more safely for future employment in the hospitality trade.

title: Realizovana obuka: „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu vaspitanja i obrazovanja“
excerpt: U prostorijama Centra za stručno obrazovanje održana je 24. decembra 2025. obuka za voditelje stručne prakse za zanimanje frizer.
content:
Dana 24.12.2025. godine, u prostorijama Centra za stručno obrazovanje, realizovana je obuka na temu „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu vaspitanja i obrazovanja“, namijenjena voditeljima stručne prakse za zanimanje frizer. Obuka je bila usmjerena na unapređenje znanja i kompetencija učesnika u oblasti bezbjednosti i zaštite zdravlja učenika tokom realizacije praktične nastave i stručne prakse u frizerskim salonima.
Obuku je vodila Đina Janković, autorka i realizatorka akreditovanog programa stručnog usavršavanja, sa dugogodišnjim iskustvom u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Program obuke prilagođen je specifičnostima frizerske struke, koja podrazumijeva svakodnevni rad sa hemijskim preparatima, električnim uređajima, oštrim alatima, kao i dugotrajno stajanje i ponavljajuće pokrete, što predstavlja potencijalne rizike po zdravlje i bezbjednost učenika.
Potreba za realizacijom ove obuke proistekla je iz prakse srednjeg stručnog obrazovanja i uočenih izazova u organizaciji bezbjedne praktične nastave u frizerskim salonima. Voditelji stručne prakse imaju ključnu ulogu u obezbjeđivanju sigurnih uslova rada za učenike, kao i u prenošenju znanja i radnih navika koje su u skladu sa pravilima zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Posebno je istaknuto da se u frizerskoj djelatnosti zaštita i zdravlje na radu često posmatraju kao formalna obaveza, bez dovoljno pažnje posvećene prevenciji rizika i dugoročnom očuvanju zdravlja.
Tokom obuke, učesnici su se upoznali sa osnovnim pojmovima i važećim normativno-pravnim okvirom zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kao i sa obavezama poslodavaca, škola i voditelja stručne prakse u procesu obrazovanja učenika. Poseban akcenat stavljen je na organizaciju sistema zaštite i zdravlja na radu u frizerskim salonima, sagledanu kroz pravni, tehničko-tehnološki i zdravstveno-socijalni aspekt, kao i kroz razvoj kulture bezbjednog rada.
Značajan dio obuke bio je posvećen procjeni rizika u frizerskoj djelatnosti, sa fokusom na identifikaciju opasnosti i štetnosti, kao što su izloženost hemijskim supstancama, rizici od posjekotina i opekotina, električni rizici, klizavi podovi, neadekvatna ergonomija radnog mjesta i biološki rizici. Učesnici su upoznati sa načinima procjene nivoa rizika, definisanjem preventivnih mjera i značajem adekvatnog dokumentovanja, što predstavlja osnov za bezbjednu realizaciju praktične nastave i stručne prakse.
Tokom obuke obrađene su i teme koje se odnose na mjere zaštite na radu, bezbjedno korišćenje frizerskih alata i uređaja, pravilnu upotrebu lične zaštitne opreme, kao i higijenske i sanitarne mjere koje su od posebnog značaja u frizerskoj struci. Posebna pažnja posvećena je odgovornosti voditelja stručne prakse u organizovanju rada učenika, nadzoru nad njihovim aktivnostima i postupanju u vanrednim situacijama, uključujući pružanje prve pomoći i zaštitu od požara.
Učesnici su istakli da im je obuka omogućila jasnije razumijevanje njihove uloge u zaštiti zdravlja i bezbjednosti učenika, kao i praktične smjernice za unapređenje uslova rada u frizerskim salonima. Naglašeno je da je kontinuirano stručno usavršavanje u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu neophodno kako bi se učenicima, još tokom školovanja, razvile bezbjedne radne navike i svijest o značaju prevencije rizika.
Zaključeno je da obuka „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu vaspitanja i obrazovanja“, realizovana za voditelje stručne prakse za frizere, predstavlja važan doprinos unapređenju kvaliteta praktične nastave i bezbjednosti u frizerskoj struci. Kontinuirane obuke ove vrste prepoznate su kao ključne za jačanje kulture bezbjednosti, smanjenje rizika od povreda i profesionalnih oboljenja, te kvalitetniju pripremu učenika za bezbjedan i odgovoran rad u budućem profesionalnom okruženju.
title_en: Training held: “Occupational safety and health in the education system”
excerpt_en: On 24 December 2025, at the premises of the Centre for Vocational Education, training was held for work placement supervisors for the occupation of hairdresser.
content_en:
On 24 December 2025, at the premises of the Centre for Vocational Education, training on the theme “Occupational safety and health in the education system” was held for work placement supervisors for the occupation of hairdresser. The training aimed to improve participants' knowledge and competences in the safety and health of pupils during practical teaching and work placements in hairdressing salons.
The training was led by Đina Janković, author and provider of an accredited professional development programme, with many years of experience in occupational safety and health. The programme was adapted to the particular features of hairdressing, which involves daily work with chemical products, electrical appliances and sharp tools, as well as prolonged standing and repetitive movements — all potential risks to pupils' health and safety.
The need for this training arose from the practice of secondary vocational education and from the challenges observed in organising safe practical teaching in hairdressing salons. Work placement supervisors play a key role in ensuring safe working conditions for pupils and in passing on knowledge and working habits that comply with occupational safety and health rules. It was particularly emphasised that in hairdressing, occupational safety and health is often seen as a formality, with too little attention paid to preventing risks and preserving health in the long term.
During the training, participants learned about the basic concepts and the current legal framework of occupational safety and health, and about the obligations of employers, schools and work placement supervisors in the education of pupils. Particular emphasis was placed on organising the occupational safety and health system in hairdressing salons, considered from the legal, technical and technological, and health and social points of view, and through the development of a culture of safe work.
A significant part of the training was devoted to risk assessment in hairdressing, focusing on identifying dangers and harmful factors such as exposure to chemical substances, the risk of cuts and burns, electrical risks, slippery floors, inadequate workstation ergonomics and biological risks. Participants learned about ways of assessing the level of risk, defining preventive measures and the importance of proper documentation, which is the basis for practical teaching and work placements being carried out safely.
The training also covered occupational safety measures, the safe use of hairdressing tools and appliances, the correct use of personal protective equipment, and the hygiene and sanitary measures that are of particular importance in the hairdressing trade. Particular attention was paid to the responsibility of work placement supervisors in organising pupils' work, supervising their activities and acting in emergencies, including giving first aid and fire protection.
Participants said the training had given them a clearer understanding of their role in protecting pupils' health and safety, and practical guidance on improving working conditions in hairdressing salons. It was emphasised that continuous professional development in occupational safety and health is essential if pupils are to develop safe working habits and an awareness of the importance of preventing risk while they are still at school.
It was concluded that the training “Occupational safety and health in the education system”, delivered for work placement supervisors for hairdressers, is an important contribution to improving the quality of practical teaching and safety in the hairdressing trade. Continuous training of this kind is recognised as key to strengthening a safety culture, reducing the risk of injuries and occupational diseases, and preparing pupils better for safe and responsible work in their future professional environment.

title: Realizovana obuka: „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu vaspitanja i obrazovanja“
excerpt: Treća u nizu obuka za nastavnike srednjih stručnih škola iz sjeverne regije Crne Gore održana je 15. decembra 2025. u Centru za stručno obrazovanje, za 17 nastavnika i organizatora stručne prakse.
content:
Dana 15.12.2025. godine, u prostorijama Centra za stručno obrazovanje, realizovana je treća obuka na temu „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu vaspitanja i obrazovanja“, namijenjena nastavnicima srednjih stručnih škola iz Sjeverne regije Crne Gore. Obuci je prisustvovalo 17 nastavnika i organizatora stručne prakse, koji su neposredno uključeni u realizaciju praktične nastave i saradnju sa poslodavcima.
Obuku je vodila Đina Janković, autorka i realizatorka akreditovanog programa stručnog usavršavanja, sa dugogodišnjim iskustvom u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Ova obuka predstavlja nastavak kontinuiranih aktivnosti usmjerenih na jačanje kompetencija nastavnika u oblasti bezbjednosti i zdravlja učenika tokom procesa obrazovanja.
Potreba za realizacijom ove vrste obuka proistekla je iz dugogodišnje prakse u srednjem stručnom obrazovanju i uočenih izazova u primjeni propisa i mjera zaštite i zdravlja na radu, naročito u kontekstu praktične nastave i stručne prakse kod poslodavaca. Nastavnici i organizatori stručne prakse često se suočavaju sa kompleksnim zahtjevima u pogledu procjene rizika, organizacije bezbjednog radnog okruženja i usklađivanja školskih aktivnosti sa zakonskim obavezama, što dodatno naglašava značaj sistematskog i kontinuiranog stručnog usavršavanja u ovoj oblasti.
Tokom obuke, učesnici su se upoznali sa osnovnim pojmovima, istorijskim razvojem i važećim normativno-pravnim okvirom zaštite i zdravlja na radu u Crnoj Gori. Posebna pažnja posvećena je organizaciji sistema zaštite i zdravlja na radu, sagledanoj kroz pravni, tehničko-tehnološki, zdravstveno-socijalni aspekt i aspekt kulture rada, čime je učesnicima omogućen cjelovit pristup razumijevanju ove kompleksne oblasti.
Značajan segment obuke odnosio se na procjenu rizika na radnom mjestu, sa fokusom na identifikaciju opasnosti i štetnosti u školskim radionicama, laboratorijama, sportskim salama, kao i u realnom radnom okruženju kod poslodavaca gdje se realizuje stručna praksa. Učesnici su upoznati sa načinima procjene nivoa rizika, definisanjem preventivnih mjera i značajem adekvatnog dokumentovanja, kao osnovom za planiranje i realizaciju bezbjedne praktične nastave.
Takođe, obrađene su teme koje se odnose na mjere zaštite na radu, bezbjedno korišćenje sredstava za rad, pravilnu upotrebu lične zaštitne opreme, kao i odgovornosti nastavnika i škole u sprovođenju mjera zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Poseban akcenat stavljen je na postupke u vanrednim situacijama, uključujući organizaciju prve pomoći, zaštitu od požara i evakuaciju.
Učesnici obuke su istakli da je kontinuirano stručno usavršavanje u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu od suštinskog značaja za kvalitetno izvođenje praktične nastave i stručne prakse. Naglašeno je da nastavnici imaju ključnu ulogu u razvoju kulture bezbjednosti kod učenika, koji se obrazuju za zanimanja sa povećanim rizicima, te da samo adekvatno osposobljeni nastavnici mogu odgovorno i kompetentno pripremiti učenike za bezbjedan rad u realnom radnom okruženju.
Zaključeno je da realizacija ove, kao i prethodnih obuka, predstavlja važan doprinos unapređenju kvaliteta srednjeg stručnog obrazovanja i jačanju sistemskog pristupa zaštiti i zdravlju na radu. Kontinuirane obuke ove vrste prepoznate su kao neophodne za održavanje i unapređenje nivoa bezbjednosti u obrazovnom procesu, smanjenje rizika od povreda i profesionalnih oboljenja, kao i za kvalitetniju pripremu učenika za tržište rada.
title_en: Training held: “Occupational safety and health in the education system”
excerpt_en: The third in a series of training sessions for teachers from secondary vocational schools in the northern region of Montenegro was held on 15 December 2025 at the Centre for Vocational Education, for 17 teachers and work placement organisers.
content_en:
On 15 December 2025, at the premises of the Centre for Vocational Education, the third training session on the theme “Occupational safety and health in the education system” was held for teachers from secondary vocational schools in the northern region of Montenegro. It was attended by 17 teachers and work placement organisers who are directly involved in delivering practical teaching and in working with employers.
The training was led by Đina Janković, author and provider of an accredited professional development programme, with many years of experience in occupational safety and health. This session continues a run of activities aimed at strengthening teachers' competences in the safety and health of pupils during their education.
The need for training of this kind arose from many years of practice in secondary vocational education and from the challenges observed in applying occupational safety and health regulations and measures, particularly in the context of practical teaching and work placements with employers. Teachers and work placement organisers often face complex requirements as regards risk assessment, organising a safe working environment and reconciling school activities with legal obligations, which further underlines the importance of systematic, continuous professional development in this field.
During the training, participants learned about the basic concepts, the historical development and the current legal framework of occupational safety and health in Montenegro. Particular attention was paid to the organisation of the occupational safety and health system, considered from the legal, technical and technological, and health and social points of view and from that of working culture, giving participants a comprehensive approach to understanding this complex field.
A significant part of the training concerned workplace risk assessment, focusing on identifying dangers and harmful factors in school workshops, laboratories and sports halls, and in the real working environment at the employers where work placements take place. Participants learned about ways of assessing the level of risk, defining preventive measures and the importance of proper documentation as the basis for planning and delivering safe practical teaching.
The training also covered occupational safety measures, the safe use of work equipment, the correct use of personal protective equipment, and the responsibilities of teachers and schools in implementing occupational safety and health measures. Particular emphasis was placed on procedures in emergencies, including the organisation of first aid, fire protection and evacuation.
Participants emphasised that continuous professional development in occupational safety and health is essential to delivering practical teaching and work placements well. It was stressed that teachers play a key role in developing a safety culture among pupils training for higher-risk occupations, and that only adequately trained teachers can responsibly and competently prepare pupils for safe work in a real working environment.
It was concluded that this session, like those before it, is an important contribution to improving the quality of secondary vocational education and strengthening a systematic approach to occupational safety and health. Continuous training of this kind is recognised as essential for maintaining and improving the level of safety in education, reducing the risk of injuries and occupational diseases, and preparing pupils better for the labour market.

title: Održana obuka: „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu vaspitanja i obrazovanja“
excerpt: U Centru za stručno obrazovanje održana je 12. decembra 2025. obuka za 13 nastavnika srednjih stručnih škola iz Nikšića, Cetinja, Ulcinja i Kotora.
content:
Dana 12.12.2025. godine, u Centru za stručno obrazovanje realizovana je obuka namijenjena nastavnicima srednjih stručnih škola na temu „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu vaspitanja i obrazovanja“. Predavanje je održala Đina Janković, autorka programa i stručna realizatorka akreditovane obuke. Obuci je prisustvovalo 13 nastavnika iz srednjih stručnih škola iz Nikšića, Cetinja, Ulcinja i Kotora, među kojima su bili nastavnici stručnih i stručno-teorijskih predmeta, kao i nastavnici zaduženi za organizaciju i realizaciju stručne prakse.
Obuka je realizovana kao odgovor na prepoznatu potrebu za jačanjem kompetencija nastavnika u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, koja predstavlja jednu od ključnih, ali često zapostavljenih komponenti stručnog obrazovanja. U praksi se pokazuje da značajan broj nastavnika, naročito onih koji su neposredno uključeni u organizaciju praktične nastave i stručne prakse kod poslodavaca, nema dovoljno sistematizovanih znanja iz ove oblasti. Iako su određeni elementi zaštite i zdravlja na radu ranije bili zastupljeni kroz pojedine stručne predmete, vremenom su ti sadržaji potisnuti ili svedeni na formalne napomene, bez dubljeg razumijevanja njihove primjene u realnim radnim uslovima.
Tokom uvodnog dijela obuke ukazano je na značaj zaštite i zdravlja na radu u kontekstu obrazovanja učenika za različita zanimanja, od kojih su mnoga povezana sa povećanim rizicima po bezbjednost i zdravlje. Nastavnici su istakli da se u svakodnevnom radu suočavaju sa izazovima u tumačenju zakonskih obaveza, procjeni rizika u školskim radionicama i laboratorijama, kao i u komunikaciji sa poslodavcima kod kojih se realizuje stručna praksa. Upravo iz tog razloga, obuka je prepoznata kao neophodan vid podrške nastavnicima u odgovornom obavljanju njihovih profesionalnih uloga.
Kroz jasno strukturiran sadržaj, učesnici su se upoznali sa osnovnim pojmovima i razvojem zaštite i zdravlja na radu, važećim zakonodavnim okvirom, kao i načinima organizovanja sistema zaštite i zdravlja na radu u radnoj sredini. Posebna pažnja posvećena je sagledavanju ove oblasti kroz više aspekata – pravnog, tehničko-tehnološkog, zdravstveno-socijalnog i aspekta kulture rada – čime je nastavnicima omogućeno da razumiju zaštitu i zdravlje na radu kao integralni dio profesionalnog i obrazovnog procesa, a ne samo kao zakonsku obavezu.
Značajan dio obuke bio je posvećen procjeni rizika na radnom mjestu, sa fokusom na prepoznavanje opasnosti i štetnosti u školskom okruženju, ali i u realnim radnim uslovima kod poslodavaca. Učesnici su imali priliku da se upoznaju sa načinima procjene nivoa rizika, definisanjem preventivnih mjera i značajem pravilnog dokumentovanja, što je posebno važno za planiranje i izvođenje bezbjedne praktične nastave. Takođe, obrađene su teme koje se odnose na bezbjedno korišćenje sredstava za rad, pravilnu upotrebu lične zaštitne opreme i stvaranje bezbjednih uslova rada za učenike.
U okviru obuke poseban akcenat stavljen je na ulogu nastavnika kao ključnih nosilaca znanja i kulture bezbjednosti. Učesnici su saglasni da nastavnici ne mogu kvalitetno i odgovorno prenijeti znanja učenicima ukoliko sami nijesu adekvatno osposobljeni u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Naglašeno je da učenici, koji se obrazuju za različita stručna i često rizična zanimanja, moraju još tokom školovanja steći navike bezbjednog rada, razumijevanje potencijalnih rizika i svijest o značaju preventivnog djelovanja.
Zaključeno je da obuka „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu vaspitanja i obrazovanja“ predstavlja važan korak ka jačanju kompetencija nastavnika srednjih stručnih škola i unapređenju bezbjednosti u procesu obrazovanja. Stečena znanja i razmijenjena iskustva doprinijeće kvalitetnijoj organizaciji praktične nastave i stručne prakse, kao i odgovornijem odnosu prema zaštiti zdravlja i bezbjednosti učenika u školama i kod poslodavaca.
title_en: Training held: “Occupational safety and health in the education system”
excerpt_en: On 12 December 2025 the Centre for Vocational Education hosted training for 13 teachers from secondary vocational schools in Nikšić, Cetinje, Ulcinj and Kotor.
content_en:
On 12 December 2025, at the Centre for Vocational Education, training for teachers from secondary vocational schools was held on the theme “Occupational safety and health in the education system”. The session was delivered by Đina Janković, author of the programme and provider of the accredited training. It was attended by 13 teachers from secondary vocational schools in Nikšić, Cetinje, Ulcinj and Kotor, among them teachers of vocational and vocational-theoretical subjects and teachers responsible for organising and delivering work placements.
The training was held in response to a recognised need to strengthen teachers' competences in occupational safety and health, one of the key but often neglected components of vocational education. Practice shows that a significant number of teachers, particularly those directly involved in organising practical teaching and work placements with employers, lack systematic knowledge in this field. Although certain elements of occupational safety and health used to feature in some vocational subjects, over time that content has been pushed aside or reduced to formal notes, without any deeper understanding of how it applies in real working conditions.
The opening part of the training pointed to the importance of occupational safety and health in the context of educating pupils for a range of occupations, many of them associated with heightened risks to safety and health. Teachers said that in their everyday work they face challenges in interpreting legal obligations, in assessing risks in school workshops and laboratories, and in communicating with the employers who host work placements. For precisely that reason, the training was recognised as essential support for teachers in carrying out their professional roles responsibly.
Through clearly structured content, participants learned about the basic concepts and development of occupational safety and health, the current legislative framework, and ways of organising an occupational safety and health system in a working environment. Particular attention was paid to viewing the field from several angles — legal, technical and technological, health and social, and that of working culture — enabling teachers to understand occupational safety and health as an integral part of the professional and educational process, and not merely as a legal obligation.
A significant part of the training was devoted to workplace risk assessment, focusing on recognising dangers and harmful factors in the school environment and in real working conditions at employers. Participants had the opportunity to learn about ways of assessing the level of risk, defining preventive measures and the importance of proper documentation, which matters particularly for planning and delivering safe practical teaching. The training also covered the safe use of work equipment, the correct use of personal protective equipment and the creation of safe working conditions for pupils.
Particular emphasis was placed on teachers' role as key bearers of knowledge and of a safety culture. Participants agreed that teachers cannot pass knowledge on to pupils well and responsibly unless they are themselves adequately trained in occupational safety and health. It was emphasised that pupils training for a range of vocational and often risky occupations must acquire safe working habits, an understanding of the potential risks and an awareness of the importance of prevention while they are still at school.
It was concluded that the training “Occupational safety and health in the education system” is an important step towards strengthening the competences of secondary vocational school teachers and improving safety in education. The knowledge gained and the experience exchanged will contribute to better organisation of practical teaching and work placements and to a more responsible attitude towards protecting the health and safety of pupils in schools and with employers.

title: Realizovana obuka: „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu vaspitanja i obrazovanja“

Tokom obuke obrađene su i teme koje se odnose na mjere zaštite na radu, bezbjedno korišćenje sredstava za rad, kao i pravilnu upotrebu sredstava i opreme lične zaštite u nastavnim radionicama i tokom praktične nastave. Posebna pažnja posvećena je odgovornosti nastavnika i škole u organizovanju i sprovođenju mjera zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kao i postupcima organizovanja prve pomoći, zaštite od požara i evakuacije u slučaju vanrednih situacija.
Učesnici su tokom obuke izrazili jasan stav da je posjedovanje znanja iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu neophodan preduslov za kvalitetno izvođenje praktične nastave i stručne prakse. Istaknuto je da nastavnici ne mogu adekvatno pripremiti učenike za bezbjedan rad u realnom radnom okruženju ukoliko sami nemaju dovoljno znanja i sigurnosti u tumačenju propisa, prepoznavanju rizika i primjeni preventivnih mjera. Obuka je prepoznata kao važan korak ka ponovnom sistemskom uvođenju kulture bezbjednosti u srednje stručno obrazovanje.
Zaključeno je da ovakvi programi stručnog usavršavanja imaju poseban značaj za unapređenje kvaliteta obrazovno-vaspitnog procesa, ali i za smanjenje rizika od povreda na radu, profesionalnih bolesti i drugih neželjenih posljedica tokom školovanja i kasnijeg zapošljavanja učenika. Stečena znanja omogućavaju nastavnicima da odgovorno i kompetentno prenesu učenicima svijest o značaju zaštite i zdravlja na radu, čime se direktno doprinosi bezbjednijem obrazovnom okruženju i kvalitetnijoj pripremi učenika za tržište rada.
title_en: Training held: “Occupational safety and health in the education system”
excerpt_en: On 8 December 2025 the Centre for Vocational Education hosted training for 19 teachers from secondary vocational schools in Podgorica, Golubovci, Tuzi and Kolašin.
content_en:
At the Centre for Vocational Education, on 8 December 2025, training for teachers from secondary vocational schools was held under the title “Occupational safety and health in the education system”. The session was delivered by Đina Janković of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, author and provider of an accredited professional development programme for teachers. It was attended by 19 teachers from secondary vocational schools in Podgorica, Golubovci, Tuzi and Kolašin, among them teachers of vocational subjects, teachers of practical instruction and work placement organisers.
The need for this training arose from many years of practice and from the challenges observed in the secondary vocational education system, particularly as regards occupational safety and health. Teachers in secondary vocational schools, and especially those with the responsible role of organising and monitoring practical teaching and work placements with employers, often lack systematic, formal knowledge in this field. Although in earlier education systems elements of occupational safety and health were an integral part of vocational subjects and curricula, over time this knowledge has become fragmented or has been left out of teachers' regular education altogether.
During the discussions, participants emphasised that occupational safety and health today is largely reduced to formally satisfying a legal obligation, without any deeper understanding of the substance of the risks, the preventive measures and the responsibilities that teachers and schools have towards pupils. This is particularly pronounced in education for occupations that involve a heightened level of risk, such as mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, construction, transport, agriculture, health care and other vocational fields in which practical teaching takes place in workshops, laboratories or the real working environment of an employer.
Through training that was well structured in content and clearly led in method, participants had the opportunity to learn about the history and basic principles of occupational safety and health and about the current legal framework in Montenegro. Particular emphasis was placed on the organisation of an employer's occupational safety and health system, considered from the legal, technical and technological, and health and social points of view and from that of working culture, giving teachers a comprehensive insight into this complex field.
One of the key parts of the training concerned workplace risk assessment, with particular reference to identifying dangers and harmful factors in classrooms, school workshops, laboratories and sports halls, and in the working environment at the employers where work placements take place. Teachers learned about ways of assessing the level of risk, defining measures to reduce it and the importance of documenting the risk assessment properly, which is the basis for planning safe practical teaching.
The training also covered occupational safety measures, the safe use of work equipment and the correct use of personal protective equipment in teaching workshops and during practical instruction. Particular attention was paid to the responsibility of teachers and schools in organising and implementing occupational safety and health measures, and to the procedures for organising first aid, fire protection and evacuation in emergencies.
During the training participants expressed the clear view that knowledge of occupational safety and health is an essential precondition for delivering practical teaching and work placements well. It was emphasised that teachers cannot adequately prepare pupils for safe work in a real working environment if they themselves lack the knowledge and the confidence to interpret the regulations, recognise risks and apply preventive measures. The training was recognised as an important step towards systematically reintroducing a safety culture into secondary vocational education.
It was concluded that professional development programmes of this kind are particularly significant for improving the quality of the educational process, but also for reducing the risk of injuries at work, occupational diseases and other unwanted consequences during pupils' schooling and later employment. The knowledge gained allows teachers to pass on to pupils, responsibly and competently, an awareness of the importance of occupational safety and health, which directly contributes to a safer educational environment and better preparation of pupils for the labour market.
