title: Realizovana radionica na temu zaštite i zdravlja na radu u sistemu obrazovanja i vaspitanja
excerpt: Na poziv JU Centra za stručno obrazovanje, UZNR CG je učestvovalo u nizu radionica za poslodavce i instruktore prakse o zaštiti na radu u obrazovnom sistemu, počev od 26. novembra 2025. u hotelu Splendid u Budvi.
content:
Na poziv JU Centra za stručno obrazovanje, a u skladu sa strateškim opredjeljenjima Reformske agende Crne Gore za period 2024–2027, Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore učestvovalo je u realizaciji radionica namijenjenih predstavnicima poslodavaca i instruktorima praktične nastave, sa fokusom na zaštitu i zdravlje na radu u sistemu obrazovanja i vaspitanja.
Radionice su organizovane kao odgovor na potrebe nastavnika praktične nastave i instruktora praktičnog obrazovanja, identifikovane kroz proces eksterne evaluacije, koje ukazuju na potrebu dodatnog jačanja znanja i kompetencija u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, posebno u dijelu koji se odnosi na bezbjednost učenika tokom izvođenja praktične nastave u redovnom i dualnom modelu obrazovanja.
Jedna od radionica održana je 26. novembra 2025. godine u hotelu Splendid u Budvi, dok su ostale radionice realizovane tokom decembra 2025. godine u prostorijama JU Centar za stručno obrazovanje i u restoranu „Radovče“ u Podgorici. U ime Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, radionice je realizovala Đina Janković, autorka programa „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u sistemu obrazovanja i vaspitanja“.
Tokom radionica obrađene su ključne teme iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, sa posebnim osvrtom na bezbjednost i zdravlje učenika tokom realizacije praktične nastave. Učesnici su upoznati sa osnovama i normativnim okvirom zaštite i zdravlja na radu, organizacijom sistema zaštite kod poslodavaca, kao i tehničko-tehnološkim, pravnim i zdravstveno-socijalnim aspektima bezbjednosti. Posebna pažnja posvećena je prepoznavanju rizika na radnom mjestu, primjeni lične zaštitne opreme, kao i mjerama zaštite i procedurama koje je neophodno sprovoditi u cilju prevencije povreda i profesionalnih oboljenja.
U realizovanim radionicama učestvovali su predstavnici poslodavaca i instruktori praktičnog obrazovanja iz oblasti turizma, ugostiteljstva i usluga. Učesnici su izrazili visok stepen zadovoljstva sadržajem i načinom realizacije radionica, ističući njihovu praktičnu usmjerenost i primjenjivost u svakodnevnom radu sa učenicima. Prema njihovim navodima, stečena znanja će značajno doprinijeti unapređenju bezbjednosti i kvaliteta praktične nastave.
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore cijeni saradnju sa JU Centrom za stručno obrazovanje i smatra da ovakve aktivnosti predstavljaju važan doprinos jačanju kulture bezbjednosti i unapređenju sistema zaštite i zdravlja na radu u oblasti stručnog obrazovanja, u najboljem interesu učenika i njihovog sigurnog profesionalnog razvoja.
title_en: Workshop held on occupational safety and health in the education system
excerpt_en: At the invitation of the Centre for Vocational Education, UZNR CG took part in a series of workshops for employers and practical training instructors on safety at work in the education system, beginning on 26 November 2025 at the Hotel Splendid in Budva.
content_en:
At the invitation of the Centre for Vocational Education, and in line with the strategic commitments of Montenegro's Reform Agenda for 2024–2027, the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro took part in workshops for employers' representatives and practical training instructors, focusing on occupational safety and health in the education system.
The workshops were organised in response to the needs of practical teaching staff and practical training instructors, identified through the external evaluation process, which point to a need to further strengthen knowledge and competences in occupational safety and health, particularly as regards the safety of pupils during practical teaching in both the regular and the dual model of education.
One of the workshops was held on 26 November 2025 at the Hotel Splendid in Budva, while the others took place during December 2025 at the premises of the Centre for Vocational Education and at the “Radovče” restaurant in Podgorica. On behalf of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, the workshops were delivered by Đina Janković, author of the programme “Occupational safety and health in the education system”.
The workshops covered key topics in occupational safety and health, with particular reference to the safety and health of pupils during practical teaching. Participants learned about the fundamentals and the legal framework of occupational safety and health, the organisation of an employer's protection system, and the technical and technological, legal and health and social aspects of safety. Particular attention was paid to recognising risks at the workplace, the use of personal protective equipment, and the protective measures and procedures that must be applied in order to prevent injuries and occupational diseases.
The workshops were attended by employers' representatives and practical training instructors from tourism, hospitality and services. Participants expressed a high degree of satisfaction with the content and delivery of the workshops, praising their practical orientation and applicability in everyday work with pupils. In their view, the knowledge gained will significantly improve the safety and quality of practical teaching.
The Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro values its cooperation with the Centre for Vocational Education and considers activities of this kind an important contribution to strengthening a safety culture and improving the occupational safety and health system in vocational education, in the best interests of pupils and their safe professional development.

title: Realizovana obuka u MERS-u: “Sistem zaštite i zdravlja na radu u MERS-u”Ministarstvo ekologije, održivog razvoja i razvoja sjevera
excerpt: U Ministarstvu ekologije, održivog razvoja i razvoja sjevera (MERS) održana je obuka o sistemu zaštite i zdravlja na radu za 17 zaposlenih ministarstva.
content:
Realizacija obuke
Obuka je održana u prostorijama Ministarstva ekologije, održivog razvoja i razvoja sjevera, kao dio planske podrške jačanju institucionalnih kapaciteta u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu (ZZNR) i pripreme za primjenu novih zakonskih rješenja.
Obuku je sprovelo Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore. Predavači su bili generalna sekretarka UZNR CG i projektna menadžerka Đina Janković i glavni inspektor ZZNR Zlatko Popović. Prisustvovalo je 17 zaposlenih Ministarstva.
Sadržaj obuke
Obuka je obuhvatila multidisciplinarne elemente ZZNR, razvoj i transformaciju ovog koncepta u industriji i javnoj upravi, zakonski okvir i podzakonske akte, kao i najaktuelnije izazove u modernim uslovima rada – od psihosocijalnih rizika i digitalizacije, do klimatskih promjena i novih organizacionih modela rada.
Pored teorijskog pristupa, učesnici su upoznati sa praksom inspekcijskog nadzora u Crnoj Gori, radom u Jedinstvenom informacionom inspekcijskom sistemu (JIIS), vrstama nadzora, statistikom nadzora i upravnim mjerama, kao i pravilnim korišćenjem javno dostupnih podataka prije izlaska u nadzo
Sistem ZZNR u javnom sektoru – stanje, problem i zašto je ovo strateški trenutak
U javnoj upravi i ministarstvima sistem ZZNR u ovom trenutku je nedovoljno razvijen. Mjere se u većini slučajeva ne sprovode u obimu koji je propisan zakonom, a zaposleni su u najvećem procentu neosposobljeni za bezbjedan rad – iako su i administrativni poslovi prepoznati kao izvor ozbiljnih rizika (posebno psihosocijalnih i ergonomskih).
Do sada je postojala široko rasprostranjena percepcija da je ZZNR „industrijski koncept“, a ne obaveza javnih organa. Međutim, novi Zakon, koji je u proceduri, sada eksplicitno definiše da su i ministarstva poslodavci u punom pravnom smislu, sa svim obavezama koje iz toga proizilaze.
Ovo predstavlja sistemsku prekretnicu, jer ZZNR prestaje da bude „preporuka“ u upravi i postaje obavezujući standard sa punim inspekcijskim nadzorom.
Međunarodni okvir
ILO, EU OSHA i evropske prakse decenijama naglašavaju da najveći zdravstveni problemi, povrede na radu i smrtni ishodi nisu više u klasično teškoj industriji nego u hibridnim, modernim i administrativnim tipovima rada (ergonomija, stres, dugi radni sati, kognitivna opterećenja). Upravo zato EU standard ZZNR danas dominantno stavlja akcenat na mentalne, organizacione i psihosocijalne rizike. Crna Gora mora uskladiti sa tim trendom i standardima.
Ova obuka predstavlja prvi korak ka tome na institucionalnom nivou MERS-a.
Efekti obuke
• povećano razumijevanje da ZZNR nije „tehnika“ nego sistem menadžmenta rizika
• osvještavanje obaveza ministarstava kao poslodavaca
• priprema zaposlenih za primjenu novog zakona
• stvaranje uslova za uspostavljanje konzistentnog internog sistema ZZNR u ministarstvu
Preporuke
• uspostavljanje kontinuiranog programa obuka iz ZZNR za sve zaposlene
• izrada procjene rizika za sve kategorije radnih mjesta u Ministarstvu
• razvoj internih procedura, registara i kontrole primjene
• uključivanje ZZNR standarda, naročito psihosocijalnih rizika i ergonomije, u kulturu upravljanja
Obuka je realizovana uspješno, kvalitetno, profesionalno i u punom obimu. Ostvarila je efekat koji je u ovom momentu ključan – razumijevanje da ZZNR u javnoj upravi nije opcija nego obaveza. Ministarstvo je time učinilo važan korak u pripremi za sistemsku, zakonsku i praktičnu primjenu standarda.
title_en: Training held at MERS: “The occupational safety and health system at MERS”. Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development and Development of the North
excerpt_en: The Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development and Development of the North (MERS) hosted training on the occupational safety and health system for 17 of the ministry's staff.
content_en:
Delivery of the training
The training was held at the premises of the Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development and Development of the North, as part of planned support for strengthening institutional capacity in occupational safety and health (OSH) and preparing for the application of new legislation.
The training was delivered by the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro. The trainers were UZNR CG's secretary general and project manager Đina Janković and the chief OSH inspector Zlatko Popović. Seventeen of the Ministry's staff attended.
Content of the training
The training covered the multidisciplinary elements of OSH, the development and transformation of the concept in industry and in public administration, the legal framework and secondary legislation, and the most pressing challenges of modern working conditions — from psychosocial risks and digitalisation to climate change and new models of work organisation.
Alongside the theory, participants learned about inspection practice in Montenegro, work in the Single Information Inspection System (JIIS), the types of inspection, inspection statistics and administrative measures, and the correct use of publicly available data before an inspection visit.
The OSH system in the public sector — the situation, the problem and why this is a strategic moment
In public administration and in ministries the OSH system is at present insufficiently developed. In most cases the measures are not applied to the extent the law requires, and the great majority of employees are untrained in safe work — even though administrative work too is recognised as a source of serious risk (particularly psychosocial and ergonomic risk).
Until now there has been a widespread perception that OSH is an “industrial concept” rather than an obligation of public bodies. The new Law, however, now in procedure, explicitly defines ministries as employers in the full legal sense, with all the obligations that follow.
This is a systemic turning point, because OSH ceases to be a “recommendation” in public administration and becomes a binding standard subject to full inspection supervision.
The international framework
The ILO, EU-OSHA and European practice have emphasised for decades that the greatest health problems, injuries at work and fatalities are no longer found in classic heavy industry but in hybrid, modern and administrative types of work (ergonomics, stress, long hours, cognitive load). That is precisely why the EU OSH standard today places its emphasis predominantly on mental, organisational and psychosocial risks. Montenegro must align itself with that trend and those standards.
This training is the first step towards doing so at the institutional level of MERS.
Effects of the training
• a greater understanding that OSH is not a “technical matter” but a risk management system
• awareness of ministries' obligations as employers
• preparation of staff for the application of the new law
• the conditions created for establishing a consistent internal OSH system in the ministry
Recommendations
• establishing a continuous OSH training programme for all staff
• producing a risk assessment for all categories of workplace in the Ministry
• developing internal procedures, registers and compliance monitoring
• building OSH standards, particularly psychosocial risks and ergonomics, into the management culture
The training was delivered successfully, professionally, to a high standard and in full. It achieved the effect that matters most at this moment — an understanding that OSH in public administration is not an option but an obligation. The Ministry has thereby taken an important step in preparing for the systematic, legal and practical application of the standards.

title: Trilateralna konferencija „EMPOWERED - Inkluzija osoba s invaliditetom, regionalna saradnja i razvoj na Zapadnom Balkanu“
excerpt: U Sarajevu je 23. oktobra 2025. održana trilateralna konferencija "EMPOWERED - Inkluzija osoba s invaliditetom, regionalna saradnja i razvoj na Zapadnom Balkanu", u organizaciji ASB South East Europe i LIR Civilnog društva iz BiH.
content:
Dana 23. oktobra 2025. godine, u Sarajevu je održana Trilateralna konferencija „EMPOWERED – Inkluzija osoba s invaliditetom, regionalna saradnja i razvoj na Zapadnom Balkanu“, u organizaciji ASB South East Europe i LIR Civilnog društva iz Bosne i Hercegovine, uz partnersko učešće organizacija iz regiona, među kojima je i ALFA Centar iz Crne Gore
Konferencija je okupila predstavnike ministarstava, lokalnih vlasti, organizacija civilnog društva, privatnog sektora i međunarodnih partnera iz Bosne i Hercegovine, Crne Gore, Srbije i drugih zemalja Zapadnog Balkana, sa ciljem jačanja regionalne saradnje i razmjene znanja u oblasti inkluzije osoba s invaliditetom.
Ciljevi i značaj konferencije
Trilateralna konferencija EMPOWERED bila je usmjerena na otvaranje dijaloga o ključnim politikama zapošljavanja, socijalne inkluzije i lokalnim rješenjima koja omogućavaju osobama s invaliditetom puno učešće u društvenom i ekonomskom životu. Poseban akcenat stavljen je na povezivanje institucionalnih aktera i civilnog sektora, kao i na razmjenu primjera dobre prakse u regionu Zapadnog Balkana.
Struktura programa i panel diskusije
Tokom jednodnevnog programa realizovana su tri tematska panela, kako je predviđeno zvaničnom agendom konferencije.
Prvi panel bio je posvećen regionalnoj saradnji, inovacijama i zagovaranju za sistemske promjene, sa fokusom na participativno kreiranje politika, institucionalne reforme i usklađivanje zakonodavstva sa međunarodnim standardima, uključujući Konvenciju Ujedinjenih nacija o pravima osoba s invaliditetom. U ovom panelu učestvovala je i Ivana Đođić, sekretarka Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga Crne Gore, koja je govorila o ulozi državnih institucija u razvoju inkluzivnih politika i važnosti regionalne saradnje u oblasti zapošljavanja i socijalne zaštite.
Drugi panel bio je posvećen politikama zapošljavanja i podrške zapošljavanju osoba s invaliditetom, sa posebnim osvrtom na obrazovanje, prevazilaženje barijera i ulogu privatnog sektora. Na ovom panelu učestvovala je Đina Janković, predstavnica Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, koja je ukazala na značaj dostojanstvenog i bezbjednog rada, potrebu prilagođavanja radnih mjesta i važnost sistemske podrške osobama s invaliditetom u procesu zapošljavanja. Njeno izlaganje naglasilo je vezu između zaštite na radu, inkluzije i dugoročne održivosti tržišta rada.
Treći panel bio je fokusiran na ulogu lokalnih vlasti u kreiranju pristupačnih i osnažujućih zajednica, kroz planiranje, budžetiranje i partnerstva sa organizacijama civilnog društva. Predstavljeni su primjeri dobre prakse iz različitih lokalnih sredina u regionu, sa ciljem jačanja lokalnih politika inkluzije.
Doprinos organizacija iz Crne Gore
Učešće organizacija i institucija iz Crne Gore, uključujući Ministarstvo rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga i Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore, dalo je značajan doprinos regionalnoj dimenziji konferencije. Njihovo prisustvo potvrdilo je opredijeljenost Crne Gore ka jačanju inkluzivnih politika i regionalnoj saradnji u oblasti zapošljavanja i prava osoba s invaliditetom.
Konferencija EMPOWERED potvrdila je da su inkluzija osoba s invaliditetom, regionalna saradnja i međusektorsko partnerstvo ključni preduslovi za održiv društveni i ekonomski razvoj Zapadnog Balkana. Kroz otvorenu razmjenu iskustava i dijalog između institucija, civilnog društva i privatnog sektora, postavljeni su temelji za dalja zajednička djelovanja i unapređenje politika koje doprinose stvaranju inkluzivnijih i pravednijih zajednica.
Trilateralna konferencija u Sarajevu predstavljala je važan korak ka jačanju regionalne mreže aktera posvećenih inkluziji, potvrđujući da su znanje, saradnja i zajednička odgovornost ključni alati za postizanje stvarnih i dugoročnih promjena.
title_en: Trilateral conference “EMPOWERED – Inclusion of people with disabilities, regional cooperation and development in the Western Balkans”
excerpt_en: On 23 October 2025 Sarajevo hosted the trilateral conference “EMPOWERED – Inclusion of people with disabilities, regional cooperation and development in the Western Balkans”, organised by ASB South East Europe and LIR Civil Society of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
content_en:
On 23 October 2025 the trilateral conference “EMPOWERED – Inclusion of people with disabilities, regional cooperation and development in the Western Balkans” was held in Sarajevo, organised by ASB South East Europe and LIR Civil Society of Bosnia and Herzegovina, with partner organisations from across the region taking part, among them the ALFA Centre from Montenegro.
The conference brought together representatives of ministries, local authorities, civil society organisations, the private sector and international partners from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Serbia and other Western Balkan countries, with the aim of strengthening regional cooperation and the exchange of knowledge on the inclusion of people with disabilities.
Aims and significance of the conference
The EMPOWERED trilateral conference set out to open a dialogue on key employment and social inclusion policies and on local solutions that enable people with disabilities to take a full part in social and economic life. Particular emphasis was placed on connecting institutional actors with the civil sector and on exchanging examples of good practice in the Western Balkans.
Programme structure and panel discussions
The one-day programme comprised three thematic panels, as set out in the conference's official agenda.
The first panel was devoted to regional cooperation, innovation and advocacy for systemic change, focusing on participatory policymaking, institutional reform and the alignment of legislation with international standards, including the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. This panel included Ivana Đođić, secretary of Montenegro's Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, who spoke about the role of state institutions in developing inclusive policy and the importance of regional cooperation in employment and social protection.
The second panel was devoted to employment policy and support for the employment of people with disabilities, with particular reference to education, overcoming barriers and the role of the private sector. It included Đina Janković, representing the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, who pointed to the importance of decent and safe work, the need to adapt workplaces and the importance of systematic support for people with disabilities in finding employment. Her presentation emphasised the connection between safety at work, inclusion and the long-term sustainability of the labour market.
The third panel focused on the role of local authorities in creating accessible, empowering communities, through planning, budgeting and partnerships with civil society organisations. Examples of good practice from various local settings in the region were presented, with the aim of strengthening local inclusion policy.
The contribution of organisations from Montenegro
The participation of organisations and institutions from Montenegro, including the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue and the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, made a significant contribution to the regional dimension of the conference. Their presence confirmed Montenegro's commitment to strengthening inclusive policy and regional cooperation on employment and the rights of people with disabilities.
The EMPOWERED conference confirmed that the inclusion of people with disabilities, regional cooperation and cross-sectoral partnership are key preconditions for sustainable social and economic development in the Western Balkans. Through an open exchange of experience and dialogue between institutions, civil society and the private sector, foundations were laid for further joint action and for improving policies that help create more inclusive and more just communities.
The trilateral conference in Sarajevo was an important step towards strengthening a regional network of actors committed to inclusion, confirming that knowledge, cooperation and shared responsibility are the key tools for achieving real, lasting change.

title: Sastanak sa Direktoratom za ZZNR u Ministarstvu rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga
excerpt: Direktorat za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu inicirao je 7. oktobra 2025. sastanak sa UZNR CG povodom predloga dopune člana 30 Zakona, kojom se uvodi obavezno osiguranje zaposlenih i poseban evidencioni fond.
content:
Dana 7. oktobra 2025. godine održan je sastanak između predstavnika Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore (UZNR CG) i Direktorata za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga. Direktorat je inicirao održavanje ovog sastanka, a povod je bio predlog Udruženja koji je već uvršten u Nacrt Zakona o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu – dopuna člana 30, kojom se prvi put u nacionalni pravni okvir uvodi koncept obaveznog osiguranja zaposlenih od povreda na radu, profesionalnih bolesti i bolesti u vezi sa radom, uz uspostavljanje posebnog evidencionog računa/fonda u okviru Ministarstva.
Suština predloga i njegov značaj
Ova dopuna ima dvostruku svrhu:
• prvo, da precizira obavezu poslodavaca u skladu sa stvarnim rizikom radnog mjesta, i
• drugo, da obezbijedi sistemski mehanizam finansiranja preventivnih aktivnosti u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
Predlog propisuje da minimalna premija osiguranja iznosi 1% minimalne zarade, ali da se ta obaveza odnosi isključivo na radna mjesta sa posebnim uslovima rada i povećanim rizikom. Takav pristup stvara pravičniji i stimulativniji model, jer veći teret osiguranja snose poslodavci koji zapošljavaju zaposlene u rizičnijim zanimanjima. Time se nagrađuje odgovorno ponašanje poslodavaca koji ulažu u bezbjednost, a istovremeno podstiče prevencija u sektorima gdje su rizici najveći.
Na taj način, sistem prelazi sa formalnog ispunjavanja obaveza na proaktivan model upravljanja rizicima, u kojem se ekonomski podstiče ulaganje u zaštitu i zdravlje zaposlenih.
Uspostavljanje evidencionog računa/fonda – model održivog finansiranja
Drugi, jednako važan element predloga, odnosi se na uvođenje posebnog evidencionog računa u okviru Ministarstva, na koji bi osiguravajuća društva uplaćivala 10% od prihoda ostvarenih po osnovu obaveznog osiguranja.
Ovaj mehanizam je inspirisan modelom koji već postoji u Zakonu o zaštiti i spašavanju, gdje se dio sredstava iz premija usmjerava za jačanje kapaciteta sistema zaštite.
Time se po prvi put u Crnoj Gori uspostavlja trajan i predvidiv izvor finansiranja za unapređenje zaštite i zdravlja na radu, koji ne zavisi od donatorskih projekata, već se zasniva na principu solidarne odgovornosti svih aktera u sistemu.
Sredstva prikupljena na evidencionom računu koristila bi se namjenski, za finansiranje programa i projekata iz oblasti prevencije, istraživanja, edukacija i kampanja podizanja svijesti o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu.
Takav pristup donosi tri ključne koristi:
• Održivo finansiranje – sistem zaštite ne zavisi više od budžetskih priliva i projektne podrške, već ima sopstveni izvor prihoda.
• Direktna veza između osiguranja i prevencije – dio sredstava iz osiguravajućih premija vraća se u sistem, čime se jača njegova funkcionalnost i efikasnost.
• Usklađenost sa evropskim principima – predlog prati praksu država članica EU koje su uspostavile fondove za zaštitu na radu finansirane iz doprinosa poslodavaca i osiguravajućih društava.
Zajednički interes i plan djelovanja
Kako je dopuna člana 30 već uvrštena u Nacrt Zakona, fokus sastanka bio je na usaglašavanju zajedničkog djelovanja Ministarstva i Udruženja u narednim fazama procesa – posebno u dijelu obrazlaganja potrebe i funkcionalnosti ovog mehanizma pred Unijom poslodavaca i osiguravajućim društvima.
Saglasili su se da će ključ uspjeha ovog rješenja biti u načinu predstavljanja i komunikacije -ne kao fiskalnog opterećenja, već kao sistemskog ulaganja u bezbjednost, produktivnost i zdravlje radne snage.
Zato će se pristup temeljiti na edukaciji i argumentaciji – objašnjenju da svaka uložena sredstva u prevenciju dugoročno znače manje povreda, manji broj bolovanja, veću efikasnost i niže troškove osiguranja.
Dogovoreno je da UZNR CG i Ministarstvo zajednički rade na definisanju modela funkcionisanja fonda, uključujući pravni okvir, upravljanje sredstvima i kriterijume za dodjelu. U tom cilju, biće organizovan sastanak sa Agencijom za nadzor osiguranja, kako bi se razmotrili regulatorni aspekti i osiguralo da rješenje bude pravno održivo i transparentno.
Predložena dopuna člana 30 predstavlja prekretnicu u razvoju politike zaštite i zdravlja na radu u Crnoj Gori.
Ona ne samo da precizira obaveze poslodavaca u skladu sa nivoom rizika, već i uvodi novi mehanizam finansiranja sistema prevencije, čime se stvaraju uslovi za dugoročnu održivost i samostalnost sektora.
UZNR CG i Direktorat za ZZNR su saglasni da ovaj model ima potencijal da postane temelj modernog i odgovornog pristupa zaštite na radu, koji se ne oslanja samo na propise, već na ekonomske i društvene podsticaje za sigurnije radno okruženje.
Sastanak je protekao u duhu saradnje i zajedničkog razumijevanja da uspjeh ovog rješenja zavisi od koordinisanog djelovanja svih aktera – države, poslodavaca, osiguravajućih društava i stručne javnosti.
title_en: Meeting with the Directorate for Occupational Safety and Health at the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue
excerpt_en: On 7 October 2025 the Directorate for Occupational Safety and Health initiated a meeting with UZNR CG on the proposed amendment to Article 30 of the Law, introducing compulsory insurance for employees and a dedicated fund account.
content_en:
On 7 October 2025 a meeting was held between representatives of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro (UZNR CG) and the Directorate for Occupational Safety and Health at the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue. The Directorate initiated the meeting, prompted by the Association's proposal already included in the draft Law on Occupational Safety and Health — an amendment to Article 30 which for the first time introduces into the national legal framework the concept of compulsory insurance of employees against injuries at work, occupational diseases and work-related illnesses, together with the establishment of a dedicated record account or fund within the Ministry.
The substance of the proposal and its significance
This amendment has a twofold purpose:
• first, to define employers' obligations more precisely in line with the actual risk of the workplace, and
• second, to provide a systemic mechanism for financing preventive activities in occupational safety and health.
The proposal sets a minimum insurance premium of 1% of the minimum wage, but applies that obligation solely to workplaces with special working conditions and heightened risk. Such an approach creates a fairer and more motivating model, because a greater insurance burden falls on employers whose staff work in riskier occupations. This rewards responsible employers who invest in safety, while at the same time encouraging prevention in the sectors where the risks are greatest.
In this way the system moves from the formal fulfilment of obligations to a proactive model of risk management, in which investment in employees' safety and health is encouraged economically.
Establishing a record account or fund — a model of sustainable financing
The second, equally important element of the proposal is the introduction of a dedicated record account within the Ministry, into which insurance companies would pay 10% of the income earned from compulsory insurance.
This mechanism is inspired by a model that already exists in the Law on Protection and Rescue, where part of the funds from premiums is directed towards strengthening the capacity of the protection system.
For the first time in Montenegro this would establish a lasting, predictable source of funding for improving occupational safety and health, one that does not depend on donor projects but rests on the principle of shared responsibility among all the actors in the system.
The funds collected in the record account would be used for a defined purpose: to finance programmes and projects in prevention, research, education and awareness-raising campaigns on occupational safety and health.
Such an approach brings three key benefits:
• Sustainable financing – the protection system no longer depends on budget allocations and project support but has its own source of income.
• A direct link between insurance and prevention – part of the money from insurance premiums returns to the system, strengthening its functioning and effectiveness.
• Alignment with European principles – the proposal follows the practice of EU member states that have established occupational safety funds financed from employers' and insurers' contributions.
Common interest and a plan of action
Since the amendment to Article 30 is already included in the draft Law, the meeting focused on agreeing joint action by the Ministry and the Association in the next stages of the process — particularly in explaining the need for this mechanism and how it would work to the Employers' Union and the insurance companies.
They agreed that the key to the success of this solution will lie in how it is presented and communicated — not as a fiscal burden, but as a systemic investment in the safety, productivity and health of the workforce.
The approach will therefore be built on education and argument — on explaining that every euro invested in prevention means, in the long run, fewer injuries, less sick leave, greater efficiency and lower insurance costs.
It was agreed that UZNR CG and the Ministry will work together to define how the fund would function, including the legal framework, the management of resources and the criteria for awarding them. To that end a meeting will be organised with the Insurance Supervision Agency, in order to consider the regulatory aspects and ensure that the solution is legally sustainable and transparent.
The proposed amendment to Article 30 is a turning point in the development of occupational safety and health policy in Montenegro.
It not only defines employers' obligations more precisely according to the level of risk, but also introduces a new mechanism for financing the prevention system, creating the conditions for the sector's long-term sustainability and independence.
UZNR CG and the Directorate for OSH agree that this model has the potential to become the foundation of a modern, responsible approach to occupational safety, one that relies not on regulations alone but on economic and social incentives for a safer working environment.
The meeting was held in a spirit of cooperation and shared understanding that the success of this solution depends on coordinated action by all the actors — the state, employers, insurance companies and the professional community.

title: Formiranje i rad Radne grupe za izradu jedinstvene metodologije za bezbjedan rad
excerpt: Predsjednik UZNR CG dr Zdenko Janković formirao je 17. septembra 2025. Radnu grupu za izradu jedinstvene metodologije za bezbjedan rad; njen prvi sastanak održan je 25. septembra u prostorijama Udruženja.
content:
1. Donošenje odluke i formiranje radne grupe
Na osnovu člana 8 Statuta Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, predsjednik UZNR CG dr sci. Zdenko Janković donio je dana 17. septembra 2025. godine Odluku o formiranju radne grupe za izradu jedinstvene metodologije za bezbjedan rad.
U radnu grupu imenovani su predstavnici relevantnih preduzeća i institucija iz različitih sektora privrede i ovlašćenih organizacija, sa ciljem da svojim stručnim iskustvom doprinesu kreiranju primjenljive i sveobuhvatne metodologije osposobljavanja zaposlenih.
Koordinatori radne grupe su:
dr sci. Zdenko Janković, predsjednik UZNR CG
mr sci. Boško Radulović, potpredsjednik UZNR CG
2. Održavanje sastanka radne grupe
Prvi sastanak radne grupe održan je 25. septembra 2025. godine u prostorijama UZNR CG. Sastanku su prisustvovali:
• Boško Radulović – ICM
• Sanja Dujović – KAP
• Milovan Gojković – DD-ing
• Bojana Kalezić – RTCG
• Marko Đuričić – Mehanizacija i programati
• Milica Filipović – 13. jul Plantaže
• Tamara Grgurović – Mtel
• Andrijana Kaljević – EPCG
• Radoman Bakić – KCCG
• Jelena Kasalica – Port of Adria
• Zdenko janković – UZNR CG
• Đina Janković – UZNR CG
Na sastanku je predstavljen okvirni koncept metodologije za osposobljavanje zaposlenih po stepenu rizika, izrađen u okviru aktivnosti na unapređenju sprovođenja Akta o procjeni rizika.
Cilj sastanka bio je da se definišu osnovne tematske cjeline koje će činiti sadržaj budućih programa obuka, te da se članovi radne grupe saglase o daljem procesu izrade dokumenta.
3. Dogovorene teme koje treba da budu akcenat obuka
Članovi radne grupe su se saglasili da akcenat budućih obuka zaposlenih mora biti na praktičnim i primjenjivim znanjima koja direktno utiču na unapređenje zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Posebno su izdvojene sljedeće tematske oblasti:
• poznavanje zakonskih obaveza i prava iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu,
• prepoznavanje rizika na radnom mjestu i mjere zaštite,
• postupanje u vanrednim situacijama (požari, evakuacija, prva pomoć),
• kultura bezbjednog rada, komunikacija i timski pristup,
• stres i psiho-socijalni rizici,
• odnos zaposlenih prema ličnoj zaštitnoj opremi i procedurama bezbjednog rada,
• uloga i odgovornost poslodavca i nadležnih organa nadzora.
Zaključeno je da buduća metodologija mora biti prilagođena stepenu rizika na radnom mjestu, uz mogućnost kombinovanja teorijskog i praktičnog dijela obuke, u skladu sa iskustvima iz prakse.
4. Dalji koraci i rokovi
Shodno dogovoru sa sastanka, svim članovima radne grupe dostavljen je dokument „Predložena metodologija za osposobljavanje zaposlenih po stepenu rizika“, sa pozivom da dostave svoje komentare, sugestije i prijedloge najkasnije do 07. oktobra 2025. godine.
Na osnovu pristiglih sugestija biće izrađena konačna verzija metodologije, koja će biti predmet razmatranja i usvajanja na narednom sastanku radne grupe.
Cilj je da se kroz participativni pristup dođe do modela osposobljavanja koji će biti praktičan, primjenljiv i održiv u realnim radnim uslovima.
Formiranjem radne grupe i pokretanjem procesa izrade jedinstvene metodologije, UZNR CG potvrđuje svoju vodeću ulogu u unapređenju sistema zaštite i zdravlja na radu u Crnoj Gori.
Očekuje se da će nova metodologija predstavljati značajan doprinos efikasnijem sprovođenju Akta o procjeni rizika i kvalitetnijem osposobljavanju zaposlenih u svim sektorima privrede.
title_en: Formation and work of the Working Group drafting a single methodology for safe work
excerpt_en: On 17 September 2025 the president of UZNR CG, Dr Zdenko Janković, formed a Working Group to draft a single methodology for safe work; its first meeting was held on 25 September at the Association's premises.
content_en:
1. The decision and the formation of the working group
On the basis of Article 8 of the Statute of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, the president of UZNR CG, Dr Zdenko Janković, adopted on 17 September 2025 a Decision forming a working group to draft a single methodology for safe work.
Representatives of relevant companies and institutions from various sectors of the economy and from licensed organisations were appointed to the working group, so that their professional experience can contribute to creating a workable, comprehensive methodology for training employees.
The working group's coordinators are:
Dr Zdenko Janković, president of UZNR CG
Boško Radulović, MSc, vice-president of UZNR CG
2. The working group's meeting
The working group's first meeting was held on 25 September 2025 at the premises of UZNR CG. It was attended by:
• Boško Radulović – ICM
• Sanja Dujović – KAP
• Milovan Gojković – DD-ing
• Bojana Kalezić – RTCG
• Marko Đuričić – Mehanizacija i programati
• Milica Filipović – 13. jul Plantaže
• Tamara Grgurović – Mtel
• Andrijana Kaljević – EPCG
• Radoman Bakić – KCCG
• Jelena Kasalica – Port of Adria
• Zdenko Janković – UZNR CG
• Đina Janković – UZNR CG
The meeting was presented with an outline concept for a methodology for training employees according to their level of risk, produced as part of work on improving the implementation of the risk assessment act.
The aim of the meeting was to define the basic thematic units that will make up the content of future training programmes, and for the working group's members to agree on the further process of drafting the document.
3. The topics agreed as the focus of the training
The working group's members agreed that future employee training must focus on practical, applicable knowledge that directly improves occupational safety and health. The following thematic areas were singled out:
• knowledge of legal obligations and rights in occupational safety and health,
• recognising risks at the workplace and the protective measures,
• acting in emergencies (fires, evacuation, first aid),
• a culture of safe work, communication and teamwork,
• stress and psychosocial risks,
• employees' attitude to personal protective equipment and safe working procedures,
• the role and responsibility of the employer and the supervisory authorities.
It was concluded that the future methodology must be tailored to the level of risk of the workplace, with the option of combining theoretical and practical training in the light of experience from practice.
4. Next steps and deadlines
As agreed at the meeting, all members of the working group were sent the document “Proposed methodology for training employees according to level of risk”, with an invitation to submit their comments, suggestions and proposals by 7 October 2025 at the latest.
On the basis of the suggestions received a final version of the methodology will be produced, to be considered and adopted at the working group's next meeting.
The aim is to arrive, through a participatory approach, at a training model that is practical, applicable and sustainable in real working conditions.
By forming the working group and beginning work on a single methodology, UZNR CG confirms its leading role in improving the occupational safety and health system in Montenegro.
The new methodology is expected to make a significant contribution to more effective implementation of the risk assessment act and to better training of employees across all sectors of the economy.

title: Sastanak u Ministarstvu prosvjete, nauke i inovacija
excerpt: Predstavnici UZNR CG (Zdenko Janković, Branislav Šebek i Đina Janković) predali su državnom sekretaru Draganu Markoviću nalaze inicijative "Ispitivanje elektro i gromobranskih instalacija u crnogorskim školama".
content:
Dana 04. septembra 2025. godine, održan je sastanak u Ministartvu prosvjete, nauke i inovacija, a sastanku su prisustvovali: Zdenko Janković, Branislav Šebek i Đina Janković – ispred UZNR CG, kao i Dragan Marković – državni sekretar Ministarstva prosvjete, nauke i inovacija.
Sastanak je održan s ciljem predaje stručnih nalaza koje su članovi Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore izradili u okviru inicijative „Ispitivanje elektro i gromobranskih instalacija u crnogorskim školama“.
Ova inicijativa je pokrenuta kao odgovor na tragične događaje u regionu i rastuću zabrinutost zbog bezbjednosnih uslova u javnim ustanovama, posebno u obrazovnim institucijama u kojima borave djeca.
Kontekst i pokretanje inicijative
Podsticaj za ovu aktivnost proistekao je iz tragičnog događaja koji se desio 16. marta 2025. godine u Sjevernoj Makedoniji, kada je u požaru u noćnom klubu život izgubilo 62 mlade osobe.
Ovaj slučaj je dramatično ukazao na posljedice nepoštovanja osnovnih bezbjednosnih standarda – nepostojanje evakuacionih planova, neispravne instalacije i izostanak redovnih kontrola.
Vođeno time, Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore je, kao strukovna organizacija sa licenciranim članovima u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, pokrenulo preventivnu akciju besplatnih ispitivanja elektro i gromobranskih instalacija u osnovnim školama širom Crne Gore.
Ministarstvo prosvjete, nauke i inovacija je prepoznalo važnost inicijative i pružilo punu institucionalnu podršku, dostavljajući listu škola koje su uključene u prvi ciklus provjera.
Realizacija aktivnosti i učesnici
Ispitivanja su sproveli stručni timovi iz ovlašćenih organizacija članica UZNR CG:
• DDIng, Berane
• Institut za crnu metalurgiju, Nikšić
• Montecontrol, Podgorica
• Montinspekt, Podgorica
• Tehno Control, Podgorica
U prvom ciklusu obuhvaćeno je osam osnovnih škola u sjevernom i centralnom dijelu Crne Gore:
• OŠ „Radomir Mitrović“ – Berane
• OŠ „Ratko Žarić“ – Nikšić
• OŠ „Džafer Nikočević“ – Gusinje
• OŠ „Braća Labudović“ – Nikšić
• OŠ „Bratstvo i jedinstvo“ – Rožaje
• OŠ „25. maj“ – Rožaje
• OŠ „Pavle Žižić“ – Bijelo Polje
• OŠ „Boško Buha“ – Pljevlja
• OŠ „Luka Simonović“, Nikšić
• OŠ „Janko Mićunović“, Nikšić
U drugom ciklusu, ispitivanja su obavljena u:
• Gimnazija „Tanasije Pejatović“, Pljevlja
Stručni nalazi su obuhvatili stanje elektro i gromobranskih sistema, uz procjenu nivoa rizika i preporuke za otklanjanje uočenih nepravilnosti.
Ključni nalazi i zaključci ispitivanja
Iako je u pojedinim školama stanje instalacija ocijenjeno kao zadovoljavajuće, u značajnom broju objekata utvrđeni su ozbiljni propusti koji mogu ugroziti bezbjednost učenika i zaposlenih:
• neispravne i oštećene utičnice bez uzemljenja,
• improvizovani električni spojevi,
• nefunkcionalna rasvjeta i zastarjele instalacije,
• potpuni izostanak gromobranske zaštite u pojedinim objektima.
Ovi nalazi potvrđuju da je neophodno uspostaviti sistematski pristup održavanju i nadzoru tehničke ispravnosti školskih objekata, sa jasno definisanim odgovornostima i redovnim kontrolama od strane ovlašćenih organizacija.
Planirane mjere Ministarstva
Državni sekretar Dragan Marković zahvalio se članovima Udruženja na uloženom trudu i istakao da su dobijeni nalazi od velikog značaja za Ministarstvo, jer pružaju realnu sliku o stanju školskih objekata.
Najavljeno je da će Ministarstvo uložiti dodatna sredstva u sanaciju i unapređenje bezbjednosnih uslova u školama gdje je stanje ocijenjeno kao nezadovoljavajuće.
Sastanak je ocijenjen kao konstruktivan i produktivan, uz obostrano opredjeljenje da se saradnja između Ministarstva i Udruženja nastavi kroz:
• izradu plana prioritetne sanacije objekata,
• uključivanje tema bezbjednosti u školske programe i menadžment planove,
• sprovođenje kontinuiranih obuka zaposlenih.
Uručenje sertifikata i prethodne aktivnosti
Tokom sastanka je izvršena i svečana dodjela sertifikata o uspješno završenom osposobljavanju zaposlenih u obrazovnim ustanovama iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu i zaštite od požara.
Ova obuka je realizovana 16. aprila 2025. godine u Gimnaziji „Miloje Dobrašinović“ u Bijelom Polju, u saradnji sa Ministarstvom prosvjete, nauke i inovacija.
Prisustvovalo je 137 učesnika iz 50 obrazovnih i predškolskih ustanova sjevernog regiona Crne Gore, što predstavlja najobimniji program obuke u ovoj oblasti do sada.
Predavači – Branislav Šebek i Zdenko Janković – kroz teorijski i praktični rad obradili su teme zaštite od požara, bezbjedne evakuacije, prve pomoći i zakonskih obaveza škola, uz poseban akcenat na razvijanje kulture prevencije i odgovornog ponašanja u radnom okruženju.
Inicijativa UZNR CG za ispitivanje elektro i gromobranskih instalacija u školama i prethodno sprovedene obuke predstavljaju sveobuhvatan i sistemski pristup jačanju bezbjednosti u obrazovnom sektoru.
Ova saradnja sa Ministarstvom prosvjete, nauke i inovacija pokazuje da se institucionalna odgovornost i stručna inicijativa mogu povezati u zajedničkom cilju – stvaranju sigurnijeg i zdravijeg okruženja za učenike i nastavnike.
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore će i u narednom periodu nastaviti sa preventivnim aktivnostima, besplatnim ispitivanjima i edukacijom zaposlenih, u namjeri da bezbjednost u školama postane standard, a ne reakcija na incidente.
„Prevencija je najsnažniji oblik zaštite – ulaganje u sigurnost djece i zaposlenih znači ulaganje u budućnost Crne Gore.“ – zaključio je dr sci. Zdenko Janković.
title_en: Meeting at the Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation
excerpt_en: Representatives of UZNR CG (Zdenko Janković, Branislav Šebek and Đina Janković) handed over to State Secretary Dragan Marković the findings of the initiative “Testing of electrical and lightning protection installations in Montenegrin schools”.
content_en:
On 4 September 2025 a meeting was held at the Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation, attended by Zdenko Janković, Branislav Šebek and Đina Janković for UZNR CG, and by Dragan Marković, state secretary at the Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation.
The meeting was held in order to hand over the expert findings that members of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro produced under the initiative “Testing of electrical and lightning protection installations in Montenegrin schools”.
The initiative was launched in response to tragic events in the region and to growing concern about safety conditions in public institutions, particularly in educational institutions where children spend their days.
Context and the launch of the initiative
The impetus for this work came from the tragedy of 16 March 2025 in North Macedonia, when 62 young people lost their lives in a nightclub fire.
That case showed in the starkest terms what follows when basic safety standards are ignored — no evacuation plans, faulty installations and no regular inspections.
With that in mind, the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, as a professional organisation whose members are licensed in occupational safety and health, launched a preventive campaign of free testing of electrical and lightning protection installations in primary schools across Montenegro.
The Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation recognised the importance of the initiative and gave it full institutional support, supplying the list of schools included in the first cycle of checks.
Delivery and participants
The testing was carried out by expert teams from licensed organisations that are members of UZNR CG:
• DDIng, Berane
• Institute of Ferrous Metallurgy, Nikšić
• Montecontrol, Podgorica
• Montinspekt, Podgorica
• Tehno Control, Podgorica
The first cycle covered eight primary schools in the northern and central parts of Montenegro:
• “Radomir Mitrović” Primary School – Berane
• “Ratko Žarić” Primary School – Nikšić
• “Džafer Nikočević” Primary School – Gusinje
• “Braća Labudović” Primary School – Nikšić
• “Bratstvo i jedinstvo” Primary School – Rožaje
• “25. maj” Primary School – Rožaje
• “Pavle Žižić” Primary School – Bijelo Polje
• “Boško Buha” Primary School – Pljevlja
• “Luka Simonović” Primary School, Nikšić
• “Janko Mićunović” Primary School, Nikšić
In the second cycle, testing was carried out at:
• “Tanasije Pejatović” Grammar School, Pljevlja
The expert findings covered the condition of the electrical and lightning protection systems, together with an assessment of the level of risk and recommendations for correcting the faults found.
Key findings and conclusions
Although at some schools the condition of the installations was assessed as satisfactory, in a significant number of buildings serious failings were found that could endanger the safety of pupils and staff:
• faulty and damaged sockets without earthing,
• improvised electrical connections,
• non-functioning lighting and outdated installations,
• a complete absence of lightning protection in some buildings.
These findings confirm the need for a systematic approach to maintaining and monitoring the technical condition of school buildings, with clearly defined responsibilities and regular inspections by licensed organisations.
Measures planned by the Ministry
State Secretary Dragan Marković thanked the Association's members for their work and said the findings were of great importance to the Ministry, because they give a real picture of the condition of school buildings.
The Ministry announced that it will invest additional funds in repairing and improving safety conditions at the schools where the condition was assessed as unsatisfactory.
The meeting was assessed as constructive and productive, with a shared commitment to continuing cooperation between the Ministry and the Association through:
• drawing up a plan for the priority repair of buildings,
• including safety topics in school programmes and management plans,
• delivering continuous training for staff.
Presentation of certificates and earlier activities
During the meeting certificates were also formally presented for the successful completion of training for staff of educational institutions in occupational safety and health and fire protection.
That training was delivered on 16 April 2025 at the “Miloje Dobrašinović” Grammar School in Bijelo Polje, in cooperation with the Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation.
It was attended by 137 participants from 50 educational and pre-school institutions in the northern region of Montenegro, making it the largest training programme in this field to date.
The trainers — Branislav Šebek and Zdenko Janković — covered fire protection, safe evacuation, first aid and schools' legal obligations through both theory and practical work, with particular emphasis on developing a culture of prevention and responsible behaviour in the working environment.
UZNR CG's initiative to test electrical and lightning protection installations in schools, together with the training delivered earlier, represents a comprehensive, systematic approach to strengthening safety in the education sector.
This cooperation with the Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation shows that institutional responsibility and professional initiative can be brought together in a shared goal — creating a safer, healthier environment for pupils and teachers.
In the period ahead the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro will continue its preventive work, free testing and staff training, with the aim that safety in schools should become a standard rather than a reaction to incidents.
“Prevention is the strongest form of protection — investing in the safety of children and staff means investing in Montenegro's future,” Dr Zdenko Janković concluded.

title: Izvještaj sa Međunarodne konferencije: Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u poljoprivredi – izazovi i perspektive za Crnu Goru 25. – 27. mart 2025.
excerpt: U Podgorici je od 25. do 27. marta 2025. održana međunarodna konferencija o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu u poljoprivredi, u okviru projekta SAGRI, uz učešće Đine Janković kao konsultantkinje.
content:
U okviru projekta SAGRI – Zdravlje i zaštita na radu u poljoprivredi, koji se realizuje kroz program Interreg IPA CBC South Adriatic 2021–2027, u Podgorici je od 25. do 27. marta 2025. godine održana međunarodna konferencija posvećena unapređenju uslova rada u jednom od najrizičnijih, ali i najzanemarenijih sektora – poljoprivredi. Konferenciju je organizovao ICT Cortex u partnerstvu sa institucijama iz Crne Gore, Italije i Albanije, na kojem je Đina Janković bila angažovana kao konsultankinja.
Tokom tri dana, konferencija je okupila više od 30 učesnika – predstavnike institucija, inspekcija, poljoprivrednih preduzeća, akademske zajednice, kao i međunarodne i lokalne stručnjake iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Poseban značaj dala je prisutnost predstavnika ključnih ministarstava: Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga, Ministarstva poljoprivrede, šumarstva i vodoprivrede, Ministarstva evropskih poslova, Ministarstva finansija, kao i Uprave za bezbjednost hrane, veterinu i fitosanitarne poslove, Inspekcije zaštite i zdravlja na radu i Udruženja za zaštitu na radu Crne Gore.
Konferencija je otvorena panelom posvećenim zakonodavnom okviru i institucionalnoj podršci zaštiti na radu u poljoprivredi. Jovana Bošković, predstavnica Direktorata za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu, upoznala je učesnike sa trenutnim stanjem zakonske regulative i planiranim izmjenama. Naglašeno je da je postojeći pravni okvir nedovoljno prilagođen potrebama poljoprivrede kao specifične grane, te da je zastarelost podzakonskog akta koji reguliše ovu oblast, a datira iz 1968. godine, jedan od ključnih problema.
Zlatko Popović, glavni inspektor ZZNR, govorio je o ograničenim kapacitetima inspekcijskog nadzora – u Crnoj Gori ima svega 10 inspektora, nijedan od njih specijalizovan za poljoprivredu. Inspekcije su, prema njegovim riječima, usmjerene uglavnom na prijave ozbiljnih i fatalnih povreda, dok se svakodnevni rizici na terenu – posebno u malim, porodičnim gazdinstvima – često ignorišu.
Ivan Ivanović, iz Uprave za bezbjednost hrane, istakao je izazove usklađivanja zdravstvenih i bezbjednosnih standarda u lancu proizvodnje hrane. Sa aspekta zaštite radnika, posebno je istaknut značaj kontrole upotrebe pesticida i bioloških agenasa.
Stručnjakinja za ZZNR iz kompanije Plantaže 13. jul, Milica Filipović, podijelila je iskustva iz prakse, ukazujući na potrebu da se zaštita na radu ne posmatra samo kao zakonska obaveza, već kao dio strategije održivog poslovanja.
Gosti iz Italije i Albanije su prezentovali studije slučaja i primjere dobre prakse u sektoru poljoprivrede u tim zemljama.
Dr Miljan Joksimović, sa Biotehničkog fakulteta, govorio je o ekonomskim aspektima primjene mjera zaštite na radu. On je istakao da investiranje u preventivne mjere donosi dugoročne benefite – smanjenje povreda, povećanje produktivnosti i smanjenje troškova osiguranja.
Drugi dan konferencije bio je posvećen dubljoj analizi evropskih standarda, pristupa i regulatornih okvira kada je riječ o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu u poljoprivredi. Panel pod nazivom „Evropski pristupi zaštiti i zdravlju na radu u poljoprivredi“ otvorio je prostor za razmjenu znanja i institucionalnih praksi, uz učešće eksperata iz Evropske unije i predstavnika crnogorskih institucija koje se bave javnim zdravljem, fitosanitarnih i veterinarskih kontrola, kao i harmonizacijom zakonodavstva u procesu evropskih integracija.
Michele Dinelli, predstavnik Evropske agencije za bezbjednost i zdravlje na radu (EU-OSHA), govorio je o ulozi agencije u prikupljanju podataka, davanju smjernica i pružanju podrške državama članicama u razvoju preventivnih politika. Naglasio je važnost sektorskog pristupa u ZZNR, pri čemu poljoprivreda zahtijeva posebnu pažnju zbog visokog stepena izloženosti fizičkim, biološkim i hemijskim rizicima, kao i zbog učestalog angažovanja sezonskih i neformalnih radnika. Dinelli je ukazao na potrebu za aktivnijim uključivanjem poslodavaca i radnika u procese identifikacije rizika, ali i važnost uspostavljanja nacionalnih baza podataka o povredama i incidentima, kao temelja za efikasnu prevenciju.
U domaćem kontekstu, dr Aleksandra Despotović, redovna profesorica Biotehničkog fakulteta i poslanica u Skupštini Crne Gore, govorila je o izazovima koje Crna Gora ima u procesu ispunjavanja mjerila iz Poglavlja 11 (Poljoprivreda i ruralni razvoj) i Poglavlja 19 (Socijalna politika i zapošljavanje) u okviru pristupanja EU. Ona je naglasila da bez preciznog normativnog definisanja odgovornosti u sektoru poljoprivrede i bez jačanja međusektorske saradnje, Crna Gora neće moći u potpunosti ispuniti obaveze iz pregovaračkih poglavlja. Posebno je istakla problem zastarjele regulative – kao što je pravilnik iz 1968. godine – koji više ne odgovara stvarnosti savremene proizvodnje.
Verica Gomilanović, iz Uprave za bezbjednost hrane, veterinu i fitosanitarne poslove, predstavila je institucionalnu perspektivu o kontroli kvaliteta hrane, s posebnim fokusom na povezanost ZZNR sa bezbjednošću krajnjeg proizvoda. Istakla je da radnici koji rukuju pesticidima, dezinfekcionim sredstvima i stočnom hranom moraju biti obučeni i zaštićeni, jer su i sami dio lanca bezbjednosti hrane.
Sa aspekta javnog zdravlja, dr Zorica Đorđević iz Instituta za javno zdravlje Crne Gore govorila je o štetnim uticajima hemijskih i bioloških agensa u poljoprivredi na zdravlje zaposlenih – od pesticida i đubriva do zaraznih bolesti koje se mogu prenijeti sa životinja na ljude. Ona je posebno upozorila na nisku stopu dijagnostifikovanja profesionalnih oboljenja u Crnoj Gori, što dodatno prikriva stvarni rizik kojem su poljoprivredni radnici izloženi.
Učesnici panela imali su priliku da uporede različite prakse u projektnoj oblasti, te da se upoznaju sa postojećim mehanizmima podrške u EU zemljama. Istovremeno, svi govornici su ukazali na potrebu bolje međuresorske koordinacije i sinergije između sektora zdravstva, rada i poljoprivrede, što je u ovom trenutku prepoznato kao jedan od ključnih nedostataka u crnogorskom sistemu.
Učesnici konferencije su tokom drugog dijela dana posjetili kompaniju 13. Jul – Plantaže, gdje su se upoznali sa konkretnim primjerima primjene ZZNR mjera, a tom prilikm je organizovana posjeta starom podrumu, flaširnici kao i podrumu Šipčanik. Održane su demonstracije pravilne upotrebe lične zaštitne opreme, rukovanja pesticidima i rada sa mehanizacijom. Kompanija je predstavljena kao primjer dobre prakse u pogledu integracije ZZNR u sve sektore poslovanja – od vinograda do pogona za flaširanje vina.
Treći dan konferencije bio je rezervisan za okrugli sto koji je na simboličan način zaokružio tematski okvir projekta SAGRI, otvarajući diskusiju o budućnosti zaštite i zdravlja na radu (ZZNR) u poljoprivredi. Panel pod nazivom „Korišćenje tehnika i alata za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu u poljoprivredi – šta nas čeka u budućnosti?“ okupio je predstavnike različitih sektora – od državne uprave i inspekcijskih organa, preko poslovne i IT zajednice, do akademije i stručnjaka iz oblasti ZZNR. Upravo ta međusektorska raznolikost bila je ključna za sagledavanje ZZNR ne samo kao zakonske obaveze, već kao razvojne šanse za crnogorsku poljoprivredu.
Zlatko Popović, predstavnik Inspekcije zaštite i zdravlja na radu, osvrnuo se na izazove sa kojima se inspekcijski nadzor suočava u praksi: nedostatak kadrovskih kapaciteta, nepostojanje specijalizovanih inspektora za poljoprivredu, ali i gotovo nepostojeću prijavu lakših i srednje teških povreda na radu. Naglasio je važnost edukacije poslodavaca, ali i predložio intenzivnije uključivanje lokalne zajednice i samih radnika u preventivne procese.
Predstavnik Privredne komore i Poljoprivrednog klastera Crne Gore, Luka Ivanović, govorio je iz perspektive agrarnog biznisa, ističući da se bez sveobuhvatne sistemske podrške i subvencionisanja preventivnih mjera, mali proizvođači ne mogu nositi sa izazovima implementacije ZZNR standarda. On je predložio uspostavljanje posebnih grant linija za kompanije koje žele da modernizuju svoju opremu ili uvedu digitalna rešenja u oblasti bezbjednosti rada.
Jedan od najautentičnijih glasova panela bio je Ilija Moric, vlasnik poljoprivredne firme iz Luštice, koji je iz ličnog iskustva govorio o rizicima s kojima se suočavaju male porodične farme. On je podvukao važnost praktične edukacije i prilagođavanja smjernica realnim mogućnostima gazdinstava. Moric je podijelio i pozitivne primjere saradnje sa stručnjacima iz oblasti ZZNR, ali i ukazao na neophodnost pojednostavljivanja procedura za primjenu osnovnih mjera zaštite.
U stručno-metodološkom dijelu diskusije, Bojana Zindović iz Instituta „Sigurnost“, predstavila je pristup koji kombinuje analizu rizika, pravnu usklađenost i obuku radne snage. Posebno je naglasila značaj sertifikovanih obuka za rukovanje pesticidima i mehanizacijom, ali i potrebu za integrisanjem ZZNR sadržaja u srednjoškolsko i fakultetsko obrazovanje iz oblasti poljoprivrede.
Iz ugla naučne zajednice, prof. dr Nedeljko Latinović sa Biotehničkog fakulteta osvrnuo se na koncept „agroinženjeringa bez rizika“, odnosno na razvoj ergonomskih rešenja i optimizaciju radnih procedura kako bi se fizički napor i izloženost opasnostima sveli na minimum. On je podržao inicijativu da Biotehnički fakultet bude spona između nauke i prakse u oblasti ZZNR.
Značajan doprinos diskusiji došao je i iz sfere inovacija. Slađana Đurović, predstavnica kompanije „Data Design“, demonstrirala je konkretne primjere digitalnih rješenja koja mogu unaprijediti bezbjednost u poljoprivredi – od GPS sistema za nadzor mašina, preko digitalnih check-lista za procjenu rizika, do senzorskih sistema za praćenje mikroklimatskih uslova i izloženosti pesticidima. Ova izlaganja su podcrtala potencijal tehnologije da ZZNR učini efikasnijom, pristupačnijom i mjerljivom.
Zaključci okruglog stola ukazali su na potrebu da se ZZNR u poljoprivredi u Crnoj Gori sagledava ne samo kao pitanje usklađivanja sa zakonima, već i kao šansa za unapređenje kvaliteta proizvoda, zaštite života zaposlenih i dugoročne održivosti sektora. Integracija inovacija, stručna podrška i institucionalno prepoznavanje problema – prepoznati su kao tri ključna pravca u kojima se budući razvoj mora kretati.
Na kraju panela, sprovedena je praktična vježba sa učesnicima – analiza rizika u deset poljoprivrednih kompanija koje su učestvovale u projektu. Kroz kontrolne liste i zajednički rad, izrađeni su preliminarni izveštaji o mogućim nesrećama i preporučenim mjerama za prevenciju. Ova sesija omogućila je direktnu primjenu znanja i povezivanje teorijskih okvira sa konkretnim situacijama na terenu, čime je dodatno potvrđen značaj integrisanja dobre prakse i realnih potreba sektora.Bottom of Form
Zaključci i ključne preporuke
Konferencija je potvrdila da je zaštita na radu u crnogorskoj poljoprivredi oblast koja zahtijeva hitne reforme. Prepoznati problemi uključuju:
• Zastarjelu regulativu – Pravilnik o zaštiti u poljoprivredi datira iz 1968. godine;
• Nedostatak stručnih inspektora i savjetodavnih službi;
• Nepostojanje specifičnih obuka za rad u poljoprivredi;
• Neprijavljivanje povreda i slab nadzor nad porodičnim gazdinstvima.
Učesnici su usaglasili potrebu za izradom savremenog pravilnika koji bi obuhvatio sve relevantne rizike: hemijske, biološke, mehaničke, klimatske i ergonomiju rada. Predložena je izrada centralizovane baze podataka o povredama, kao i jačanje saradnje između sektora zdravlja, rada i poljoprivrede.
Projekat SAGRI je ovim događajem napravio važan korak ka sistemskom uređenju oblasti ZZNR u poljoprivredi u Crnoj Gori. Očekuje se da će zajedničke smjernice koje su u pripremi biti podržane i kroz nacionalne strategije i zakonske izmjene.
title_en: Report from the international conference: Occupational safety and health in agriculture – challenges and prospects for Montenegro, 25–27 March 2025
excerpt_en: From 25 to 27 March 2025 Podgorica hosted an international conference on occupational safety and health in agriculture, under the SAGRI project, with Đina Janković taking part as a consultant.
content_en:
Under the SAGRI project – Health and safety at work in agriculture, carried out through the Interreg IPA CBC South Adriatic 2021–2027 programme, an international conference was held in Podgorica from 25 to 27 March 2025, devoted to improving working conditions in one of the riskiest but also most neglected sectors — agriculture. The conference was organised by ICT Cortex in partnership with institutions from Montenegro, Italy and Albania, with Đina Janković engaged as a consultant.
Over three days the conference brought together more than 30 participants — representatives of institutions, inspectorates, agricultural businesses and the academic community, as well as international and local experts in occupational safety and health. Particular significance was lent by the presence of representatives of key ministries: the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management, the Ministry of European Affairs and the Ministry of Finance, as well as the Administration for Food Safety, Veterinary and Phytosanitary Affairs, the Occupational Safety and Health Inspectorate and the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro.
The conference opened with a panel devoted to the legislative framework and institutional support for safety at work in agriculture. Jovana Bošković, representing the Directorate for Occupational Safety and Health, briefed participants on the current state of the legislation and the changes planned. It was emphasised that the existing legal framework is insufficiently adapted to the needs of agriculture as a distinctive branch, and that the obsolescence of the secondary legislation governing the field — dating from 1968 — is one of the key problems.
Zlatko Popović, chief OSH inspector, spoke about the limited capacity for inspection supervision: Montenegro has just 10 inspectors, none of them specialised in agriculture. Inspections, he said, are directed mainly at reports of serious and fatal injuries, while the everyday risks in the field — particularly on small family holdings — are often ignored.
Ivan Ivanović, of the Administration for Food Safety, highlighted the challenges of aligning health and safety standards along the food production chain. From the point of view of protecting workers, he stressed in particular the importance of controlling the use of pesticides and biological agents.
Milica Filipović, an OSH specialist at the company Plantaže 13. jul, shared experience from practice, pointing to the need for safety at work to be seen not merely as a legal obligation but as part of a strategy of sustainable business.
Guests from Italy and Albania presented case studies and examples of good practice in the agricultural sector in their countries.
Dr Miljan Joksimović, of the Biotechnical Faculty, spoke about the economic aspects of applying occupational safety measures. He emphasised that investing in preventive measures brings long-term benefits — fewer injuries, higher productivity and lower insurance costs.
The second day of the conference was devoted to a deeper analysis of European standards, approaches and regulatory frameworks in occupational safety and health in agriculture. The panel “European approaches to occupational safety and health in agriculture” opened up space for an exchange of knowledge and institutional practice, with the participation of experts from the European Union and representatives of Montenegrin institutions dealing with public health, phytosanitary and veterinary controls, and the harmonisation of legislation in the European integration process.
Michele Dinelli, representing the European Agency for Safety and Health at Work (EU-OSHA), spoke about the agency's role in collecting data, issuing guidance and supporting member states in developing preventive policy. He emphasised the importance of a sectoral approach to OSH, with agriculture requiring particular attention because of the high degree of exposure to physical, biological and chemical risks and the frequent use of seasonal and informal workers. Dinelli pointed to the need for employers and workers to be more actively involved in identifying risks, and also to the importance of establishing national databases of injuries and incidents as the foundation of effective prevention.
In the domestic context, Dr Aleksandra Despotović, professor at the Biotechnical Faculty and a member of the Parliament of Montenegro, spoke about the challenges Montenegro faces in meeting the benchmarks of Chapter 11 (Agriculture and Rural Development) and Chapter 19 (Social Policy and Employment) in the EU accession process. She emphasised that without a precise legal definition of responsibilities in the agricultural sector and without stronger cross-sectoral cooperation, Montenegro will not be able to meet the obligations of the negotiating chapters in full. She singled out the problem of outdated regulation — such as the 1968 rulebook — which no longer corresponds to the realities of modern production.
Verica Gomilanović, of the Administration for Food Safety, Veterinary and Phytosanitary Affairs, presented an institutional perspective on food quality control, focusing on the connection between OSH and the safety of the end product. She emphasised that workers handling pesticides, disinfectants and animal feed must be trained and protected, because they too are part of the food safety chain.
From the public health perspective, Dr Zorica Đorđević of the Institute of Public Health of Montenegro spoke about the harmful effects of chemical and biological agents in agriculture on employees' health — from pesticides and fertilisers to infectious diseases transmissible from animals to humans. She warned in particular about the low rate at which occupational diseases are diagnosed in Montenegro, which further conceals the real risk agricultural workers are exposed to.
Panel participants had the opportunity to compare different practices across the project area and to learn about the support mechanisms that exist in EU countries. At the same time, all the speakers pointed to the need for better cross-sectoral coordination and synergy between the health, labour and agriculture sectors, currently recognised as one of the key shortcomings of the Montenegrin system.
During the second part of the day participants visited the company 13. Jul – Plantaže, where they saw concrete examples of OSH measures in practice, with visits organised to the old cellar, the bottling plant and the Šipčanik cellar. Demonstrations were held of the correct use of personal protective equipment, the handling of pesticides and work with machinery. The company was presented as an example of good practice in integrating OSH across all areas of its business — from the vineyards to the wine bottling plant.
The third day of the conference was given over to a round table that fittingly rounded off the SAGRI project's themes, opening a discussion about the future of occupational safety and health (OSH) in agriculture. The panel “Using techniques and tools for occupational safety and health in agriculture – what lies ahead?” brought together representatives of a range of sectors — from public administration and the inspection authorities, through the business and IT community, to academia and OSH specialists. That cross-sectoral diversity was key to seeing OSH not merely as a legal obligation but as a development opportunity for Montenegrin agriculture.
Zlatko Popović, representing the Occupational Safety and Health Inspectorate, reflected on the challenges inspection supervision faces in practice: a shortage of staff, the absence of inspectors specialised in agriculture, and the near-complete failure to report minor and moderate injuries at work. He emphasised the importance of educating employers and proposed involving the local community and the workers themselves more intensively in preventive work.
Luka Ivanović, representing the Chamber of Economy and the Agricultural Cluster of Montenegro, spoke from the perspective of agribusiness, emphasising that without comprehensive systemic support and subsidies for preventive measures, small producers cannot cope with the challenges of implementing OSH standards. He proposed establishing dedicated grant lines for companies wishing to modernise their equipment or introduce digital solutions in workplace safety.
One of the most authentic voices on the panel was Ilija Moric, the owner of an agricultural business from Luštica, who spoke from personal experience about the risks facing small family farms. He stressed the importance of practical education and of adapting guidance to what holdings can realistically manage. Moric also shared positive examples of working with OSH specialists, while pointing to the need to simplify the procedures for applying basic protective measures.
In the professional and methodological part of the discussion, Bojana Zindović of the “Sigurnost” Institute presented an approach combining risk analysis, legal compliance and workforce training. She emphasised in particular the importance of certified training in handling pesticides and machinery, and the need to integrate OSH content into secondary and university education in agriculture.
From the point of view of the scientific community, Professor Nedeljko Latinović of the Biotechnical Faculty discussed the concept of “risk-free agricultural engineering”, that is, the development of ergonomic solutions and the optimisation of working procedures so as to reduce physical effort and exposure to hazards to a minimum. He supported the idea that the Biotechnical Faculty should be the link between science and practice in OSH.
A significant contribution to the discussion also came from the field of innovation. Slađana Đurović, representing the company “Data Design”, demonstrated concrete examples of digital solutions that can improve safety in agriculture — from GPS systems for monitoring machinery, through digital checklists for risk assessment, to sensor systems for monitoring microclimate conditions and exposure to pesticides. These presentations underlined technology's potential to make OSH more effective, more accessible and more measurable.
The round table's conclusions pointed to the need to see OSH in Montenegrin agriculture not only as a question of complying with the law, but also as an opportunity to improve product quality, protect employees' lives and secure the sector's long-term sustainability. The integration of innovation, professional support and institutional recognition of the problems were identified as the three key directions for future development.
At the end of the panel a practical exercise was held with participants — a risk analysis of ten agricultural companies that took part in the project. Using checklists and working together, preliminary reports were produced on possible accidents and the preventive measures recommended. This session allowed knowledge to be applied directly and theoretical frameworks to be connected with concrete situations in the field, further confirming the importance of bringing together good practice and the sector's real needs.
Conclusions and key recommendations
The conference confirmed that safety at work in Montenegrin agriculture is a field in urgent need of reform. The problems identified include:
• outdated regulation — the rulebook on protection in agriculture dates from 1968;
• a shortage of specialist inspectors and advisory services;
• the absence of training specific to work in agriculture;
• the failure to report injuries and weak oversight of family holdings.
Participants agreed on the need to draw up a modern rulebook covering all the relevant risks: chemical, biological, mechanical, climatic and ergonomic. The creation of a centralised database of injuries was proposed, as was stronger cooperation between the health, labour and agriculture sectors.
With this event the SAGRI project took an important step towards putting OSH in agriculture in Montenegro on a systematic footing. The joint guidelines now in preparation are expected to be supported through national strategies and legislative changes.

title: Okrugli sto – Zakon o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu: Struka složna, ali ignorisana 28.07.2028.
excerpt: UZNR CG je 28. jula 2025. učestvovalo na Okruglom stolu o Nacrtu izmjena Zakona o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu u Naučno-tehnološkom parku, kritikujući netransparentnost procesa izrade.
content:
Udruženje za zaštitu na radu Crne Gore učestvovalo je 28. jula 2025. godine na Okruglom stolu povodom Javne rasprave o Nacrtu Zakona o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu, održanom u Naučno-tehnološkom parku Crne Gore.
Iako je Okrugli sto trebao biti centralno mjesto za razmjenu stavova između struke, sindikata, poslodavaca i predstavnika Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga sam proces izmjena zakona prethodio je ovom događaju pod znakom netransparentnosti i formalizma.
Šta se dešavalo u radu Radne grupe?
Radna grupa, formirana još u aprilu 2024. godine, suočila se s ozbiljnim zastojima. Nakon nekoliko sastanaka, posljednji je održan u novembru 2024. godine. Od tada do jula 2025. godine, radna grupa nije bila aktivna. Kao razlog za obustavu rada navodilo se sporno pitanje izbora predstavnika sindikata, iako je UZNRCG konstantno ukazivalo da to pitanje ne smije blokirati cjelokupan proces.
Kada je konačno, nakon osam mjeseci, zakazan sastanak za 4. jul 2025. godine, očekivao se nastavak stručne rasprave. Međutim, članovi Radne grupe su samo obaviješteni da će objedinjeni nacrt Zakona biti dostavljen 7. jula, uz rok za komentare do 10. jula. UZNRCG je upozorilo na proceduralni propust jer je nacrt već 8. jula bio proslijeđen Sekretarijatu za zakonodavstvo – bez mogućnosti da članovi dostave svoje komentare.
Naši komentari i prijedlozi
UZNRCG je, bez obzira na proceduralne barijere, pripremilo 18 konkretnih primjedbi, prijedloga i sugestija koje su prezentovane na Okruglom stolu. Među ključnim tačkama ističemo:
• Formiranje Nacionalnog savjeta za ZZNR – mehanizam koji postoji u gotovo svim zemljama EU i regiona.
• Jasno definisanje zaštite zaposlenih koji rade na daljinu (remote work/telework).
• Uvođenje koordinatora za ZZNR u fazama projektovanja i izvođenja radova, u skladu sa EU Direktivom 92/57/EEZ.
• Zaštita prava zaposlenih na izbor svojih predstavnika i osiguranje vremena i sredstava za njihovo djelovanje.
• Zadržavanje izuzetaka od polaganja stručnog ispita za visoko kvalifikovana lica sa dokazanim iskustvom.
• Uspostavljanje javnog registra ovlašćenih organizacija i uključivanje nezavisnih stručnjaka u komisije za ovlašćivanje.
Ovi prijedlozi nisu puka forma – oni su rezultat dugogodišnje stručne prakse i usmjereni su na rješavanje konkretnih problema sa kojima se suočavaju svi akteri sistema zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
