Naše primjedbe su naišle na punu podršku prisutnih – predstavnika sindikata, stručnih udruženja i poslodavaca. Svi prisutni su jasno ukazali na činjenicu da su izmjene Zakona vođene bez istinske participacije struke, uz zanemarivanje ključnih problema iz prakse.
Struka je bila jednoglasna: ovakav zakon, ako bude usvojen bez suštinskih korekcija, ne samo da neće unaprijediti sistem zaštite i zdravlja na radu, već će dodatno produbiti postojeće probleme.
Poziv na uključivanje u Javnu raspravu
Javna rasprava traje do 11. avgusta 2025. godine i to je posljednja prilika da svi koji su dio ovog sistema – stručnjaci, sindikati, poslodavci, radnici – upute svoje komentare i zahtijevaju da se struka uvaži.
Pozivamo sve zainteresovane strane da dostave svoje komentare Ministarstvu rada, zapošlajvanja i socijalnog dijaloga i time doprinesu izradi Zakona koji će biti u interesu svih.
UZNR CG ostaje posvećeno stručnom dijalogu i borbi za stvarno unapređenje sistema zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
title_en: Round table – The Law on Occupational Safety and Health: the profession united, but ignored, 28 July 2025
excerpt_en: On 28 July 2025 UZNR CG took part in a round table on the draft amendments to the Law on Occupational Safety and Health at the Science and Technology Park, criticising the lack of transparency in the drafting process.
content_en:
On 28 July 2025 the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro took part in a round table held as part of the public consultation on the draft Law amending the Law on Occupational Safety and Health, at the Science and Technology Park of Montenegro.
Although the round table should have been the central forum for an exchange of views between the profession, the trade unions, employers and representatives of the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, the process of amending the law that preceded it was marked by a lack of transparency and by formalism.
What happened in the Working Group?
The working group, formed back in April 2024, ran into serious delays. After several meetings, the last was held in November 2024. From then until July 2025 the working group was inactive. The reason given for the suspension of its work was the disputed question of how trade union representatives were chosen, even though UZNRCG repeatedly pointed out that this question must not be allowed to block the whole process.
When a meeting was finally scheduled, eight months later, for 4 July 2025, a resumption of the professional debate was expected. Instead, the working group's members were merely informed that the consolidated draft Law would be sent to them on 7 July, with a deadline for comments of 10 July. UZNRCG warned of a procedural failure, since the draft had already been forwarded to the Secretariat for Legislation on 8 July — leaving members no opportunity to submit their comments.
Our comments and proposals
Despite the procedural obstacles, UZNRCG prepared 18 concrete objections, proposals and suggestions, which were presented at the round table. Among the key points:
• Establishing a National Council for OSH — a mechanism that exists in almost every country of the EU and the region.
• Clearly defining the protection of employees working remotely (remote work / telework).
• Introducing OSH coordinators at the design and construction phases of works, in line with EU Directive 92/57/EEC.
• Protecting employees' right to choose their representatives and securing the time and resources for them to act.
• Retaining the exemptions from the professional examination for highly qualified people with proven experience.
• Establishing a public register of licensed organisations and including independent experts on licensing panels.
These proposals are not mere formalities — they are the product of many years of professional practice and are aimed at solving concrete problems faced by everyone involved in the occupational safety and health system.
Our objections met with full support from those present — representatives of the trade unions, professional associations and employers. Everyone present made clear that the amendments to the Law have been driven forward without genuine participation by the profession and with the key problems of practice ignored.
The profession was unanimous: a law of this kind, if adopted without substantial correction, will not only fail to improve the occupational safety and health system but will deepen the existing problems.
A call to take part in the public consultation
The public consultation runs until 11 August 2025, and it is the last opportunity for everyone who is part of this system — professionals, trade unions, employers, workers — to submit comments and to demand that the profession be listened to.
We call on all interested parties to send their comments to the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue and thereby help produce a Law that serves everyone's interests.
UZNR CG remains committed to professional dialogue and to the fight for a real improvement of the occupational safety and health system.

title: Izvještaj sa završnih događaja u Italiji u okviru projekta SAGRI
excerpt: U Campobassu i Bariju održani su 22. i 23. jula 2025. završni događaji projekta SAGRI - Health and Safety in Agriculture - diseminacioni seminar i završna konferencija.
content:
Campobasso i Bari, Italija | 22–23. jul 2025.
U okviru završne faze implementacije projekta SAGRI – Health and Safety in Agriculture, koji se realizuje kroz Interreg IPA CBC South Adriatic 2021–2027 program, održana su dva ključna događaja u Italiji:
• Diseminacioni seminar u Campobasso-u, 22. jula 2025.
• Završna konferencija u Bariju, 23. jula 2025.
Događaji su okupili predstavnike partnerskih organizacija iz Italije 🇮🇹, Albanije 🇦🇱 i Crne Gore 🇲🇪, kao i eksperte iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, predstavnike institucija, agrobiznisa, akademije i civilnog sektora.
Diseminacioni seminar | Campobasso, 22. jul 2025.
Seminar je održan u prostorijama GAL Molise, a cilj je bio da se predstavi sveobuhvatan pregled rezultata projekta SAGRI, kao i da se diskutuje o regulatornim okvirima i izazovima vezanim za bezbjednost u poljoprivredi.
Ključne teme
Uvodne riječi dali su predstavnici GAL Molise, Stručne agronomske komore i Zajedničkog sekretarijata programa South Adriatic.
Roberto D’Amico, projekt menadžer, predstavio je ciljeve i rezultate projekta SAGRI – uključujući izradu smjernica, obuku poljoprivrednika i identifikaciju sektorskih rizika.
Đina Janković je prezentovala stanje i izazove zaštite i zdravlja na radu u poljoprivredi u Crnoj Gori – ističući zastarjelu regulativu (Pravilnik iz 1968. godine), slab inspekcijski nadzor i veliki broj neformalnih porodičnih gazdinstava van sistema kontrole.
Predstavnici iz Albanije iznijeli su slične izazove, ali i naglasili dobre prakse u okviru obuke i integracije ZZNR u obrazovne institucije.
Tematske sesije
Ulogu INAIL-a (Italijanski institut za osiguranje od povreda na radu), predstavljenu kroz izlaganje Rocca Maria Del Nera, koji je govorio o prevenciji i kompenzaciji povreda u poljoprivredi.
Smjernice za Molise region i njihovo usklađivanje sa EU direktivama, predstavljene od strane Renata Colonne.
Posebno interesantna bila je sesija o termalnim rizicima i bezbjednosti mašina, koju je predstavila Paola Bucci iz Nacionalne inspekcije rada Italije.
Seminar je završen interaktivnim dijalogom sa publikom, tokom kojeg su učesnici iznijeli niz prijedloga za unapređenje sistema zaštite i zdravlja u ruralnim oblastima.
Završna konferencija | Bari, 23. jul 2025.
Završna konferencija održana je u prostorijama CIA Puglia u Bariju i predstavljala je finalni i svečani korak u implementaciji SAGRI projekta.
Ključni momenti događaja
Uvodno obraćanje održao je Danilo Lo Latte, generalni direktor CIA Puglia, koji je istakao značaj projekta u harmonizaciji standarda ZZNR u regionu Jadrana.
Stefano Massa, projekt menadžer CIA Puglia, predstavio je Zajednički Akcioni plan i Smjernice projekta SAGRI. Izložene su zajedničke preporuke za politike, standarde i mjere koje treba usvojiti na regionalnom nivou.
Ida Borrelli, stručnjakinja CIA Puglia, predstavila je Memorandum o razumijevanju (MoU), koji su partneri potom svečano potpisali. Dokument definiše obaveze potpisnika da i nakon završetka projekta nastave da sarađuju u unapređenju ZZNR, posebno u sektoru maslinarstva i hortikulture.
Terenski primjeri i prezentacije dobre prakse
Popodne je bilo posvećeno predstavljanju konkretnih primjera dobre prakse iz dvije italijanske poljoprivredne kompanije iz sektora maslinarstva i povrtarstva. Učesnici su imali priliku da se upoznaju sa:
• Integracijom bezbjednosnih protokola u svakodnevni rad.
• Upotrebom digitalnih alata za procjenu rizika.
• Strategijama obuke i uključivanja zaposlenih u mjere zaštite.
Zaključci i doprinos SAGRI projekta
Završni događaji u Italiji predstavljali su krunu dvogodišnje saradnje između Italije, Albanije i Crne Gore. Tokom konferencije i seminara potvrđeno je:
• Da je bezbjednost u poljoprivredi i dalje marginalizovana, ali da postoji značajan potencijal za unapređenje kroz regulativu, edukaciju i inovacije.
• Da je regionalni pristup ključan za rješavanje zajedničkih izazova u ruralnim i poljoprivrednim zajednicama.
• Da će rezultati projekta (npr. MoU, smjernice, zajednički akcioni plan) poslužiti kao osnova za buduće politike i intersektorsku saradnju.
Delegaciju iz Crne Gore predvodio je ICT Cortex, koji je u prethodnim fazama projekta realizovao niz nacionalnih aktivnosti: analize, seminare, terenske posjete i izradu nacionalnih smjernica.
Na završnoj konferenciji, Đina Janković predstavila je izvještaj o stanju ZZNR u Crnoj Gori, naglašavajući potrebu za reformom zakonodavstva, obukom malih proizvođača i digitalizacijom procesa procjene rizika.
SAGRI je kroz svoju implementaciju pokazao da zaštita i zdravlje na radu u poljoprivredi ne mogu biti tretirani kao sekundarni prioritet. Naprotiv, oni su temelj održive proizvodnje, zaštite života i evropske integracije sektora. Završni događaji u Italiji dodatno su učvrstili regionalnu mrežu aktera posvećenih tom cilju i otvorili vrata za nastavak saradnje i nakon formalnog završetka projekta.
title_en: Report from the closing events in Italy under the SAGRI project
excerpt_en: On 22 and 23 July 2025 Campobasso and Bari hosted the closing events of the SAGRI – Health and Safety in Agriculture project: a dissemination seminar and the final conference.
content_en:
Campobasso and Bari, Italy | 22–23 July 2025
As part of the closing phase of the SAGRI – Health and Safety in Agriculture project, carried out through the Interreg IPA CBC South Adriatic 2021–2027 programme, two key events were held in Italy:
• a dissemination seminar in Campobasso, on 22 July 2025
• the final conference in Bari, on 23 July 2025
The events brought together representatives of the partner organisations from Italy 🇮🇹, Albania 🇦🇱 and Montenegro 🇲🇪, together with experts in occupational safety and health and representatives of institutions, agribusiness, academia and the civil sector.
Dissemination seminar | Campobasso, 22 July 2025
The seminar was held at the premises of GAL Molise, with the aim of presenting a comprehensive overview of the SAGRI project's results and of discussing the regulatory frameworks and challenges relating to safety in agriculture.
Key topics
Opening remarks were given by representatives of GAL Molise, the professional chamber of agronomists and the Joint Secretariat of the South Adriatic programme.
Roberto D'Amico, project manager, presented the aims and results of the SAGRI project — including the production of guidelines, the training of farmers and the identification of sectoral risks.
Đina Janković presented the state of, and challenges facing, occupational safety and health in agriculture in Montenegro — highlighting outdated regulation (a rulebook dating from 1968), weak inspection supervision and the large number of informal family holdings outside any system of control.
Representatives from Albania described similar challenges, while also highlighting good practice in training and in integrating OSH into educational institutions.
Thematic sessions
The role of INAIL (the Italian institute for insurance against accidents at work), presented by Rocco Maria Del Nero, who spoke about the prevention and compensation of injuries in agriculture.
Guidelines for the Molise region and their alignment with EU directives, presented by Renato Colonna.
Particularly interesting was the session on thermal risks and machinery safety, presented by Paola Bucci of Italy's National Labour Inspectorate.
The seminar closed with an interactive dialogue with the audience, during which participants put forward a range of proposals for improving safety and health in rural areas.
Final conference | Bari, 23 July 2025
The final conference was held at the premises of CIA Puglia in Bari and marked the closing, formal step in the implementation of the SAGRI project.
Key moments of the event
The opening address was given by Danilo Lo Latte, director general of CIA Puglia, who emphasised the project's importance in harmonising OSH standards across the Adriatic region.
Stefano Massa, project manager at CIA Puglia, presented the SAGRI project's Joint Action Plan and Guidelines, setting out shared recommendations for policies, standards and measures to be adopted at regional level.
Ida Borrelli, an expert at CIA Puglia, presented the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), which the partners then formally signed. The document sets out the signatories' commitment to continue working together to improve OSH after the project ends, particularly in the olive-growing and horticulture sectors.
Field examples and presentations of good practice
The afternoon was devoted to presenting concrete examples of good practice from two Italian agricultural companies in the olive-growing and vegetable-growing sectors. Participants had the opportunity to learn about:
• the integration of safety protocols into everyday work;
• the use of digital tools for risk assessment;
• strategies for training employees and involving them in protective measures.
Conclusions and the SAGRI project's contribution
The closing events in Italy crowned two years of cooperation between Italy, Albania and Montenegro. The conference and seminar confirmed:
• that safety in agriculture is still marginalised, but that there is significant potential for improvement through regulation, education and innovation;
• that a regional approach is key to solving shared challenges in rural and agricultural communities;
• that the project's outputs (the MoU, the guidelines, the joint action plan) will serve as a basis for future policy and cross-sectoral cooperation.
The delegation from Montenegro was led by ICT Cortex, which in earlier phases of the project carried out a range of national activities: analyses, seminars, field visits and the production of national guidelines.
At the final conference, Đina Janković presented a report on the state of OSH in Montenegro, emphasising the need to reform the legislation, to train small producers and to digitalise the risk assessment process.
Through its implementation SAGRI showed that occupational safety and health in agriculture cannot be treated as a secondary priority. On the contrary, it is the foundation of sustainable production, of protecting lives and of the sector's European integration. The closing events in Italy further consolidated a regional network of actors committed to that goal and opened the door to continued cooperation after the project's formal end.

title: Izvještaj sa Diseminacionog seminara
excerpt: U Naučno-tehnološkom parku u Podgorici održan je 17. jula 2025. diseminacioni seminar projekta SAGRI, na kojem je predstavljena Analiza stanja i smjernice za prevenciju rizika u poljoprivredi u Crnoj Gori.
content:
SAGRI – Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u poljoprivredi
17. jul 2025. godine
U organizaciji ICT Cortex-a, u okviru projekta SAGRI – Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u poljoprivredi, 17. jula 2025. godine u Naučno-tehnološkom parku u Podgorici održan je diseminacioni seminar posvećen predstavljanju rezultata projekta u Crnoj Gori, prije svega dokumenta „Analiza stanja i smjernice za prevenciju rizika u poljoprivredi“, koji predstavlja temelj za dalje institucionalne, zakonodavne i obrazovne inicijative u ovoj oblasti.
U uvodnim obraćanjima je istaknuta važnost saradnje između institucija, stručnjaka i sektora agrobiznisa u cilju unapređenja zaštite i zdravlja na radu, posebno u poljoprivredi, koja se smatra jednim od najrizičnijih, ali i najmanje regulisanih sektora u Crnoj Gori.
Nakon uvodnog dijela, Đina Janković, konsultantkinja na projektu, predstavila je Analizu stanja i smjernice za prevenciju rizika u poljoprivredi u Crnoj Gori. Dokument je rezultat višemjesečnog rada na terenu, uključujući konsultacije sa poljoprivrednim proizvođačima, institucijama i stručnjacima, kao i pregled zakonskog okvira. Istaknuto je da nepostojanje savremenog pravilnika za ovu oblast, kao i nedostatak inspekcijskog i edukativnog kapaciteta, predstavljaju ključne prepreke za efikasno sprovođenje mjera zaštite na radu u poljoprivredi.
ZZNR kao faktor konkurentnosti u agrobiznisu
Dr Miljan Joksimović, sa Biotehničkog fakulteta, održao je prezentaciju na temu ekonomske održivosti mjera ZZNR u poljoprivredi, ističući da implementacija ovih mjera, uz primjenu savremenih tehnologija i adekvatan menadžment, ne samo da doprinosi bezbjednosti radnika, već direktno utiče na produktivnost, kvalitet proizvoda i dugoročnu održivost agrobiznisa. Takođe je istaknuta potreba da se ZZNR uključi u agrobiznis strategije, a ne da ostane samo u domenu zakonske obaveze.
Panel diskusija – Institucionalni pregled stanja
U okviru centralnog dijela seminara, održan je panel „Institucionalni pregled stanja – zaštita i zdravlje na radu u poljoprivredi“, u kojem su učestvovali predstavnici ključnih institucija i stručne zajednice:
• Jovana Bošković, Direktorat za ZZNR – istakla je da je važeći pravilnik koji reguliše zaštitu u poljoprivredi još iz 1968. godine, što je neprihvatljivo u savremenom kontekstu. Naglasila je da su izmjene zakonskog okvira u pripremi, ali i da se čeka veća koordinacija sa sektorom poljoprivrede.
• Zlatko Popović, Inspekcija za ZZNR – govorio je o nedostatku inspektora specijalizovanih za poljoprivredu, kao i o činjenici da je nadzor često reaktivan, tj. usmjeren na posljedice, umjesto na prevenciju.
• Ivan Ivanović, Uprava za bezbjednost hrane – ukazao je na slabu kontrolu primjene pesticida, upotrebe opasnih supstanci i procedura rukovanja životinjama, što direktno utiče i na zdravlje radnika i na bezbjednost hrane.
• Vasilije Mirović, stručnjak za OSH iz kompanije Plantaže 13. Jul – predstavio je sistem internih protokola, obuka i mjera zaštite koje se sprovode u ovoj kompaniji, navodeći da je ključno uložiti u edukaciju i tehničku zaštitu kako bi se smanjili rizici i povećala svijest zaposlenih.
• Verica Gomilanović, stručnjakinja iz oblasti stočarstva – govorila je o visokom stepenu fizičkog i biološkog rizika u radu sa stokom, te o niskoj informisanosti radnika o pravima i obavezama iz oblasti ZZNR.
• Branislav Šebek, Udruženje za zaštitu na radu – upozorio je na nedostatak eksternih servisa i podrške manjim gazdinstvima, te naglasio potrebu za specifičnim obukama za mikro i porodična poljoprivredna domaćinstva, koja su posebno ranjiva.
Diskusija i povratne informacije
U završnom dijelu seminara organizovan je otvoreni forum za komentare, u okviru kojeg su prisutni učesnici – poljoprivrednici, predstavnici institucija i civilnog sektora – dali svoje komentare na prezentovani dokument i preporuke za njegovo poboljšanje. Posebno su istaknuti sljedeći prioriteti:
• izrada novog pravilnika o ZZNR u poljoprivredi,
• kreiranje sektorskih obuka i smjernica,
• jačanje međuresorske saradnje,
• institucionalno prepoznavanje porodičnih gazdinstava kao subjekata sa visokim stepenom rizika.
Zaključci i naredni koraci
U završnom obraćanju, najavljeno je da će komentari sa seminara biti integrisani u finalnu verziju dokumenta i predstavljeni kao dio zajedničkog regionalnog okvira. Takođe je istaknuto da ICT Cortex ostaje posvećen daljoj saradnji sa institucijama i međunarodnim partnerima u cilju stvaranja sveobuhvatne politike zaštite i zdravlja na radu u crnogorskoj poljoprivredi.
Seminar je završen neformalnim druženjem i ručkom, koji je omogućio dodatnu razmjenu mišljenja i ideja među učesnicima.
🔵 Projekat SAGRI Projekat SAGRI – Health and Safety in Agriculture sufinansiran je od strane Evropske unije 🇪🇺 kroz Interreg IPA CBC South Adriatic 2021–2027 program i predstavlja zajedničku inicijativu partnera iz Crne Gore, Italije i Albanije, s ciljem jačanja preventivnih mehanizama i promocije zdravih i bezbjednih radnih uslova u sektoru poljoprivrede.
title_en: Report from the dissemination seminar
excerpt_en: On 17 July 2025 the Science and Technology Park in Podgorica hosted the SAGRI project's dissemination seminar, at which the “Analysis of the situation and guidelines for preventing risk in agriculture” was presented.
content_en:
SAGRI – Occupational safety and health in agriculture
17 July 2025
Organised by ICT Cortex under the SAGRI – Occupational safety and health in agriculture project, a dissemination seminar was held on 17 July 2025 at the Science and Technology Park in Podgorica, devoted to presenting the project's results in Montenegro, above all the document “Analysis of the situation and guidelines for preventing risk in agriculture”, which forms the basis for further institutional, legislative and educational initiatives in this field.
The opening addresses emphasised the importance of cooperation between institutions, experts and the agribusiness sector in improving occupational safety and health, particularly in agriculture, which is considered one of the riskiest but least regulated sectors in Montenegro.
After the opening, Đina Janković, a consultant on the project, presented the Analysis of the situation and guidelines for preventing risk in agriculture in Montenegro. The document is the result of several months of fieldwork, including consultations with agricultural producers, institutions and experts, and a review of the legal framework. It was emphasised that the absence of a modern rulebook for this field, together with the shortage of inspection and educational capacity, are the key obstacles to applying occupational safety measures effectively in agriculture.
OSH as a factor of competitiveness in agribusiness
Dr Miljan Joksimović, of the Biotechnical Faculty, gave a presentation on the economic sustainability of OSH measures in agriculture, emphasising that applying these measures, together with modern technology and proper management, not only makes workers safer but directly affects productivity, product quality and the long-term sustainability of agribusiness. He also emphasised the need for OSH to be built into agribusiness strategy rather than remaining merely a legal obligation.
Panel discussion – an institutional review of the situation
The central part of the seminar was a panel on “An institutional review of the situation – occupational safety and health in agriculture”, with representatives of key institutions and the professional community:
• Jovana Bošković, Directorate for OSH – emphasised that the rulebook governing protection in agriculture dates from 1968, which is unacceptable in a modern context. She said changes to the legal framework are being prepared, but that better coordination with the agricultural sector is still awaited.
• Zlatko Popović, OSH Inspectorate – spoke about the shortage of inspectors specialised in agriculture and about the fact that supervision is often reactive, directed at consequences rather than at prevention.
• Ivan Ivanović, Administration for Food Safety – pointed to weak control over the use of pesticides, the use of hazardous substances and animal handling procedures, all of which directly affect both workers' health and food safety.
• Vasilije Mirović, OSH specialist at the company Plantaže 13. Jul – presented the internal protocols, training and protective measures applied at the company, noting that investment in education and technical protection is essential if risks are to be reduced and employees' awareness raised.
• Verica Gomilanović, a livestock specialist – spoke about the high degree of physical and biological risk in work with livestock and about workers' limited awareness of their OSH rights and obligations.
• Branislav Šebek, Occupational Safety Association – warned of the lack of external services and support for smaller holdings and emphasised the need for training tailored to micro and family farms, which are particularly vulnerable.
Discussion and feedback
The closing part of the seminar was an open forum for comments, in which those present — farmers and representatives of institutions and the civil sector — gave their comments on the document presented and their recommendations for improving it. The following priorities were singled out:
• drawing up a new rulebook on OSH in agriculture,
• creating sector-specific training and guidance,
• strengthening cross-sectoral cooperation,
• institutional recognition of family holdings as high-risk entities.
Conclusions and next steps
The closing address announced that the comments from the seminar will be incorporated into the final version of the document and presented as part of a joint regional framework. It was also emphasised that ICT Cortex remains committed to continued cooperation with institutions and international partners in order to create a comprehensive occupational safety and health policy for Montenegrin agriculture.
The seminar ended with an informal gathering and lunch, allowing participants to exchange further views and ideas.
🔵 The SAGRI project – Health and Safety in Agriculture is co-financed by the European Union 🇪🇺 through the Interreg IPA CBC South Adriatic 2021–2027 programme and is a joint initiative of partners from Montenegro, Italy and Albania, aimed at strengthening preventive mechanisms and promoting healthy, safe working conditions in agriculture.

title: Izvještaj sa nacionalnog seminara o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu u poljoprivredi
excerpt: U Fieru (Albanija) održan je od 30. juna do 2. jula 2025. trodnevni nacionalni seminar projekta SAGRI o unapređenju zaštite i zdravlja na radu u poljoprivredi, u saradnji sa školom "Rakip Kryeziu".
content:
Fier, Albanija | 30. jun – 02. jul 2025.
U okviru projekta SAGRI – Health and Safety in Agriculture, koji se realizuje kroz Interreg IPA CBC South Adriatic 2021–2027 program, u gradu Fier (Albanija) održan je trodnevni nacionalni seminar posvećen unapređenju zaštite i zdravlja na radu u poljoprivredi.
Seminar je organizovan u saradnji sa Srednjom stručnom školom „Rakip Kryeziu“, jednom od najznačajnijih obrazovnih institucija u oblasti poljoprivredne obuke u regionu.
Cilj i značaj seminara
Glavni cilj događaja bio je razmjena iskustava, znanja i praksi između stručnjaka i institucija iz Albanije, Italije i Crne Gore, uz fokus na sigurnu upotrebu pesticida, hemikalija i mehanizacije, kao i na razvoj zajedničkih pristupa unapređenju radnih uslova u poljoprivredi.
Seminar je takođe predstavljao važnu fazu implementacije projekta SAGRI, u okviru koje se rezultati nacionalnih istraživanja i testiranja povezuju kroz regionalni dijalog i zajedničke preporuke.
Učesnici i predstavnici Crne Gore
Delegaciju Crne Gore koordinisao je ICT Cortex, kao nacionalni partner na projektu.
U njenom sastavu bili su:
• Đina Janković, konsultantkinja za ZZNR na projektu u Crnoj Gori,
• Milica Filipović i Vasilije Mirović, stručna lica za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu iz kompanije „13. jul – Plantaže“,
• Slavenko Blažević, poljoprivredni proizvođač iz Mojkovca,
• Luka Janjušević, poljoprivredni proizvođač iz Nikšića.
Učesnici iz Crne Gore aktivno su učestvovali u panelima, terenskim posjetama i radionicama, dijeleći iskustva i izazove iz nacionalnog konteksta, ali i primjere dobre prakse koji mogu poslužiti kao model za druge zemlje regiona.
Tok seminara i glavne teme
Program trodnevnog događaja obuhvatio je teorijski, praktični i terenski segment, uz aktivno učešće stručnjaka iz oblasti agronomije, bezbjednosti hrane, veterinarstva i zaštite na radu.
Prvog dana održane su sesije posvećene:
• zakonodavnom okviru i institucionalnim praksama u Albaniji,
• bezbjednoj upotrebi pesticida i hemikalija u okviru farmi i plastenika,
• značaju pravilnog rukovanja poljoprivrednom mehanizacijom u prevenciji povreda.
Predstavnici Ministarstva poljoprivrede Albanije, Poljoprivrednog fakulteta i lokalnih inspekcija istakli su da su hemijski rizici i neadekvatna primjena zaštitne opreme među najčešćim uzrocima profesionalnih oboljenja u ovom sektoru.
Drugog dana održane su radionice i panel diskusije o integrisanju nacionalnih praksi u zajedničke smjernice projekta SAGRI.
Predstavnici Crne Gore su prezentovali stanje i izazove u nacionalnom kontekstu, s posebnim osvrtom na nedostatak stručnog kadra, zastarjelu regulativu i potrebu za sektorskim obukama.
Prezentacija dobre prakse iz Crne Gore
Tokom tehničke sesije drugog dana, Milica Filipović, stručnjak za ZZNR iz kompanije „13. jul – Plantaže“, održala je prezentaciju o primjeni standarda zaštite i zdravlja na radu u jednoj od najvećih agroindustrijskih kompanija u Crnoj Gori.
Kroz primjere iz vinograda i proizvodnih pogona, ona je prikazala način sprovođenja internih procedura, upotrebu lične zaštitne opreme i sistem obuke zaposlenih, ističući da kontinuirana edukacija i digitalizacija procesa značajno doprinose smanjenju rizika i jačanju kulture bezbjednosti.
Prezentacija Plantaža izazvala je veliko interesovanje i bila prepoznata kao model dobre prakse u regionu.
Trećeg dana održane su terenske posjete nizu poljoprivrednih objekata u okolini Fiera:
• modernoj farmi krava i mljekari za preradu mlijeka,
• staklenicima za povrće,
• fabrici za proizvodnju i distribuciju đubriva i pesticida.
Tokom ovih posjeta, učesnici su imali priliku da se direktno upoznaju sa načinima primjene mjera ZZNR u praksi – od kontrole ventilacije i mikroklime u plastenicima, preko bezbjednog skladištenja hemikalija, do primjene lične zaštitne opreme i procedura dezinfekcije u prehrambenim pogonima.
Poseban fokus bio je na digitalnim alatima i internim sistemima praćenja bezbjednosnih procedura, koji su već uvedeni u pojedinim kompanijama u Albaniji.
Glavni zaključci i preporuke
Na kraju seminara usaglašeni su glavni zaključci i preporuke za unapređenje ZZNR u poljoprivredi na regionalnom nivou:
• Neophodna je revizija zastarjele regulative i njeno usklađivanje sa direktivama EU (posebno 2009/104/EC i 2009/128/EC);
• Potrebno je jačanje inspekcijskih kapaciteta i specijalizacija inspektora za poljoprivredu;
• Uvesti redovne programe obuke za rukovanje hemikalijama i poljoprivrednim mašinama;
• Razviti digitalne alate za evidenciju rizika, povreda i preventivnih mjera;
• Podsticati razmjenu dobrih praksi između obrazovnih institucija i poljoprivrednih proizvođača.
Učesnici su se složili da je saradnja između Crne Gore, Italije i Albanije kroz projekat SAGRI doprinijela boljem razumijevanju specifičnih rizika i uspostavljanju temelja za zajedničku regionalnu politiku zaštite i zdravlja na radu u poljoprivredi.
Seminar u Fieru predstavljao je važan korak u regionalnoj implementaciji projekta SAGRI, potvrđujući posvećenost partnerskih zemalja da kroz obrazovanje, inovacije i institucionalnu saradnju unaprijede bezbjednost poljoprivrednika i modernizuju sektor u skladu sa evropskim standardima.
Projekat SAGRI – Health and Safety in Agriculture sufinansiran je od strane Evropske unije 🇪🇺 kroz Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPA III) u okviru Interreg IPA South Adriatic 2021–2027 programa.
title_en: Report from the national seminar on occupational safety and health in agriculture
excerpt_en: From 30 June to 2 July 2025 Fier (Albania) hosted a three-day national seminar of the SAGRI project on improving occupational safety and health in agriculture, in cooperation with the “Rakip Kryeziu” school.
content_en:
Fier, Albania | 30 June – 2 July 2025
Under the SAGRI – Health and Safety in Agriculture project, carried out through the Interreg IPA CBC South Adriatic 2021–2027 programme, a three-day national seminar devoted to improving occupational safety and health in agriculture was held in the town of Fier, Albania.
The seminar was organised in cooperation with the “Rakip Kryeziu” Secondary Vocational School, one of the region's most important educational institutions in agricultural training.
Aim and significance of the seminar
The main aim of the event was to exchange experience, knowledge and practice between experts and institutions from Albania, Italy and Montenegro, focusing on the safe use of pesticides, chemicals and machinery and on developing shared approaches to improving working conditions in agriculture.
The seminar was also an important phase in the implementation of the SAGRI project, in which the results of national research and testing are brought together through regional dialogue and joint recommendations.
Participants and Montenegro's representatives
Montenegro's delegation was coordinated by ICT Cortex, the national partner on the project.
It comprised:
• Đina Janković, OSH consultant on the project in Montenegro,
• Milica Filipović and Vasilije Mirović, occupational safety and health specialists at the company “13. jul – Plantaže”,
• Slavenko Blažević, an agricultural producer from Mojkovac,
• Luka Janjušević, an agricultural producer from Nikšić.
The participants from Montenegro took an active part in the panels, field visits and workshops, sharing experience and challenges from the national context as well as examples of good practice that can serve as a model for other countries in the region.
The course of the seminar and its main themes
The three-day programme comprised theoretical, practical and field segments, with the active participation of experts in agronomy, food safety, veterinary medicine and occupational safety.
The first day held sessions devoted to:
• the legislative framework and institutional practice in Albania,
• the safe use of pesticides and chemicals on farms and in greenhouses,
• the importance of handling agricultural machinery correctly in preventing injuries.
Representatives of Albania's Ministry of Agriculture, the Faculty of Agriculture and the local inspectorates emphasised that chemical risks and the inadequate use of protective equipment are among the most common causes of occupational disease in this sector.
The second day held workshops and panel discussions on integrating national practice into the SAGRI project's joint guidelines.
Montenegro's representatives presented the situation and the challenges in the national context, with particular reference to the shortage of qualified staff, outdated regulation and the need for sector-specific training.
A presentation of good practice from Montenegro
During the technical session on the second day, Milica Filipović, an OSH specialist at the company “13. jul – Plantaže”, gave a presentation on the application of occupational safety and health standards at one of Montenegro's largest agro-industrial companies.
Using examples from the vineyards and production plants, she showed how internal procedures are applied, how personal protective equipment is used and how employees are trained, emphasising that continuous education and the digitalisation of processes significantly reduce risk and strengthen the safety culture.
The Plantaže presentation aroused great interest and was recognised as a model of good practice in the region.
The third day held field visits to a number of agricultural facilities around Fier:
• a modern dairy cattle farm and milk processing plant,
• vegetable greenhouses,
• a plant producing and distributing fertilisers and pesticides.
During these visits participants had the opportunity to see at first hand how OSH measures are applied in practice — from ventilation and microclimate control in greenhouses, through the safe storage of chemicals, to the use of personal protective equipment and disinfection procedures in food production plants.
Particular focus was placed on the digital tools and internal systems for monitoring safety procedures that some companies in Albania have already introduced.
Main conclusions and recommendations
At the end of the seminar the main conclusions and recommendations for improving OSH in agriculture at regional level were agreed:
• outdated regulation must be revised and aligned with EU directives (particularly 2009/104/EC and 2009/128/EC);
• inspection capacity must be strengthened and inspectors specialised in agriculture;
• regular training programmes in handling chemicals and agricultural machinery should be introduced;
• digital tools should be developed for recording risks, injuries and preventive measures;
• the exchange of good practice between educational institutions and agricultural producers should be encouraged.
Participants agreed that cooperation between Montenegro, Italy and Albania through the SAGRI project has led to a better understanding of the specific risks and laid the foundations for a joint regional policy on occupational safety and health in agriculture.
The seminar in Fier was an important step in the regional implementation of the SAGRI project, confirming the partner countries' commitment to improving farmers' safety and modernising the sector in line with European standards through education, innovation and institutional cooperation.
The SAGRI – Health and Safety in Agriculture project is co-financed by the European Union 🇪🇺 through the Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPA III) within the Interreg IPA South Adriatic 2021–2027 programme.

title: Konferencija „Potpuna implementacija zaštite i zdravlja na radu nema alternativu“ Petrovac, 15–17. maj 2025. | Hotel Vile Oliva
excerpt: U Petrovcu je od 15. do 17. maja 2025. održana konferencija "Potpuna implementacija zaštite i zdravlja na radu nema alternativu", u organizaciji UZNR CG i Ministarstva rada, sa 67 učesnika.
content:
U organizaciji Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore i Ministarstva rada, zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga, od 15. do 17. maja 2025. godine u Petrovcu je održana konferencija pod nazivom „Potpuna implementacija zaštite i zdravlja na radu nema alternativu“. Događaj je okupio 67 predstavnika relevantnih institucija, kompanija i profesionalaca iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, čime je potvrđena njegova važnost i aktuelnost za sistemski razvoj ove oblasti u Crnoj Gori.
🔍 Tematske cjeline i ključni akcenti
Program konferencije bio je koncipiran tako da odgovori na izazove savremene prakse ZZNR, kroz interaktivne sesije, panel diskusije i stručna izlaganja. Poseban fokus bio je na sljedećim temama:
✅Efektivna komunikacija kao osnova bezbjednosne kulture, uključujući značaj aktivnog slušanja, jasnoće u prenošenju poruka i dvosmjerne razmjene među zaposlenima.
✅Primjena LEAN metodologije i upravljanje kvalitetom u cilju optimizacije procesa, smanjenja rizika i povećanja efikasnosti.
✅Modernizacija edukacije za rad u uslovima povećanog rizika, kroz kraće, praktične i ciljano orijentisane obuke.
✅Zakonodavni okvir i odgovornosti stručnih lica i koordinatora, sa akcentom na potrebu za preciznijim regulisanjem ovlašćenja i komunikacije sa inspekcijama.
✅Digitalizacija i upotreba vještačke inteligencije u ZZNR, kao podrška u procjeni rizika, izvještavanju i planiranju preventivnih mjera.
✅Rodna ravnopravnost u zaštiti na radu, sa posebnim osvrtom na prilagođavanje zaštitnih mjera specifičnim potrebama žena i drugih grupa zaposlenih.
✅Bezbjednost na gradilištima, uključujući zakonske obaveze investitora, upotrebu lične zaštitne opreme i upravljanje izvođačima.
✅Radno-pravni status zaposlenih sa smanjenom radnom sposobnošću, gdje je istaknut problem pravne i institucionalne praznine u slučajevima kada poslodavac nije u mogućnosti da obezbijedi drugo radno mjesto. Poseban apel upućen je Ministarstvu rada i Ministarstvu zdravlja da pokrenu sistemska rješenja za ovu kategoriju zaposlenih, kroz:
o razvoj modela profesionalne rehabilitacije,
o institucionalnu zaštitu i naknade,
o međuresornu saradnju zapošljavanja i zdravstvene zaštite.
🎯 Zaljučci i preporuke konferencije
Učesnici su usvojili niz preporuka koje bi mogle značajno doprinijeti unapređenju sistema ZZNR u Crnoj Gori:
🔹Uspostavljanje sistema obaveznih stručnih radionica i kontinuirane edukacije za stručna lica i koordinatore.
🔹Reforma modela osposobljavanja, sa fokusom na fleksibilne, praktične i sektorski specifične pristupe.
🔹Izrada pravilnika o kriterijumima i obavezama edukacije za stručna lica.
🔹Digitalizacija upravljanja ZZNR, uključujući pilot testiranja softverskih alata u saradnji sa privredom i inspekcijskim organima.
🔹Razrada međuresornog modela zaštite za zaposlene sa smanjenim radnim kapacitetom.
🔹Veća podrška ženama u oblasti ZZNR, kroz konkretne mjere koje prepoznaju i uvažavaju njihove specifične potrebe.
🔹Uvođenje ZZNR sadržaja u formalne obrazovne programe, kroz srednje stručne škole i fakultete, uključujući razvoj praktikuma i stručne prakse.
🔹Reforma modela osposobljavanja za rad po stepenu rizika, kroz razvoj praktičnih treninga za specifične sektore (građevina, industrija, zdravstvo…).
💡 Zaštita i zdravlje na radu nisu administrativna obaveza, već ljudsko pravo i temelj održivog poslovanja. Ova konferencija je još jednom pokazala da znanje, saradnja i posvećenost donose rezultate.
🙏 Hvala svim učesnicima na poverenju, energiji i inspiraciji!
📆 Vidimo se na sledećem skupu — sa još više rezultata, ideja i entuzijazma!
title_en: Conference “There is no alternative to full implementation of occupational safety and health”. Petrovac, 15–17 May 2025 | Hotel Vile Oliva
excerpt_en: From 15 to 17 May 2025 Petrovac hosted the conference “There is no alternative to full implementation of occupational safety and health”, organised by UZNR CG and the Ministry of Labour, with 67 participants.
content_en:
Organised by the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro and the Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Dialogue, a conference entitled “There is no alternative to full implementation of occupational safety and health” was held in Petrovac from 15 to 17 May 2025. The event brought together 67 representatives of relevant institutions and companies and professionals in occupational safety and health, confirming its importance and topicality for the systematic development of this field in Montenegro.
🔍 Themes and key emphases
The conference programme was designed to address the challenges of modern OSH practice, through interactive sessions, panel discussions and expert presentations. Particular focus was placed on the following topics:
✅ Effective communication as the basis of a safety culture, including the importance of active listening, clarity in conveying messages and two-way exchange among employees.
✅ The application of LEAN methodology and quality management in order to optimise processes, reduce risk and increase efficiency.
✅ Modernising training for work in higher-risk conditions, through shorter, practical and targeted courses.
✅ The legislative framework and the responsibilities of safety professionals and coordinators, with an emphasis on the need to regulate powers and communication with the inspectorates more precisely.
✅ Digitalisation and the use of artificial intelligence in OSH, as support in risk assessment, reporting and the planning of preventive measures.
✅ Gender equality in occupational safety, with particular reference to adapting protective measures to the specific needs of women and other groups of employees.
✅ Safety on construction sites, including investors' legal obligations, the use of personal protective equipment and the management of contractors.
✅ The employment status of employees with reduced working capacity, where the problem of a legal and institutional vacuum was highlighted in cases where an employer cannot provide another position. A particular appeal was made to the Ministry of Labour and the Ministry of Health to bring forward systemic solutions for this group of employees, through:
o the development of a vocational rehabilitation model,
o institutional protection and compensation,
o cross-sectoral cooperation between employment and health care.
🎯 Conclusions and recommendations of the conference
Participants adopted a set of recommendations that could significantly improve the OSH system in Montenegro:
🔹 Establishing a system of compulsory professional workshops and continuous education for safety professionals and coordinators.
🔹 Reforming the training model, focusing on flexible, practical and sector-specific approaches.
🔹 Drawing up a rulebook on the criteria and obligations for the education of safety professionals.
🔹 Digitalising OSH management, including pilot testing of software tools together with industry and the inspection authorities.
🔹 Developing a cross-sectoral model of protection for employees with reduced working capacity.
🔹 Greater support for women in OSH, through concrete measures that recognise and respect their specific needs.
🔹 Introducing OSH content into formal education programmes, in secondary vocational schools and faculties, including the development of practical courses and work placements.
🔹 Reforming the model of training for work by level of risk, through practical training developed for specific sectors (construction, industry, health care and others).
💡 Occupational safety and health is not an administrative obligation but a human right and the foundation of sustainable business. This conference showed once again that knowledge, cooperation and commitment produce results.
🙏 Thank you to all participants for their trust, energy and inspiration!
📆 See you at the next gathering — with even more results, ideas and enthusiasm!

title: Ispitivanje elektro i gromobranskih instalacija u crnogorskim školama
excerpt: UZNR CG je pokrenulo inicijativu besplatnog ispitivanja elektro i gromobranskih instalacija u osnovnim školama, nakon požara u noćnom klubu u Sjevernoj Makedoniji u kojem je 16. marta 2025. poginulo 62 mlade osobe.
content:
U svjetlu nedavne tragedije koja je 16. marta 2025. godine potresla region, kada je u požaru u noćnom klubu u Sjevernoj Makedoniji život izgubilo 62 mlade osobe, pitanje bezbjednosti javnih objekata, a naročito obrazovnih ustanova, postavljeno je kao jedan od prioriteta javne politike. Ovaj događaj ukazao je na dramatične posljedice nepoštovanja osnovnih bezbjednosnih standarda, poput nedostatka evakuacionih planova, nefunkcionalnih instalacija i nepostojanja nadzora nad tehničkom ispravnošću objekata.
Vođeno ovim saznanjima i brigom za najmlađe, Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore pokrenulo je inicijativu za besplatno ispitivanje elektro i gromobranskih instalacija u osnovnim školama širom Crne Gore. Ministarstvo prosvjete, nauke i inovacija prepoznalo je značaj ove inicijative i pružilo punu podršku njenoj realizaciji dostavljanjem liste škola koje su ušle u prvi ciklus provjera.
Cilj ove inicijative nije bio samo tehnička provjera instalacija, već i otvaranje šireg dijaloga o potrebi sistematskog pristupa zaštiti na radu i unapređenju bezbjednosne kulture u školama. Stručni timovi članova Udruženja – ovlašćene organizacije DDIng iz Berana, Institut za crnu metalurgiju iz Nikšića i Montecontrol i Montinspekt iz Podgorice, izvršili su ispitivanja u osam osnovnih škola:
• OŠ „Radomir Mitrović“ – Berane
• OŠ „Ratko Žarić“ – Nikšić
• OŠ „Džafer Nikočević“ – Gusinje
• OŠ „Braća Labudović“ – Nikšić
• OŠ „Bratstvo i jedinstvo“ – Rožaje
• OŠ „25. maj“ – Rožaje
• OŠ „Pavle Žižić“ – Bijelo Polje
• OŠ „Boško Buha“ – Pljevlja
Iako je u pojedinim ustanovama zabilježeno tehnički zadovoljavajuće stanje, brojni nalazi ukazali su na značajne propuste koji mogu ozbiljno ugroziti bezbjednost učenika i zaposlenih: od oštećenih i neuzemljenih utičnica, improvizovanih električnih spojeva, neispravne rasvjete, do potpunog izostanka gromobranske zaštite.
Na osnovu dostavljenih stručnih nalaza, Ministarstvo prosvjete, nauke i inovacija planira da uloži dodatna sredstva u sanaciju i unapređenje stanja tamo gdje bezbjednosni uslovi nijesu na zadovoljavajućem nivou. Ova reakcija predstavlja odgovoran institucionalni odgovor na identifikovane probleme i važan korak ka izgradnji sigurnijeg obrazovnog sistema.
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore nastaviće sa sprovođenjem besplatnih akcija i u narednom periodu, sa ciljem da se u svim školama obezbijedi visok nivo zaštite, kako bi djeca i zaposleni mogli svakodnevno boraviti i raditi u bezbjednom okruženju.
Ova inicijativa nije samo odgovor na tragediju – ona je izraz posvećenosti da se proaktivno djeluje, da se izgrade standardi i ojača svijest o važnosti prevencije u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Dugoročno, sistematsko ulaganje u bezbjednost škola predstavlja ulaganje u budućnost naše djece i u povjerenje koje obrazovne ustanove moraju da imaju u očima roditelja, nastavnika i društva u cjelini.
title_en: Testing of electrical and lightning protection installations in Montenegrin schools
excerpt_en: UZNR CG launched an initiative to test electrical and lightning protection installations in primary schools free of charge, following the nightclub fire in North Macedonia on 16 March 2025 in which 62 young people died.
content_en:
In the light of the recent tragedy that shook the region on 16 March 2025, when 62 young people lost their lives in a nightclub fire in North Macedonia, the safety of public buildings, and of educational institutions in particular, has become a public policy priority. That event showed the dramatic consequences of ignoring basic safety standards, such as the absence of evacuation plans, non-functioning installations and the lack of any supervision of buildings' technical condition.
Guided by this and by concern for the youngest, the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro launched an initiative to test electrical and lightning protection installations in primary schools across Montenegro free of charge. The Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation recognised the importance of the initiative and gave its full support by supplying the list of schools included in the first cycle of checks.
The aim of the initiative was not merely a technical check of the installations but also to open a wider dialogue about the need for a systematic approach to safety at work and for a stronger safety culture in schools. Expert teams from the Association's member organisations — the licensed organisations DDIng of Berane, the Institute of Ferrous Metallurgy of Nikšić, and Montecontrol and Montinspekt of Podgorica — carried out testing at eight primary schools:
• “Radomir Mitrović” Primary School – Berane
• “Ratko Žarić” Primary School – Nikšić
• “Džafer Nikočević” Primary School – Gusinje
• “Braća Labudović” Primary School – Nikšić
• “Bratstvo i jedinstvo” Primary School – Rožaje
• “25. maj” Primary School – Rožaje
• “Pavle Žižić” Primary School – Bijelo Polje
• “Boško Buha” Primary School – Pljevlja
Although at some institutions the technical condition was found to be satisfactory, numerous findings pointed to significant failings that could seriously endanger the safety of pupils and staff: from damaged and unearthed sockets, improvised electrical connections and faulty lighting to the complete absence of lightning protection.
On the basis of the expert findings submitted, the Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation plans to invest additional funds in repairs and improvements where safety conditions are not at a satisfactory level. This response is a responsible institutional answer to the problems identified and an important step towards building a safer education system.
The Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro will continue with free campaigns of this kind in the period ahead, with the aim of securing a high level of protection in every school, so that children and staff can spend their days and work in a safe environment.
This initiative is not merely a response to a tragedy — it expresses a commitment to acting proactively, to building standards and to strengthening awareness of the importance of prevention in occupational safety and health. In the long run, systematic investment in the safety of schools is an investment in the future of our children and in the trust that educational institutions must enjoy in the eyes of parents, teachers and society as a whole.

title: Obuka zaposlenih u obrazovnim institucijama iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu i zaštite od požara - Bijelo Polje, 16. APRIL 2025.
excerpt: U Gimnaziji "Miloje Dobrašinović" u Bijelom Polju održana je 16. aprila 2025. obuka o zaštiti od požara i zaštiti na radu za 137 zaposlenih iz 50 obrazovnih i predškolskih ustanova sjevernog regiona.
content:
U srijedu, 16. aprila 2025. godine, u Gimnaziji „Miloje Dobrašinović“ u Bijelom Polju, realizovana je obuka za zaposlene u obrazovnim ustanovama na teme zaštite i zdravlja na radu i zaštita od požara u školama. Obuku je organizovalo Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore u saradnji sa Ministarstvom prosvjete, nauke i inovacija.
Ova obuka, kojoj je prisustvovalo 137 učesnika iz 50 škola i predškolskih ustanova sjevernog regiona Crne Gore, okupila je zaposlene sa različitih pozicija – od direktora, domara, vozača i ložača, do profesora, pedagoga, IT stručnjaka i medicinskih sestara. Upravo ta profesionalna raznolikost učesnika dala je dodatnu vrijednost obuci, jer su svi doprinosili diskusiji iz perspektive sopstvene prakse i radnih izazova.
Radionicu su vodili istaknuti stručnjaci u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu –Branislav Šebek i Zdenko Janković. U prvom dijelu radionice, Šebek je govorio o rizicima požara u školama i praktičnim aspektima bezbjedne evakuacije, dok je Janković predstavio ključne obaveze poslodavaca prema zakonu, ali i prava zaposlenih u oblasti zaštite na radu. Poseban akcenat bio je na tome da škole nijesu samo obrazovni prostori već kompleksi koji funkcionišu kao „male fabrike“ sa nizom potencijalnih rizika.
Učesnici su imali priliku da kroz praktičnu vježbu nauče kako da upotrebljavaju protivpožarne aparate, kao i pravilne reakcije u kriznim situacijama. Kroz teorijska izlaganja i otvorenu diskusiju, obrađena su brojna pitanja – od pravilnog postupanja u slučaju povrede, do zakonskih obaveza škole kada se radi o infrastrukturi i mjerama zaštite.
Obuka je još jednom potvrdila koliko je važno ulagati u kontinuiranu edukaciju zaposlenih, naročito u sektorima kao što je obrazovanje, gdje je bezbjednost učenika i osoblja od presudne važnosti. Jasno je da je znanje o zaštiti na radu više od tehničke obaveze – ono je preduslov za stvaranje sigurnog, dostojanstvenog i odgovornog radnog okruženja.
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore nastaviće sa sličnim aktivnostima širom zemlje, sa ciljem da svaki zaposleni, bez obzira na radno mjesto, bude informisan, obučen i zaštićen.
title_en: Training for staff of educational institutions in occupational safety and health and fire protection – Bijelo Polje, 16 April 2025
excerpt_en: On 16 April 2025 the “Miloje Dobrašinović” Grammar School in Bijelo Polje hosted training on fire protection and safety at work for 137 staff from 50 educational and pre-school institutions in the northern region.
content_en:
On Wednesday 16 April 2025, at the “Miloje Dobrašinović” Grammar School in Bijelo Polje, training was held for staff of educational institutions on occupational safety and health and fire protection in schools. The training was organised by the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro in cooperation with the Ministry of Education, Science and Innovation.
The training, attended by 137 participants from 50 schools and pre-school institutions in the northern region of Montenegro, brought together staff in a range of roles — from head teachers, caretakers, drivers and boiler operators to teachers, educational psychologists, IT specialists and nurses. That very diversity gave the training added value, since everyone contributed to the discussion from the perspective of their own practice and working challenges.
The workshop was led by two prominent specialists in occupational safety and health — Branislav Šebek and Zdenko Janković. In the first part, Šebek spoke about fire risks in schools and the practical aspects of safe evacuation, while Janković set out employers' key legal obligations and employees' rights in occupational safety. Particular emphasis was placed on the fact that schools are not merely places of education but complexes that function as “small factories” with a range of potential risks.
Through a practical exercise, participants learned how to use fire extinguishers and how to respond correctly in a crisis. Through the presentations and open discussion, a wide range of questions was covered — from the correct procedure in the event of an injury to a school's legal obligations regarding infrastructure and protective measures.
The training confirmed once again how important it is to invest in the continuous education of staff, particularly in sectors such as education, where the safety of pupils and staff is of decisive importance. It is clear that knowledge of safety at work is more than a technical obligation — it is a precondition for creating a safe, dignified and responsible working environment.
The Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro will continue with similar activities across the country, with the aim that every employee, whatever their role, should be informed, trained and protected.

title: 54. Regionalna akademija dostojanstvenog rada – Saradnja kao preduslov za napredak radnih prava28.11. do 01.12.2024.  Hotel Palmon Bay, Igalo
excerpt: UZNR CG je krajem novembra 2024. u Igalu, u saradnji sa Institutom za socijalnu politiku "Musine Kokalari" iz Prištine, Centrom za politike emancipacije iz Beograda i Udruženjem Zora iz Zenice, organizovalo Regionalnu akademiju dostojanstvenog rada sa 45 organizacija i sindikata i 60 učesnika.
content:
Ovogodišnja Regionalna akademija dostojanstvenog rada, koju je Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore organizovalo krajem novembra u saradnji sa Institutom za socijalnu politiku „Musine Kokalari“ iz Prištine, Centrom za politike emancipacije iz Beograda i Udruženjem za socijalni, kulturni i kreativni razvoj – ZORA iz Zenice, okupila je 45 organizacija i sindikata i 60 učesnika i učesnica. Konferenciju su otvorili predsjednik Instituta za socijalnu politiku „Musine Kokalari“ – Visar Ymeri i Đina Janković iz UZNR CG.
Tokom dva radna dana u Igalu razgovarali smo o saradnja sindikata i organizacija civilnog društva, zajedničkim kampanjama, razmenjivali iskustva o štrajkovima i pregovaračkim strategijama u borbi za zaštitu radnih prava. Teme koje smo pokrili tokom panel diskusija, predavanja i radionica uključivale su i rodnu ravnopravnost na tržištu rada, borbu za platu za život, zaštita i zdravlje na radu u kontekstvu klimatskih promjena, neplaćeni rad u domaćinstvu.
O važnost uključivanja socijalnih i radnih prava u „Zelenu agendu“ i uopšte bilo kakvo promišljanje održive budućnosti razgovarali smo sa Aleksandrom Kiković, predstavnicom UNDP za Crnu Goru, dok smo o Nemačkom zakonu o lancima snabdevanja i EU Direktivi o dužnoj pažnji i značaju ovih zakonskih okvira za region Zapadnog Balkana razgovarali sa Maren Lajfker (Maren Leifker) iz fondacije Brot für die Welt. Predsednik Novog sindikata iz Hrvatske, Mario Iveković, preneo je iskustva saradnje ovog sindikata sa organizacijama civilnog društva u borbi za radnička prava.
Tokom konferencije predstavljeni su i izveštaji o stanju radnih prava u pojedinačnim državama Zapadnog Balkana. Izveštaju su rađeni na osnovu indikatora dostojanstvenog rada Međunarodne organizacije rada, u saradnji sa Mariom Reljanovićem, naučnim saradnikom na Institutu za uporedno pravo u Beogradu.
Konferenciju smo organizovali kao nastavak regionalnog okupljanja koje smo započeli prošle godine u Draču, kada je 20 organizacija potpisalo Manifest o dostojanstvenom radu. Na ovogodišnjem skupu još 24 organizacije, među kojima je i 14 sindikata, potpisalo je Manifest i time pokazalo je svoju posvećenost regionalnoj borbi za bolje uslove života i rada.
Mreža organizacija koju u ovom procesu formiramo služiće u budućnosti kao platforma za jačanje regionalne saradnje, razmenu ideja i iskustava i razvoj zajedničke strategija koje će omogućiti unapređenje radnih i socijalnih prava na Zapadnom Balkanu. Regionalna solidarnost i povezivanje od ključnog su značaja za napredak naših društava.
U radu ovogodišnje Regionalne akademije dostojanstvenog rada iz Crne Gore su ove godine učestvovali predstavnice i predstavnici Saveza samostalnih sindikata Crne Gore, Sindikata uprave i pravosuđa Crne Gore, Unije slobodnih sindikata Crne Gore, Sindikata medija Crne Gore, NVO Prima i NVO KOD
Organizacija konferencije podržana je od strane European Fund for the Balkans i Western Balkan Fund.
Više o regionalnoj inicijativi možete pročitati na sajtu DecentWorkBalkans.com. gde se nalaze i izveštaji i stanju radnih prava na Zapadnom Balkanu.
title_en: 54th Regional Academy of Decent Work – Cooperation as a precondition for progress in labour rights, 28 November – 1 December 2024, Hotel Palmon Bay, Igalo
excerpt_en: In late November 2024, in Igalo, UZNR CG organised the Regional Academy of Decent Work together with the “Musine Kokalari” Institute for Social Policy from Pristina, the Centre for Politics of Emancipation from Belgrade and the Zora association from Zenica, bringing together 45 organisations and trade unions and 60 participants.
content_en:
This year's Regional Academy of Decent Work, organised in late November by the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro together with the “Musine Kokalari” Institute for Social Policy from Pristina, the Centre for Politics of Emancipation from Belgrade and the Association for Social, Cultural and Creative Development – ZORA from Zenica, brought together 45 organisations and trade unions and 60 participants. The conference was opened by the president of the “Musine Kokalari” Institute for Social Policy, Visar Ymeri, and by Đina Janković of UZNR CG.
Over two working days in Igalo we discussed cooperation between trade unions and civil society organisations and joint campaigns, and exchanged experience of strikes and negotiating strategies in the fight to protect labour rights. The topics covered in the panel discussions, lectures and workshops also included gender equality on the labour market, the fight for a living wage, occupational safety and health in the context of climate change, and unpaid domestic work.
We discussed the importance of including social and labour rights in the “Green Agenda” — and in any thinking about a sustainable future — with Aleksandra Kiković, UNDP's representative for Montenegro, while we discussed the German supply chain act and the EU due diligence directive and what these legal frameworks mean for the Western Balkans with Maren Leifker of the Brot für die Welt foundation. The president of Croatia's Novi sindikat, Mario Iveković, shared that union's experience of working with civil society organisations in the fight for workers' rights.
The conference also presented reports on the state of labour rights in the individual countries of the Western Balkans. The reports were produced on the basis of the International Labour Organization's decent work indicators, in cooperation with Mario Reljanović, research associate at the Institute of Comparative Law in Belgrade.
We organised the conference as a continuation of the regional gathering we began last year in Durrës, when 20 organisations signed the Manifesto on Decent Work. At this year's meeting a further 24 organisations, among them 14 trade unions, signed the Manifesto, demonstrating their commitment to the regional fight for better living and working conditions.
The network of organisations we are forming through this process will serve in future as a platform for strengthening regional cooperation, exchanging ideas and experience and developing joint strategies to advance labour and social rights in the Western Balkans. Regional solidarity and connection are of key importance to the progress of our societies.
Montenegro was represented at this year's Regional Academy of Decent Work by the Confederation of Independent Trade Unions of Montenegro, the Trade Union of Administration and Justice of Montenegro, the Union of Free Trade Unions of Montenegro, the Media Trade Union of Montenegro, the NGO Prima and the NGO KOD.
The conference was supported by the European Fund for the Balkans and the Western Balkans Fund.
You can read more about the regional initiative at DecentWorkBalkans.com, where the reports on the state of labour rights in the Western Balkans are also available.

title: Izveštaj o projektu „Akademija dostojanstvenog rada za Zapadni Balkan“ Tirana, 17. do 19. septembar 2024.
excerpt: Đina Janković je od 17. do 19. septembra 2024. boravila u Tirani na obuci za dobitnike granta u okviru projekta "Akademija dostojanstvenog rada za Zapadni Balkan", koji vodi Institut za socijalnu politiku "Musine Kokalari" iz Prištine.
content:
Projekat „Akademija dostojanstvenog rada za Zapadni Balkan“ pokrenut je kao rezultat uspješne aplikacije Instituta za socijalnu politiku Musine Kokalari iz Prištine za sredstva iz Fonda za Zapadni Balkan (Western Balkans Fund). Ovaj projekat je odobren, što znači da su sredstva za sprovođenje aktivnosti u okviru „The Decent Work Academy for Western Balkans“ obezbjeđena. Ovo odobrenje dolazi nakon šestomjesečnog procesa aplikacije, tokom kojeg je Institut za socijalnu politiku Musine Kokalari podnio predlog projekta sa ciljem promocije dostojanstvenog rada u regionu Zapadnog Balkana.
Priprema i obuka za dobitnike granta
U periodu od 17. do 19. septembra 2024. godine, Đina Janković, predstavnica Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, boravila je u Tirani. Tokom ovog boravka, Western Balkans Fund organizovao je obuku za dobitnike grantova, kao i svečanu ceremoniju dodjele sertifikata. Obuka je obuhvatala ključne aspekte upravljanja projektima i pravilno korišćenje sredstava, a sertifikati su uručeni svim predstavnicima odobrenih projekata.
Ciljevi i aktivnosti projekta
Cilj projekta „Akademija dostojanstvenog rada za Zapadni Balkan“ je podsticanje održivih regionalnih partnerstava i jačanje angažovanja organizacija civilnog društva u regionu, s naglaskom na promovisanje dostojanstvenog rada i održivih poslovnih praksi. Projekat je usklađen sa Direktivom EU o dužnoj pažnji u oblasti korporativne održivosti i ciljevima održivog razvoja (SDG 8 – Dostojanstven rad i ekonomski rast). Planirane aktivnosti obuhvataju održavanje regionalnih radionica, distribuciju edukativnih materijala i jačanje kapaciteta organizacija civilnog društva (OCD) kroz treninge i seminare.
Partneri u projektu
Institut za socijalnu politiku Musine Kokalari nosilac je ovog projekta, dok su partneri u projektu:
• Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore,
• NVO Centar za politike emancipacije iz Srbije,
• NVO Udruženje za socijalni, kulturni i kreativni razvoj Zora iz Bosne i Hercegovine.
Zajednički, ove organizacije će raditi na organizaciji regionalne akademije o dostojanstvenom radu, koja će okupiti učesnike iz svih šest zemalja Zapadnog Balkana (WB6). Glavna aktivnost ovog projekta biće organizacija više radionica tokom sedmomjesečnog perioda, koje će obuhvatiti približno 60 učesnika iz regiona.
Ključni aspekti projekta
Projekat dolazi u ključnom trenutku, budući da je Vlada Crne Gore, četiri dana prije početka aktivnosti na projektu, usvojila Program dostojanstvenog rada za period 2024-2027. Ovaj program predstavlja srednjoročni strateški okvir koji usmjerava rad Međunarodne organizacije rada (MOR) u Crnoj Gori, i bavi se izazovima poput visoke stope nezaposlenosti, unaprjeđenja radnih prava i jačanja zaštite i zdravlja na radu. U skladu sa ovim ciljevima, „Akademija dostojanstvenog rada za Zapadni Balkan“ ima za cilj da pruži podršku ovim naporima kroz regionalnu saradnju.
Planirane aktivnosti u okviru projekta
Cilj projekta je jačanje održivih regionalnih partnerstava i angažovanja civilnog društva, s naglaskom na dostojanstveni rad.
Aktivnosti uključuju:
• Uspostavljanje robustnog regionalnog okvira partnerstva sa najmanje 20 ključnih aktera (preduzeća, vlade i OCD).
• Održavanje onlajn sastanka partnera.
• Kreiranje i distribucija priručnika, smjernica i istraživačkih publikacija o kapacitetima, zelenoj agendi i uključivanju marginalizovanih grupa.
• Organizacija četiri regionalne radionice sa najmanje 80% zadovoljnih učesnika i pokretanje pet novih zajedničkih projekata.
• Razvoj modula za obuku.
• Organizacija i sprovođenje akademije u Crnoj Gori za 60 učesnika.
• Razvoj programa i agende.
• Sveobuhvatan program izgradnje kapaciteta za 60 OCD, s 75% učesnika koji izveštavaju o poboljšanim vještinama u zagovaranju održivih poslovnih praksi.
• Treninzi o zagovaranju u Beogradu.
• Podrška partnerstvima kroz sastanke i tehničku pomoć.
• Priručnik o održivim praksama, uz pozitivne povratne informacije korisnika.
• Kampanja za podizanje svijesti.
• Godišnji izvještaj sa analizom uspjeha i izazova, sa preporukama za dalje akcije.
Značaj projekta
Ovaj projekat ne samo da odgovara na trenutne izazove u oblasti zapošljavanja i socijalnog dijaloga, već omogućava i dugoročnu saradnju među organizacijama civilnog društva na regionalnom nivou. Takođe, kroz implementaciju ovog projekta, zemljama Zapadnog Balkana pruža se prilika da učestvuju u regionalnim inicijativama koje su u skladu sa evropskim direktivama i ciljevima održivog razvoja.
Projekat „Akademija dostojanstvenog rada za Zapadni Balkan“ teži da osnaži kapacitete civilnog društva u regionu, promoviše održive poslovne prakse, i podstakne dijalog između ključnih aktera na tržištu rada. Na taj način, doprinosi jačanju regionalne saradnje i unapređenju uslova rada u skladu sa evropskim standardima.
title_en: Report on the project “The Decent Work Academy for the Western Balkans”, Tirana, 17–19 September 2024
excerpt_en: From 17 to 19 September 2024 Đina Janković was in Tirana for training for grant recipients under the project “The Decent Work Academy for the Western Balkans”, led by the “Musine Kokalari” Institute for Social Policy from Pristina.
content_en:
The project “The Decent Work Academy for the Western Balkans” came about as the result of a successful application by the Musine Kokalari Institute for Social Policy from Pristina for funds from the Western Balkans Fund. The project was approved, which means the funds for carrying out the activities of “The Decent Work Academy for Western Balkans” are secured. The approval follows a six-month application process, during which the Musine Kokalari Institute for Social Policy submitted a project proposal aimed at promoting decent work in the Western Balkans.
Preparation and training for grant recipients
From 17 to 19 September 2024, Đina Janković, representing the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, was in Tirana. During the visit the Western Balkans Fund organised training for grant recipients and a formal certificate ceremony. The training covered the key aspects of project management and the proper use of funds, and certificates were presented to the representatives of all the approved projects.
Aims and activities of the project
The aim of the project “The Decent Work Academy for the Western Balkans” is to encourage sustainable regional partnerships and to strengthen the engagement of civil society organisations in the region, with an emphasis on promoting decent work and sustainable business practice. The project is aligned with the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive and with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth). The activities planned include regional workshops, the distribution of educational materials and capacity building for civil society organisations (CSOs) through training and seminars.
Project partners
The Musine Kokalari Institute for Social Policy leads the project, and the partners are:
• the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro,
• the NGO Centre for Politics of Emancipation from Serbia,
• the NGO Association for Social, Cultural and Creative Development Zora from Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Together these organisations will work on organising a regional academy on decent work, bringing together participants from all six Western Balkan countries (WB6). The project's main activity will be a series of workshops over a seven-month period, involving approximately 60 participants from the region.
Key aspects of the project
The project comes at a key moment, since four days before its activities began the Government of Montenegro adopted the Decent Work Country Programme for 2024–2027. That programme is a medium-term strategic framework guiding the work of the International Labour Organization (ILO) in Montenegro, addressing challenges such as high unemployment, the advancement of labour rights and the strengthening of occupational safety and health. In line with those aims, “The Decent Work Academy for the Western Balkans” sets out to support these efforts through regional cooperation.
Activities planned under the project
The project aims to strengthen sustainable regional partnerships and civil society engagement, with an emphasis on decent work.
The activities include:
• Establishing a robust regional partnership framework with at least 20 key actors (businesses, governments and CSOs).
• Holding an online partners' meeting.
• Producing and distributing handbooks, guidelines and research publications on capacity, the green agenda and the inclusion of marginalised groups.
• Organising four regional workshops with at least 80% of participants satisfied, and launching five new joint projects.
• Developing training modules.
• Organising and running the academy in Montenegro for 60 participants.
• Developing the programme and agenda.
• A comprehensive capacity-building programme for 60 CSOs, with 75% of participants reporting improved skills in advocating sustainable business practice.
• Advocacy training in Belgrade.
• Supporting partnerships through meetings and technical assistance.
• A handbook on sustainable practices, with positive feedback from users.
• An awareness-raising campaign.
• An annual report analysing successes and challenges, with recommendations for further action.
The significance of the project
The project not only responds to current challenges in employment and social dialogue but also enables long-term cooperation among civil society organisations at regional level. Through its implementation, the countries of the Western Balkans also have the opportunity to take part in regional initiatives aligned with European directives and the Sustainable Development Goals.
“The Decent Work Academy for the Western Balkans” seeks to strengthen the capacity of civil society in the region, to promote sustainable business practice and to encourage dialogue between key actors on the labour market. In doing so it helps strengthen regional cooperation and improve working conditions in line with European standards.

title: Druga Regionalna IPA konferencija: Nesreće na radnom mjestu 10-11. septembar 2024, Bukurešt
excerpt: U Bukureštu je od 10. do 11. septembra 2024. održana 2. IPA regionalna konferencija o nesrećama na radnom mjestu, u organizaciji EU-OSHA.
content:
U periodu od 10. do 11. septembra 2024. godine, u Bukureštu, Rumunija, održana je 2. IPA Regionalna konferencija na temu nesreća na radnom mjestu, u organizaciji EU OSHA. Konferencija je okupila stručnjake iz oblasti zaštite na radu, iz IPA zemalja i članica EU, kako bi razmjenili iskustva i diskusovali o prevenciji nesreća na radnom mestu. Ispred Crne Gore, na konferenciji su učestvovali Đina Janković iz Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, Zlatko Popović, glavni inspektor zaštite i zdravlja na radu, i Marina Blaletić, profesorica srednje stručne Elektrotehničke škole „Vaso Aligrudić“ – VET OSH ambasadorka.
Konferencija je započela prezentacijom Tima Tregenze, višeg menadžera mreže EU-OSHA, Michele Dinellia, menadžera IPA projekta EU-OSHA, i Doru Costin Darabonta, generalnog direktora INCDPM – FOP autoriteta. Glavna tema prvog dana bila je statistika i zakonodavni okvir za nesreće na radu u zemljama EU.
Tim Tregenza je predstavio statističke podatke o nesrećama na radu, dok je Michele Dinelli dao uvod u pravni okvir EU koji reguliše ovu oblast. Petru Mureșan s Univerziteta u Transilvaniji govorio je o iskustvima Rumunije u podizanju svijesti i borbi za smanjenje nesreća na radnom mjestu.
Maria José Tiago, inspektorka rada iz Portugala, predstavila je kampanju SLIC (Senior Labour Inspectors’ Committee) o nesrećama na radu. Padraic McMahon, viši inspektor iz Irske, govorio je o procesu istrage nesreća na radu u Irskoj, sa naglaskom na metodologiju i izazove u sprovođenju istraga.
Diskusija i sesija pitanja i odgovora sa svim govornicima zatvorila je prvi dan konferencije.
Drugi dan konferencije fokusirao se na razmjenu iskustava o inspekcijama u vezi sa prevencijom nesreća na radu. Michele Dinelli je otvorio dan, a govornici iz IPA zemalja predstavili su svoje institucionalne prioritete i strategije.
Predstavnici iz Turske, Albanije, Bosne i Hercegovine i Kosova govorili su o nacionalnim sistemima prijavljivanja nesreća i analizama podataka o nesrećama na radu. Učesnici iz Crne Gore, Đina Janković i Zlatko Popović, zajedno sa Marinom Blaletić, istakli su izazove i iskustva Crne Gore u vezi sa prijavljivanjem nesreća i njihovom prevencijom. Posebno su naglasili potrebu za unapređenjem svijesti o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu i boljoj obuci zaposlenih, mentalnom zdravlju, ali i o važnosti edukacija iz ove oblasti u obrazovnim institucijama, posebno u srednjim stručnim školama.
Diskusije su se dotakle i inspekcijskih strategija i prioriteta u različitim sektorima, sa fokusom na visoko rizične grupe radnika, kao što su radnici u obrazovanju, zdravstvu i migranti.
Sesija pitanja i odgovora omogućila je interakciju učesnika i razmjenu najboljih praksi, dok je završni dio dana bio rezervisan za iskustva iz NDICI zemalja i zaključke konferencije.
Konferencija je zaključena sa jasnim porukama o potrebi za jačanjem međunarodne saradnje u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kao i važnosti prevencije nesreća na radnom mjestu kroz edukaciju, inspekcijske aktivnosti i implementaciju efikasnih zakonskih okvira. Crnogorska delegacija dala je značajan doprinos razmjenom svojih iskustava, naglašavajući potrebu za dodatnim ulaganjima u podizanje svijesti o važnosti zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
title_en: Second Regional IPA conference: Accidents at work, 10–11 September 2024, Bucharest
excerpt_en: From 10 to 11 September 2024 Bucharest hosted the 2nd IPA regional conference on accidents at work, organised by EU-OSHA.
content_en:
From 10 to 11 September 2024, in Bucharest, Romania, the 2nd IPA Regional Conference on accidents at work was held, organised by EU-OSHA. The conference brought together occupational safety specialists from the IPA countries and EU member states to exchange experience and discuss the prevention of accidents at work. Montenegro was represented by Đina Janković of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, Zlatko Popović, chief occupational safety and health inspector, and Marina Blaletić, a teacher at the “Vaso Aligrudić” secondary electrical engineering school and a VET OSH ambassador.
