The conference opened with presentations by Tim Tregenza, senior network manager at EU-OSHA, Michele Dinelli, manager of EU-OSHA's IPA project, and Doru Costin Darabont, director general of INCDPM – the FOP authority. The main theme of the first day was statistics and the legislative framework for accidents at work in EU countries.
Tim Tregenza presented statistical data on accidents at work, while Michele Dinelli gave an introduction to the EU legal framework governing the field. Petru Mureșan of Transilvania University spoke about Romania's experience in raising awareness and working to reduce accidents at work.
Maria José Tiago, a labour inspector from Portugal, presented the SLIC (Senior Labour Inspectors' Committee) campaign on accidents at work. Padraic McMahon, a senior inspector from Ireland, spoke about the process of investigating accidents at work in Ireland, focusing on methodology and the challenges of carrying out investigations.
A discussion and question-and-answer session with all the speakers closed the first day of the conference.
The second day focused on exchanging experience of inspections relating to the prevention of accidents at work. Michele Dinelli opened the day, and speakers from the IPA countries presented their institutional priorities and strategies.
Representatives from Türkiye, Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Kosovo spoke about national systems for reporting accidents and about the analysis of accident data. The participants from Montenegro, Đina Janković and Zlatko Popović, together with Marina Blaletić, highlighted Montenegro's challenges and experience in reporting accidents and preventing them. They emphasised in particular the need to raise awareness of occupational safety and health and to train employees better, the importance of mental health, and the importance of education in this field in educational institutions, particularly in secondary vocational schools.
The discussions also touched on inspection strategies and priorities in different sectors, focusing on high-risk groups of workers such as those in education and health care and migrant workers.
The question-and-answer session allowed participants to interact and exchange best practice, while the closing part of the day was given over to experience from the NDICI countries and to the conference's conclusions.
The conference closed with clear messages about the need to strengthen international cooperation in occupational safety and health and about the importance of preventing accidents at work through education, inspection and the implementation of effective legal frameworks. The Montenegrin delegation made a significant contribution by sharing its experience, emphasising the need for further investment in raising awareness of the importance of occupational safety and health.

title: Konferencija o kancerogenim i mutagenim materijamaBrisel, 11. do 14. jun 2024.
excerpt: Đina Janković je predstavljala UZNR CG na konferenciji u Briselu, održanoj od 11. do 14. juna 2024, posvećenoj lansiranju Roadmap on Carcinogens 3.0 - evropske inicijative za smanjenje izloženosti kancerogenima na radnom mjestu.
content:
U periodu od 11. do 14. juna 2024. godine, u Briselu je održana konferecija Roadmaponcarcinogens, u okviru evropske inicijative koja je u proteklih nekoliko godina podigla svijest o rizicima od izlaganja kancerogenima na radnom mjestu. Takođe je doprinijela razmjeni i promociji dobrih praksi između kompanija i organizacija kako bi se spriječilo izlaganje kancerogenima na radu.
Konferenciji je, ispred Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, prisustvovala Đina Janković.
Događaj je obilježen formalnim lansiranjem Roadmap on Carcinogens 3.0 (Mapa puta kancerogenih materija). Kao dio novog sporazuma, 9 država članica EU, kao i BusinessEurope, CES – ETUC, Evropska agencija za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu (EU-OSHA), Evropska agencija za hemikalije i belgijsko predsjedavanje Savjetu Evropske unije 2024. godine, obnovili su svoju posvećenost ovoj dobrovoljnoj šemi djelovanja EU.
Zakonodavne i ne-zakonodavne mjere za borbu protiv kancera povezanog s radom i zaštitu zaposlenih od rizika po njihovo zdravlje i bezbjednost usljed izlaganja kancerogenima, mutagenima ili reprotoksičnim supstancama na radnom mjestu, mogu značajno poboljšati živote mnogih zaposlenih, ali ono što se trenutno vidi je tek vrh ledenog brijega. Prevencija profesionalnog kancera mora se temeljiti na savremenim naučnim i tehničkim podacima, a rješavanje ovog problema zahtijeva zajednički napor vlada, socijalnih partnera, stručnjaka, poslodavaca i zaposlenih, što je razlog zašto su podrške inicijativama poput ove neophodne.
title_en: Conference on carcinogenic and mutagenic substances, Brussels, 11–14 June 2024
excerpt_en: Đina Janković represented UZNR CG at a conference in Brussels from 11 to 14 June 2024, devoted to the launch of Roadmap on Carcinogens 3.0 — the European initiative to reduce exposure to carcinogens at work.
content_en:
From 11 to 14 June 2024 the Roadmap on Carcinogens conference was held in Brussels, as part of a European initiative that over the past few years has raised awareness of the risks of exposure to carcinogens at the workplace. It has also encouraged the exchange and promotion of good practice between companies and organisations in order to prevent exposure to carcinogens at work.
Đina Janković attended on behalf of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro.
The event was marked by the formal launch of Roadmap on Carcinogens 3.0. As part of the new agreement, 9 EU member states, together with BusinessEurope, ETUC, the European Agency for Safety and Health at Work (EU-OSHA), the European Chemicals Agency and the 2024 Belgian Presidency of the Council of the European Union, renewed their commitment to this voluntary EU action scheme.
Legislative and non-legislative measures to combat work-related cancer and to protect employees from risks to their health and safety arising from exposure to carcinogens, mutagens or reprotoxic substances at the workplace can significantly improve the lives of a great many employees, but what is visible at present is only the tip of the iceberg. The prevention of occupational cancer must be founded on current scientific and technical evidence, and tackling the problem requires a joint effort by governments, the social partners, experts, employers and employees — which is why support for initiatives like this one is essential.

title: EU-OSHA participates at a workshop on EU OSH policies in Podgorica, Montenegro
excerpt: EU-OSHA je 28. maja 2024. učestvovala na radionici o EU OSH politikama u Podgorici, koju su organizovali Uprava za inspekcijske poslove i NVO Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore (SWAM).
content:
On 28 May 2024, EU-OSHA participated at the workshop on „EU OSH policies“ organised by the Administration of Inspection Affairs, EU-OSHA Focal point of Montenegro, and the NGO „Safety at Work Association of Montenegro“ (SWAM). The workshop had the aim to raise awareness on the EU and EUMS OSH practices; as well as on the importance of social dialogue and the involvement of national social partners in the policy making process to strengthen the prevention of OSH risks in the workplace.
The workshop was opened by interventions from Darko Rašović, deputy director of the Administration of Inspection Affairs, Michele Dinelli, EU-OSHA IPA project manager, and Birgitte Kuchar, EUD to Montenegro project manager, who all underlined the importance of tripartism. Afterwards, Ivan Williams, IOSH, presented the global OSH framework and the support to knowledge sharing provided by IOSH; Michele Dinelli, EU-OSHA, explained how the Agency strategy and work programme are tailored to the EU OSH Strategic Framework 2021-2027, and he introduced the main EU OSH principles deriving from the EU framework directive; Károly Győrgy, former international secretary of the Hungarian Trade Union Confederation, underlined the importance of social dialogue and shared important practical experiences regarding the OSH tripartite system; Đina Janković, who was also acting as event moderator, underlined the work done by SWAM in supporting OSH dialogue at national level and within the Region, through the support of EU funded projects and through the regional network BalkanOSH, and stressed the importance of raising OSH awareness among students; finally, Zlatko Popović, FOP manager, shared information on the work of the Administration for Inspection Affairs within the context of supporting compliance and the implementation of the EU OSH legislation in Montenegro. Following the presentations, the audience had the possibility to raise questions and to seek for advice from the panel on how to best implement social dialogue. The audience was represented by social partners’ representatives (trade union and employers’ associations) and one representative from the ministry of Health. No attendance was registered from the ministry of Labour.

title: "EU radionica o podizanju javne svijesti u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu" 28. maj 2024.
excerpt: Istog dana, 28. maja 2024, održana je i "EU radionica o podizanju javne svijesti u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu", u organizaciji EU-OSHA, Uprave za inspekcijske poslove i UZNR CG.
content:
Održana je radionica pod nazivom „EU radionica o podizanju javne svijesti u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu“, koja je okupila stručnjake iz Evropske unije i Crne Gore kako bi razmijenili znanja i iskustva u ovoj važnoj oblasti. Radionicu su organizovali EU OSHA, Uprava za inspekcijske poslove i Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore.
Povod za organizaciju ove radionice bila je prepoznata potreba za usklađivanjem sa zakonodavstvom i standardima EU u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Ovo je posebno značajno s obzirom na aktuelne izmjene i dopune Zakona o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu u Crnoj Gori, ali i ubrzavanja procesa neophodnih za zatvaranje Poglavlja 19. Cilj je bio da se osiguraju zdraviji i bezbjedniji radni uslovi za sve zaposlene.
Među predavačima su bili vodeći stručnjaci iz Evropske agencije za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu, Delegacije EU u Crnoj Gori, međunarodne Unije sindikata, kao i predstavnici crnogorskih institucija. Michele Dinelli iz EU OSHA, Brigitte Kuchar iz Delegacije EU u Crnoj Gori, Dr. Iván Williams Jiménez iz IOSH, Károly György, bivši međunarodni sekretar Mađarske sindikalne konfederacije, Đina Janković iz Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore i Zlatko Popović, glavni inspektor Uprave za inspekcijske poslove, dali su svoje uvide i preporuke.
Radionica je zaključila da je uspostavljanje visokih standarda zaštite i zdravlja na radu u Crnoj Gori ključna za ispunjenje EU zahtjeva i poboljšanje radnih uslova. Posebno su istaknute sljedeće oblasti:
1. Usklađivanje sa EU standardima: Potrebno je striktno pridržavanje EU smjernica i regulativa, kao i kontinuirano ažuriranje nacionalnog zakonodavstva.
2. Regulisanje izveštavanja i statistike: Pouzdani podaci i efikasna medicina rada su od suštinske važnosti za regulisanje profesionalnih bolesti.
3. Socijalni dijalog: Ključan za razvoj i implementaciju efikasnih politika zaštite na radu.
4. Edukacija i podizanje svijesti: Neophodna je za efikasnu primjenu zakona i standarda, uz redovne treninge i seminare za zaposlene, poslodavce, stručna lica iz oblasti ZZNR, inspektore ZZNR.
5. Primjeri dobre prakse iz EU: Pomažu u smanjenju povreda na radu i profesionalnih oboljenja.
6. Poboljšanje inspekcijskih mehanizama: Jačanje kapaciteta inspekcijskih službi i obezbeđivanje adekvatnih resursa za inspektore.
Preporučeno je i razvijanje nacionalnog programa zaštite na radu, kontinuirana edukacija i trening, osnivanje Savjeta za ZZNR, podsticanje inovacija i tehnološkog napretka, jačanje inspekcijskih službi i aktivno učešće zaposlenih.
Radionica je podvukla važnost adekvatne zaštite i zdravlja na radu kao preduslova za bezbjedno i produktivno radno okruženje u Crnoj Gori, naglašavajući da su trenutne zakonodavne promjene idealna prilika za uvođenje trajnih i efikasnih rešenja u ovoj oblasti.
title_en: “EU workshop on raising public awareness of occupational safety and health”, 28 May 2024
excerpt_en: On the same day, 28 May 2024, the “EU workshop on raising public awareness of occupational safety and health” was also held, organised by EU-OSHA, the Administration of Inspection Affairs and UZNR CG.
content_en:
A workshop entitled “EU workshop on raising public awareness of occupational safety and health” was held, bringing together experts from the European Union and Montenegro to exchange knowledge and experience in this important field. The workshop was organised by EU-OSHA, the Administration of Inspection Affairs and the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro.
The workshop was prompted by the recognised need to align with EU legislation and standards in occupational safety and health. This is particularly significant given the current amendments to the Law on Occupational Safety and Health in Montenegro and the need to accelerate the steps required to close Chapter 19. The aim was to secure healthier and safer working conditions for all employees.
The speakers included leading experts from the European Agency for Safety and Health at Work, the EU Delegation to Montenegro and the international trade union confederation, as well as representatives of Montenegrin institutions. Michele Dinelli of EU-OSHA, Brigitte Kuchar of the EU Delegation to Montenegro, Dr Iván Williams Jiménez of IOSH, Károly György, former international secretary of the Hungarian Trade Union Confederation, Đina Janković of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro and Zlatko Popović, chief inspector at the Administration of Inspection Affairs, all offered their insights and recommendations.
The workshop concluded that establishing high standards of occupational safety and health in Montenegro is key to meeting EU requirements and improving working conditions. The following areas were highlighted in particular:
1. Alignment with EU standards: strict adherence to EU guidance and regulations is needed, as is the continuous updating of national legislation.
2. Regulating reporting and statistics: reliable data and effective occupational medicine are essential to the regulation of occupational diseases.
3. Social dialogue: key to developing and implementing effective occupational safety policy.
4. Education and awareness-raising: essential to the effective application of the law and of standards, with regular training and seminars for employees, employers, OSH professionals and OSH inspectors.
5. Examples of good practice from the EU: they help reduce injuries at work and occupational diseases.
6. Improving inspection mechanisms: strengthening the capacity of the inspection services and providing inspectors with adequate resources.
It was also recommended that a national occupational safety programme be developed, that education and training be continuous, that a Council for OSH be established, that innovation and technological progress be encouraged, that the inspection services be strengthened and that employees take an active part.
The workshop underlined the importance of adequate occupational safety and health as a precondition for a safe, productive working environment in Montenegro, emphasising that the current legislative changes are an ideal opportunity to introduce lasting, effective solutions in this field.

title: Savjetovanje ‘’Unapređenje kvaliteta u sprovođenju ZZNR - važan korak ka članstvu u EU’’  24. do 26. april 2024. godine, hotel Palas, Petrovac
excerpt: Od 24. do 26. aprila 2024. u hotelu Palas u Petrovcu održano je savjetovanje "Unapređenje kvaliteta u sprovođenju ZZNR - važan korak ka članstvu u EU", u organizaciji UZNR CG i Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja, sa 96 stručnjaka.
content:
U periodu od 24. do 26. aprila 2024. godine održano je savjetovanje pod nazivom „Unapređenje kvaliteta u sprovođenju ZZNR – važan korak ka članstvu u EU“. Organizatori ovog značajnog događaja bili su Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore i Ministarstvo rada i socijalnog staranja Crne Gore.
Savjetovanje je okupilo 96 stručnjaka iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, uključujući predstavnike poslodavaca, inspektore, profesore sa relevantnih fakulteta, doktore medicine rada, kao i eksperte iz Crne Gore i regiona. Cilj savjetovanja bio je identifikacija nedostataka i izazova u sprovođenju Zakona o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu kako bi se ispunili standardi i zahtjevi EU, te osiguralo zdravije i bezbjednije radno okruženje za sve zaposlene u Crnoj Gori.
Tokom trodnevnog savjetovanja, učesnici su imali priliku da se upoznaju sa najnovijim trendovima i praksama u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kao i da razmjene iskustva sa kolegama iz struke. Ključne teme koje su obuhvaćene bile su procedure za procjenu profesionalnog rizika, učešće stručnih lica u osposobljavanju za bezbjedan rad, izgradnja kulture rada u skladu sa zakonskim obavezama i uticaj psihosocijalnih rizika na bezbjednost i zdravlje zaposlenih, kao i uloga doktora medicine rada.
Predavači na savjetovanju bili su vodeći stručnjaci iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, uključujući profesore sa Fakulteta zaštite na radu u Nišu, Fakulteta tehničkih nauka u Novom Sadu i medicinskog fakulteta u Skoplju, kao i predstavnike struke iz Hrvatske, Srbije i Makedonije, Uprave za inspekcijske poslove i Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja.
Tokom panel diskusija, interaktivnih sesija i predavanja, učesnici su aktivno učestvovali u razmatranju ključnih pitanja i izazova sa kojima se susreću u praksi. Dinamične diskusije doprinijele su boljem razumijevanju suštinske uloge stručnih lica u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kao i podizanju svijesti o važnosti ovog segmenta za radno okruženje.
Zaključci Savjetovanja su ključni za dalji razvoj i implementaciju politika zaštite i zdravlja na radu u Crnoj Gori.
Neki od ključnih zaključaka:
1. Identifikacija važnosti stručnih lica: Prepoznato je da stručna lica imaju ključnu ulogu u sprovođenju ZZNR radi obezbjeđivanja sigurnog i zdravog radnog okruženja. Njihovo aktivno učešće u savjetovanju, kao i potreba za kontinuiranom obukom i podrškom, istaknuta su kao prioritet.
2. Saradnja i odgovornost poslodavaca: Naglašena je odgovornost poslodavaca u izgradnji kulture rada u kojoj se poštuju sve obaveze prema Zakonu o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu. Ovo uključuje ulaganje u obuku zaposlenih, procjenu profesionalnih rizika i podršku stručnim licima.
3. Potreba za unapređenjem praksi i procedura: Prepoznata je potreba za usklađivanjem praksi i procedura sa najnovijim standardima i zahtjevima EU. Ovo uključuje uspostavljanje efikasnih mehanizama za procjenu i upravljanje rizicima, kao i pravilnu dokumentaciju i izvještavanje.
4. Razmjena iskustava i edukacija: Važnost razmjene iskustava i kontinuirane edukacije u oblasti zaštite na radu istaknuta je kao ključni faktor za unapređenje kvaliteta sprovođenja ZZNR. Savjetovanje je pružilo platformu za ove aktivnosti i potrebno je nastaviti slične inicijative u budućnosti.
5. Angažovanje relevantnih aktera: Kako bi se ostvarili napredak i implementacija zakonskih zahtjeva, važno je dalje angažovati relevantne aktere, uključujući stručnjake iz akademske zajednice, predstavnike Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja, inspekcije, sindikata i poslodavaca.
Zaključno, Savjetovanje je označilo važan korak ka unapređenju kvaliteta sprovođenja ZZNR u Crnoj Gori, ali kontinuirani napor.
Zaključno, prisustvo i aktivno učešće svih učesnika na savjetovanju doprinijeli su ostvarenju postavljenih ciljeva, ali i podsjetili na neophodnost ulaganja kontinuiranih napora uz saradnju svih relevantnih aktera, za postizanje punog uspjeha u ovoj ključnoj oblasti. Očekuje se da će predložene mjere i strategije, koje su proizašle iz ovog skupa, biti od velike koristi u unapređenju kvaliteta sprovođenja ZZNR u Crnoj Gori.
title_en: Conference “Improving the quality of OSH implementation – an important step towards EU membership”, 24–26 April 2024, Hotel Palas, Petrovac
excerpt_en: From 24 to 26 April 2024 the Hotel Palas in Petrovac hosted the conference “Improving the quality of OSH implementation – an important step towards EU membership”, organised by UZNR CG and the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare, with 96 specialists taking part.
content_en:
From 24 to 26 April 2024 a conference was held under the title “Improving the quality of OSH implementation – an important step towards EU membership”. It was organised by the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro and the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare of Montenegro.
The conference brought together 96 specialists in occupational safety and health, including employers' representatives, inspectors, professors from relevant faculties, occupational medicine doctors and experts from Montenegro and the region. Its aim was to identify the shortcomings and challenges in implementing the Law on Occupational Safety and Health, so that EU standards and requirements can be met and a healthier, safer working environment secured for everyone employed in Montenegro.
Over the three days, participants had the opportunity to learn about the latest trends and practice in occupational safety and health and to exchange experience with colleagues in the field. The key topics covered were procedures for assessing occupational risk, the involvement of safety professionals in training for safe work, building a working culture that complies with legal obligations, the effect of psychosocial risks on employees' safety and health, and the role of occupational medicine doctors.
The speakers were leading specialists in occupational safety and health, including professors from the Faculty of Occupational Safety in Niš, the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad and the medical faculty in Skopje, as well as practitioners from Croatia, Serbia and North Macedonia and representatives of the Administration of Inspection Affairs and the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare.
Through panel discussions, interactive sessions and presentations, participants took an active part in considering the key questions and challenges they meet in practice. The lively discussions led to a better understanding of the essential role of safety professionals in occupational safety and health and raised awareness of the importance of this field for the working environment.
The conference's conclusions are key to the further development and implementation of occupational safety and health policy in Montenegro.
Some of the key conclusions:
1. Recognising the importance of safety professionals: it was recognised that safety professionals have a key role in implementing OSH in order to secure a safe and healthy working environment. Their active participation in the conference, and the need for continuous training and support, were highlighted as a priority.
2. Cooperation and the responsibility of employers: the responsibility of employers to build a working culture in which all the obligations under the Law on Occupational Safety and Health are respected was emphasised. This includes investing in employee training, assessing occupational risks and supporting safety professionals.
3. The need to improve practice and procedures: the need to align practice and procedures with the latest EU standards and requirements was recognised. This includes establishing effective mechanisms for assessing and managing risk and proper documentation and reporting.
4. Exchange of experience and education: the importance of exchanging experience and of continuous education in occupational safety was highlighted as a key factor in improving the quality of OSH implementation. The conference provided a platform for this, and similar initiatives should continue in future.
5. Engaging the relevant actors: in order to make progress and implement the legal requirements, it is important to continue engaging the relevant actors, including experts from the academic community, representatives of the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare, the inspectorates, the trade unions and employers.
In conclusion, the conference marked an important step towards improving the quality of OSH implementation in Montenegro, but continuous effort is required.
In conclusion, the presence and active participation of everyone at the conference helped achieve the objectives set, while also serving as a reminder that continuous effort and cooperation between all the relevant actors are essential to full success in this key field. The measures and strategies proposed at the meeting are expected to be of great use in improving the quality of OSH implementation in Montenegro.

title: Nagrada „Naj menadžerka u Crnoj Gori“ za 2023. godinu
excerpt: Generalna sekretarka UZNR CG Đina Janković dobitnica je nagrade „Naj menadžerka u Crnoj Gori“ za 2023. godinu, koju dodjeljuju Unija poslodavaca Crne Gore, Skupština Glavnog grada Podgorice i Međunarodna organizacija rada.
content:
Sa velikim ponosom ističemo da je naša Đina Janković ovogodišnja laureatkinja prestižne nagrade „NAJ MENADŽERKA U CRNOJ GORI“ za 2023. godinu! Ovo izvanredno priznanje se dodjeljuje od strane Unije poslodavaca Crne Gore, Skupštine Glavnog grada Podgorica i Međunarodne organizacije rada.
Tom prilikom je organizovana konferencija „Žene u menadžmentu – snaga promjena i ekonomskog napretka“, koja je imala za cilj da promocijom uspješnih poslovnih žena u Crnoj Gori dodatno ukaže na ulogu, snagu i potencijal ženskog liderstva, kao i značaj većeg učešća žena na pozicijama upravljanja i rukovođenja.
Događaj su otvorili predsjednik UPCG 𝐒𝐥𝐨𝐛𝐨𝐝𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐢𝐤𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐜𝐚, predsjednica Skupštine Glavnog grada Podgorica 𝐉𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐚 𝐁𝐨𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐢ć 𝐁𝐨𝐣𝐨𝐯𝐢ć i nacionalna koordinatorka ILO-a 𝐍𝐢𝐧𝐚 𝐊𝐫𝐠𝐨𝐯𝐢ć.
Radni dio konferencije otvorila je guvernerka Centralne banke Crne Gore 𝐝𝐫 𝐈𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐚 𝐑𝐚𝐝𝐨𝐯𝐢ć koja je održala uvodno izlaganje na temu „Više žena u menadžmentu: Put do ravnopravnosti i ekonomskog razvoja“.
U nastavku je održan panel „Žene u menadžmentu u Crnoj Gori: Stanje i perspektive“ u kojem su učestvovale ministarka Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja 𝐍𝐚𝐢𝐝𝐚 𝐍𝐢š𝐢ć, samostalna savjetnica, iz Ministarstva ekonomskog razvoja 𝐀𝐧𝐚 Š𝐞𝐛𝐞𝐤, nacionalna projektna koordinatorka #ILO 𝐝𝐫 𝐈𝐧𝐞𝐬 𝐏𝐚𝐣𝐨𝐯𝐢ć i predsjednica Asocijacija poslovnih zena Crne Gore/Business Women Association Montenegro 𝐋𝐣𝐮𝐛𝐢𝐜𝐚 𝐊𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐢ć 𝐁𝐮𝐤𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚.
U okviru svečane ceremonije, dodijeljene su 𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐞 #UPCG „𝐍𝐀𝐉 𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐝ž𝐞𝐫𝐤𝐞 𝐮 𝐂𝐫𝐧𝐨𝐣 𝐆𝐨𝐫𝐢“ za 2023. godinu. Za laureatkinje UPCG proglašeno je osam uspješnih poslovnih žena – dobitnica nagrada u sledećim kategorijama: Privreda, Javni sektor, Civilni sektor i Mediji.
title_en: The “Top Woman Manager in Montenegro” award for 2023
excerpt_en: UZNR CG's secretary general Đina Janković has won the “Top Woman Manager in Montenegro” award for 2023, presented by the Employers' Union of Montenegro, the Assembly of the Capital City of Podgorica and the International Labour Organization.
content_en:
It is with great pride that we announce that our own Đina Janković is this year's winner of the prestigious “TOP WOMAN MANAGER IN MONTENEGRO” award for 2023. This outstanding recognition is presented by the Employers' Union of Montenegro, the Assembly of the Capital City of Podgorica and the International Labour Organization.
The award was accompanied by a conference, “Women in management – a force for change and economic progress”, which set out to promote successful businesswomen in Montenegro and thereby highlight the role, strength and potential of women's leadership and the importance of greater participation by women in management and leadership positions.
The event was opened by the president of the Employers' Union of Montenegro, 𝐒𝐥𝐨𝐛𝐨𝐝𝐚𝐧 𝐌𝐢𝐤𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐜𝐚, the president of the Assembly of the Capital City of Podgorica, 𝐉𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐚 𝐁𝐨𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐢ć 𝐁𝐨𝐣𝐨𝐯𝐢ć, and the ILO's national coordinator, 𝐍𝐢𝐧𝐚 𝐊𝐫𝐠𝐨𝐯𝐢ć.
The working part of the conference was opened by the governor of the Central Bank of Montenegro, 𝐝𝐫 𝐈𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐚 𝐑𝐚𝐝𝐨𝐯𝐢ć, who gave the keynote address on “More women in management: the path to equality and economic development”.
There followed a panel on “Women in management in Montenegro: the situation and the prospects”, with the Minister of Labour and Social Welfare 𝐍𝐚𝐢𝐝𝐚 𝐍𝐢š𝐢ć, independent adviser at the Ministry of Economic Development 𝐀𝐧𝐚 Š𝐞𝐛𝐞𝐤, #ILO national project coordinator 𝐝𝐫 𝐈𝐧𝐞𝐬 𝐏𝐚𝐣𝐨𝐯𝐢ć and the president of the Business Women Association Montenegro 𝐋𝐣𝐮𝐛𝐢𝐜𝐚 𝐊𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐢ć 𝐁𝐮𝐤𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐚.
At the formal ceremony the #UPCG “𝐓𝐎𝐏 𝐰𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐧 𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐠𝐫𝐨” awards for 2023 were presented. Eight successful businesswomen were named as laureates, receiving awards in the following categories: Business, Public sector, Civil sector and Media.

title: Sastanak predstavnika UZNR CG i Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja
excerpt: Predstavnici UZNR CG i Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja sastali su se 13. marta 2024. kako bi dogovorili zajedničku organizaciju savjetovanja o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu povodom 28. aprila.
content:
Sastanak predstavnika Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore i predstavnika Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja
13.03.2024.
U današnjem globalnom kontekstu, zaštita i zdravlje na radu predstavljaju esencijalne elemente socijalne politike svake države. U Crnoj Gori, ova tema postaje sve značajnija s obzirom na napore države ka evropskim integracijama i unapređenju standarda rada. Upravo u tom kontekstu, održan je sastanak između predstavnika Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja – ministarke Naide Nišić, sekretara ministarstva Adisa Pepića i direktora Direktorata za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu Aleksandra Memčevića i Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore - predsjednika Zdenka Jankovića i generalne sekretarke Đine Janković.
Centralni fokus sastanka je bilo zajedničko organizovanje Savjetovanja iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, koje će se održati od 24. do 26. aprila, povodom Svjetskog dana zaštite i zdravlja na radu, u hotelu Palas u Petrovcu. Ministarka će otvoriti ovaj skup, a prisustvo ministarke prosvjete je takođe predloženo, imajući u vidu neophodnost uvođenja zaštite i zdravlja na radu u obrazovni sistem Crne Gore.
Jedan od ključnih momenata sastanka je bio na naglašavanju važnosti formalizacije i unapređenja saradnje između Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja i Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kroz potpisivanje Memoranduma o saradnji, čiji bi opšti cilj bio zalaganje za efikasnije funkcionisanje sistema zaštite i zdravlja na radu u zemlji, kao i unapređivanje politika u ovoj oblasti u skladu sa evropskim standardima. Obje strane su se složile da je neophodno uspostaviti bolje partnerske odnose i sarađivati na projektima koji će doprinijeti poboljšanju stanja u ovoj oblasti.
Posebni ciljevi saradnje su istaknuti kao ključni elementi koji će definisati konkretne aktivnosti. To uključuje zajedničko praćenje, proučavanje i podsticanje unapređenja zaštite i zdravlja na radu, identifikovanje potreba i realizaciju projekata koji će unaprijediti kvalitet rada stručnih lica i ovlašćenih organizacija iz ove oblasti, kao i edukaciju zaposlenih i poslodavaca.
Takođe, istaknuta je važnost Strategije za unapređenje zaštite i zdravlja na radu 2022-2027. godine i njenog Akcionog plana. Sagovornici su se složili da je neophodno raditi na stvaranju okvira koji će omogućiti efikasnu primjenu strateških ciljeva.
U zaključku, sastanak je bio izuzetno produktivan, a dogovoreno potpisivanje Memoranduma o saradnji predstavlja važan korak ka unapređenju zaštite i zdravlja na radu u Crnoj Gori. Očekuje se da će implementacija ovog Memoranduma doprinijeti ostvarivanju evropskih standarda i podizanju nivoa zaštite na radu, što će imati pozitivan uticaj na sve slojeve društva.
title_en: Meeting between representatives of UZNR CG and the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare
excerpt_en: On 13 March 2024 representatives of UZNR CG and the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare met to agree on jointly organising a conference on occupational safety and health to mark 28 April.
content_en:
Meeting between representatives of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro and representatives of the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare
13 March 2024
In today's global context, occupational safety and health is an essential element of any country's social policy. In Montenegro the subject is becoming ever more significant given the country's efforts towards European integration and improved labour standards. It was in that context that a meeting was held between representatives of the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare — Minister Naida Nišić, the ministry's secretary Adis Pepić and the director of the Directorate for Occupational Safety and Health Aleksandar Memčević — and the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, represented by its president Zdenko Janković and secretary general Đina Janković.
The central focus of the meeting was the joint organisation of a conference on occupational safety and health, to be held from 24 to 26 April to mark World Day for Safety and Health at Work, at the Hotel Palas in Petrovac. The Minister will open the event, and the attendance of the Minister of Education was also proposed, given the need to introduce occupational safety and health into Montenegro's education system.
One of the key moments of the meeting was the emphasis on formalising and strengthening cooperation between the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare and the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro in occupational safety and health, through the signing of a Memorandum of Cooperation whose general aim would be to work for a more effective occupational safety and health system in the country and to improve policy in this field in line with European standards. Both sides agreed on the need to establish better partnership and to work together on projects that will improve the situation in this field.
The specific aims of the cooperation were highlighted as the key elements that will define concrete activities. They include jointly monitoring, studying and encouraging improvements in occupational safety and health, identifying needs and carrying out projects that will improve the quality of the work of safety professionals and licensed organisations in this field, and educating employees and employers.
The importance of the Strategy for Improving Occupational Safety and Health 2022–2027 and its Action Plan was also emphasised. Participants agreed on the need to work on creating a framework that will allow the strategic objectives to be applied effectively.
In conclusion, the meeting was highly productive, and the agreement to sign a Memorandum of Cooperation is an important step towards improving occupational safety and health in Montenegro. Implementing the Memorandum is expected to help achieve European standards and raise the level of safety at work, which will have a positive effect on every part of society.

title: Završna konferencija „Iza kamere ispred zdravlja: Novinarski životni vijek u sjenci rizika“
excerpt: UZNR CG i MADOP predstavili su 28. februara 2024. rezultate prvog istraživanja u Crnoj Gori o psihosocijalnim rizicima kojima su izloženi novinari i zaposleni u medijima.
content:
Dana 28. februara 2024. godine održana je završna konferencija posvećena prezentaciji rezultata istraživanja i Studije nastale u okviru projekta „Iza kamere ispred zdravlja: Novinarski životni vijek u sjenci rizika“. Ovaj projekat je predstavljao pionirski korak u istraživanju psihosocijalnih rizika koji značajno utiču na kvalitet života, zdravlje i dužinu radnog i životnog vijeka novinara i novinarki u Crnoj Gori. Važno je naglasiti da je ovo istraživanje prvo ovakve vrste koje je sprovedeno u Crnoj Gori, čime je postavljena značajna osnova za dalje razumijevanje i unapređenje zdravlja novinara.
Konferenciji je prisustvovalo 34 učesnika, uključujući zaposlene u medijima i predstavnike relevantnih ministarstava, inspekcijskih organa, Instituta za javno zdravlje, Uprave za statistiku i organizacija civilnog društva. Ovo široko učešće pokazuje visok stepen interesovanja i važnost tema koje su bile predmet istraživanja.
Gospodin Milan Radović iz Građanske Aliejnse, u ime donatora, pozdravio je prisutne i predstavio projekat „Bez nekažnjivosti za povredu i kršenje ljudskih prava u Crnoj Gori“, koji doprinosi borbi za ljudska prava u zemlji i jačanje demokratije, a koji se sprovodi u saradnji sa Beogradskim centrom za ljudska prava i Međunarodnom komisijom pravnika.
Đina Janković, u ime MADOP-a u UZNR CG, detaljno je prezentovala aktivnosti realizovane u okviru projekta „Iza kamere ispred zdravlja“ tokom prethodnih 6 mjeseci. Naglasila je važnost istraživanja u razumijevanju dubokih slojeva problema s kojima se novinari suočavaju, kao i potrebu za daljim koracima ka rješavanju tih problema.
Dražen Đurašković iz Sindikata medija Crne Gore je iznio rezultate istraživanja koji su ukazali na alarmantno stanje u vezi sa zaštitom i zdravljem na radu zaposlenih u medijima. Posebno je istaknuto da samo 20% zaposlenih u medijima ima adekvatno razumijevanje koncepta zaštite i zdravlja na radu, što zahtijeva hitne intervencije.
Predsjednik Sindikata medija Crne Gore, Radomir Kračković, govorio je o različitim rizicima sa kojima se novinari suočavaju, ističući nedovoljnu pažnju koja se posvećuje ovom pitanju i neophodnost konkretnih akcija kako bi se zaštitili zaposleni.
Snežana Ivanović iz Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja je istakla brojne psihosocijalne rizike sa kojima se zaposleni u javnim institucijama, posebno u PR službama i biroima za odnose s javnošću, suočavaju svakodnevno. Podvukla je potrebu za sveobuhvatnim pristupom zaštiti zdravlja zaposlenih.
Kroz analizu stresa, pritiska, prijetnji i nesigurnosti s kojima se novinari suočavaju, istraživanje je imalo za cilj osvijetliti dublje slojeve problema i podstaknuti na konkretne akcije i rješenja.
Predstavljeni su egzaktni podaci i nalazi do kojih se došlo, koji ukazuju na sistemske manjkavosti u sprovođenju cilja zaštite zdravlja zaposlenih u medijskom sektoru. Diskutovano je o preporukama i koracima ka unapređenju situacije.
Zaključno, istaknuto je da zaštita i zdravlje na radu ne smiju se posmatrati isključivo kao pravna obaveza, već kao odgovornost poslovanja. Investiranje u sigurnost zaposlenih donosi dugoročne koristi kroz povećanje produktivnosti, zadovoljstvo zaposlenih i održivost organizacije. Naglašeno je da su zaštita i zdravlje na radu i procjena rizika za zaposlene u medijima važne iz najmanje tri razloga:
1. Sigurnost zaposlenih
U medijskom sektoru, gdje novinari često rade na terenu, izlažući se različitim rizicima, procjena rizika i zaštita i zdravlje na radu postaju izuzetno važni. Identifikacija i procjena potencijalnih opasnosti, bilo da su to fizički rizici na terenu ili digitalni rizici vezani uz onlajn sigurnost, omogućuju poslodavcima stvaranje strategija zaštite kojima se minimalizuju rizici po zaposlene. Ovo je posebno ključno u situacijama gdje novinari izvještavaju iz konfliktnih područja ili rade na pričama koje uključuju izloženost opasnostima.
2. Očuvanje slobode medija
Zaštita i zdravlje na radu u medijima takođe doprinosi očuvanju slobode medija. Novinari, kamermani i drugi profesionalci u medijima često se suočavaju s izazovima kao što su prijetnje, fizički napadi ili digitalni napadi s ciljem ograničavanja njihove slobode izražavanja. Postojanje jasnih sigurnosnih protokola i zaštitnih mjera ne samo da štiti novinare, već i osigurava neometano izvještavanje o relevantnim temama, čime se čuva ključna uloga medija u demokratskom društvu.
3. Reputacija i odgovornost medijskih organizacija
Organizacije u medijskom sektoru koje ozbiljno pristupaju procjeni rizika i zaštiti na radu ne samo da čuvaju svoje zaposlene, već i čuvaju svoju reputaciju. Negativni događaji vezani uz povrede ili sigurnosne propuste mogu imati ozbiljne posljedice po imidž medijske kuće. Stvaranje sigurnog radnog okruženja pokazuje odgovornost prema zaposlenima i društvu te doprinosi izgradnji pozitivne percepcije organizacije. Sveukupno, važnost procjene rizika i zaštite i zdravlja na radu u medijima odražava se na ljudske aspekte, slobodu medija i poslovnu reputaciju.
Na kraju je prezentovano 11 preporuka, koje su proizašle iz ovog istraživanja i koje će biti dostavljene i prezentovane donosiocima odluka.
1. Obuke i edukacija
Neophodno je kreirati i implementirati plan redovne obuke novinara i ostalih zaposlenih u medijima o specifičnim rizicima u ovoj branši, s posebnim naglaskom na rad na terenu, sigurnosti digitalnog novinarstva i postupcima u vanrednim situacijama.
2. Bezbjednosni protokoli
Neophodno je razvijanje i redovno ažuriranje protokola koji obuhvataju sve aspekte rada u medijima.
3. Zaštitna oprema
Osiguranje odgovarajuće zaštitne opreme, poput prsluka s oznakama, kaciga, rukavica i drugih sredstava potrebnih za rad u opasnim uslovima.
4. Psihološka podrška
Uspostavljanje servisa za podršku zaposlenima u svrhu pružanja psihološog savjetovanja.
5. Pravna zaštita
Osiguranje pravne zaštite za novinare, uključujući informacije o njihovim pravima, pravne savjete u vezi s izvještavanjem o kontroverznim temama i potrebne procedure u slučaju pravnih napada.
6. Evaluacija i povratne informacije
Redovna evaluacija implementiranih mjera kroz povratne informacije zaposlenih, izvještavanje o incidentima i prilagođavanje protokola stvarnim potrebama i promjenama u radnom okruženju.
7. Promovisanje kulture bezbjednosti
Razvijanje kulture bezbjednosti koja podstiče svijest o važnosti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, odgovornog ponašanja i međusobne podrške među zaposlenima.
8. Izmjene i dopune Zakona o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu i podzakonskih akata
Izmjene su neophodne kako bi se obezbjedilo adekvatno adresiranje psihosocijalnih rizika na radnom mjestu. Trenutna praksa ne uključuje odgovarajuću procjenu ovih rizika, što stvara ozbiljne nedostatke u zaštiti zdravlja i bezbjednosti zaposlenih. Stoga, preporučuje se detaljna revizija zakona i podzakonske regulative kako bi se obezbjedilo da psihosocijalni rizici budu uključeni i na odgovarajući način tretirani u okviru sistema zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Ovo će pružiti bolju zaštitu zaposlenih od potencijalnih štetnih uticaja na njihovo mentalno i emocionalno zdravlje tokom obavljanja radnih aktivnosti.
9.Provjera kvaliteta Akta o procjeni rizika
Neophodno je da se sprovede kontrola urađenih Akata o procjeni rizika u medisjkim organizacijama, ukoliko su oni donijeti.
10. Imenovanje zaposlenih za zaštitu na radu
Neophodno je da svi poslodavci u medijima imenuju zaposlene za zaštitu na radu i otvore dijalog sa predstavnicima zaposlenih o ovom pitanju.
11. Procjena psihosocijalnih rizika zaposlenih u PR službama i biroima za odnose s javnošću
Procjena psihosocijalnih rizika zaposlenih u PR službama i biroima za odnose s javnošću je bitna jer omogućava prepoznavanje potencijalnih izvora stresa, pritiska i konflikata na radnom mjestu. To pomaže u identifikaciji faktora koji mogu negativno uticati na mentalno i emocionalno zdravlje zaposlenih. Takođe, takva procjena omogućava implementaciju preventivnih mjera i intervencija kako bi se obezbjedilo zdravo radno okruženje i smanjio rizik od burnouta, depresije i drugih mentalnih problema. Ovo je važno ne samo za dobrobit zaposlenih već i za produktivnost organizacije i očuvanje njenog ugleda i odnosa s javnošću.
Projekat „Iza kamere, ispred zdravlja: Novinarski životni vijek u sjenci rizika“, koji realizuje #MADOP u saradnji sa Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore / SWAM, podržan je kroz poziv „Bez nekažnjivosti za kršenje i povredu ljudskih prava u Crnoj Gori - IPA/2022/439-819“, koji sprovode Gradjanska alijansa, Beogradski centar za ljudska prava|BCHR i Međunarodna komisija pravnika.
Projekat finansira EU i Ministarstvo javne uprave u Crnoj Gori.
title_en: Closing conference “Behind the camera, ahead of health: a journalist's working life in the shadow of risk”
excerpt_en: On 28 February 2024 UZNR CG and MADOP presented the results of the first research in Montenegro into the psychosocial risks that journalists and media workers are exposed to.
content_en:
On 28 February 2024 a closing conference was held to present the results of the research and the study produced under the project “Behind the camera, ahead of health: a journalist's working life in the shadow of risk”. The project was a pioneering step in researching the psychosocial risks that significantly affect the quality of life, the health and the length of the working life and life expectancy of journalists in Montenegro. It should be emphasised that this is the first research of its kind carried out in Montenegro, laying an important foundation for further understanding and improvement of journalists' health.
The conference was attended by 34 participants, including media workers and representatives of the relevant ministries, the inspection authorities, the Institute of Public Health, the Statistical Office and civil society organisations. This broad participation shows the high level of interest in, and the importance of, the topics the research addressed.
Milan Radović of Civic Alliance, on behalf of the donor, welcomed those present and introduced the project “No impunity for violations and abuses of human rights in Montenegro”, which contributes to the fight for human rights in the country and to the strengthening of democracy, and which is carried out in cooperation with the Belgrade Centre for Human Rights and the International Commission of Jurists.
Đina Janković, on behalf of MADOP at UZNR CG, presented in detail the activities carried out under the project “Behind the camera, ahead of health” over the previous 6 months. She emphasised the importance of the research in understanding the deeper layers of the problems journalists face, and the need for further steps to solve them.
Dražen Đurašković of the Media Trade Union of Montenegro presented the research findings, which pointed to an alarming situation as regards the occupational safety and health of media workers. It was noted in particular that only 20% of media workers have an adequate understanding of occupational safety and health, which calls for urgent intervention.
The president of the Media Trade Union of Montenegro, Radomir Kračković, spoke about the various risks journalists face, emphasising the insufficient attention paid to the issue and the need for concrete action to protect employees.
Snežana Ivanović of the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare highlighted the many psychosocial risks that employees in public institutions, particularly in PR services and public relations offices, face every day. She stressed the need for a comprehensive approach to protecting employees' health.
Through its analysis of the stress, pressure, threats and insecurity journalists face, the research set out to shed light on the deeper layers of the problem and to prompt concrete action and solutions.
Exact data and findings were presented, pointing to systemic shortcomings in efforts to protect the health of employees in the media sector. Recommendations and steps towards improving the situation were discussed.
In conclusion, it was emphasised that occupational safety and health must not be seen solely as a legal obligation but as a business responsibility. Investing in employees' safety brings long-term benefits through higher productivity, greater employee satisfaction and the sustainability of the organisation. It was emphasised that occupational safety and health and risk assessment for media workers matter for at least three reasons:
1. Employee safety
In the media sector, where journalists often work in the field and are exposed to a range of risks, risk assessment and occupational safety and health become extremely important. Identifying and assessing potential dangers — whether physical risks in the field or digital risks relating to online security — allows employers to create protective strategies that minimise the risks to employees. This is particularly crucial where journalists report from conflict areas or work on stories that expose them to danger.
2. Preserving media freedom
Occupational safety and health in the media also helps preserve media freedom. Journalists, camera operators and other media professionals often face challenges such as threats, physical attacks or digital attacks aimed at restricting their freedom of expression. Clear safety protocols and protective measures not only protect journalists but also ensure that reporting on important subjects can continue unhindered, preserving the media's key role in a democratic society.
3. The reputation and responsibility of media organisations
Organisations in the media sector that take risk assessment and safety at work seriously protect not only their employees but also their own reputation. Negative events involving injuries or safety failures can have serious consequences for a media house's image. Creating a safe working environment shows responsibility towards employees and towards society and helps build a positive perception of the organisation. Overall, the importance of risk assessment and occupational safety and health in the media is reflected in human terms, in media freedom and in business reputation.
Finally, 11 recommendations arising from the research were presented, to be submitted and presented to decision-makers.
1. Training and education
A plan must be created and implemented for regular training of journalists and other media workers on the specific risks of this industry, with particular emphasis on fieldwork, the security of digital journalism and procedures in emergencies.
2. Safety protocols
Protocols covering every aspect of media work must be developed and regularly updated.
3. Protective equipment
Appropriate protective equipment must be provided, such as marked vests, helmets, gloves and other items needed for work in dangerous conditions.
4. Psychological support
A support service should be established to provide employees with psychological counselling.
5. Legal protection
Legal protection must be provided for journalists, including information about their rights, legal advice on reporting controversial subjects and the necessary procedures in the event of legal attacks.
6. Evaluation and feedback
The measures implemented should be regularly evaluated through employee feedback, incident reporting and the adaptation of protocols to real needs and to changes in the working environment.
7. Promoting a safety culture
A safety culture should be developed that fosters awareness of the importance of occupational safety and health, responsible behaviour and mutual support among employees.
8. Amendments to the Law on Occupational Safety and Health and to secondary legislation
Amendments are essential to ensure that psychosocial risks at the workplace are adequately addressed. Current practice does not include a proper assessment of these risks, which creates serious gaps in the protection of employees' health and safety. A detailed revision of the law and the secondary legislation is therefore recommended, so that psychosocial risks are included and properly treated within the occupational safety and health system. This will give employees better protection from the potential harm to their mental and emotional health that their work can cause.
9. Checking the quality of risk assessment acts
The risk assessment acts produced by media organisations, where they exist, must be checked.
10. Appointing employees responsible for safety at work
All employers in the media must appoint employees responsible for safety at work and open a dialogue with employees' representatives on the subject.
11. Assessing the psychosocial risks facing employees in PR services and public relations offices
Assessing the psychosocial risks facing employees in PR services and public relations offices matters because it makes it possible to identify potential sources of stress, pressure and conflict at the workplace. This helps identify the factors that can harm employees' mental and emotional health. Such an assessment also makes it possible to implement preventive measures and interventions to secure a healthy working environment and reduce the risk of burnout, depression and other mental health problems. This matters not only for employees' wellbeing but also for the organisation's productivity and for preserving its reputation and public relations.
The project “Behind the camera, ahead of health: a journalist's working life in the shadow of risk”, carried out by #MADOP in cooperation with the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro / SWAM, is supported through the call “No impunity for violations and abuses of human rights in Montenegro – IPA/2022/439-819”, implemented by Civic Alliance, the Belgrade Centre for Human Rights | BCHR and the International Commission of Jurists.
The project is financed by the EU and the Ministry of Public Administration of Montenegro.

title: Sastanak Upravnog odbora UZNR CG (februar 2024)
excerpt: Upravni odbor UZNR CG održao je 23. februara 2024. sastanak na kojem je usvojeno formiranje tri nove stručne komisije Udruženja i dogovorena organizacija aprilskog savjetovanja.
content:
Dana 23.02.2024. godine održan je sastanak Upravnog odbora, sa sljedećim dnevnim redom:
1. Verifikacija članova Upravnog odbora i potpredsjednika
2. Usvajanje komisija UZNR CG kao stručnih tijela
3. Organizacija Savjetovanja iz ZZNR povodom 28. aprila i formiranje organizacionog odbora
4. Dogovor oko organizacije sastanka sa MRSS oko zajedničkih ingerencija.
5. Razno
Sastanku su prisustvovali: Rajko Radusinović, Anđa Strugar, Zdenko Janković, Sanja Dujović, Branislav Šebek, Klara Vuletić (umjesto člana UO Igora Bakića), Andrijana Kaljević, Zlatko Popović i Đina Janković. Ostali članovi UO: Dušan Bjelica, Miroslav Jaredić, Radmila Mićović, Marko Burić, Boško Radulović, Filip Lopičić i Milorad Terzić, iz opravdanih razloga nisu bili u mogućnosti da prisustvuju sastanku.
Jednoglasno je usvojen dnevni red i verifikovani članovi Upravnog odbora
Usvojen je predlog da se, na nivou Udruženja, formiraju stručna tijela:
1. Komisija za rješavanje spornih pitanja iz oblasti ZZNR
2. Komisija za kontroju kvaliteta i cijena usluga iz oblasti ZZNR
3. Komisija za saradnju sa državnim organima i organizaciju edukacija iz ZZNR
Ovi predlozi će biti dostavljene svim članovima Udruženja kako bi imali priliku da se izjasne i predlože sebe ili nekoga od kolega, ko bi mogao dati najveći doprinos u radu ovih komisija. Zdenko se obavezao da će u narednom periodu uraditi pravilnike o radu komisija
Kao i mnogo puta ranije, diskusija je vođena i oko načina i kvaliteta izrade Akta o procjeni rizika, koji je prema mišljenju svih prisutnih često vrlo upitan pa su se usaglasili da jedna od aktivnosti Udruženja u narednom periodu mora biti usmjerena na provjeru kvaliteta rada ovlašćenih orgnaizacija.
Kada je u pitanju često prisutno „dampingovanje“ cijena usluga, koje u najvećoj mjeri utiče na stalno slabljenje kvaliteta usluga, bez obzira na postojanje potrebe za usvajanje univerzalnog cjenovnika, najveći broj prisutnih je bio mišljenja da bi tako nešto bilo gotovo nemoguće uzimajući u obzir činjenicu da je donošenjem Zakona o prestanku važenja Zakona o društvenoj kontroli cijena, koji je stupio na snagu 2006. godine, propisano slobodno formiranje cijena na tržištu, čime je Vladi ili bilo kojem drugom tijelu onemogućeno da vrši uticaj na cjenovnu politiku.
Rješenje ovog problema bi se moglo postići kroz izmjene Zakona o javnim nabavkama i dodavanjem/vraćanjem člana kojim se definiše da se, prilikom razmatranja ponuda, ne uzimaju u razmatranje najmanja i najveća cijena/ponuda.
Shodno tome, neophodno je da Udruženje podnese Inicijativu za izmjene Zakona o javnim nabavkama. Važno se naglasiti da ovo dovodi do problema u svim oblastima, a ne samo u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
Predloženo je da se, u narednom periodu, napravi plan procjene psihosocijalnih rizika. Ovo je zanemarivana tema kojoj se u razvijenim zemljama posvećuje posebna pažnja pa je i od strane EU OSHA-e prepoznato kao jedan od najvećih problema kojem treba posvetiti posebnu pažnju i kroz kampanje i aktivnosti, u naredne dvije godine, djelovati u cilju podizanja svijesti. Na izradi plana o procjeni psihosocijalnih rizika će raditi Zdenko Janković, Zlatko Popović i Đina Janković.
Kada je u pitanju organizacija Savjetovanja/Konferencije iz ZZNR povodom 28. aprila, potvrđeno je da će događaj biti organizovan prema unaprijed predloženom i usvojenom programu, u periodu od 24. do 26. aprila, u hotelu Palas, u Petrovcu. Zdenko i Đina su podijelili utiske sa sastanka koji je održan 16.02.2024. u Ministartvu rada i socijalnog staranja, sa predstavnicima Direkcije za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu, kao i sa sastanka koji je održan prije toga 13.02.2024. sa direktorom Direktorata za rad i radne odnose – Aleksandrem Memčevićem. Najvažniji zaključak oba sastanka je bio taj da će Ministartvo rada i socijalnog staranja biti jedan od suorganizatora planirane konferencije.
Uzimajući u obzir velike probleme, koji se javljaju u praksi, zbog neadekvatnog funkcionisanja medicine rada, značajno je da, u skladu s predloženim programom, jedna od tema bude posvećena upravo medicini rada, ali njihovo učešće će zavisiti od raspoloženja i raspoloživosti vremena samih doktora medicine rada, kako je dr Marko Burić informisao Đinu u komunikaciji koju su imali u prethodnom periodu.
Gostujući predavači na konferenciji će biti sa Fakulteta zaštite na radu u Nišu – prof. dr Ivan Krstić i sa Fakulteta tehničkih nauka u Novom Sadu – prof. dr Bojana Zoraja.
O standardizaciji i uvođenju standarda, kroz iskustvo u kompaniji Tarkett, koja ima preko 2500 zaposlenih, će govoriti Miodrag Meseldžija. On će kroz prezentaciju Sistemski pristup i standardizacija u organizaciji poslova zaštite i zdravlja na radu u kompaniji podijeliti iskustva iz regiona, a o tome kakva je praksa kod nas u Crnoj Gori, predloženo je da govori neko iz EPCG. Andrijana Kaljević će razgovarati sa svojim pretpostavljenima i iznijeto ovaj predlog Velimiru Strugaru.
Dogovor oko toga ko će iz Udruženja biti predavač po ostalim predloženim temama će biti napravljen u narednom periodu, a nakon toga će biti sačinjena draft agenda, koja će moći da se šalje uz pozivno pismo potencijalnim učesnicima konferencije.
title_en: Meeting of the UZNR CG Management Board (February 2024)
excerpt_en: On 23 February 2024 the UZNR CG Management Board met and adopted the formation of three new expert committees, and agreed the organisation of the April conference.
content_en:
On 23 February 2024 a meeting of the Management Board was held, with the following agenda:
1. Verification of the members of the Management Board and of the vice-presidents
2. Adoption of UZNR CG's committees as expert bodies
3. Organisation of the OSH conference marking 28 April and formation of an organising committee
4. Agreement on organising a meeting with the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare on shared responsibilities
5. Any other business
The meeting was attended by: Rajko Radusinović, Anđa Strugar, Zdenko Janković, Sanja Dujović, Branislav Šebek, Klara Vuletić (in place of board member Igor Bakić), Andrijana Kaljević, Zlatko Popović and Đina Janković. The other board members — Dušan Bjelica, Miroslav Jaredić, Radmila Mićović, Marko Burić, Boško Radulović, Filip Lopičić and Milorad Terzić — were unable to attend for good reason.
The agenda was adopted unanimously and the members of the Management Board verified.
The proposal to form expert bodies at the level of the Association was adopted:
1. Committee for resolving disputed questions in OSH
2. Committee for monitoring the quality and prices of OSH services
3. Committee for cooperation with state bodies and the organisation of OSH training
These proposals will be sent to all members of the Association so that they can give their views and put themselves or a colleague forward as someone who could contribute most to the work of these committees. Zdenko undertook to draw up rules of procedure for the committees in the period ahead.
As on many previous occasions, there was discussion of the way risk assessment acts are produced and of their quality, which in the view of everyone present is often highly questionable; they agreed that one of the Association's activities in the period ahead must be directed at checking the quality of the work of licensed organisations.
On the frequent “dumping” of service prices, which more than anything else drives the continuing decline in the quality of services, most of those present took the view that — despite the need for a universal price list — such a thing would be all but impossible, given that the Law repealing the Law on Social Control of Prices, which came into force in 2006, provides for the free formation of prices on the market, leaving the Government or any other body unable to influence pricing policy.
A solution to this problem could be found through amendments to the Law on Public Procurement, by adding or restoring a provision stating that the lowest and highest price or bid are not taken into consideration when bids are assessed.
Accordingly, the Association must submit an initiative to amend the Law on Public Procurement. It is important to emphasise that this causes problems in every field, not only in occupational safety and health.
It was proposed that a plan for assessing psychosocial risks be drawn up in the period ahead. This is a neglected subject to which developed countries pay particular attention, and EU-OSHA too has recognised it as one of the greatest problems requiring particular attention and action over the next two years through campaigns and activities aimed at raising awareness. Zdenko Janković, Zlatko Popović and Đina Janković will work on the plan for assessing psychosocial risks.
As regards the organisation of the OSH conference marking 28 April, it was confirmed that the event will be organised according to the programme previously proposed and adopted, from 24 to 26 April at the Hotel Palas in Petrovac. Zdenko and Đina shared their impressions of the meeting held on 16 February 2024 at the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare with representatives of the Directorate for Occupational Safety and Health, and of the meeting held before that, on 13 February 2024, with the director of the Directorate for Labour and Employment Relations, Aleksandar Memčević. The most important conclusion of both meetings was that the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare will be one of the co-organisers of the planned conference.
Given the major problems that arise in practice because occupational medicine does not function adequately, it is significant that, in line with the proposed programme, one of the topics should be devoted to occupational medicine — though their participation will depend on the willingness and availability of the occupational medicine doctors themselves, as Dr Marko Burić informed Đina in their earlier correspondence.
The guest speakers at the conference will be Professor Ivan Krstić of the Faculty of Occupational Safety in Niš and Professor Bojana Zoraja of the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad.
Miodrag Meseldžija will speak about standardisation and the introduction of standards, drawing on experience at the company Tarkett, which has more than 2,500 employees. Through his presentation “A systematic approach and standardisation in organising occupational safety and health work in a company” he will share experience from the region, and it was proposed that someone from EPCG speak about practice here in Montenegro. Andrijana Kaljević will discuss this with her superiors and put the proposal to Velimir Strugar.
Agreement on who from the Association will speak on the other proposed topics will be reached in the period ahead, after which a draft agenda will be produced and can be sent with the letter of invitation to potential participants.

title: Obuka za zaposlene u medijima iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu
excerpt: MADOP i UZNR CG organizovali su 6. februara 2024. obuku o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu za 30 novinara, u okviru projekta „Iza kamere ispred zdravlja“.
content:
U okviru projekta „Iza kamere ispred zdravlja: Novinarski životni vijek u sjenci rizika“, koji realizuje Mreža za afirmaciju društveno odgovornog poslovanja – MADOP i Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore organizovana je obuka za zaposlene u medijima iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
Obuci koja je održana 06.02.2024. prisustvovalo je 30 novinara.
Obuku su voditi eksperti iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu: Zlatko Popović, glavni inspeltot zaštite i zdravlja na radu, Đina Janković iz Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore i Dragana Đokić. psihološkinja/psohoterapeutkinja s bogatim iskustvom u ovoj oblasti.
Glavni cilj obuke je bilo osvješćivanje zaposlenih u medijima o psihosocijalnim rizicima i izazovima sa kojima se novinari i ostali zaposleni u medijima suočavaju, uzimajući u obzir činjenicu da često rade u teškim uslovima, izloženi pritiscima, prijetnjama i nasilju. Nedostatak efikasne zaštite novinara i druga kršenja njihovih prava dodatno otežava situaciju. Novinarska profesija nosi sa sobom specifične probleme i prepreke koji utiču na dužinu životnog vijeka novinara. Stres, tortura, psihosocijalni rizici i drugi izazovi imaju ozbiljan uticaj na njihovo fizičko i mentalno zdravlje, što rezultira skraćenjem životnog vijeka i visokom stopom umiranja u mladim godinama. Ova tema je često zanemarena, iako ima ozbiljne posljedice po novinare i novinarstvo u Crnoj Gori uopšte.
Povećanje svijesti o tim problemima i njihova adekvatna adresacija su ključni za jačanje demokratije, vladavine prava i zaštite ljudskih prava u zemlji. Stoga, cilj je bio da se istakne važnost zaštite novinara i njihovih prava, te da se podstaknu relevantne institucije da preduzmu konkretne korake za poboljšanje radnih uslova novinara i smanjenje psihosocijalnih rizika.
Takođe, bitno je bilo da se sami novinari, kao i ostali zaposleni u medijima, upoznaju sa različitim rizicima, poput psiho-socijalnih rizika, uticaja stresa, burnout-a i načinima na koje mogu upravljati njima, kao i o zakonskoj regulativi u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, obavezama i odgovornostima poslodavaca, kao i pravima i odgovornostima zaposlenih.
Projekat „Iza kamere, ispred zdravlja: Novinarski životni vijek u sjenci rizika“, koji realizuje #MADOP u saradnji sa Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore / SWAM, podržan je kroz poziv „Bez nekažnjivosti za kršenje i povredu ljudskih prava u Crnoj Gori - IPA/2022/439-819“, koji sprovode Gradjanska alijansa, Beogradski centar za ljudska prava|BCHR i Međunarodna komisija pravnika.
Projekat finansira EU i djelom Ministarstvo javne uprave u Crnoj Gori.
title_en: Occupational safety and health training for media workers
excerpt_en: On 6 February 2024 MADOP and UZNR CG organised occupational safety and health training for 30 journalists, under the project “Behind the camera, ahead of health”.
content_en:
Under the project “Behind the camera, ahead of health: a journalist's working life in the shadow of risk”, carried out by the Network for the Affirmation of Socially Responsible Business – MADOP and the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, occupational safety and health training was organised for media workers.
The training, held on 6 February 2024, was attended by 30 journalists.
It was led by specialists in occupational safety and health: Zlatko Popović, chief occupational safety and health inspector, Đina Janković of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, and Dragana Đokić, a psychologist and psychotherapist with extensive experience in the field.
The main aim of the training was to raise media workers' awareness of the psychosocial risks and challenges journalists and other media employees face, given that they often work in difficult conditions, exposed to pressure, threats and violence. The lack of effective protection for journalists and other violations of their rights make the situation worse. The journalistic profession carries specific problems and obstacles that affect journalists' life expectancy. Stress, harassment, psychosocial risks and other challenges have a serious effect on their physical and mental health, resulting in a shortened lifespan and a high rate of death at a young age. This subject is often neglected, even though it has serious consequences for journalists and for journalism in Montenegro as a whole.
Raising awareness of these problems and addressing them properly is key to strengthening democracy, the rule of law and the protection of human rights in the country. The aim was therefore to highlight the importance of protecting journalists and their rights and to encourage the relevant institutions to take concrete steps to improve journalists' working conditions and reduce psychosocial risks.
It was also important for journalists themselves, and other media workers, to learn about the various risks — psychosocial risks, the effects of stress, burnout and how to manage them — and about the legislation on occupational safety and health, employers' obligations and responsibilities and employees' rights and responsibilities.
The project “Behind the camera, ahead of health: a journalist's working life in the shadow of risk”, carried out by #MADOP in cooperation with the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro / SWAM, is supported through the call “No impunity for violations and abuses of human rights in Montenegro – IPA/2022/439-819”, implemented by Civic Alliance, the Belgrade Centre for Human Rights | BCHR and the International Commission of Jurists.
The project is financed by the EU and in part by the Ministry of Public Administration of Montenegro.

title: Sastanak sa predstavnicima Unije poslodavaca (januar 2024)
excerpt: UZNR CG je 22. januara 2024. održalo sastanak sa Unijom poslodavaca o radnim pravima mladih i mogućnostima jačanja saradnje na podizanju svijesti poslodavaca o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu.
content:
Dana 22. januara 2024. godine održan je važan sastanak sa predstavnicima Unije poslodavaca, okupljajući relevantne aktere sa ciljem istraživanja pitanja radnih prava mladih, njihove zaštite, kao i promocije zdravlja na radu.
Sastanku su prisustvovali ključni predstavnici organizacija i udruženja posvećenih ovim temama:
1. Đina Janković, projektna menadžerka Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore,
2. Rumica Kostić, Šefica Sektora za pravna pitanja i socijalni dijalog, Unija poslodavca,
3. Marina Jovanović, Savjetnica za marketing i edukaciju, Unija poslodavca,
4. Pavić Radović, izvršni direktor NVO Kuća, i
5. Miljan Lončar, predstavnik UMHCG (Udruženje mladih sa hendikepom Crne Gore) i MOACG (Mreža za omladinski aktivizam Crne Gore).
Centralna tema sastanka bila je posvećena radnim pravima mladih, uz fokus na njihovu zaštitu i zdravlje na radu. Cilj je bio istražiti mogućnosti jačanja saradnje sa Unijom poslodavaca i ojačati njihovu ulogu u podizanju svijesti poslodavaca o ovim pitanjima. Đina Janković, kao projektna menadžerka Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, predstavila je relevantne podatke i izazove sa kojima se mladi suočavaju u oblasti radnih prava i zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
Rumica Kostić, Šefica Sektora za pravna pitanja i socijalni dijalog u Uniji poslodavaca, izrazila je otvorenost za saradnju i razgovor o mogućim inicijativama koje bi unaprijedile položaj mladih na radnom mjestu. Marina Jovanović, Savjetnica za marketing i edukaciju u istoj organizaciji, istakla je važnost edukacije poslodavaca o pravima mladih radnika i ulozi poslodavaca u unapređenju radnih uslova.
Pavić Radović, izvršni direktor NVO Kuća, pružio je dodatne uvide u potrebu za partnerstvom između nevladinog sektora i poslodavaca radi unapređenja programa radnih prava mladih. Miljan Lončar, predstavnik Udruženja mladih sa hendikepom Crne Gore i Mreže za omladinski aktivizam Crne Gore, dao je perspektivu mladih sa hendikepom i predstavio konkretne izazove s kojima se ova ranjiva grupa suočava.
Sastanak je rezultirao konkretnim dogovorima o budućim koracima, uključujući planiranje zajedničkih edukativnih programa, kampanja osvješćivanja i aktivnosti koje će doprinijeti stvaranju pozitivnih promjena u oblasti radnih prava i zaštite i zdravlja na radu mladih. Saradnja sa Unijom poslodavaca postavlja temelje za održive inicijative usmjerene ka poboljšanju radnih uslova i prava mladih u Crnoj Gori.
title_en: Meeting with representatives of the Employers' Union (January 2024)
excerpt_en: On 22 January 2024 UZNR CG met the Employers' Union to discuss young people's labour rights and ways of strengthening cooperation in raising employers' awareness of occupational safety and health.
content_en:
On 22 January 2024 an important meeting was held with representatives of the Employers' Union, bringing together the relevant actors to examine questions of young people's labour rights, their protection and the promotion of health at work.
The meeting was attended by key representatives of organisations and associations working on these subjects:
1. Đina Janković, project manager at the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro,
2. Rumica Kostić, head of the legal affairs and social dialogue department, Employers' Union,
3. Marina Jovanović, adviser for marketing and education, Employers' Union,
4. Pavić Radović, executive director of the NGO Kuća, and
5. Miljan Lončar, representing UMHCG (Association of Youth with Disabilities of Montenegro) and MOACG (Network for Youth Activism of Montenegro).
The central theme of the meeting was young people's labour rights, focusing on their protection and their safety and health at work. The aim was to explore ways of strengthening cooperation with the Employers' Union and of reinforcing its role in raising employers' awareness of these questions. Đina Janković, as project manager at the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, presented relevant data and the challenges young people face in labour rights and occupational safety and health.
Rumica Kostić, head of the legal affairs and social dialogue department at the Employers' Union, expressed openness to cooperation and to discussing possible initiatives that would improve young people's position at work. Marina Jovanović, adviser for marketing and education at the same organisation, emphasised the importance of educating employers about young workers' rights and about employers' role in improving working conditions.
Pavić Radović, executive director of the NGO Kuća, offered further insight into the need for partnership between the non-governmental sector and employers in order to improve programmes on young people's labour rights. Miljan Lončar, representing the Association of Youth with Disabilities of Montenegro and the Network for Youth Activism of Montenegro, offered the perspective of young people with disabilities and set out the concrete challenges this vulnerable group faces.
The meeting resulted in concrete agreements on next steps, including the planning of joint educational programmes, awareness campaigns and activities that will help bring about positive change in young people's labour rights and occupational safety and health. Cooperation with the Employers' Union lays the foundations for sustainable initiatives aimed at improving young people's working conditions and rights in Montenegro.

title: Sastanak sa predstavnicima Sindikata uprave i pravosuđa
excerpt: UZNR CG je 15. januara 2024. održalo sastanak sa Sindikatom uprave i pravosuđa o jačanju saradnje na promociji zaštite i zdravlja na radu i unapređenju radnih prava mladih.
content:
Dana 15.01.2024. održan je ključni sastanak u prostorijama Sindikata uprave i pravosuđa, sa ciljem jačanja saradnje u promociji zaštite i unapređenja zdravlja na radu, kao i unapređenja radnih prava, sa posebnim naglaskom na pitanja koja se odnose na mlade.
Sastanku su prisustvovali relevantni akteri iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu i sindikalnog pokreta:
1. Đina Janković, projektna menadžerka Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore,
2. Nenad Rakočević, predsjednik Sindikata uprave i pravosuđa,
3. Ivan Ivanović, predsjednik Asocijacije mladih Sindikata uprave i pravosuđa CG, i
4. Pavić Radović, izvršni direktor NVO Kuća.
Glavna tema sastanka bila je razmatranje mogućnosti i strategija za unapređenje uslova rada i obezbeđenje adekvatne zaštite i zdravlja mladih radnika. Đina Janković, projektna menadžerka Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, prezentovala je relevantne podatke o trenutnom stanju u oblasti zaštite na radu, istakavši izazove s kojima se mladi suočavaju. Nenad Rakočević, predsjednik Sindikata uprave i pravosuđa, izrazio je podršku inicijativama usmjerenim ka unapređenju radnih uslova i naglasio važnost ujedinjenog sindikalnog djelovanja.
Ivan Ivanović, predsjednik Asocijacije mladih Sindikata uprave i pravosuđa CG, iznio je perspektivu mladih radnika i predstavio predloge za konkretna poboljšanja, uz istovremeno isticanje važnosti edukacije i informisanja mladih o njihovim pravima na radu. Pavić Radović, izvršni direktor NVO Kuća, doprinio je diskusiji pružanjem uvida u mogućnosti partnerske saradnje sa nevladinim sektorom radi efikasnije implementacije programa iz oblasti radnih prava i promocije zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
Na sastanku su definisani naredni koraci u cilju zajedničkih inicijativa, uključujući planiranje edukativnih kampanja, lobiranje za poboljšane zakonskih okvira i zajedničke akcije usmjerene ka jačanju svijesti o značaju zaštite prava i zdravlja mladih radnika. Svi prisutni su izrazili odlučnost za daljom saradnjom kako bi se postigle pozitivne promjene u oblasti rada, posebno sa fokusom na omladinske radničke potrebe. Sastanak je bio koristan forum za razmjenu ideja i resursa, čime je postavljena čvrsta osnova za buduće zajedničke inicijative u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu i radnih prava mladih.
title_en: Meeting with representatives of the Trade Union of Administration and Justice
excerpt_en: On 15 January 2024 UZNR CG met the Trade Union of Administration and Justice to discuss stronger cooperation in promoting occupational safety and health and improving young people's labour rights.
content_en:
On 15 January 2024 a key meeting was held at the premises of the Trade Union of Administration and Justice, with the aim of strengthening cooperation in promoting protection and improving health at work and in advancing labour rights, with particular emphasis on questions affecting young people.
The meeting was attended by relevant actors from occupational safety and health and from the trade union movement:
1. Đina Janković, project manager at the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro,
2. Nenad Rakočević, president of the Trade Union of Administration and Justice,
3. Ivan Ivanović, president of the Youth Association of the Trade Union of Administration and Justice of Montenegro, and
4. Pavić Radović, executive director of the NGO Kuća.
The main theme of the meeting was to consider ways and strategies for improving working conditions and providing adequate safety and health protection for young workers. Đina Janković, project manager at the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, presented relevant data on the current state of occupational safety, highlighting the challenges young people face. Nenad Rakočević, president of the Trade Union of Administration and Justice, expressed support for initiatives aimed at improving working conditions and emphasised the importance of united trade union action.
