Montenegro's experience was presented by Đina Janković, secretary general and programme coordinator of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, and Zlatko Popović, chief inspector of the Occupational Safety and Health Department at the Administration of Inspection Affairs.
Because of the sheer volume of EU legislation to be transposed into national law, the negotiations are difficult and lengthy. The Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPA) allows candidate countries to adopt and carry out the key political, institutional, social and economic reforms needed to respect EU values and gradually align with EU rules, standards and policies.
The European Agency for Safety and Health at Work (EU-OSHA), through the IPA instrument, supports candidate countries and potential candidates in occupational safety and health, and organised this conference in cooperation with the Ministry of Labour, Family, Social Affairs and Equal Opportunities of the Republic of Slovenia (MDDSZ). The event was aimed at strengthening knowledge of occupational safety and health in candidate countries and potential candidates and at exchanging good practice in the inspection of psychosocial risks at work.
Psychosocial risks are among the hardest challenges in occupational safety and health. They arise from poor planning, organisation and management of work and from poor relationships in the working environment. They can have a powerful effect on individuals' health and negative psychological, physical and social consequences such as work-related stress, exhaustion or depression. All of that is of course reflected in companies' productivity and in a country's economic development. Labour inspectors for occupational safety and health have a particularly demanding role in this field.
The 1st Regional IPA Conference brought together representatives of the ministries and inspectorates responsible for labour from Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Türkiye, who discussed ways of raising awareness among employers and employees and the inspection of psychosocial risks at the workplace. Representatives of EU-OSHA, MDDSZ and the Labour Inspectorate of the Republic of Cyprus also took part in the exchange of knowledge on occupational safety and health.

title: Konferencija „Zdravo radno okruženje kao osnovno pravo na rad“
excerpt: Povodom Svjetskog dana zaštite i zdravlja na radu, Međunarodna organizacija rada, Ministarstvo rada i socijalnog staranja i Uprava za inspekcijske poslove organizovali su 28. aprila 2023. konferenciju u hotelu CUE u Podgorici.
content:
Hotel CUE, 28.04.2023.
Povodom Svjetskog dana zaštite i zdravlja na radu, u organizaciji Međunarodne organizacije rada, Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja i Uprave za inspekcijske poslove, održana je konferencija pod sloganom „Zdravo radno okruženje kao osnovno pravo na rad“ 28.04.2023. godine u hotelu CUE, u Podgorici.
Ministar rada i socijalnog staranja Admir Adrović naglasio je da je sigurno i zdravo radno mjesto ključni faktor za očuvanje fizičkog i mentalnog zdravlja zaposlenih, a da je podizanje svijesti o značaju zaštite i zdravlja na radu ključni cilj ovog dana. Nadalje, naglasio je da je potrebno uticati na podizanje svijesti, kako među zaposlenima, tako i među poslodavcima.
Rezidentni koordinator UN-a u Crnoj Gori Peter Lundberg skrenuo je pažnju na važnost saradnje između organizacija, sindikata, vlada, poslodavaca i sektora javnog zdravlja u obezbeđivanju zdravstvenih i bezbednosnih standarda za sve radnike. Ovaj dan služi kao podsjetnik na značaj saradnje u smanjenju povreda na radu, nesreća, bolesti i smrtnih slučajeva.
Direktorica Uprave inspekcijske poslove Crne Gore Ana Vujošević navela je da je uz podršku Međunarodne organizacije rada i Evropske Unije, Vlada Crne Gore značajno unaprijedila rad inspektora, kako u pogledu administrativnih kapaciteta, tako i u pogledu unapređenja načina i metoda rada, kao i tehničke opremljenosti. Naglasila je da je potrebno nastaviti sa unapređenjem rada inspekcije i jačanjem kapaciteta kako bi se osigurao nulti nivo povreda na radu i bolesti u vezi sa radom.
U panel diskusijama učestvovali su predstavnici poslodavaca, sindikata i vlade, kao i stručnjaci iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu i Udruženja zaštite i zdravlja na radu, koje je predtavljala Đina Janković. Učesnici su razgovarali o problemima i izazovima sa kojima se susreću zaposleni u Crnoj Gori u vezi sa zdravljem i zaštitom na radu, kao i o mogućim rješenjima za poboljšanje stanja. Svi su se složili da u Crnoj Gori neophodno imati viziju sigurnog i zdravog radnog mjesta za sve.
Jovana Bošković, predstavnica Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja, prezentovala je rezultate povreda u 2022. godini, na osnovu evidencija o povredama koje dostavlja Fond za zdravstveno osiguranje. Milan Kilibarda, stručno lice iz Nikšićke pivare, govorio je o tome kako je zaštita i zdravlje na radu uređena u jednom velikom sistemu, dok je Vladimir Lacmanović podijelio svoja iskustva iz ove oblasti, koja je imao kao stručne lice tokom izgradnje auto-puta. Branislav Šebek, predstavnik Montinspekta, predstavio je poslove kojima se bave ovlašćene organizacije, kao i izazove s kojima se suočavaju na terenu. Đina Janković je prezentovala rezultate projekata koje je Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore realizovalo u prethodnoj godini i podsjetila na neophodnost kontinuiranih edukacija u ovoj oblasti, s kojima je neophodno početi tokom sistema obrazovanja.
Učesnici panela istakli su važnost uspostavljanja novih ciljeva u zaštiti zdravlja i sigurnosti na radu, posebno u svjetlu novih tehnologija i promjenljivih radnih uslova. Takođe su naglasili da je edukacija i osnaživanje zaposlenih važan faktor u ovoj oblasti, kao i da je neophodno osigurati bolju saradnju između nadležnih institucija i privatnih sektora radi efikasnije zaštite zdravlja i sigurnosti na radu. Panel je takođe naglasio važnost praćenja i primjene uporednog zakonodavstva u ovoj oblasti, kao i unapređenja postojećih praksi i procedura.
Ukupno gledano, panel je pružio dragocjen uvid u aktuelna dostignuća i izazove u zaštiti zdravlja i sigurnosti na radu, i dao doprinos razvoju novih ciljeva i praksi u ovoj oblasti.
Ministarstvo zdravlja je saopštilo da je novim Zakonom o zdravstvenoj zaštiti, koji je pripremljen i u proceduri usvajanja, predviđeno vraćanje medicine rada na državni budžet, kako bi se ojačali kadrovski kapaciteti i unaprijedio kvalitet usluga. Poručili su da je prioritet Ministarstva zdravlja reforma zdravstvenog sistema sa sveobuhvatnijom organizacijom pružanja kvalitetnih usluga na svim nivoima zdravstvene zaštite, zbog čega je novi Zakon o zdravstvenoj zaštiti i donešen.
Novim zakonskim tekstom omogućiće se građanima da o trošku države određena profesionalna oboljenja dokazuju u referentnim centrima iz regiona u ovoj oblasti medicine. Kako kažu, novim zakonskim rješenjima sistem zdravstvene zaštite biće organizovan da obezbijedi dostupniju zaštitu stanovništvu, bolju organizaciju, povezanost i funkcionisanje sistema zaštite na svim nivoima.
Dodali su da konkretno u oblasti medicine rada, usvajanjem novog zakona o zdravstvenoj zaštiti, ljekarske preglede radi utvrđivanja radne sposobnosti zaposlenih, obavljaće doktor medicine, specijalista medicine rada i doktor medicine druge specijalnosti. Na osnovu njih će doktor medicine specijalista medicine rada sačinjavati izvještaj o izvršenom zdravstvenom pregledu zaposlenog. Ovaj izvještaj će sadržati nalaz i mišljenje o radnoj sposobnosti, u skladu sa zakonom kojim se uređuje zaštita i zdravlje na radu“, zaključuje se u saopštenju.
title_en: Conference “A healthy working environment as a fundamental right at work”
excerpt_en: To mark World Day for Safety and Health at Work, the International Labour Organization, the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare and the Administration of Inspection Affairs held a conference on 28 April 2023 at the Hotel CUE in Podgorica.
content_en:
Hotel CUE, 28 April 2023
To mark World Day for Safety and Health at Work, and organised by the International Labour Organization, the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare and the Administration of Inspection Affairs, a conference was held under the banner “A healthy working environment as a fundamental right at work” on 28 April 2023 at the Hotel CUE in Podgorica.
The Minister of Labour and Social Welfare, Admir Adrović, emphasised that a safe and healthy workplace is a key factor in preserving employees' physical and mental health, and that raising awareness of the importance of occupational safety and health is the key aim of the day. He further emphasised the need to raise awareness among employees and employers alike.
The UN Resident Coordinator in Montenegro, Peter Lundberg, drew attention to the importance of cooperation between organisations, trade unions, governments, employers and the public health sector in securing health and safety standards for all workers. The day serves as a reminder of the importance of cooperation in reducing injuries at work, accidents, illness and deaths.
The director of the Administration of Inspection Affairs of Montenegro, Ana Vujošević, said that with the support of the International Labour Organization and the European Union, the Government of Montenegro has significantly improved the work of inspectors, both in administrative capacity and in working methods and technical equipment. She emphasised the need to continue improving the inspectorate's work and strengthening its capacity in order to secure zero injuries at work and work-related illnesses.
The panel discussions brought together representatives of employers, trade unions and the government, together with specialists in occupational safety and health and the Occupational Safety and Health Association, represented by Đina Janković. Participants discussed the problems and challenges employees in Montenegro face regarding health and safety at work and possible ways of improving the situation. All agreed that Montenegro needs a vision of a safe and healthy workplace for everyone.
Jovana Bošković, representing the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare, presented the injury figures for 2022, based on the injury records supplied by the Health Insurance Fund. Milan Kilibarda, a safety professional at the Nikšić brewery, spoke about how occupational safety and health is organised in a large enterprise, while Vladimir Lacmanović shared his experience as a safety professional during the construction of the motorway. Branislav Šebek, representing Montinspekt, presented the work of licensed organisations and the challenges they face in the field. Đina Janković presented the results of the projects the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro carried out over the previous year and reiterated the need for continuous education in this field, beginning within the education system.
The panellists emphasised the importance of setting new goals in occupational health and safety, particularly in the light of new technology and changing working conditions. They also emphasised that educating and empowering employees is an important factor in this field, and that better cooperation between the competent institutions and the private sector is essential if health and safety at work are to be protected more effectively. The panel also emphasised the importance of following and applying comparative legislation in this field and of improving existing practice and procedures.
Overall, the panel offered valuable insight into current achievements and challenges in occupational health and safety and contributed to the development of new goals and practice in the field.
The Ministry of Health announced that the new Law on Health Care, which has been prepared and is in the process of adoption, provides for occupational medicine to be returned to the state budget, in order to strengthen staffing capacity and improve the quality of services. It said the Ministry of Health's priority is to reform the health system with a more comprehensive organisation of quality service provision at every level of health care, which is why the new Law on Health Care was adopted.
The new legislation will allow citizens to have certain occupational diseases diagnosed at the state's expense at reference centres in the region specialising in this area of medicine. Under the new arrangements, the health care system will be organised so as to provide more accessible protection for the population and better organisation, connection and functioning of the protection system at every level.
The Ministry added that specifically in occupational medicine, with the adoption of the new Law on Health Care, medical examinations to determine employees' fitness for work will be carried out by a doctor of medicine, an occupational medicine specialist and a doctor of another speciality. On the basis of these, an occupational medicine specialist will produce a report on the employee's medical examination. That report will contain findings and an opinion on fitness for work, in accordance with the law governing occupational safety and health, the statement concludes.

title: Obuka „Izrada planova prikupljanja sredstava“
excerpt: CRNVO je 26. aprila 2023. organizovalo obuku o prikupljanju sredstava za 16 predstavnika nevladinih organizacija, među kojima su bile i predstavnice UZNR CG Sandra Lalević i Karolina Popović.
content:
Podgorica, Upbeat Hub
26.04.2023.
U organizaciji CRNVO, 26.04.2023. godine je održana obuka koja je okupila 16 predstavnika različitih NVO organizacija, među kojima su bile i dvije predstavnice iz Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore, Sandra Lalević i Karolina Popović. Cilj obuke bio je upoznavanje učesnika o važnosti prikupljanja sredstava, izvorima finansiranja i koracima izrade strateškog plana.
Trener obuke, Marko Pejović, govorio je o istraživanjima koje je CRNVO sproveo u okviru poziva Delegacije Evropske unije u Crnoj Gori. Objasnio je da je ključni cilj „fundraisinga“ prikupljanje što više sredstava, jer održivost organizacije dolazi u pitanje ukoliko se ne prikupe dovoljna sredstva. Međutim, naglasio je da polazište treba da bude ostvarivanje ciljeva organizacije, a ne samo prikupljanje sredstava.
Jedan od početnih koraka u „fundraisingu“ jeste saradnja sa medijima, jer to pomaže u poboljšanju vidljivosti organizacije i čini je prepoznatljivijom u okviru civilnog sektora u Crnoj Gori i među donatorima. Ciljna grupa jesu građani, posebno kada je riječ o srednje razvijenim organizacijama.
Ključne faze prikupljanja sredstava predstavljale su osnovu obuke, što uključuje prepoznavanje i poznavanje perspektiva, odnosno potencijalnih donatora s kojima se može raditi i mjesta na kojima se mogu potencijalno aplicirati projektne ideje.
Kako bi bolje shvatili realizaciju ove obuke, učesnici su prošli kroz dvije vježbe o aktivnostima za prikupljanje sredstava njihove organizacije. Na pomenutim vježbama, učesnici su definisali viziju, misiju i ciljeve svojih organizacija koji bi privukli potencijalne donatore. Prema rezultatima, organizacije su ostvarile dobre rezultate.
Nakon obuke, učesnici su bili u stanju da primijene naučene tehnike i alate u svom radu i da kreiraju jasniju viziju, misiju i ciljeve svojih organizacija, što će im pomoći da budu efikasniji u prikupljanju sredstava. Takođe, učesnici su dobili uvid u perspektive i mogućnosti za saradnju sa različitim donatorima, kao i u značaj faza prikupljanja sredstava.
Zaključak obuke je da je prikupljanje sredstava važan segment rada svake NVO organizacije i da je strateško planiranje „fundraisinga“ neophodno za dugoročnu održivost organizacije. Učesnici su dobili vrijedne informacije i alate koji će im pomoći u daljem razvijanju svojih organizacija i ostvarivanju njihovih ciljeva.
Zaključeno je, takođe, da su organizacije na pravom putu i da je uvijek moguće napraviti neka poboljšanja, čak i ako do sada nisu imale iskustva u organizovanju strateških sastanaka za dugoročno planiranje.
title_en: Training: “Drawing up fundraising plans”
excerpt_en: On 26 April 2023 CRNVO held fundraising training for 16 representatives of non-governmental organisations, among them UZNR CG's representatives Sandra Lalević and Karolina Popović.
content_en:
Podgorica, Upbeat Hub
26 April 2023
Organised by CRNVO, training was held on 26 April 2023 that brought together 16 representatives of various NGOs, among them two representatives of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, Sandra Lalević and Karolina Popović. The aim of the training was to familiarise participants with the importance of fundraising, the sources of funding and the steps involved in drawing up a strategic plan.
The trainer, Marko Pejović, spoke about research CRNVO carried out under a call from the Delegation of the European Union to Montenegro. He explained that the key aim of fundraising is to raise as much money as possible, since an organisation's sustainability is called into question if it does not raise enough. He emphasised, however, that the starting point should be achieving the organisation's goals, not merely raising funds.
One of the first steps in fundraising is working with the media, because that helps improve an organisation's visibility and makes it better known within the civil sector in Montenegro and among donors. The target group is citizens, particularly in the case of medium-sized organisations.
The key stages of fundraising formed the basis of the training, including recognising and understanding prospects — that is, the potential donors one can work with — and the places where project ideas can potentially be submitted.
To help them understand the material, participants worked through two exercises on fundraising activities for their organisation. In these exercises they defined the vision, mission and goals of their organisations in a way that would attract potential donors. The results showed that the organisations did well.
After the training, participants were able to apply the techniques and tools they had learned in their own work and to create a clearer vision, mission and set of goals for their organisations, which will help them fundraise more effectively. Participants also gained insight into the prospects and opportunities for working with different donors and into the importance of the stages of fundraising.
The conclusion of the training is that fundraising is an important part of the work of every NGO and that strategic fundraising planning is essential to an organisation's long-term sustainability. Participants received valuable information and tools that will help them develop their organisations further and achieve their goals.
It was also concluded that the organisations are on the right track and that improvements are always possible, even for those with no previous experience of holding strategic meetings for long-term planning.

title: Predavanje u JU Srednja građevinsko-geodetska škola „Inž. Marko Radević“ (mart 2023)
excerpt: UZNR CG je 10. marta 2023, u saradnji sa NVO MADOP, održalo jedanaesto po redu predavanje za buduće tehničare geodezije, vodoinstalatere i montere suve gradnje u školi „Inž. Marko Radević“.
content:
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore je, u saradnji sa NVO MADOP, 10.03.2023. godine uspješno realizovalo jedanaesto po redu predavanje iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu za učenike JU Srednje građevinsko-geodetske škole „Inž. Marko Radević“. Zbog velike zainteresovanosti profesora i uprave škole, ovo je već drugo predavnje u istoj obrazovnoj instituciji, kojem su ovoga puta prisutvovali budući tehničari geodezije niskogradnje i hidrogradnje, vodoinstalateri i monteri suve gradnje.
Cilj ovih predavanja, koja su realizovana u okviru projekta „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“, finansiranog od strane Evropske komisije i dijelom Ministratva javne uprave u Crnoj Gori, je da se učenici upoznaju sa osnovnim načelima zaštite i zdravlja na radu, njihovim pravima i odgovornostima koje imaju kada zasnuju radni odnos, ali i obavezama i odgovornostima koje poslodavci imaju prema njima kao svojim zaposlenima.
Takođe, predstavnici NVO Mreže za afirmaciju dtuštveno odgovornog poslovanja, koji su bili predavači na ovom projektu, učenike su upoznali sa brojnim opsnim materijama sa kojima će biti u kontaktu na svojim budućim radnim mjestima. Govorili su im o brojnim štetnim efektima koje opasne materije mogu imati po zdravlje čovjeka i izazvati brojna profesionalna oboljenja, ukoliko se rizici ne prepoznaju na vrijeme i ne preduzmu mjere zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Takođe, skrenuli su im pažnju da sve te opasne materije mogu izazvati trajen eposljedice po živornu sredinu, ukoliko se nekontrolisano odlažu i na taj način dospiju u vazduh, žemljište i vode.
Shodno odgovorima koje su učenici dali, popunjavajući upitnik prije predavanja, kao i kroz interakciju tokom obuke, može se zaključiti da ne posjeduju gotovo nikakva znanja iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, što je posljedica neizučavanja ove teme u okviru obrazovnog procesa. Uzimajući u obzir da je sektor građevinarstva jedan od najrizičnijih s apekta povređivanja, neophodno je uložiti dodatne napore kada je u pitanju edukacija iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kako učenika tako i nastvanika.

title_en: Lecture at the “Inž. Marko Radević” Secondary School of Construction and Geodesy (March 2023)
excerpt_en: On 10 March 2023, together with the NGO MADOP, UZNR CG delivered its eleventh lecture, this time for future geodesy technicians, plumbers and drywall fitters at the “Inž. Marko Radević” school.
content_en:
On 10 March 2023 the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, together with the NGO MADOP, successfully delivered its eleventh lecture on occupational safety and health for pupils of the “Inž. Marko Radević” Secondary School of Construction and Geodesy. Because of the keen interest shown by the teachers and the school's management, this was the second lecture at the same institution, attended this time by future geodesy technicians in civil and hydraulic engineering, plumbers and drywall fitters.
The aim of these lectures, delivered under the project “Decent work starts while you are young”, financed by the European Commission and in part by the Ministry of Public Administration of Montenegro, is to acquaint pupils with the basic principles of occupational safety and health, with the rights and responsibilities they will have when they enter employment, and with the obligations and responsibilities employers have towards them as employees.
Representatives of the NGO Network for the Affirmation of Socially Responsible Business, who lectured on this project, also introduced pupils to the many hazardous substances they will come into contact with in their future workplaces. They spoke about the many harmful effects hazardous substances can have on human health, and about the occupational diseases they can cause if risks are not recognised in time and occupational safety and health measures are not taken. They also drew attention to the fact that all these hazardous substances can cause lasting damage to the environment if they are disposed of without control and thereby enter the air, soil and water.
Judging by the answers the pupils gave in the questionnaire completed before the lecture, and by the interaction during the session, it can be concluded that they have almost no knowledge of occupational safety and health, the result of the subject not being taught within the educational process. Given that construction is one of the riskiest sectors for injury, further effort must be invested in occupational safety and health education, for pupils and teachers alike.

content:
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore je,u saradnji sa NVO MADOP, 09.03.2023. uspješno realizovalo dvanaesto po redu predavanje iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Ovo je drugo predavanje koje je, na molbu predmetnih nastavnika, organizovano za učenike 1. i 2. razreda – smjera automehatronika, u JU Srednja stručna škola „Ivan Uskoković''.
Cilj ovog predavanja je bilo pružanje osnovnih informacija iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, koje su učenicima neophodne za bezbjedno pohađanje praktične nastave u radionicama u školi, kao i prakse kod poslodavca, kao i podizanje svijesti o važnosti rada na bezbjedan način.. Osim toga, predstavnici NVO MADOP su ih upoznali sa rizicima rada sa opasnim materijama, kako po zdravlje, tako i po životnu sredinu. Sa učenicima su razgovarali o tome koji se opasne materije mogu naći u građevinskim materijalima i u građevinskom otpadu.
!!!Kada su srednje stručne škole u pitanju, škola i poslodavac su dužni da, shodno zakonu, osposobe učenike za bezbjedan rad i da ih upoznaju sa rizicima i osnovnim mjerama zaštite i zdravlja na radu pri izvođenju praktičnog dijela obuke.
Shodno odgovorima koje su učenici dali, popunjavajući upitnik prije predavanja, može se zaključiti da ne posjeduju gotovo nikakva znanja iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, što je posljedica neizučavanja ove teme u okviru obrazovnog procesa.

title_en: Lecture at the “Ivan Uskoković” Secondary Vocational School (March 2023)
excerpt_en: On 9 March 2023, together with the NGO MADOP, UZNR CG delivered its twelfth lecture on occupational safety and health, this time for pupils on the auto-mechatronics stream at the “Ivan Uskoković” school.
content_en:
On 9 March 2023 the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, together with the NGO MADOP, successfully delivered its twelfth lecture on occupational safety and health. This was the second lecture organised, at the request of the subject teachers, for first- and second-year pupils on the auto-mechatronics stream at the “Ivan Uskoković” Secondary Vocational School.
The aim of the lecture was to give pupils the basic information about occupational safety and health they need in order to attend practical instruction safely in the school workshops and on placements with employers, and to raise their awareness of the importance of working safely. The lecturers gave them the basic information about employment relationships they need in order to understand their rights and responsibilities when entering employment, and the obligations and responsibilities employers have towards them as employees.
Representatives of the NGO MADOP also introduced them to the risks of working with hazardous substances, both to health and to the environment. They discussed with the pupils which hazardous substances can be found in construction materials and in construction waste.
!!! In the case of secondary vocational schools, the school and the employer are required by law to train pupils in safe work and to acquaint them with the risks and the basic occupational safety and health measures during the practical part of their training.
Judging by the answers the pupils gave in the questionnaire completed before the lecture, it can be concluded that they have almost no knowledge of occupational safety and health, the result of the subject not being taught within the educational process.

title: Završna konferencija projekta „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“
excerpt: UZNR CG je 23. februara 2023. u Podgorici predstavilo rezultate projekta „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“, uključujući anketu o iskustvima 555 mladih u vezi sa zaštitom i zdravljem na radu.
content:
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore je, u okviru projekta „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“, na završnoj konferenciji, prezentovalo rezultate projekta i istraživanja koje su sprovedena prethodnih mjeseci.
Projekat „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“ finansira Evropska unija, a kofinansira Ministarstvo javne uprave u Crnoj Gori, a realizovan je uz podršku NVO Prima i Mreže Omladinski HUB za Zapadni Balkan i Tursku, koja ima 67 članica.
Događaj je održan 23. februara u Podgorici.
Panelisti na ovoj konferenciji su bili:
• Branka Kankaraš, Ministarstvo prosvjete, Direktorat za opšte srednje obrazovanje, stručno obrazovanje i cjeloživotno učenje
• Jovana Bošković, Ministarstvo rada i socijalnog staranja, Direkcija za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu
• Snežana Mijušković, Kancelarija Zaštitnika ljudskih prava i sloboda Crne Gore
• Uroš Bulatović, Mreža za mlade
• Dragiša Damjanović, Nacionalna organizacija za podršku eTwinning mreže u Crnoj Gori
Đina Janković, projektna menadžerka u NVO Udruženju zaštite na radu Crne Gore, je predstavila rezultate anketiranja mladih starosti 16 do 29 godina, koje je Udruženje u projektnom periodu sprovodilo. Na taj način su, kroz anonimnu anketu u kojoj je učestvovalo 555 mladih, prikupljeni brojni podaci koji daju jasniju sliku o njihovom poznavanju prava, obaveza i odgovornosti iz radnih odnosa i iskustvima koja su imali na radnim mjestima na kojima su bili angažovani u prethodnih 5 godina, kada je u pitanju zaštita i zdravlje na radu, što je veoma važno, uzimajući u obzir činjenicu da u Crnoj Gori takvi podaci ne postoje.
S obzirom na to da je Crna Gora jedina zemlja u regionu i Evropi, u kojoj zaštita i zdravlje na radu nisu uključeni u obrazovni sistem, tokom prethodnih mjeseci Udruženje je realizovalo brojne edukativne radionice u srednjim stručnim školama u Podgorici, Bijelom Polju i Nikšiću, kao i na tehničkim fakultetima u Podgorici i na taj način, barem djelimično, upoznalo mlade ljude sa izazovima i problemima u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, s kojima će se suočiti dolaskom na tržište rada, nakon završenog procesa obrazovanja.
Upitnici koje su učenici i studenti popunjavali prilikom predavanja, koja su organizovana u srednjim stručnim školama i na fakultetima, daju uvid u nivo znanja mladih o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu, koji je na zabrinjavajuće niskom nivou. Kroz ovaj vid radionica je prošlo 298 učenika i studenata.
Branka Kankaraš iz Ministarstva prosvjete je naglasila da je u narednom periodu neophodno sprovoditi edukacije nastavnika i koordinatora prakse iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Jedino ukoliko se bude dodatno radilo sa njima oni će moći da prenesu svoje znanje na učenike.
Osim toga, predložila je da bi bilo veoma korisno organizovati različite vidove kreativnih radionica sa učenicima osnovnih škola, kako bi se oni na taj način mogli više zainteresovati za ovu temu i da bi shvatili koliko je za njih ovo značajno.
Jovana Bošković – Ministarstvo rada i socijalnog staranja, Direkcija za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu je podsjetila na posvjećenost Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja radi na promovisanju dostojanstvenog rada zajedno sa socijalnim partnerima, ali i sa civilnim sektorom.
Podsjetila je da su povrede na radu mladih ljudi veoma česte i da se shodno podacima Evropske agencije za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu, svakih 9 minuta jedna mlada osoba povrijedi na radnom mjestu. Do sada se samo moglo pretpostavljati da su ti podaci slični i kada je u pitanju Crna Gora, ali zahvaljujući rezultatima istraživanja do kojih je došlo Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore, stiče se jasnija slika, a ti rezultati će biti od velike koristi u budućem kreiranju politika. Naglasila je da će Direkcija za zaštitu na radu, u budućem periodu, raditi na proizvodnji statističkih podataka, pratiti rizike za mlade i podržavati kroz razne modele razmjenu dobrih praksi kako bi ih zaštitili na radnom mjestu.
Navela je i to da je Ministarstvo rada i socijalnog staranja je u prethodnom periodu radilo na propisima koji bi trebalo da ograniče mlade ljude da učestvuju u nizu opasnih poslova i daju određene odgovornosti poslodavcima koje su ključne.
Snežana Mijušković – zamjenica Ombudsmana je podsjetila na ulogu Institucije Zaštitnika ljudskih prava i sloboda Crne Gore da se bavi promocijom, zaštitom i unapređenjem ostvarivanja prava i sloboda i u oblasti prava djeteta, mladih i socijalne zaštite, kao i na to da svaka država treba da omogući takve uslove u kojima neće doći do eksploatacije djece i da neće biti dječijeg rada.
„Suština je da naučimo djecu kao i njihove roditelje kome mogu da se obrate kada se nešto desi“ naglasila je u svom obraćanju. Iznijela je i svoj stav da djecu, od najranijeg uzrasta, treba edukovati o tome šta je to zaštita na radu i šta sve donosi uključenje u proces rada i da sa tim treba započeti što ranije – već u vrtićima, kako bi oni usvojili pozitivna znanja na vrijeme, jer dolaskom u srednju školu i na fakulet za sticanje takvih znanja je već kasno.
Apelovala je da se ulože dodatni napori kako bi Lista opasnih poslova za mlade konačno ugledala svjetlost dana, što bi svima olakšalo proces. Lista je finalizovana još 2020. godine, ali se još uvijek čeka validacija pravnog instrumenta od strane Sekreterijata za zakonodavstvo.
Uroš Bulatović – je natjerao sve prisutne da se zamisle kada je, kao član UO Mreže za mlade, podsjetio da su mladi u velikoj mjeri izgubili povjerenje, budući da se kao društvo bavimo samo pojedinačnim problemima i ne vodimo računa o tome da 70-80% zanimanja, za koja se mladi ljudi trenutno obrazuju, neće postojati za par godina. Smatra da da se mladima bavimo samo „od teme do teme“ i „od inicijative do inicijative“, a da zapravo mladi treba više da budu uključeni u donošenje politika koje se tiču mladih i da je potrebno mnogo više uraditi na njihovom ekonomskom osnaživanju, ali im i kroz sistem obrazovanja pružiti adekvatna, neophodna znanja.
Kao predsjednik Unije mladih preduzetnika dodao je da mladi poslodavci nemaju jasno definisane obaveze i odgovornosti i da nisu upućeni u postojanje Zakona o ZZNR i da se taj problem mora rješavati na međuresornom nivou i međusektorskom nivou, gdje je neophodno prisustvo obrazovnih institucija.
Dragiša Damjanović – iz Nacionalne organizacija za podršku eTwinning mreže u Crnoj Gori je podsjetio da su znanja učenika o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu na nekom ne tako zavidnom nivou, a da je realizacija tih nastavnih jedinica je na još manjem nivou.
Iznio je svoja zapažanja da mladi nastavnici - pripravnici ne poseduju gotovo nikakva znanja koja proističu iz radnih odnosa, kao ni ona koja se odnose na zaštitu i zdravlje na radu i mobing koji je regulisan Zakonom o zabrani zlostavljanja na radu. Budući da ne poznaju svoja prava, obaveze i odgovornosti, teško je očekivati da znanja mogu prenijeti učenicima.
Upoznao je prisutne sa jednim vrlo zanimljivim i zabrinjavajućim podatkom - da se samo 4,8% mladih u Crnoj Gori izjasnilo da su zanimanja, za koje postoji ponuda u obrazovnom sistemu, zanimljiva i prihvatljiva.
Zaključci konferencije „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“:
1. Iako su rezultati istraživanja zabrinjavajući, nikoga nisu iznenadili, što dovodi do zaključka da je većina svjesna stanja u ovoj oblasti;
2. Neophodno je o ovoj temi govoriti mnogo više, a konferencije koje se bave ovom tematikom ne bi trebalo da traju kraće od tri dana, uzimajući u obzir činjenicu koliko je ova oblast multidisciplinarna i koliko je prisutne podstakla na diskusiju;
3. Budućnost ovog društva je u mladima, a odgovornost za kreiranje njihove bezbjedne i zdrave budućnosti je u školama. Da bismo to postigli, neophodno je što prije započeti sa edukacijom nastavnika iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kako bi oni mogli svoja znanja prenijeti učenicima, što je već definisano obrazovnim programima srednjih stručnih škola, a što se do sada u praksi, uglavnom, nije primjenjivalo;
4. Neophodno je nastaviti sa obukama iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu i time doprinijeti podizanju svijesti o ovoj temi, ali bi najbolji efekat mogao biti postignut organizovanjem radionica koje bi uključivale djecu predškolskog uzrasta (u vrtićima) i djecu u osnovnim školama;
5. Prema mišljenju svih prisutnih, poražavajuće je da se niko od medija nije odazvao pozivu da isprati jedan ovako značajan događaj, pa je u budućem periodu neophodno uraditi mnogo više na animiranju novinara kako bi prepoznali značaj ove teme.

title_en: Closing conference of the project “Decent work starts while you are young”
excerpt_en: On 23 February 2023 in Podgorica UZNR CG presented the results of the project “Decent work starts while you are young”, including a survey of 555 young people's experience of occupational safety and health.
content_en:
At the closing conference of the project “Decent work starts while you are young”, the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro presented the project's results and the research carried out over the preceding months.
The project “Decent work starts while you are young” is financed by the European Union and co-financed by the Ministry of Public Administration of Montenegro, and was carried out with the support of the NGO Prima and the Youth HUB network for the Western Balkans and Türkiye, which has 67 members.
The event was held on 23 February in Podgorica.
The panellists were:
• Branka Kankaraš, Ministry of Education, Directorate for General Secondary Education, Vocational Education and Lifelong Learning
• Jovana Bošković, Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare, Directorate for Occupational Safety and Health
• Snežana Mijušković, Office of the Protector of Human Rights and Freedoms of Montenegro
• Uroš Bulatović, Youth Network
• Dragiša Damjanović, National Support Organisation for the eTwinning network in Montenegro
Đina Janković, project manager at the NGO Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, presented the results of the survey of young people aged 16 to 29 that the Association carried out during the project. Through an anonymous survey in which 555 young people took part, a great deal of data was collected that gives a clearer picture of their knowledge of the rights, obligations and responsibilities arising from employment and of their experience of occupational safety and health at the workplaces where they have worked over the past 5 years — which matters greatly, given that no such data exists in Montenegro.
Since Montenegro is the only country in the region and in Europe where occupational safety and health is not included in the education system, over the preceding months the Association held numerous educational workshops in secondary vocational schools in Podgorica, Bijelo Polje and Nikšić and at the technical faculties in Podgorica, thereby acquainting young people, at least in part, with the challenges and problems in occupational safety and health that they will face when they enter the labour market after finishing their education.
The questionnaires that pupils and students completed at the lectures held in secondary vocational schools and at faculties give an insight into young people's knowledge of occupational safety and health, which is worryingly low. A total of 298 pupils and students took part in these workshops.
Branka Kankaraš of the Ministry of Education emphasised that in the period ahead it is essential to train teachers and work placement coordinators in occupational safety and health. Only if further work is done with them will they be able to pass their knowledge on to pupils.
She also suggested that it would be very useful to organise various kinds of creative workshops with primary school pupils, so that they can become more interested in the subject and understand how important it is for them.
Jovana Bošković of the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare, Directorate for Occupational Safety and Health, recalled the Ministry's commitment to promoting decent work together with the social partners and with the civil sector.
She noted that injuries at work among young people are very frequent and that, according to European Agency for Safety and Health at Work data, a young person is injured at work every 9 minutes. Until now it could only be assumed that the figures are similar in Montenegro, but thanks to the research findings produced by the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro a clearer picture is emerging, and those results will be of great use in shaping future policy. She emphasised that in the period ahead the Directorate for Occupational Safety will work on producing statistics, monitoring the risks to young people and supporting the exchange of good practice through various models in order to protect them at work.
She also noted that the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare has been working on regulations that would restrict young people from taking part in a range of dangerous jobs and place certain key responsibilities on employers.
Snežana Mijušković, deputy Ombudsman, recalled the role of the Protector of Human Rights and Freedoms of Montenegro in promoting, protecting and advancing rights and freedoms in the field of children's and young people's rights and social protection, and said that every state should create conditions in which children are not exploited and child labour does not occur.
“The essence is to teach children and their parents whom they can turn to when something happens,” she said in her address. She also expressed the view that children should be taught from the earliest age what safety at work is and what being part of the world of work involves, and that this should begin as early as possible — already in nursery school — so that they take in this knowledge in good time, because by the time they reach secondary school and university it is already too late.
She appealed for further effort so that the List of dangerous jobs for young people can finally see the light of day, which would make the process easier for everyone. The list was finalised back in 2020, but validation of the legal instrument by the Secretariat for Legislation is still awaited.
Uroš Bulatović gave everyone present pause for thought when, as a member of the Youth Network's management board, he noted that young people have largely lost trust, since as a society we deal only with individual problems and take no account of the fact that 70–80% of the occupations young people are currently training for will not exist in a few years' time. He believes we engage with young people only “from topic to topic” and “from initiative to initiative”, whereas young people should in fact be far more involved in shaping the policies that concern them, and far more should be done for their economic empowerment and to give them adequate, necessary knowledge through the education system.
As president of the Union of Young Entrepreneurs he added that young employers have no clearly defined obligations and responsibilities and are unaware of the existence of the Law on Occupational Safety and Health, and that this problem must be addressed across ministries and across sectors, with the involvement of educational institutions.
Dragiša Damjanović of the National Support Organisation for the eTwinning network in Montenegro noted that pupils' knowledge of occupational safety and health is at a rather unenviable level, and that the delivery of these teaching units is at an even lower one.
He shared his observation that young trainee teachers have almost no knowledge of employment relationships, nor of occupational safety and health or of the workplace harassment regulated by the Law on the Prohibition of Harassment at Work. Since they do not know their own rights, obligations and responsibilities, it is hard to expect them to pass such knowledge on to pupils.
He shared a very interesting and worrying figure with those present — that only 4.8% of young people in Montenegro said that the occupations on offer in the education system are interesting and acceptable to them.
Conclusions of the conference “Decent work starts while you are young”:
1. Although the research findings are worrying, they surprised no one, which leads to the conclusion that most people are aware of the situation in this field;
2. This subject needs to be discussed far more, and conferences on it should last no less than three days, given how multidisciplinary the field is and how much discussion it prompted among those present;
3. The future of this society lies with young people, and responsibility for creating their safe and healthy future lies with schools. To achieve that, training for teachers in occupational safety and health must begin as soon as possible, so that they can pass their knowledge on to pupils — something already set out in the curricula of secondary vocational schools but until now largely not applied in practice;
4. Training in occupational safety and health must continue, thereby helping raise awareness of the subject, but the greatest effect could be achieved by organising workshops involving pre-school children (in nurseries) and children in primary schools;
5. In the view of everyone present, it is dispiriting that no media outlet responded to the invitation to cover such a significant event, so in the period ahead much more must be done to engage journalists so that they recognise the importance of this subject.

title: Monitoring projekta „Unapređenje uslova rada i zaštite i zdravlja na radu“
excerpt: U okviru EU monitoringa rezultata (ROM), 9. i 10. februara 2023. Crnu Goru je posjetio monitor Edin Jahić radi provjere napretka aktivnosti regionalnog projekta unapređenja uslova rada.
content:
U okviru aktivnosti od strane EU - Result Oriented Monitoring (ROM) - 9. i 10. februara je došlo do posjete projektu „Enhance labour conditions and occupational safety and health as a support to the Western Balkans towards accessing the European Union“, od strane, za ovu priliku određenog monitora iz Brisela – Edina Jahića. Cilj ROM-a je da u ime EU, koja finasira ovaj projekat utvrdi napredak projektnih aktivnosti do tog datuma, u svakoj od zemalja uključenih u ovaj regionalni projekat.
Edin Jahić je u cilju monitoringa imao niz sastanaka koje je Đina Janaković unaprijed organizovala. Svrha sastanaka sa učesnicima projekta u Crnoj Gori je bila da se porazgovara o dosadašnjim aktivnostima projekta u zemlji kao i ostvarenim rezultatima po određenoj aktivnosti. Fokus je bio na uspješno realizovanim aktivnostima, ali i na onim koje nisu realizovane, među kojima je najznačajnija – „Formiranje Nacionalnog savjeta za ZZNR u Crnoj Gori“, kao i o razlozima koji su doprinijeli da ne dođe do realizacije ovog unaprijed postavljenog cilja. Kao razlog je navedena nestabilna politička situacija u zemlji prethodnih par godina, ali i nedostatak volje za formiranje jednog takvog tijela, u resornom ministarstvu.
Sastanci su održani sa predstavnicima UZNR CG i sa učesnicima radionica koje je udruženje realizovalo u prethodnom periodu. Jedan dio sastanaka je održan u kancelarijama organizacije, a jedan dio u Ministarstvu prosvjete.
Učešće u ovom monitoringu su imali:
1. Đina Janković - Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore, koordinatorka projekta,
2. Zdenko Janković - Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore, predsjednik,
3. Branislav Šebek – izvršni direktor i vlasnik Montispekt-a, ovlašćene organizacije za poslove zaštite i zdravlja na radu,
4. Zlatko Popović - Uprava za inspekcijske poslove, inspektor zaštite i zdravlja na radu,
5. Anđa Strugar – Institut za razvoj i istraživanja iz oblasti zaštite na radu,
6. Sandra Obradović - Unija slobodnih sindikata Crne Gore,
7. Dejan Nuculović - Unija poslodavaca Crne Gore,
8. Lidija Brnović - Ekspertikinja u edukaciji i kreiranju javnih politika i trenerica javnog zagovaranja u okviru NVO za oblasti ljudskih prava,
9. Jelena Raičević -Ministarstvo ekologije, prostornog planiranja i urbanizma,
10. Tamara Martinović, Ministartsvo prosvjete, Direktorat za opšte srednje obrazovanje, stručno obrazovanje i cjeloživotno učenje,
11. Marija Milić, Ministarstvo prosvjete, Direktorat za opšte srednje obrazovanje, stručno obrazovanje i cjeloživotno učenje
12. Marko Burić, doktor medicine rada
Đina Janković je monitoru Jahiću dostavila i sve izvještaje o realizovanim aktivnostima u prethodnom periodu:
• Godišnji izveštaj o radu UZNR CG 01.02.2020. do 31.01. 2021
• Godišnji izveštaj o radu UZNR CG 01.02.2021. do 31.01. 2022.
• Godišnji izveštaj o radu UZNR CG 01.02.2022. do 31.01.2023.
title_en: Monitoring of the project “Improving working conditions and occupational safety and health”
excerpt_en: As part of the EU's Result Oriented Monitoring (ROM), on 9 and 10 February 2023 the monitor Edin Jahić visited Montenegro to review progress on the regional project to improve working conditions.
content_en:
As part of the EU's Result Oriented Monitoring (ROM) activities, on 9 and 10 February the project “Enhance labour conditions and occupational safety and health as a support to the Western Balkans towards accessing the European Union” was visited by the monitor appointed for the purpose from Brussels, Edin Jahić. The aim of ROM is to establish, on behalf of the EU which finances the project, what progress the project's activities have made to date in each of the countries involved in this regional project.
For the purposes of the monitoring, Edin Jahić held a series of meetings that Đina Janković had arranged in advance. The purpose of the meetings with the project's participants in Montenegro was to discuss the project's activities in the country so far and the results achieved under each activity. The focus was on the activities successfully carried out, but also on those that were not — the most significant being “Establishing a National Council for OSH in Montenegro” — and on the reasons why this pre-set objective was not achieved. The reasons given were the unstable political situation in the country over the past few years and the lack of will in the responsible ministry to establish such a body.
Meetings were held with representatives of UZNR CG and with participants in the workshops the Association held in the preceding period. Some of the meetings were held at the organisation's offices and some at the Ministry of Education.
The following took part in the monitoring:
1. Đina Janković – Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, project coordinator,
2. Zdenko Janković – Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro, president,
3. Branislav Šebek – executive director and owner of Montinspekt, a licensed occupational safety and health organisation,
4. Zlatko Popović – Administration of Inspection Affairs, occupational safety and health inspector,
5. Anđa Strugar – Institute for Development and Research in Occupational Safety,
6. Sandra Obradović – Union of Free Trade Unions of Montenegro,
7. Dejan Nuculović – Employers' Union of Montenegro,
8. Lidija Brnović – expert in education and public policy and trainer in public advocacy within human rights NGOs,
9. Jelena Raičević – Ministry of Ecology, Spatial Planning and Urbanism,
10. Tamara Martinović, Ministry of Education, Directorate for General Secondary Education, Vocational Education and Lifelong Learning,
11. Marija Milić, Ministry of Education, Directorate for General Secondary Education, Vocational Education and Lifelong Learning,
12. Marko Burić, occupational medicine doctor
Đina Janković also supplied the monitor, Mr Jahić, with all the reports on the activities carried out in the preceding period:
• Annual report on the work of UZNR CG, 1 February 2020 – 31 January 2021
• Annual report on the work of UZNR CG, 1 February 2021 – 31 January 2022
• Annual report on the work of UZNR CG, 1 February 2022 – 31 January 2023

title: Sastanak članova projektnog tima i Upravnog odbora UZNR CG
excerpt: Upravni odbor UZNR CG sastao se 1. februara 2023. kako bi razmotrio rezultate radionica u srednjim školama i fakultetima i isplanirao obilježavanje Svjetskog dana zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
content:
Dana 01.02.2023. održan je sastanak članova Upravnog odbora. Sastanku su prisustvovali Zdenko Janković, Zlatko Popović, Slavica Grgurović, Anđa Strugar, Marjan Brčić, Andrijana Kaljević, Sanja Dujović, Radmila Mićović, Rajko Radusinović, Đina Janković i pripravnice Sandra Lalević i Karolina Popović.
Đina Janković je prezentovala uspješne rezultate realizovanih radionica u srednjim stručnim školama i na tehničkim fakultetima, koje su održane prethodnih mjeseci u okviru projekta „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“. Prisutnima je prenijela utiske nastavnika i njihove potrebe da se sa ovakvom vrstom aktivnosti nastavi i narednom periodu, budući da nastavnici imaju vrlo nizak nivo znanja o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu i da im je potrebna edukacija da bi znanja mogli prenijeti učenicima.
Iako se Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore, u prethodnih 25 godina postojanja, kroz svoje aktivnosti nije bavilo mladima, kroz zabrinjavajuće rezultate istraživanja koja su u prethodnom periodu sprovedena, prepoznata je potreba da mladi budu u fokusu narednih planiranih aktivnosti UZNR CG, naglasila je Janković, s čim su prisutni bili saglasni.
Predsjednik UZNR CG je prezentovao program rada za naredni period i zadužio članove UO da formiraju komisiju koja će u narednom periodu pripremiti i organizovati redovnu Skupštinu.
Đina Janković je zamolila prisutne da razmisle o temi ovogodišnjeg Svjetskog dana zaštite i zdravlja na radu,, i da svoje ideje i predloge dostave što prije kako bi se na vrijeme započelo sa organizacijom događaja, koji će tradicionalno biti obilježen 28.aprila. Predložila je da, nakon usvajanja teme, budu održani sastanci sa socijalnim partnerima, koji bi mogli biti suorganizatori ovog događaja.
U znak zahvalnosti prema predavačima koji su dali veliki doprinos da radionice u srednjim stručnim školama i na fakultetima budu uspješno realizovane, nakon sastanka je upriličen ručak i neformalno druženje članova projektnog tima i UO, u podgoričkom restoranu „Desetka“.

title_en: Meeting of the project team and the UZNR CG Management Board
excerpt_en: On 1 February 2023 the UZNR CG Management Board met to review the results of the workshops in secondary schools and faculties and to plan the marking of World Day for Safety and Health at Work.
content_en:
On 1 February 2023 a meeting of the Management Board was held. It was attended by Zdenko Janković, Zlatko Popović, Slavica Grgurović, Anđa Strugar, Marjan Brčić, Andrijana Kaljević, Sanja Dujović, Radmila Mićović, Rajko Radusinović, Đina Janković and the trainees Sandra Lalević and Karolina Popović.
Đina Janković presented the successful results of the workshops held in secondary vocational schools and at the technical faculties over the preceding months under the project “Decent work starts while you are young”. She conveyed the teachers' impressions and their wish for activities of this kind to continue in the period ahead, since teachers have a very low level of knowledge about occupational safety and health and need training in order to pass knowledge on to pupils.
Although over the 25 years of its existence the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro has not worked with young people, the worrying results of the research carried out in the preceding period have made clear the need for young people to be the focus of UZNR CG's next planned activities, Janković emphasised, and those present agreed.
The president of UZNR CG presented the work programme for the period ahead and instructed board members to form a committee that will prepare and organise the regular Assembly.
Đina Janković asked those present to consider the theme for this year's World Day for Safety and Health at Work and to submit their ideas and proposals as soon as possible so that organisation of the event, traditionally marked on 28 April, can begin in good time. She proposed that, once the theme is adopted, meetings be held with the social partners, who could co-organise the event.
In recognition of the lecturers who contributed so much to the success of the workshops in secondary vocational schools and at the faculties, the meeting was followed by lunch and an informal gathering of the project team and the Management Board at the “Desetka” restaurant in Podgorica.

title: Predstavljanje Indeksa učešća mladih Crne Gore za 2021. godinu
excerpt: NVO Prima je tokom Nedjelje učešća mladih, od 23. do 30. januara 2023, predstavila Indeks učešća mladih za 2021. godinu, koji šestu godinu zaredom prati položaj mladih u Crnoj Gori.
content:
NVO Prima, u okviru Nedjelje učešća mladih, predstavila je Indeks učešća mladih za 2021. godinu. Istraživanje se sprovodi već 6 godina u okviru projekta „Zapadni Balkan i Turska za EmploYouth“, koji finansira Evropska unija a kofinansira Ministarstvo javne uprave Crne Gore Nedjelja učešća mladih je održana od 23. do 30. januara ove godine, tokom koje je javnost upoznata sa položajem mladih ljudi u Crnoj Gori i nalazima Indeksa učešća mladih.
Aida Perović, izvršna direktorica u NVO Prima i nacionalna koordinatorka Mreže Omladinski HUB za Zapadni Balkan i Tursku u Crnoj Gori, objasnila je da je Indeks učešća mladih važan instrument za lobiranje za bolje politike za mlade, naročito za one mlade koji dolaze iz osjetljivih grupa: „Indeks učešća mladih koji NVO Prima objavljuje poslednjih šest godina u okviru projekta „WB&T for EmploYouth – Podrška zapošljavanju mladih iz osjetljivih grupa“, je važan za praćenje trenda napretka, odnosno nazadovanja naše zemlje kada je u pitanju uključenost mladih. NVO Prima implementira projekat u Crnoj Gori, a u zemljama partnerima projekat realizuju Fondacija Ana i Vlade Divac iz Srbije, Pokret za promjene i razvoj iz Albanije, Savez mladih – Kruševo iz Sjeverne Makedonije i Fondacija volontera zajednice iz Turske. Projekat je dio aktivnosti Mreže Omladinski HUB za Zapadni Balkan i Tursku, koja ima 67 članica.“
Aleksandra Gligorović, viša istraživačica u NVO Prima, predstavila je Indeks učešća mladih koji uključuje podatke o političkoj, društvenoj i ekonomskoj participaciji mladih u Crnoj Gori, koji obuhvata indikatore iz 2021. godine: „Mladi u Crnoj Gori nisu dovoljno uključeni u sve sfere koje istraživanje obuhvata. Podaci o ekonomskom učešću mladih govore da se kvalitet života mladih smanjuje - u 2021. stopa nezaposlenih mladih bila je najveća u poslednjih 7 godina, i to 32,5 %. Svaka peta mlada osoba nezaposlena je duže od 12 mjeseci.
Na osnovu prikupljenih podataka, evidentno je da stepen društvenog učešća mladih u svim zemljama koje su obuhvaćene istraživanjem još uvijek nije dovoljno visok. Stanje društvene participacije mladih je slično u Crnoj Gori, Sjevernoj Makedoniji i Srbiji, dok je situacija nešto više zabrinjavajuća u Turskoj i Albaniji.
Alarmantan je nalaz da je 25% od ukupnog broja osoba u zatvoru u Crnoj Gori čine mladi.
Situacija u pogledu političkog učešća u svim zemljama učesnicama je nepovoljna i treba je značajno poboljšati. Vrijednosti indeksa političkog učešća u 2021. godini kretale su se od oko 29 u Turskoj do 50 u Srbiji, što je daleko od cilja od 100.
Zabrinjavajući je podatak da u našoj zemlji tradicionalno nemamo mladih gradonačelnika ni gradonačelnica, kao ni ministara i ministarki. Takođe, mladi u crnogorskom parlamentu čine samo 5%, preciznije 4 poslanika, dok mladih poslanica uopšte nema.“
Danijela Vujošević, predstavnica Ministarstva sporta i mladih objasnila je da se Ministarstvo zalaže za pobolšanje položaja mladih, i prilagođavanje politika njihovim potrebama: „Ministarstvo ulaže kontinuirane napore kako bi obezbijedilo uslove za bolje učešće mladih u Crnoj Gori, a to će biti primijenjeno i u Strategiji za mlade za period od naredne 4 godine. Strategiju kreiramo zajedno sa predstavnicima civilnog sektora, Omladinskih servisa i mladih, kako bi napravili dokument koji je po mjeri mladih. Strategija će najvjerovatnije biti usvojena u drugom kvartalu ove godine. Takođe, nadamo se da će Ministarstvo nakon 3 godine pauze ponovo otvoriti konkurs za podršku projektima NVO koje realizuju aktivnosti predviđene Akcionim planom i Strategijom.“
Elvis Beriša, potpredsjednik Mreže za mlade, predstavio je rad Omladinskog parlamenta koji je po prvi put organizovan na Dan volontera, petog decembra prošle godine: „Omladinski parlament je rezultat višemjesečnog rada mladih iz organizacija civilnog društva i političkih partija, sa ciljem da uključimo mlade koji će govoriti o prioritetnim problemima sa kojima se suočavaju. Fokusirali smo se na dvije teme od značaja za mlade: oblast obrazovanja i ekonomske politike. Veliki broj mladih je iskazalo interesovanje, okupili smo raznoliku grupu iz sve 3 regije Crne Gore. Ti mladi su predstavili svoje inicijative i nadamo se da u narednom periodu neće izostati podrška institucija. Nažalost, pitanje položaja mladih i dalje nije jedna od prioritetnih stavki. Ohrabruje nas što smo uspjeli da pošaljemo poruku da mladi žele promjene i da su spremni da budu dio promjena.“

title_en: Presentation of Montenegro's Youth Participation Index for 2021
excerpt_en: During Youth Participation Week, from 23 to 30 January 2023, the NGO Prima presented the Youth Participation Index for 2021, which has tracked the position of young people in Montenegro for six years running.
content_en:
As part of Youth Participation Week, the NGO Prima presented the Youth Participation Index for 2021. The research has been carried out for 6 years under the project “Western Balkans and Türkiye for EmploYouth”, financed by the European Union and co-financed by the Ministry of Public Administration of Montenegro. Youth Participation Week was held from 23 to 30 January this year, during which the public learned about the position of young people in Montenegro and the findings of the Youth Participation Index.
Aida Perović, executive director of the NGO Prima and national coordinator of the Youth HUB Network for the Western Balkans and Türkiye in Montenegro, explained that the Youth Participation Index is an important instrument for lobbying for better youth policy, particularly for young people from vulnerable groups: “The Youth Participation Index, which the NGO Prima has published for the past six years under the project ‘WB&T for EmploYouth – Support for the employment of young people from vulnerable groups', is important for tracking whether our country is progressing or falling back when it comes to the inclusion of young people. The NGO Prima implements the project in Montenegro, while in the partner countries it is carried out by the Ana and Vlade Divac Foundation from Serbia, Partners Albania for Change and Development, the Youth Alliance – Kruševo from North Macedonia and the Community Volunteers Foundation from Türkiye. The project is part of the work of the Youth HUB Network for the Western Balkans and Türkiye, which has 67 members.”
Aleksandra Gligorović, senior researcher at the NGO Prima, presented the Youth Participation Index, which includes data on the political, social and economic participation of young people in Montenegro and covers indicators from 2021: “Young people in Montenegro are not sufficiently involved in any of the spheres the research covers. The data on young people's economic participation shows that their quality of life is declining — in 2021 youth unemployment was at its highest in 7 years, at 32.5%. One in five young people has been unemployed for more than 12 months.
On the basis of the data collected, it is evident that the level of young people's social participation in all the countries covered by the research is still not high enough. The state of young people's social participation is similar in Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia, while the situation is somewhat more worrying in Türkiye and Albania.
One alarming finding is that 25% of all prisoners in Montenegro are young people.
The situation regarding political participation in all the participating countries is unfavourable and needs significant improvement. Political participation index values in 2021 ranged from about 29 in Türkiye to 50 in Serbia, far from the target of 100.
It is worrying that our country traditionally has no young mayors and no young ministers. Young people also make up only 5% of the Montenegrin parliament — 4 members precisely — and there are no young women members at all.”
Danijela Vujošević, representing the Ministry of Sport and Youth, explained that the Ministry is working to improve the position of young people and to adapt policy to their needs: “The Ministry is making continuous efforts to create the conditions for better participation by young people in Montenegro, and that will also be reflected in the Youth Strategy for the next 4 years. We are drawing up the strategy together with representatives of the civil sector, youth services and young people themselves, in order to produce a document tailored to young people. The strategy will most likely be adopted in the second quarter of this year. We also hope that after a 3-year break the Ministry will once again open a call for support to NGO projects carrying out the activities set out in the Action Plan and the Strategy.”
Elvis Beriša, vice-president of the Youth Network, presented the work of the Youth Parliament, held for the first time on Volunteers' Day, 5 December last year: “The Youth Parliament is the result of several months' work by young people from civil society organisations and political parties, with the aim of involving young people who will speak about the priority problems they face. We focused on two subjects of importance to young people: education and economic policy. A great many young people expressed interest, and we brought together a diverse group from all 3 regions of Montenegro. Those young people presented their initiatives, and we hope that institutional support will not be lacking in the period ahead. Unfortunately, the position of young people is still not among the priorities. It encourages us that we managed to send the message that young people want change and are ready to be part of that change.”

title: Sastanak sa predstavnicima NVO Mladi Romi
excerpt: UZNR CG je razgovaralo sa predstavnicima NVO Mladi Romi, Samirom Jahom i Nermom Softić, o potrebi osposobljavanja sakupljača sekundarnih sirovina za bezbjedan rad.
content:
Na sastanku sa predstavnicima NVO Mladi Romi – Samirom Jahom i Nermom Softić, koji su kroz projekat koji finansira Američka ambasada u Crnoj Gori obezbjedila alat i opremu za 30 sakupljača sekundarnih sirovina u 11 opština, što će, smatraju, doprinijeti poboljšanju uslova rada u narednom periodu, bilo je govora o neophodnosti njihovog osposoblajvanja za bezbjedan rad i upoznavanja sa rizicima koje ta vrsta posla nosi.
Nedostatak dostojnog posla, je posebno izražen među ranjivim grupacijama kojima pripadaju mladi Romi, kojih prema podacima sa posljednjeg popisa stanovništva, u Crnoj Gori živi nešto više od 8 hiljada, dok su procjene da je taj broj veći od 12 hiljada.
58% mladih Roma je bez posla i van sistema obrazovanja i obuke (NEET kategorija) u poređenju sa 13% mladih na nivou EU. U tu kategoriju spadaju sakupljači sekundarnih sirovina koji obavljaju taj posao na crno, odnosno bez bilo kakvih prava iz oblasti radnih odnosa, bez osiguranja i drugih benifita koji imaju zaposlena lica, kao i bez neophodne zaštite na radu.
Povrede su, tokom obavljanja ovih poslova česte, ali ih oni ne prijavljuju jer najčešće nemaju zdravstveno osiguranje, a i zbog potrebe svakodnevnog obavljanja posla i prehranjivanja porodice, usljed čega nemaju vremena za liječenje.
Nezaposlenost mladih Roma, NEET status i okolnosti koje ih primoravaju da rade u zoni sive ekonomije u neadekvatnim uslovima – pogađa ne samo te mlade osobe, već i njihove porodice, onemogućavajući lični i profesionalni razvoj pojedinaca i negativno se odražavajući na društvo u cjelini.

title_en: Meeting with representatives of the NGO Young Roma
excerpt_en: UZNR CG met representatives of the NGO Young Roma, Samir Jaha and Nerma Softić, to discuss the need to train collectors of recyclable materials for safe work.
content_en:
At a meeting with representatives of the NGO Young Roma — Samir Jaha and Nerma Softić, who through a project financed by the US Embassy in Montenegro provided tools and equipment for 30 collectors of recyclable materials in 11 municipalities, which they believe will improve working conditions in the period ahead — there was discussion of the need to train them for safe work and to acquaint them with the risks this kind of work carries.
The lack of decent work is particularly pronounced among vulnerable groups such as young Roma, of whom, according to the last census, somewhat more than 8,000 live in Montenegro, though the number is estimated to be higher than 12,000.
58% of young Roma are not in employment, education or training (the NEET category), compared with 13% of young people at EU level. That category includes collectors of recyclable materials, who do that work undeclared — that is, without any employment rights, without insurance and without the other benefits employed people have, and without the necessary protection at work.
Injuries during this work are frequent, but they go unreported because those affected usually have no health insurance, and because they need to work every day to feed their families, leaving them no time for treatment.
Unemployment among young Roma, their NEET status and the circumstances that force them to work in the grey economy in inadequate conditions affect not only those young people but also their families, preventing personal and professional development and having a negative effect on society as a whole.
