excerpt_en: On 31 May 2022 UZNR CG signed a contract with “Alfa Centar Nikšić” for the project “For healthier workplaces 2022–2024 in Montenegro”.
content_en:
Podgorica, 31 May 2022
A contract has been signed with “Alfa Centar Nikšić” for the project “For healthier workplaces 2022-2024 in Montenegro”.
The project will be carried out under the regional project “Improving working conditions and occupational safety and health in support of the Western Balkan countries in the EU accession process”, whose activities are also carried out in the IPA countries — North Macedonia, Kosovo, Montenegro, Serbia and Albania.

title: Radionica „Bezbjednost kao izbor“ u Pivari „Trebjesa“
excerpt: Pivara „Trebjesa“ iz Nikšića organizovala je 25. maja 2022. dan posvećen zaštiti i zdravlju na radu i radionicu „Bezbjednost kao izbor“, uz učešće UZNR CG i Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja.
content:
Nikšić, 25. maj 2022.
Pivara „Trebjesa“ Nikšić je 25. maja 2022. godine organizovala dan posvećen zaštiti i zdravlju na radu i tim povodom je održana radionica „BEZBJEDNOST KAO IZBOR“.
Sve proizvodne i procesne aktivnosti, oprema i transport su zaustavljeni tog dana, kako bi svi zaposleni u proizvodnji i logistici mogli da uzmu učešće na radionici.
Radionica se sastojala iz dva dijela. U prvom dijelu su, nakon uvodnih riječi Milana Kilibarde,
EHS rukovodioca, i Vanje Lazarevića, direktora proizvodnje i logistike - svoja izlaganja imale Đina Janković, sekretarka i projektna koordinatorka UZNRCG, koja je prezentovala na temu „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu iz perspektive Udruženja zaštite na radu Crne Gore“ i Danijela Šuković, načelnica direkcije za poslove zastite i zdravlja na radu u Ministarstvu rada i socijalnog staranja, koja je prezentovala na temu „Zaštita i zdravlje na radu iz perspektive Ministarstva rada i socijalnog staranja“.
U drugom dijelu su bile organizovane teorijske i praktične radionice iz nekoliko različitih tema: Prva pomoć, Zaštita od požara, Rad na visini i LOTO standard.
Na kraju dana je bilo proglašenje najbolja 3 slogana i uručenje nagrada sa konkursa.
title_en: Workshop “Safety as a choice” at the “Trebjesa” brewery
excerpt_en: On 25 May 2022 the “Trebjesa” brewery in Nikšić held a day devoted to occupational safety and health and the workshop “Safety as a choice”, with UZNR CG and the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare taking part.
content_en:
Nikšić, 25 May 2022
On 25 May 2022 the “Trebjesa” brewery in Nikšić held a day devoted to occupational safety and health, and marked the occasion with the workshop “SAFETY AS A CHOICE”.
All production and process activities, equipment and transport were halted for the day so that everyone working in production and logistics could take part in the workshop.
The workshop had two parts. In the first, following opening remarks by Milan Kilibarda, EHS manager, and Vanja Lazarević, director of production and logistics, presentations were given by Đina Janković, secretary and project coordinator of UZNR CG, on “Occupational safety and health from the perspective of the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro”, and by Danijela Šuković, head of the occupational safety and health directorate at the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare, on “Occupational safety and health from the perspective of the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare”.
The second part comprised theoretical and practical workshops on several topics: first aid, fire protection, work at height and the LOTO standard.
The day ended with the announcement of the three best slogans from the competition and the presentation of prizes.

title: Svjetski dan zaštite i zdravlja na radu – konferencija „Saradnjom do kulture zaštite i zdravlja na radu“
excerpt: Povodom Svjetskog dana zaštite i zdravlja na radu, UZNR CG je 28. aprila 2022. organizovalo konferenciju i dodijelilo priznanja institucijama i pojedincima koji su najviše doprinijeli razvoju ove oblasti tokom prethodne godine.
content:
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore je povodom obilježavanja Svjetskog dana zaštite i zdravlja na radu organizovalo konferenciju, s ciljem podsjećanja na sve one koji su u prethodnoj godini izgubili živote – zarađujući za život.
Kako bi se postigli pozitivni rezulati u ovoj djelatnosti od javnog interesa, koji se ogledaju u podizanju svijesti, smanjenju broja povreda, profesionalnih bolesti i oboljenja u vezi s radom, neophodno je zajedničko djelovanje i uključivanje svih aktera.
Budući da ostvarenju navedenih ciljeva doprinose svi, učesnici konferencije su bili organi vlasti, poslodavci, zaposleni, ovlašćene organizacije za obavljanje poslova iz oblasti zaštite na radu, zdravstvene i naučno-istraživačke institucije, sudski vještaci, sudstvo, tužilaštvo i organizacije civilnog društva. Uzimajući u obzir činjenicu da zaštita i zdravlje na radu pozitivno utiče na motivaciju zaposlenih, produktivnost rada, konkurentnost i poslovni uspjeh poslodavaca, kao i ukupan ekonomski i socijalni razvoj svake države, to zahtijeva otvorenu komunikaciju i dijalog izgrađen na povjerenju i međusobnom poštovanju svih učesnika ovog procesa, što je i bila poruka ovog skupa. Svoju ulogu u vrlo kompleksnom lancu zaštite na radu na konferenciji su prezentovali:
1. Đina Janković, Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore, Godina za nama – aktivnosti UZNRCG koje su obilježile prethodni period, strateški ciljevi razvoja zaštite i zdravlja na radu u regionu
2. Doc. dr Dragan Žarković, dipl.građ.ing., Predsjednik Nezavisnog udruženja sudskih vještaka Crne Gore, ovlašćeni: projektant, revizor, sudski vještak i procjenitelj Crnogorska iskustva u implementaciji standarda zaštite na radu
3. Radovan Vlaović, sudija Osnovnog suda Podgorica, Iskustva iz prakse
4. Arman Selmanović, Rukovodilac Državnog tužilaštva Podgorica, Značaj poštovanja propisa koji regulišu oblast ZZNR i posljedice njihovog nepridržavanja – primjeri prakse
S ciljem promovisanja dobre prakse UZNRCG je dodijelilo priznanja institucijama i pojedincima koji su dali najveći doprinos razvoju zaštite i zdravlja na radu u prethodnoj godini.
Plakete su dobili:
Pravna lica
1. Unija poslodavaca Crne Gore
2. Pivara „Trebjesa“, Nikšić
3. EPCG AD
4. Institut za javno zdravlje
5. Daido Metal, Kotor
6. Neregelia
Fuzička lica
7. Mihailo Caušević, predsjednik sindikalne organizacije CNP-a
8. Nenad Marković predsjednik sindikata gradjevinarstva i IGM Crne Gore
Unija poslodavaca Crne Gore, prepoznata je od strane Udruženja kao organizacija koja je svih prethodnih godina, od svog osnivanja 2005. davala nemjerljiv doprinos razvoju oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu i podizanju svijesti svojih članova – poslodavaca - kroz brojne okrugle stolove i seminare, koje su organizovali na ovu temu. Takođe su dali veliki doprinos svojim učešćem u radnim grupama za izradu i unapređenje nacionalne zakonske regulative i strateških dokumenata iz ove oblasti. Osim toga, uvjek su davali nesebičnu podršku svim aktivnostima koje je Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore sprovodilo.
Poruka Unije poslodavaca svih prethodnih godina je bila da „zaštita na radu i bezbjedno radno mjesto jesu i treba da budu prioritet za sve aktere na tržištu rada – i poslodavce i zaposlene i državu. Sa aspekta privrede, kada su zaposleni zadovoljni i bezbjedni, za očekivati je da će njihovi poslovni rezultati biti bolji, odnosno da će produktivnost biti veća, a poslovanje kompanije ekonomičnije, rentabilnije i uspješnije.“
Mnogo puta su se mogle čuti riječi, izgovorene od strane predstavnika Unije poslodavaca, da je jedan od preduslova poslovne uspješnosti upravo kvalitetan sistem zaštite zdravlja zaposlenih, čime su uticali na promjenu načina razmišljanja mnogih poslodavaca u Crnoj Gori.
Pivara „Trebjesa“ je značajno doprinijela razvoju zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kao društveno odgovorna kompanija koja brine o bezbjednosti i zdravlju na radu, kao i o zaštiti životne sredine. Ona svoju djelatnost temelji na socijalnim, ekološkim i ekonomskim načelima, svrstavajući otvoren i pošten odnos prema društvenoj zajednici u najveće prioritete. U 2021. godini, Pivara „Trebjesa“ je organizovala dvodnevni trening na temu kreiranja kulture zaštite na radu „Safe by choice“ iliti „Sigurni po izboru“, zahvaljujući kom su učesnici mogli doći do zaista važne poruke – Biti bezbjedan je stvar izbora, a ne oslanjanja na sreću. Takođe, ova kompanije je u istoj godini relizovala cijeli niz projekata iz oblasti ZZNR.
Institut za javno zdravlje Crne Gore učestvovao je u radnim grupama za izradu nacionalne zakonske regulative i strateških dokumenata iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu. Ova visoko specijalizovana javna ustanova je, u cilju sprovođenja i unaprijeđenja mjera zaštite i zdravlja na radu, implementirala standard za sistem menadžmenta i formirala radnu grupu za implementaciju i praćenje Integrisanog menadžment sistema. IJZCG je sproveo cjelodnevnu edukaciju za zaposlene iz kulture rada i kulture dijaloga „Kako da komuniciramo a da se razumijemo“, radi oslobađanja od stresa, podizanja raspoloženja i motivacije za rad. Osim brige o zdravstvenom stanju stanovništva Crne Gore, IJZCG kroz brojne obuke i predavanja brine o zdravlju i bezbjednosti svojih zaposlenih.
Pažnju Udruženja zavrijedila je i kompanija Daido Metal Kotor AD, koja posluje kao dio grupe fabrika, a prva je osnovana u Japanu 1945. godine. Radi se o fabrici koja ima izrađenu procjenu rizika za svako radno mjesto u njoj. Kada dođe do povreda u bilo kojoj kompaniji koja pripada Daido Metal Group-u, obavezujuće je za istu kompaniju da uradi analizu uzroka i nastanka povrede na radu, kao i da sačini sveobuhvatan izvještaj o povredi.Kompanija posjeduje obrazac za pomenuti izvještaj, koji se koristi za podjelu informacija svim kompanijama unutar Daido Metal Group-a. Izvještaj se prevodi na službeni jezik kompanije DMK i kao takav se stavlja na oglasnu tablu, da bi bio dostupan svakom radniku.
Kompanija osnovana prije dvije decenije, a danas već vodeća na polju distribucije u Crnoj Gori - Neregelia, posjeduje Pravilnik o ZZNR i kompanija je čije redovne obavezne aktivnosti uključuju inicijalnu i ponovnu obuku zaposlenih prije zapošljavanja, prethodne i periodične ljekarske preglede u skladu sa Aktom o procjeni rizika i kompanijskim pravilnikom o ZZNR. Unutar kompanije se vrše redovne kontrole prohodnosti evakuacionih puteva, stanja i dostupnosti hidranata i PP aparata, a takođe se i uredno vode evidencije o povredama na radu. Neregelia čini dio sistema više pravnih lica, u kojem svako pravno lice ima svoje stručno lice za ZZNR, što potvrđuje njihovu nameru da zaštiti na radu posvećuju neophodnu pažnju. Zaposlenima su pružene obuke iz prve pomoći i zaštite od požara, Neregelia je partner Podgoričkog maratona preko 10 godina, organizovala je akcije dobrovoljnog davanja krvi, online radionice o upravljanju stresom i karijerom, akciju kompanijski ljekar-besplatan pregled za sve zaposlene, učestvovala i u radnim akcijama zaštite životne sredine.
Neko ko se trudi da zadovolji standarde u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, zaštite životne sredine i društvene odgovornosti, te je sertifikovana po zahtjevima internacionalnih standarda je nacionalna elektroenergetska kompanija - Elektroprivreda Crne Gore AD Nikšić.
Kompanija je koja se razvija sa ciljem da unaprijedi odnos prema svojim korisnicima, zaposlenima i ostalim zainteresovanim stranama. U skladu sa Zakonom o UZNR i Aktom o procjeni rizika, EPCG organizuje i sprovodi ljekarske i sanitarne preglede zaposlenih. Takođe, posjeduje i sopstveni Program osposobljavanja za rad. Zaposlenima se svake godine nabavlja i obezbjeđuje LZSO, koju isti redovno zadužuju, u skladu sa Zakonskim zahtjevima i rokovima definisanim Normativom LZS i KZS, o čemu se vodi evidencija. Na godišnjem nivou se donosi i Plan internih kontrola i prema istom se vrše provjere iz oblasti ZZNR.
Elektroprivreda Crne Gore, u okviru svojih aktivnosti odnosa sa javnostima, realizuje sponzorstva i donacije. Kada je briga o zaposlenima u pitanju, posebno se izdvajaju rješavanje stambenih potreba zaposlenih, rehabilitacija zaposlenih, finansijska pomoć i njihovo liječenje, naknada štete nastala usljed povrede na radu, podsticanje zaposlenih za učešće u kulturnim manifestacijama i događajima, kao i briga o porodicama preminulih radnika kroz stipendiranje i zapošljavanje članova njihove porodice i obezbeđivanje stambenih kredita. U EPCG-u se iz godine u godinu dešava sve manji broj povreda na radu, što dodatno svjedoči o njihovoj posvećenosti ZZNR.
Mihailo Caušević, predsjednik je sindikalne organizacije CNP-a, i neko je ko je u zaista dugom vremenskom periodu ukazivao na probleme zaposlenih koji se posebno odražavaju na radni, profesionalni i ekonomsko-socijalni položaj zaposlenih.
Njegova dobro poznata rečenica glasi: „Ako je kultura stub društva, pozorište je stub kulture“.
CNP se dugi niz godina suočavao sa problemom nedonošenja akta o sistematizaciji, što je za sobom povuklo i izradu više ključnih akata, svih vezanih za zaštitu i zdravlje zaposlenih, među kojima je i Akt o procjeni rizika. Zaslugu za donošenje pomenutih akata pripisujemo upravo upornom i istrajnom radu i trudu Mihaila Cauševića.
Neko ko je zaslužio priznanje i nagradu od strane Udruženja je i Nenad Marković predsjednik sindikata gradjevinarstva i IGM Crne Gore, koji je baveći se sindikalnim radom organizovao dvadesetak seminara na temu ZZNR. Zaključio je GKU za građevinarstvo i doprinosio razvoju ZZNR-a kroz različite projekte i projektne aktivnosti.
Uloga Nenada Markovića posebno je bitna jer je građevinarstvo najrizičnija industrijska grana sa najvećim brojem povreda na radu - od kojih se mnoge završe smrtnim ishodom.
title_en: World Day for Safety and Health at Work – conference “Through cooperation to a culture of occupational safety and health”
excerpt_en: To mark World Day for Safety and Health at Work, on 28 April 2022 UZNR CG held a conference and presented awards to the institutions and individuals who contributed most to the field over the previous year.
content_en:
To mark World Day for Safety and Health at Work, the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro organised a conference in memory of all those who lost their lives over the past year while earning a living.
If positive results are to be achieved in this field of public interest — greater awareness and fewer injuries, occupational diseases and work-related illnesses — joint action and the involvement of every actor is essential.
Since everyone contributes to achieving those goals, the conference brought together public authorities, employers, employees, organisations licensed to carry out occupational safety work, health and research institutions, court experts, the judiciary, the prosecution service and civil society organisations. Given that occupational safety and health has a positive effect on employees' motivation, on productivity, on competitiveness and on employers' business success, as well as on the overall economic and social development of any country, it requires open communication and a dialogue built on trust and mutual respect among everyone involved in the process — which was the message of this gathering. Their role in the highly complex chain of occupational safety was presented at the conference by:
1. Đina Janković, Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro — “The year behind us: UZNR CG's activities over the past period and the strategic objectives for developing occupational safety and health in the region”
2. Dr Dragan Žarković, civil engineer, president of the Independent Association of Court Experts of Montenegro, licensed designer, auditor, court expert and assessor — “Montenegro's experience in implementing occupational safety standards”
3. Radovan Vlaović, judge at the Basic Court in Podgorica — “Experience from practice”
4. Arman Selmanović, head of the State Prosecutor's Office in Podgorica — “The importance of complying with the regulations governing OSH and the consequences of failing to do so — examples from practice”
In order to promote good practice, UZNR CG presented awards to the institutions and individuals who made the greatest contribution to the development of occupational safety and health over the past year.
Plaques were awarded to:
Organisations
1. Employers' Union of Montenegro
2. “Trebjesa” brewery, Nikšić
3. EPCG AD
4. Institute of Public Health
5. Daido Metal, Kotor
6. Neregelia
Individuals
7. Mihailo Caušević, president of the trade union organisation of the Montenegrin National Theatre
8. Nenad Marković, president of the construction and building materials trade union of Montenegro
The Employers' Union of Montenegro was recognised by the Association as an organisation that, ever since its founding in 2005, has made an immeasurable contribution to the development of occupational safety and health and to raising awareness among its members — employers — through the many round tables and seminars it has organised on the subject. It has also contributed greatly through its participation in the working groups drafting and improving national legislation and strategic documents in this field. Beyond that, it has always given generous support to every activity the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro has carried out.
The Employers' Union's message over all these years has been that “occupational safety and a safe workplace are, and should be, a priority for every actor on the labour market — employers, employees and the state alike. From a business point of view, when employees are satisfied and safe, their results can be expected to be better, productivity higher and the company's operations more economical, more profitable and more successful.”
On many occasions representatives of the Employers' Union have said that one of the preconditions of business success is precisely a good system for protecting employees' health, thereby changing the thinking of many employers in Montenegro.
The “Trebjesa” brewery has made a significant contribution to the development of occupational safety and health as a socially responsible company that cares about safety and health at work and about protecting the environment. It bases its work on social, environmental and economic principles, placing an open and honest relationship with the community among its highest priorities. In 2021 the “Trebjesa” brewery organised a two-day training session on creating a culture of safety at work, “Safe by choice”, through which participants took away a truly important message — being safe is a matter of choice, not of relying on luck. In the same year the company also carried out a whole series of OSH projects.
The Institute of Public Health of Montenegro took part in the working groups drafting national legislation and strategic documents on occupational safety and health. In order to implement and improve occupational safety and health measures, this highly specialised public institution has implemented a management system standard and formed a working group to implement and monitor an Integrated Management System. It ran a full day of training for staff on working culture and a culture of dialogue, “How to communicate and understand each other”, aimed at relieving stress and improving morale and motivation. Alongside caring for the health of Montenegro's population, the Institute looks after the health and safety of its own staff through numerous training sessions and lectures.
The Association's attention was also earned by Daido Metal Kotor AD, which operates as part of a group of factories first established in Japan in 1945. This is a factory with a risk assessment produced for every workplace within it. When an injury occurs at any company belonging to the Daido Metal Group, that company is required to analyse the cause and occurrence of the injury and to produce a comprehensive report on it. The company has a form for that report, which is used to share information with all the companies within the Daido Metal Group. The report is translated into DMK's official language and posted on the noticeboard so that it is available to every worker.
Founded two decades ago and today already a leader in distribution in Montenegro, Neregelia has an OSH rulebook and is a company whose regular mandatory activities include initial and refresher training for employees before they start work and prior and periodic medical examinations in line with the risk assessment act and the company's OSH rulebook. The company carries out regular checks of the passability of escape routes and of the condition and availability of hydrants and fire extinguishers, and keeps proper records of injuries at work. Neregelia is part of a system of several legal entities, in which each entity has its own OSH professional, confirming its intention to give safety at work the attention it requires. Employees have received training in first aid and fire protection; Neregelia has been a partner of the Podgorica Marathon for more than 10 years, has organised blood donation drives, online workshops on stress and career management and a “company doctor” campaign offering free check-ups for all employees, and has taken part in environmental clean-up campaigns.
One organisation that works to meet standards in occupational safety and health, environmental protection and social responsibility, and is certified to international standards, is the national electricity company Elektroprivreda Crne Gore AD Nikšić.
The company is developing with the aim of improving its relationship with its customers, its employees and other stakeholders. In line with the Law on Occupational Safety and Health and its risk assessment act, EPCG organises and carries out medical and sanitary examinations for employees. It also has its own training programme for work. Every year employees are supplied with personal protective equipment, which they are duly issued with in line with legal requirements and the deadlines set out in the norms for personal and collective protective equipment, and records are kept accordingly. An annual internal audit plan is adopted and OSH checks are carried out under it.
As part of its public relations work, Elektroprivreda Crne Gore provides sponsorship and donations. As regards care for employees, particular mention should be made of help with housing, rehabilitation, financial assistance and treatment, compensation for damage arising from injuries at work, encouragement for employees to take part in cultural events, and care for the families of deceased workers through scholarships, employment for family members and housing loans. Year by year EPCG records fewer injuries at work, further testifying to its commitment to OSH.
Mihailo Caušević, president of the trade union organisation of the Montenegrin National Theatre, has over a very long period drawn attention to the problems of employees that particularly affect their working, professional and economic and social position.
His well-known line is: “If culture is the pillar of society, the theatre is the pillar of culture.”
For many years the Montenegrin National Theatre faced the problem of having no job classification act adopted, which held up the production of several key documents relating to employees' safety and health, among them the risk assessment act. The credit for those documents finally being adopted belongs precisely to Mihailo Caušević's persistent, determined work and effort.
Another who has earned the Association's recognition and award is Nenad Marković, president of the construction and building materials trade union of Montenegro, who through his trade union work has organised some twenty seminars on OSH. He concluded the branch collective agreement for construction and has contributed to the development of OSH through various projects and activities.
Nenad Marković's role is particularly important because construction is the riskiest industrial sector, with the highest number of injuries at work — many of them fatal.

title: Dostojanstven rad – počinje dok si mlad
excerpt: UZNR CG je najavilo istraživanje o položaju mladih 16–29 godina u Crnoj Gori u okviru projekta „Dostojanstven rad – počinje dok si mlad“, koji finansira Evropska unija kroz mrežu Youth HUB za Zapadni Balkan i Tursku.
content:
Svakog dana u svijetu pogine na radnom mjestu ili umre od profesionalnih bolesti - 7.600 ljudi, a oko milion ljudi bude povrijeđeno na poslu. Najveću stopu povreda na radu trpe mladi, zbog nedostatka svijesti o pravilima i pravima zaposlenih o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu, ograničenih radnih vještina i radnog iskustva, nedostatka obuke, prevencije opasnosti ili izbjegavanja izloženosti štetnim agensima, dugog radnog vremena i neadekvatnih uslova rada.
Kakvo je stanje u Crnoj Gori kada su u pitanju mladi ljudi starosti 16-29 godina, istražuje UZNRCG u okviru projekta „Dostojanstven rad – počinje dok si mlad“, koji finansira Evropska unija, u okviru mreže Youth HUB for WB&T.
title_en: Decent work starts while you are young
excerpt_en: UZNR CG announced research into the position of young people aged 16–29 in Montenegro under the project “Decent work starts while you are young”, financed by the European Union through the Youth HUB network for the Western Balkans and Türkiye.
content_en:
Every day around the world 7,600 people die at work or from occupational diseases, and about a million are injured on the job. Young people suffer the highest rate of injuries at work, because of a lack of awareness of the rules and of employees' rights regarding occupational safety and health, limited working skills and experience, a lack of training, a failure to prevent hazards or avoid exposure to harmful agents, long working hours and inadequate working conditions.
UZNR CG is researching the situation in Montenegro for young people aged 16–29 under the project “Decent work starts while you are young”, financed by the European Union within the Youth HUB for WB&T network.

title: Sastanak članova projektnog tima „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“
excerpt: Nakon što je UZNR CG postalo član mreže YouthHUB za Zapadni Balkan i Tursku, projektni tim se sastao 16. marta 2022. kako bi isplanirao aktivnosti novog projekta „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“.
content:
Budući da je Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore postalo član YouthHUB mreže Zapadnog Balkana i Turske i uz podršku i koordinaciju NVO Prima, u narednih godinu dana će realizovati projekat „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“, koji finansira Evropska komisija, članovi projektnog tima održali su sastanak 16.03.2022. Sastanku su prisustvovali predsjednik Zdenko Janković, potpredsjednici Zlatko Popović i Branislav Šebek, član Upravnog odbora Nebojša Vujošević, projektna koordinatorka Đina Janković i praktikantkinja Ana Vuković.
Budući da je cilj ovog projekta povećanje udjela mladih iz NEET kategorije na tržištu rada, kroz unaprjeđenje bezbjednosti na radnim mjestima i izgradnju kulture sprečavanja povreda i oboljevanja, napravljen je plan za realizaciju planiranih aktivnosti za naredni period.
U prvom periodu fokus aktivnosti će biti na razvoju Upitnika u svrhu istraživanja o broju i vrstama povređivanja mladih na radu, kao i o vrstama profesionalnih oboljenja i bolesti u vezi sa radom (za dvije kategorije mladih – onih koji su nadležnoj instituciji prijavili povredu/profesionalno oboljenje i bolest u vezi sa radom i onih koji to, iz nekih razloga nijesu uradili, čime su bili ukraćeni za sva prava koja ih po tom osnovu sljeduju.
title_en: Meeting of the project team for “Decent work starts while you are young”
excerpt_en: After UZNR CG became a member of the YouthHUB network for the Western Balkans and Türkiye, the project team met on 16 March 2022 to plan the activities of the new project “Decent work starts while you are young”.
content_en:
Since the Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro has become a member of the YouthHUB network of the Western Balkans and Türkiye and, with the support and coordination of the NGO Prima, will over the coming year carry out the project “Decent work starts while you are young”, financed by the European Commission, the project team met on 16 March 2022. The meeting was attended by president Zdenko Janković, vice-presidents Zlatko Popović and Branislav Šebek, management board member Nebojša Vujošević, project coordinator Đina Janković and intern Ana Vuković.
Since the project aims to increase the share of young people from the NEET category on the labour market by improving workplace safety and building a culture of preventing injuries and illness, a plan was drawn up for carrying out the planned activities in the period ahead.
In the first phase the focus will be on developing a questionnaire for research into the number and types of injuries young people suffer at work and into the types of occupational disease and work-related illness — covering two categories of young people: those who reported an injury, occupational disease or work-related illness to the competent institution, and those who for whatever reason did not, thereby losing all the rights that would have followed.

title: Potpisivanje ugovora sa NVO Prima – početak projekta „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“
excerpt: UZNR CG je 15. marta 2022. postalo član mreže YouthHUB za Zapadni Balkan i Tursku i, uz podršku NVO Prima, započelo realizaciju projekta „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“, koji finansira Evropska komisija.
content:
Potpisivanje ugovora sa NVO Prima – članstvo u YouthHUB mreži Zapadnog Balkana i Turske i početak realizacije projekta „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“
15.03.2022.
Udruženje zaštite na radu Crne Gore je postalo član YouthHUB mreže Zapadnog Balkana i Turske i uz podršku i koordinaciju NVO Prima, u narednih godinu dana će relizovati projekat „Dostojanstven rad počinje dok si mlad“, koji finansira Evropska komisija.
Budući da svi podaci EU OSHA govore da su mladi između 18 – 24 godine u mnogo većem riziku od povređivanja, a EU strateški okvir zaštite i zdravlja na radu 2022 – 2027, poseban akcenat stavlja na mlade ljude, cilj ovog projekta će biti povećanje udjela mladih iz NEET kategorije, kroz unaprjeđenje bezbjednosti na radnim mjestima i izgradnjom kulture sprečavanja i oboljevanja.
Kroz upitnik koji ćemo razviti, očekujemo da ćemo na kraju projektne godine imati jasniju sliku o broju povreda koje su mladi ljudi doživjeli na svojim radnim mjestima, posebno u zoni sive ekonomije.
Realizovaćemo edukativne radionice u srednjim stručnim školama u Podgorici, Bijelom Polju i Nikšiću, kao i na tehničkim fakultetima i na taj način, barem djelimično, upoznati mlade ljude sa izazovima i problemima u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, s kojima će se suočiti dolaskom na tržište rada, nakon završenog procesa obrazovanja.
title_en: Signing of a contract with the NGO Prima – the start of the project “Decent work starts while you are young”
excerpt_en: On 15 March 2022 UZNR CG became a member of the YouthHUB network for the Western Balkans and Türkiye and, with the support of the NGO Prima, began carrying out the project “Decent work starts while you are young”, financed by the European Commission.
content_en:
Signing of a contract with the NGO Prima – membership of the YouthHUB network of the Western Balkans and Türkiye and the start of the project “Decent work starts while you are young”
15 March 2022
The Occupational Safety Association of Montenegro has become a member of the YouthHUB network of the Western Balkans and Türkiye and, with the support and coordination of the NGO Prima, will over the coming year carry out the project “Decent work starts while you are young”, financed by the European Commission.
Since all EU-OSHA data show that young people aged 18–24 are at a far greater risk of injury, and since the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work 2021–2027 places particular emphasis on young people, the aim of this project will be to increase the share of young people from the NEET category by improving workplace safety and building a culture of preventing accidents and illness.
Through the questionnaire we will develop, we expect to have a clearer picture at the end of the project year of the number of injuries young people have suffered at their workplaces, particularly in the grey economy.
We will hold educational workshops in secondary vocational schools in Podgorica, Bijelo Polje and Nikšić, as well as at the technical faculties, and in this way acquaint young people, at least in part, with the challenges and problems in occupational safety and health that they will face when they enter the labour market after finishing their education.

title: Snimanje priloga o stanju zaštite i zdravlja na radu u Crnoj Gori
excerpt: Novinarska ekipa iz Skoplja, predvođena Julijom Cvetkovskom, boravila je od 18. do 20. januara 2022. u Crnoj Gori radi snimanja priloga o problemima u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu.
content:
18-20.01.2022.
Kako je jedna od aktivnosti projekta „Unapređenje uslova rada i zaštite i zdravlja na radu kao podrška zemljama Zapadnog Balkana u procesu pristupanja Evropskoj uniji“ bilo snimanje emisije/priloga o problemima i izazovima u oblasti ZZNR, u Crnoj Gori je boravila novinarka Julija Cvetkovska, iz Skoplja, sa svojom ekipom snimatelja i saradnika, u periodu od 18. do 20. januara 2022. Urađeni su intrvjui u kojema su predstavnici različitih institucija govorili o temi zaštite i zdravlja na radu iz svog ugla. Takođe je neophodno bilo imati i jedan primjer iz prakse - intervju sa osobom koja je doživjela povredu na radu i načinu na koji je ili nije ostvarila svoja prava.
UZNRCG je u svojim prostorijama ugostilo Damjana Šišovića. Damjan, koji nije imao validan ugovor o radu, je februara 2020. godine doživeo tešku povredu na radu, gdje je bio angažovan na montiranju lifta na gradilištu zgrade u Nikšiću. Dok je radio u kućištu lifta, elektromotor od 170 kilograma je kliznuo sa šina i udario ga u potiljak, a zatim ga prignječio uz skelu. Taj motor su dan ranije montirali neki drugi radnici i zaboravili da postave graničnik, a Damjan pri tom nikada nije dobio zaštitnu opremu. Završio je u Urgentnom centru u Podgorici sa napuklom vilicom, polomljenim prednjim zubima, uz nagnječenje ramena i lijeve ruke i oštećenje dva kičmena pršljena.
Inspekcija je poslije nezgode utvrdila da je Šišovićev poslodavac imao propuste u zaštiti na radu koji su uzrokovali nesreću i izrekla novčane kazne od 1.000 eura za njegovog poslodavca kompaniju Tri best i 60 eura za tadašnje ovlašćeno lice - direktora firme koji je u međuvremenu preminuo. Osnovno državno tužilaštvo, međutim, nije utvrdilo bilo čiju krivicu.
Ovo je klasični primjer kako se veliki broj poslodavaca u građevinarstvu odnosi prema zaposlenima.
Đina Janković je govorila o ulozi UZNRCG u ovoj oblasti, uticaju koji ova organizacija ima na podizanje svijesti, ulozi u edukacijama zaposlenih i poslodavaca iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kao i u segmentu kreiranja javnih politika, ali i o aktivnostima koje realizuju i strateškim ciljevima na čijoj realizaciji rade poslednjih godina, u saradnji sa kolegama iz regiona.
Predstavnici UZNRCG su tom prilikom, zajedno sa novinarskom ekipom, bili u posjeti Upravi za inspekcijske poslove. Razgovor su vodili sa inspektorima rada za oblast zaštite i zdravlja na radu – Zlatkom Popovićem i Radmilom Mićović. Oni su govorili o položaju inspektora u Crnoj Gori, broju nadzora koje su obavili u toku prošle godine i broju kazni koje su izrečene zbog nepoštovanja Zakona o zaštiti i zdravlju a radu, u tom periodu, kao i o problemima s kojima se suočava ova oblast zbog nedostatka jedinsvenih statističkih podataka o povredama. Osvrnuli su se i na problem nedostatka vremena i prostora, koje bi inspektori trebalo da imaju za edukativni nadzor, kako bi pomogli i doprinijeli da se situacija poboljša, što je uzrokovano nedovoljnim brojem angažovanih inspektora.
Ekipa je boravila i u posjeti Ministarstvu ekonomskog razvoja. O ZZNR se razgovaralo sa Danijelom Šuković, načelnicom Direkcije za zaštitu na radu. G-đa Šuković je govorila o samom Zakonu o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu u Crnoj Gori, o tome kada je usvojen i o tome kolika je odgovornost i uloga Ministarstva ekonomskog razvoja u kreiranju politika zaštite i zdravlja na radu, za sve zaposlene, i koliko je to uspješno. Bilo je riječi o mehanizmima kontrole i nadzora, kojima raspolaže MER, da bi moglo da kontroliše koliko i kako se zakon sprovodi. Govorilo se o tome zašto ne postoji jedinsvena statistika o broju nezgoda na radu, ali i kakva je procedura u Crnoj Gori kada dođe do nezgode na radu i koji se koraci sprovode. Novinarka je pokušala da sazna kakva je komunikacija zakonodavstva i inspektorata sa organizacijama civilnog društva koje se bave zaštitom i zdravljem na radu, da li su ovi odnosi transparentni i odgovorni kako bi obje strane zajedno doprinijele smanjenju nesreća na radnim mjestima i da li jedni druge slušaju i uvažavaju. Na kraju je bilo riječi o tome kako je izgledala primjena zaštite i zdravlja na radu u vrijeme pandemije.
Budući da je medicina rada neizostavni dio zaštite i zdravlja na radu, predstavnici UZNRCG su zajedno sa novinarskom ekipom organizovali sastanak sa doktorkom medicine rada Ljiljanom Kezunović. Doktorka je govorila o stanju medicine rada u Crnoj Gori, kao i o tome ko po zakonu treba da učestvuje u postupku u slučaju povrede na radu. Fokus razgovora je bio na malom broju doktora medicine rada, kao i o nepostojanja Zavoda za medicinu rada u Crnoj Gori, što predstavlja veliki problem, naročito s aspekta dokazivanja profesionalnih bolesti i bolesti u vezi sa radom.
Ekipa je razgovarala i sa Željkom Mirković, novinarkom TV NovaM, koja je govorila o ulozi medija Crnoj Gori u kreiranju javne svijesti i preventivne kulture u oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, kao i neophodnosti njihovog većeg angažovanja.
title_en: Filming a report on the state of occupational safety and health in Montenegro
excerpt_en: A television crew from Skopje, led by Julija Cvetkovska, was in Montenegro from 18 to 20 January 2022 to film a report on the problems facing occupational safety and health.
content_en:
18–20 January 2022
Since one of the activities of the project “Improving working conditions and occupational safety and health in support of the Western Balkan countries in the EU accession process” was to film a programme about the problems and challenges facing OSH, the journalist Julija Cvetkovska from Skopje was in Montenegro with her crew and colleagues from 18 to 20 January 2022. Interviews were recorded in which representatives of various institutions spoke about occupational safety and health from their own perspective. It was also necessary to have an example from practice — an interview with someone who had suffered an injury at work and how they did or did not manage to exercise their rights.
UZNR CG hosted Damjan Šišović at its premises. In February 2020 Damjan, who had no valid employment contract, suffered a serious injury at work while installing a lift on a building site in Nikšić. As he was working inside the lift shaft, a 170-kilogram electric motor slipped off its rails and struck him on the back of the head, then crushed him against the scaffolding. The motor had been installed the previous day by other workers who forgot to fit a stop, and Damjan had never been given any protective equipment. He ended up in the emergency centre in Podgorica with a fractured jaw, broken front teeth, a crushed shoulder and left arm and damage to two vertebrae.
After the accident the inspectorate established that Šišović's employer had failed in its occupational safety duties, causing the accident, and imposed fines of 1,000 euros on his employer, the company Tri best, and 60 euros on the then authorised person — the company's director, who has since died. The Basic State Prosecutor's Office, however, established no one's guilt.
This is a classic example of how a great many employers in construction treat their employees.
Đina Janković spoke about UZNR CG's role in this field, the influence the organisation has on raising awareness, its role in educating employees and employers about occupational safety and health and in shaping public policy, and about the activities it carries out and the strategic objectives it has been working towards in recent years together with colleagues from the region.
Representatives of UZNR CG and the television crew also visited the Administration of Inspection Affairs. They spoke with the labour inspectors for occupational safety and health, Zlatko Popović and Radmila Mićović, who described the position of inspectors in Montenegro, the number of inspections they carried out over the past year and the number of penalties imposed for breaches of the Law on Occupational Safety and Health during that period, and the problems the field faces because of the absence of unified statistics on injuries. They also touched on the lack of time and scope inspectors have for educational inspections that would help improve the situation, caused by there being too few inspectors.
The crew also visited the Ministry of Economic Development. OSH was discussed with Danijela Šuković, head of the Directorate for Occupational Safety. Ms Šuković spoke about the Law on Occupational Safety and Health in Montenegro, when it was adopted, and how great the Ministry of Economic Development's responsibility and role is in shaping occupational safety and health policy for all employees, and how successful that has been. There was discussion of the control and supervision mechanisms available to the Ministry for monitoring how far and how well the law is applied. There was discussion of why there are no unified statistics on the number of accidents at work, and of the procedure in Montenegro when an accident at work occurs and the steps that follow. The journalist sought to find out what communication there is between the legislature and the inspectorate and the civil society organisations working on occupational safety and health, whether these relationships are transparent and accountable so that both sides can together help reduce accidents at work, and whether each side listens to and respects the other. Finally there was discussion of how occupational safety and health was applied during the pandemic.
Since occupational medicine is an indispensable part of occupational safety and health, representatives of UZNR CG and the television crew arranged a meeting with the occupational medicine doctor Ljiljana Kezunović. She spoke about the state of occupational medicine in Montenegro and about who by law should be involved in the procedure following an injury at work. The discussion focused on the small number of occupational medicine doctors and the absence of an institute of occupational medicine in Montenegro, which is a major problem, particularly as regards proving occupational diseases and work-related illnesses.
The crew also spoke with Željka Mirković, a journalist at TV NovaM, who discussed the media's role in Montenegro in creating public awareness and a preventive culture in occupational safety and health, and the need for them to be more actively engaged.

title: Regionalni poziv za dodjelu grant sredstava lokalnim NVO

content:

title: Radionica Zajedničkim rješenjima do rezultata u poglavlju 19 – Socijalna politika i zapošljavanje
excerpt: Ministarstvo ekonomskog razvoja i Generalni sekretarijat Vlade organizovali su 29. i 30. novembra 2021. u Bečićima radionicu za Radnu grupu za pregovaračko poglavlje 19, uz učešće predstavnika UZNRCG.
content:
29. i 30. novembar 2021.
Radionicu, koja je održana 29. i 30. novembra 2021. godine, u hotelu Mediteran, u Bečićima, su organizovali Ministarstvo ekonomskog razvoja i Generalni sekretarijat Vlade Crn Gore, u okviru projekta ME4EU koji finansira EU.
Radionici su prisustvovali članovi Radne grupe za pripremu i vođenje pregovora o pristupanju Crne Gore Evropskoj uniji za oblast pravne tekovine Evropske unije koja se odnosi na pregovaračko poglavlje 19 – Socijalna politika i zapošljavanje. Osim Đine Janković koja je, kao predstavnica UZNRCG, članica Radne grupe za poglavlje 19, učesnik radionice je, kao predstavnik Udruženja, bio i potpredsjednik Branislav Šebek.
Učesnici radionice, članovi Radne grupe su razmatrali implementaciju i nadzor nad primjenom Zakona o radu i Zakona o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu. Razmijenjena su mišljenja u pogledu dosadašnje primjene zakona i unapređenja prava zaposlenih u skladu sa pravnom tekovinom EU.
Prisutni su se podsjetili da je Zakon o radu donijet krajem 2019. godine i da je usklađen sa 14 direktiva Evropske unije, ali je, takođe, skrenuta pažnja da zbog pandemije koronavirusa koja je proizvela izvjesna ograničenja u primjeni pojedinih instituta radnog prava, nisu postojali svi uslovi da se vidi njegova sveobuhvatna primjena na terenu.
Budući da implementacija Zakona o radu čini jedan od uslova za zatvaranje Poglavlja 19, potvrđeno je da je zajednička odgovornost svih da se ulože napore kako bi se, kroz kreiranje propisa, kao i dalju primjenu zakona, došlo do željenog cilja.
Kada je bilo rječi o Zakonu o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu, koji je izmijenjen i dopunjen sredinom 2018. godine, a usklađen je sa dvije relevantne direktive EU, iskorištena je prilika da se skrene pažnja na to da je i implementacija ovog zakona jedan od uslova za zatvaranje poglavlja 19, ali i na probleme i izazove na koje nas je pandemija podsjetila. Stavljajući na test spremnost i fleksibilnost, zaposlenih i posldavca u prethodnom periodu, podsjetila je koliko je oblast zaštite i zdravlja na radu važna, i koliko je neophodno raditi na njenoj implementaciji kako bi se osigurala zaštita i zdravlje najvećeg i najbitnijeg resursa svake kompanije, a to su zaposleni.
Ova radionica je iskoriščena kao odlična prilika da se, u Crnoj Gori, promoviše dvogodišnja kampanja EU-OSHA-e „Zdrava radna mjesta – smanjenje opterećenja“. Shodno tome, prezentaciju na ovu temu je imao Michele Dinelli iz EU-OSHA, Menadžer projekta za predpristupne zemlje. Govorio je trogodišnjem projektu koji je sprovela EU-OSHA, a čiji je cilj bio da se istraže pitanja poremećaja mišićno-koštanog sistema, povezanih sa radom i politike koje se na to odnose, poboljša razumijevanje te teme i utvrde djelotvorni načini sprječavanja poremećaja mišićno-kooštanog sistema povezanih sa radom.
Cilj ove radionice je bio da se, između ostalog, razmotri na koji način je moguće djelotvornije raditi na pripremi i primjeni zakonskih rješenja u cilju ostvarivanja prava i zaštite zaposlenih u Crnoj Gori. Budući da ovo poglavlje obuhvata najvažnije segmente politika koji su preduslov za ekonomski razvoj zasnovan na znanju, visokom nivou zaposlenosti i socijalne kohezije, neophodno je da nacionalni normativni okvir jasno odslikava potrebe našeg društva i države koja stremi evropskim vrijednostima, čime će se jedino postići napredak u pregovaračkom procesu.
Predstavljen je pregovarački proces s osvrtom na ciljeve EU u oblasti socijalne politike i zapošljavanja, koordinacija evropskih poslova u Crnoj Gori, kao i uloga i aktivnosti Radne grupe za poglavlje 19. Ukazano je na oblasti i pitanja važna za ispunjavanje obaveza iz pregovaračkog procesa, kroz prizmu završnih mjerila i preporuka EK u posljednjem Izvještaju o Crnoj Gori.
Zaključeno je da su pravedan pristup socijalnim službama, napredan sistem socijalne zaštite, obrazovan kadar, visoka stopa zaposlenosti i podsticajne mjere za one koji su manje prisutni na tržištu rada, ciljevi države koja vodi brigu o svojim građanima. Takođe je naglašeno da su završna mjerila izazovna i da je pred nama period intenziviranja dinamike cjelokupnog pregovaračkog procesa, i da jedino konstruktivnim radom i posvećenošću svih relevantnih poslenika oblasti koje pokriva ovo poglavlje, možemo dokazati da smo kredibilan partner u ovom procesu.
title_en: Workshop “Joint solutions for results in Chapter 19 – Social Policy and Employment”
excerpt_en: On 29 and 30 November 2021 the Ministry of Economic Development and the General Secretariat of the Government held a workshop in Bečići for the Working Group on negotiating Chapter 19, with UZNR CG taking part.
content_en:
29 and 30 November 2021
The workshop, held on 29 and 30 November 2021 at the Hotel Mediteran in Bečići, was organised by the Ministry of Economic Development and the General Secretariat of the Government of Montenegro, under the EU-financed ME4EU project.
It was attended by members of the Working Group for preparing and conducting Montenegro's EU accession negotiations for the area of the EU acquis covered by negotiating Chapter 19 – Social Policy and Employment. Besides Đina Janković, who as UZNR CG's representative is a member of the Working Group for Chapter 19, the Association was also represented at the workshop by vice-president Branislav Šebek.
The workshop's participants, members of the Working Group, considered the implementation of, and supervision over, the Labour Law and the Law on Occupational Safety and Health. Views were exchanged on how the laws have been applied so far and on advancing employees' rights in line with the EU acquis.
Participants recalled that the Labour Law was adopted at the end of 2019 and is aligned with 14 European Union directives, but attention was also drawn to the fact that because the coronavirus pandemic placed certain limits on the application of some labour law institutions, the conditions did not exist for its comprehensive application in the field to be observed.
Since implementation of the Labour Law is one of the conditions for closing Chapter 19, it was confirmed that it is everyone's shared responsibility to make the effort needed — through the drafting of regulations and the further application of the law — to reach the desired goal.
As regards the Law on Occupational Safety and Health, amended in mid-2018 and aligned with two relevant EU directives, the opportunity was taken to point out that implementation of this law too is one of the conditions for closing Chapter 19, and also to note the problems and challenges the pandemic reminded us of. By testing the preparedness and flexibility of employees and employers, the pandemic reminded us how important occupational safety and health is, and how necessary it is to work on implementing it in order to protect the safety and health of every company's greatest and most important resource — its employees.
The workshop was used as an excellent opportunity to promote EU-OSHA's two-year campaign “Healthy Workplaces Lighten the Load” in Montenegro. Michele Dinelli of EU-OSHA, project manager for the pre-accession countries, gave a presentation on the subject. He spoke about the three-year project EU-OSHA carried out with the aim of examining work-related musculoskeletal disorders and the policies relating to them, improving understanding of the subject and identifying effective ways of preventing work-related musculoskeletal disorders.
The aim of the workshop was, among other things, to consider how work on preparing and applying legislation to secure employees' rights and protection in Montenegro can be made more effective. Since this chapter covers the most important policy areas underpinning knowledge-based economic development, a high level of employment and social cohesion, the national legal framework must clearly reflect the needs of our society and of a state that aspires to European values — the only way progress in the negotiating process will be achieved.
The negotiating process was presented, with reference to the EU's objectives in social policy and employment, the coordination of European affairs in Montenegro, and the role and activities of the Working Group for Chapter 19. Attention was drawn to the areas and questions important for meeting the obligations of the negotiating process, through the prism of the closing benchmarks and the European Commission's recommendations in its most recent report on Montenegro.
It was concluded that fair access to social services, an advanced social protection system, an educated workforce, a high employment rate and incentives for those less present on the labour market are the goals of a state that cares for its citizens. It was also emphasised that the closing benchmarks are demanding and that the period ahead will intensify the pace of the whole negotiating process, and that only through constructive work and the commitment of everyone active in the fields this chapter covers can we prove ourselves a credible partner in the process.

title: Priprema Nacrta Strategije za unapređenje zaštite i zdravlja na radu 2022-2027. sa akcionim planom za 2022. godine
excerpt: Ministarstvo ekonomskog razvoja organizovalo je krajem novembra 2021. trodnevnu radionicu u Petrovcu za izradu Strategije za unapređenje zaštite i zdravlja na radu 2022–2027, uz učešće predstavnice UZNRCG.
content:
23. do 25. novembar 2021.
U cilju obezbjeđivanja implementacije Zakona o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu i podzakonskih akata koji prate oblast zaštite i zdravlja na radu, a shodno Programu rade Vlade Crne Gore za 2021. godinu i Programu pristupanja Crne Gore Evropskoj uniji 2020 - 2022. godine, pristupilo se izradi Predloga Strategije za unapređenje zaštite i zdravlja na radu u Crnoj Gori 2022. – 2027. godine, sa Akcionim planom implementacije za 2022. godinu.
Ministarstvo ekonomskog razvoja je formiralo Radnu grupu za izradu ovog veoma važnog dokumenta. Radna grupa broji 27 članova i u njoj su predstavnici Ministartva ekonomskog razvoja, Ministarstva zdravlja, Ministarstva ekologije, prostornog planiranja i urbanizma, Ministarstva finansija i socijalnog staranja, Uprave za inspekcijske poslove, Unije poslodavaca, SSCG, USSCG, Fonda za zdravstveno osiguranje, Fonda penzijsko invalidskog osiguranja, Instituta za javno zdravlje, MOR-a i nevladinog sektora. Prdstavnica UZNRCG u Radnoj grupi je Đina Jankovć.
Ministartvo ekonomskog razvoja je u periodu od 23. do 25. novembra 2021. godine organizovalo radionicu, u hotelu Palas u Petrovcu. Na toj trodnevnoj radionici, članovi Radne grupe su doprinijeli da se kroz zajednički rad i sagledavanje stanja zaštite i zdravlja na radu u Crnoj Gori, iz različitih uglova, prepoznaju glavni strateški ali i operativni ciljevi, kao i kvalitativni i kvantitaivni indikatori ovog strateškog dokumenta.
Budući da je zaštita i zdravlje na radu djelatnost od javnog interesa, članovi radne grupe su prepoznali svoju odgovornost i ulogu u obezbjeđivanju kvalitetnih temelja za sprovođenje i primjenu mjera zaštite i zdravlja na radu i iznijeli brojna zapaženja i predloge, koji bi, po njihovom mišljenju mogli doprinijeti dostizanju zajedničkog zacrtanog cilja, a to je „VISION ZERO“, rad bez povreda za sve zaposlene u Crnoj Gori.
Svi predlozi i sugestije, koji su se mogli čuti tokom trodnevnog rada, kao i ponuđeni modeli za implementaciju istih kroz operativne ciljeve, su u velikoj mjeri bazirani na novom EU okviru zaštite i zdravlja na radu 2021-2027. kojim se utvrđeni ključni prioriteti i aktivnosti neophodne za poboljšanje zaštite i zdravlja na radu zaposlenih tokom narednih godina u kontekstu postpandemijskih uslova. Akcenat je stavljen i na zelene i digitalne tranzicije, kao ekonomski i demografski izazov koji je donio velike promjene tradicionalnog okruženja na radnom mjestu.
Zajednički stav svih članova Radne grupe je bio da su zdravi i sigurni uslovi rada preduslov za zdravu i produktivniju radnu snagu. Niko ne bi smio da pati od bolesti ili povreda povezanih sa radom. To je važan aspekt održivosti i konkurentnosti ekonomije EU, pa bi trebalo da tako bude i u Crnoj Gori.
Članovi Radne grupe su bili saglasni oko toga da je neophodno da u nacrt Strategije budu unijeti predlozi koji se odnose na sve one izmjene koje je potrebno preduzeti, kako bi se doprinijelo ostvarenju željenih ciljeva.
To se odnosilo, između ostalog, na izradu softvera koji bi omogućio efikasnu prijavu povreda na radu. Da bi do toga došlo, konstatovano je da je neohodno uraditi reviziju postojećih pravilnika koji se odnose na povrede na radu, kao i omogućiti uvođenje elktronske forme PPR, koja bi bila uvezana sa postojećim registrima PPR i PB. Takođe je navedeno da je neophodno, što prije, izraditi jedinsvenu listu profesionalnih bolesti.
Nepostojanje Zavoda za medicinu rada je prepoznato kao veliki problem, pa je predložena izrada studije izvodljivosti za formiranje jedne takve institucije. Tom studijom bi se, takođe, obuhvatila procjena institucionalne spremnosti ključnih aktera za uvođenje jedinsvenog softvera, kao i specifikacija ulupnih softverskih troškova sa finansijskom primjenom.
Budući da je za rješavanje brojnih izazova i nedostataka u sistemu zaštite i zdravlja na radu neophodna revizija podzakonskih akata, predloženo je formiranje međuresorne radne grupe sa ciljem analize važeće zakonske regulative.
Nepostojanje nacionalnog Savjeta za ZZNR je, takođe, prepoznato kao jedan od prioriteta, pa bi buduće aktivnosti trebalo da budu usmjerene ka njegovom formiranju.
Predavanja na temu ZZNR u svim srednjim školama, kao i uvođenje ZZNR u obrazovni sistem, prilagođeno specifičnim potrebama ciljnih grupa, je predloženo da bude definisano Akcionim planom implementacije za period 2022.
U cilju savladavanja problema do kojih dovodi neusaglašenost Zakona o radu i Zakona o ZZNR, predložene su izmjene radnog zakonodavstva.
Naglašeno je i da su neophodne izmjene Pravilnika o procjeni rozika, uspostavljanje modela procjene rizike sa zdravstvenog aspekta, kao i uspostavljanje modela osposobljavanja zaposlenih sa zdravstvenog aspekta. S ciljem što bezbjednijeg savladavanja prepreka izazvanih epidemiološkom situacijom, analizirana je mogućnost da se COVID-19 uvrsti na listu profesionalnih bolesti.
Skrenuta je pažnja na neophodnost transponovanja Direktive 2010/32 o sprečavanju povreda oštrim predmetima.
Postignuta je saglasnost oko neophodnosti uvođenja izmjena kada su u pitanju stručna lica iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu, koordinatori K1 i K2, ali i rad ovlašćenih organizacija za poslove ZZNR:
Da bi se predloženo realizovalo neophodna su izmjene brojnih pravilnika koji regulišu ovu oblast.
Da bi se došlo do kvalitetnih stručnih lica koji će svojim radom uticati na poboljšanje stanja na terenu, neophodno je, na prvom mjestu, izraditi priručnik za polaganje stručnog ispita, organizovati obuke za pripremu kandidata za polaganje stručnog ispita, kao i organizovati kontinuirane kvartalne obuke, sa najmanje 4 modula, koje bi stručna lica bila u obavezi da pohađaju, kao uslov koji bi im omogućavao da zadrže/produže licencu.
Slični predlozi su se mogli čuti i po pitanju koordinatora na gradilištima. Osim priručnika koji bi služio kandidatima za pripremu za polaganje ispita za koordinatora K1 i K2, takođe bi bilo neophodno organizovati obuke, kroz koje bi kandidati bili u obavezi da prođu, kako bi stekli uslov da polažu ispit i kako bi kasnije mogli da se kontinuirano edukuju u cilju što kvalitetnijeg obavljanja izuzetno odgovornih zadataka na gradilištima.
Za poboljšanje kvaliteta usluga, koje poslodavcima pružaju ovlašćene organizacije, neophodno je usvojiti godišnji plan nadzora, a rezultate nadzora učiniti javnim. Predloženo je i pronalaženje mehanizma za kontrolu kvaliteta akta o procjeni rizika i njegova verifikacija. Za postizanje ovih predloženih mjera i postizanje predviđenih ciljeva, neophodno je jačanje kapaciteta Direkcije za ZZNR, a kao najbolje rješenje je predloženo formiranje Uprave za ZZNR.
title_en: Preparing the draft Strategy for Improving Occupational Safety and Health 2022–2027 with an action plan for 2022
excerpt_en: In late November 2021 the Ministry of Economic Development held a three-day workshop in Petrovac to draft the Strategy for Improving Occupational Safety and Health 2022–2027, with UZNR CG taking part.
content_en:
23–25 November 2021
In order to secure the implementation of the Law on Occupational Safety and Health and of the secondary legislation covering the field, and in line with the Government of Montenegro's Work Programme for 2021 and Montenegro's Programme of Accession to the European Union 2020–2022, work began on drafting the Strategy for Improving Occupational Safety and Health in Montenegro 2022–2027, with an implementation action plan for 2022.
The Ministry of Economic Development formed a Working Group to draft this very important document. The Working Group has 27 members and includes representatives of the Ministry of Economic Development, the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Ecology, Spatial Planning and Urbanism, the Ministry of Finance and Social Welfare, the Administration of Inspection Affairs, the Employers' Union, the Confederation of Trade Unions of Montenegro, the Union of Free Trade Unions of Montenegro, the Health Insurance Fund, the Pension and Disability Insurance Fund, the Institute of Public Health, the ILO and the non-governmental sector. UZNR CG's representative on the Working Group is Đina Janković.
From 23 to 25 November 2021 the Ministry of Economic Development held a workshop at the Hotel Palas in Petrovac. Over those three days the Working Group's members, working together and considering the state of occupational safety and health in Montenegro from different angles, helped identify the main strategic and operational objectives of this strategic document and its qualitative and quantitative indicators.
Since occupational safety and health is an activity of public interest, the Working Group's members recognised their responsibility and role in laying good foundations for implementing and applying occupational safety and health measures, and put forward numerous observations and proposals which in their view could help achieve the shared goal set: “VISION ZERO”, work without injuries for everyone employed in Montenegro.
All the proposals and suggestions made over the three days of work, and the models offered for implementing them through operational objectives, are largely based on the new EU strategic framework on health and safety at work 2021–2027, which sets out the key priorities and actions needed to improve employees' safety and health at work over the coming years in post-pandemic conditions. Emphasis was also placed on the green and digital transitions as an economic and demographic challenge that has brought major changes to the traditional workplace.
The shared view of all the Working Group's members was that healthy and safe working conditions are a precondition for a healthy, more productive workforce. No one should suffer work-related illness or injury. That is an important aspect of the sustainability and competitiveness of the EU economy, and it should be so in Montenegro too.
The Working Group's members agreed that the draft Strategy must include proposals covering all the changes that need to be made in order to help achieve the desired objectives.
Those included, among other things, developing software that would allow injuries at work to be reported effectively. For that to happen, it was noted that the existing rulebooks on injuries at work must be revised and an electronic injury report form introduced, linked to the existing registers of injuries at work and occupational diseases. It was also noted that a single list of occupational diseases must be produced as soon as possible.
The absence of an institute of occupational medicine was identified as a major problem, so a feasibility study for establishing such an institution was proposed. That study would also cover an assessment of the key actors' institutional readiness to introduce a single software system, and a specification of the total software costs and their financial implications.
Since addressing the many challenges and shortcomings in the occupational safety and health system requires a revision of the secondary legislation, it was proposed that a cross-ministerial working group be formed to analyse the legislation in force.
The absence of a national Council for OSH was also identified as a priority, so future work should be directed at establishing one.
It was proposed that lectures on OSH in all secondary schools, and the introduction of OSH into the education system tailored to the specific needs of the target groups, be set out in the implementation action plan for 2022.
In order to overcome the problems caused by the inconsistency between the Labour Law and the Law on OSH, changes to employment legislation were proposed.
It was also emphasised that changes are needed to the Rulebook on risk assessment, together with the establishment of a model for assessing risk from a health point of view and a model for training employees from a health point of view. With a view to overcoming the obstacles caused by the epidemiological situation as safely as possible, the possibility of adding COVID-19 to the list of occupational diseases was analysed.
Attention was drawn to the need to transpose Directive 2010/32 on the prevention of sharps injuries.
Agreement was reached on the need for changes regarding occupational safety and health professionals, K1 and K2 coordinators, and the work of organisations licensed for OSH work.
Carrying out these proposals requires changes to numerous rulebooks governing the field.
If we are to have good-quality safety professionals whose work improves the situation in the field, it is first of all essential to produce a handbook for the professional examination, to organise training to prepare candidates for the examination, and to organise continuous quarterly training with at least 4 modules, which safety professionals would be required to attend as a condition of keeping or renewing their licence.
Similar proposals were made regarding site coordinators. Besides a handbook to help candidates prepare for the K1 and K2 coordinator examinations, it would also be necessary to organise training that candidates would have to complete in order to qualify to sit the examination and to be able to continue their education thereafter, so that they can carry out their extremely responsible tasks on construction sites as well as possible.
To improve the quality of the services licensed organisations provide to employers, an annual supervision plan must be adopted and the results of that supervision made public. It was also proposed that a mechanism be found for checking the quality of the risk assessment act and verifying it. Achieving these proposed measures and objectives requires the capacity of the Directorate for OSH to be strengthened, and the best solution proposed was the establishment of an Administration for OSH.

title: Poziv medijima za formiranje regionalne medijske mreže
excerpt: BALcanOSH mreža je u okviru regionalnog EU projekta organizovala radionicu u Ohridu (20–23. oktobra 2021) za petnaest novinara iz pet zemalja, uz poziv medijima da se pridruže regionalnoj medijskoj mreži.
content:
Organizacije koja se bave zaštitom i zdravljem na radu iz Makedonije, Srbije, Crne Gore Kosova i Albanije, odnosno BALcanOSH mreža, realizuju regionalni projekat „Unapređenje uslova rada i zaštite i zdravlja na radu kao podrška zemljama Zapadnog Balkanu u procesu pristupanja Evropskoj uniji“, koji je finansiran od strane Evropske Komisije, a čija realizacija će trajati narednih 46 meseci.
Do sada su pripremljene i distribuirane brojne brošure o zaštiti i zdravlju na radu u uslovima pandemije Covid19. Takođe je urađen i promotivni film o Covid19 i rizicima na radnim mjestima izazvanim pandemijom, na jezicima svih 5 IPA zemalja, učesnica projekta.
Pripremljen je i distribuiran „Izvještaj o procjeni organizacionih i institucionalnih kapaciteta Nacionalnih saveta za zaštitu i zdravlje na radu u IPA zemljama“.
U okviru ovog projekta BALcanOSH mreža je pozvala sve zainteresovane medijske organizacije i novinare da se pridruže formiranju regionalne medijske mreže u oblasti rada.
Svrha formiranja i funkcionisanja regionalne mreže je potreba za poboljšanjem komunikacije i saradnje između organizacija civilnog društva, medija/medijskih orzanizacija i novinara u promovisanju pitanja koja se odnose na rad, uslove rada i zaštitu i zdravlje na radu na Zapadnom Balkanu. Osim toga ova mreža će imati za cilj jačanje stabilnosti zemalja i ubrzavanje njene političke, ekonomske i društvene reforme u evropskim integracijama.
U okviru projekta održana je prva radionica iz oblasti zaštite i zdravlja na radu i standarda iz oblasti istraživačkog novinarstva i izveštavanja na regionalnom nivou od 20. do 23. oktobra u Ohridu.
Na radionici je učestvovalo 15 novinara iz Makedonije, Srbije, Crne Gore, Kosova i Albanije a predavači su bili poznati makednoski komunikolog i novinarka Bojan Kordalov i Santa Argirova.
S poštovanjem,
Kordinatorka projekta Đina Janković

title_en: Call to the media to form a regional media network
excerpt_en: Under a regional EU project, the BALcanOSH network held a workshop in Ohrid (20–23 October 2021) for fifteen journalists from five countries, and invited media organisations to join a regional media network.
content_en:
Organisations working on occupational safety and health from North Macedonia, Serbia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Albania — the BALcanOSH network — are carrying out the regional project “Improving working conditions and occupational safety and health in support of the Western Balkan countries in the EU accession process”, financed by the European Commission and running for the next 46 months.
Numerous brochures on occupational safety and health during the Covid-19 pandemic have been produced and distributed so far. A promotional film about Covid-19 and the workplace risks the pandemic has caused has also been made, in the languages of all 5 IPA countries taking part in the project.
The “Report on the assessment of the organisational and institutional capacity of national councils for occupational safety and health in the IPA countries” has also been produced and distributed.
Under this project the BALcanOSH network has invited all interested media organisations and journalists to join in forming a regional media network in the field of labour.
The purpose of forming and running the regional network is the need to improve communication and cooperation between civil society organisations, media outlets and journalists in promoting issues relating to labour, working conditions and occupational safety and health in the Western Balkans. Beyond that, the network will aim to strengthen the stability of the countries and to accelerate their political, economic and social reform on the path of European integration.
Under the project, the first regional workshop on occupational safety and health and on standards of investigative journalism and reporting was held from 20 to 23 October in Ohrid.
The workshop was attended by 15 journalists from North Macedonia, Serbia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Albania, and the trainers were the well-known Macedonian communications expert Bojan Kordalov and the journalist Santa Argirova.
Yours sincerely,
Project coordinator Đina Janković
